children.translated_text: First Chapter

children.text: yasmin sarvaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ | yaḥ sarvaṃ sarvataś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He in whom is everything, from whom is everything, who is everything and is everywhere,

children.text: yaś ca sarvamayo nityaṃ | tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ || (RA_1.1)
children.translated_text: and who is eternally the essence of all — to that all-Self, salutations. (RA 1.1)
On the delightful peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, adorned with various jewels,
covered with various trees and creepers, free from concealed [unwanted] associations, (RA 1.2)
bowing with her head to the god of gods, seated in comfort, blue-throated, three-eyed,
<s>Pārvatī</s> the goddess asks: (RA 1.3)
The blessed Goddess said:
O god of gods, great god, O Time, O burner of the body of <s>Kāma</s>,
O destroyer of the <s>Kula</s>, <s>Kaula</s>, <s>Mahākaula</s>, <s>Siddhakaula</s>, and the rest — (RA 1.4)
By your grace, I have heard everything, understood it without remainder.

children.text: yadi te 'ham anugrāhyā | yadyahaṃ tava vallabhā || (RA_1.5)
children.translated_text: If I am worthy of your grace, if I am your beloved — (RA 1.5)
That which is hinted at in all the <s>tantras</s> but never fully revealed —
this <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), O Lord — what is it like? Please tell me. (RA 1.6)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Excellent, excellent, O greatly fortunate one! Excellent, O daughter of the mountain!

children.text: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi | bhaktānāṃ hitakāmyayā || (RA_1.7)
children.translated_text: Excellently asked by you, O goddess, out of desire for the welfare of devotees. (RA 1.7)
The knowledge of identity with <s>Śiva</s> in a body free from old age and death —
that is <s>jīvanmukti</s>, O great goddess, difficult to attain even for the gods. (RA 1.8)

children.text: piṇḍapāte ca yo mokṣaḥ | sa ca mokṣo nirarthakaḥ |
children.translated_text: The liberation that comes upon the fall of the body — that liberation is useless.

children.text: piṇḍe tu patite devi | gardabho 'pi vimucyate || (RA_1.9)
children.translated_text: For upon the fall of the body, O goddess, even a donkey is liberated! (RA 1.9)

children.text: yadi muktirbhagakṣobhe | kiṃ na muñcanti gardabhāḥ |
children.translated_text: If liberation comes through the agitation of the genitals, why are donkeys not liberated?

children.text: ajāś ca vṛṣabhāścaiva | kiṃna muktā gaṇāmbike || (RA_1.10)
children.translated_text: And goats and bulls — are they not liberated, O mother of the <s>gaṇas</s>? (RA 1.10)
Therefore, one should preserve the body through <s>rasas</s> (mercury/elixirs) and <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenating preparations).
If liberation comes from the consumption of semen, urine, and excrement, (RA 1.11)
why are dogs and pigs not liberated, O great goddess?
In all six <s>darśanas</s> (philosophical systems), liberation is shown [only] at the fall of the body. (RA 1.12)
But even that [liberation], [said to be] like an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit in the palm, is not directly perceived.

children.text: akathyam api deveśi | sadbhāvaṃ kathayāmi te || (RA_1.13)
children.translated_text: Even what is unspeakable, O queen of gods, I shall tell you truly. (RA 1.13)

children.text: śūnyapāpo mantrayājī | na piṇḍaṃ dhārayet kvacit |
children.translated_text: One who is free from sin, a worshipper with <s>mantras</s>, should never [fail to] sustain the body.
Even for the gods, O queen of gods, the sustaining of the body is difficult to achieve. (RA 1.14)
How much more so for human beings, dwellers on the surface of the earth!

children.text:
dharme naṣṭe kuto dharmaḥ | dharme naṣṭe kutaḥ kriyā ||
                    (RA_1.15)
children.translated_text: When <s>dharma</s> is lost, whence [comes] <s>dharma</s>? When <s>dharma</s> is lost, whence [comes] ritual action? (RA 1.15)

children.text: kriyānaṣṭe kuto yogaḥ | yoge naṣṭe kuto gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: When ritual action is lost, whence [comes] <s>yoga</s>? When <s>yoga</s> is lost, whence [comes] the path?

children.text: gatinaṣṭe kuto mokṣo | mokṣe naṣṭe na kiṃcana || (RA_1.16)
children.translated_text: When the path is lost, whence [comes] liberation? When liberation is lost — nothing remains. (RA 1.16)
The blessed Goddess said:
The nature of <s>jīvanmukti</s>, O god of gods, I have heard.

children.text: tatpratyupāyaṃ me brūhi | yadyasti karuṇā mayi || (RA_1.17)
children.translated_text: Now tell me its means, if you have compassion for me. (RA 1.17)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Through <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action), O queen of gods, the sustaining of the body is attained.

children.text: rasaś ca pavanaśceti | karmayogo dvidhā mataḥ || (RA_1.18)
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>pavana</s> (breath) — <s>karmayoga</s> is considered twofold. (RA 1.18)

children.text: mūrchito harati vyādhiṃ | mṛto jīvayati svayam |
children.translated_text: When swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>), [<s>rasa</s>] destroys disease; when killed (<s>mṛta</s>), it revives [the dead].

children.text:
baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ kuryāt | raso vāyuś ca bhairavi ||
                    (RA_1.19)
children.translated_text: When bound (<s>baddha</s>), it bestows the power of moving through the sky — [such is] <s>rasa</s> and <s>vāyu</s> (breath), O <s>Bhairavī</s>. (RA 1.19)
Liberation comes from knowledge, O queen of the gods; knowledge comes from the retention of breath.

children.text:
tatra devi sthiraṃ piṇḍaṃ | yatra sthairye rasaḥ prabhuḥ ||
                    (RA_1.20)
children.translated_text: Therein, O goddess, the body becomes stable; in that stability, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is the master. (RA 1.20)
In a short time, O goddess, a body free from old age and death is produced.
And the meditation of the mind is attained through the practice of <s>rasa</s> (mercury). (RA 1.21)

children.text: satyaṃ sa labhate devi | jñānaṃ vijñānapūrvakam |
children.translated_text: Truly, O goddess, one obtains knowledge preceded by direct experience.

children.text:
tasya mantrāś ca sidhyanti | yo 'śnāti mṛtasūtakam ||
                    (RA_1.22)
children.translated_text: <s>Mantras</s> become efficacious for one who consumes killed mercury (<s>mṛtasūtaka</s>). (RA 1.22)

children.text: yāvanna śaktipātas tu | na yāvat pāśakṛntanam |
children.translated_text: As long as there is no descent of <s>Śakti</s>, as long as the bonds are not cut,
until then, how can understanding of killed mercury arise for that person? (RA 1.23)
Those who are always devoted to liquor and meat, who delight in vulvas and phalluses —
for those whose understanding is destroyed, knowledge of <s>rasa</s> is extremely difficult to obtain. (RA 1.24)
For those devoid of the <s>Kula</s> doctrine, who are desirous of the true vision —

children.text: na sidhyati raso devi | pibanti mṛgatṛṣṇikām || (RA_1.25)
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s> does not become efficacious, O goddess; they drink a mirage. (RA 1.25)
One who eats the flesh of the cow and drinks the immortal liquor —
I consider him of noble lineage, a knower of <s>rasa</s>; the rest are base. (RA 1.26)

children.text: na garbhaḥ sampradāyārthe | raso garbho vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: There is no embryo in the meaning of the tradition; <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is the embryo that is prescribed.

children.text:
tenāyaṃ labhate siddhiṃ | na siddhiḥ sūtakaṃ vinā ||
                    (RA_1.27)
children.translated_text: Through it, one obtains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection); there is no <s>siddhi</s> without mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>). (RA 1.27)

children.text: yāvanna harabījaṃ tu | bhakṣayet pāradaṃ rasam |
children.translated_text: As long as one does not consume mercury (<s>pārada</s>) — the seed of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —

children.text:
tāvattasya kuto muktiḥ | kutaḥ piṇḍasya dhāraṇam ||
                    (RA_1.28)
children.translated_text: until then, how can liberation come? How can the body be sustained? (RA 1.28)
Those whose understanding is [clouded by] devotion to liquor and meat, deluded by the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: jalpanti ca vayaṃ muktā | yāsyāmaḥ śivamandiram || (RA_1.29)
children.translated_text: they prattle: 'We are liberated, we shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.' (RA 1.29)
Indifferent to the yoga of sustaining the body, dull-witted,
with fragmentary knowledge, O queen of gods, the entire world of movable and immovable [beings] is deluded. (RA 1.30)

children.text: svadehe khecaratvaṃ ca | śivatvaṃ yena labhyate |
children.translated_text: The power of traversing the sky in one's own body and the attainment of <s>Śivahood</s> —

children.text: tādṛśe tu rasajñāne | nityābhyāsaṃ kuru priye || (RA_1.31)
children.translated_text: in such knowledge of <s>rasa</s>, practice constantly, O beloved! (RA 1.31)
The blessed Goddess said:
The descent (<s>avatāra</s>) of <s>Rasendra</s> (the lord of mercury), and its greatness, O lord of the gods —
I wish to hear, O lord of gods; please tell me the truth. (RA 1.32)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Excellently asked, O greatly fortunate one — the most secret of secrets.
[This is] a meditation that bestows grace, beneficial to the worlds. (RA 1.33)

children.text: tvaṃ mātā sarvabhūtānāṃ | pitā cāhaṃ sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: You are the mother of all beings, and I am the eternal father.

children.text: dvayoś ca yo raso devi | mahāmaithunasambhavaḥ || (RA_1.34)
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> (essence/mercury) of us two, O goddess, is born from the great union. (RA 1.34)
Because it arises from spontaneous union (<s>svairatas</s>), O goddess, it is called <s>pārada</s> (mercury).

children.text: pārado gadito yaś ca | parārthaṃ sādhakottamaiḥ || (RA_1.35)
children.translated_text: And it is called <s>pārada</s> because it is [said to be] for the benefit of others (<s>parārtha</s>) by the greatest of practitioners. (RA 1.35)
This <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is equal to me, O goddess, born from my own limbs.
Because it is the <s>rasa</s> (essence/fluid) of my body, it is called <s>rasa</s>. (RA 1.36)
From seeing it, from touching it, from consuming it, from remembering it,

children.text:
pūjanāc ca pradānāc ca | dṛśyate ṣaḍvidhaṃ phalam ||
                    (RA_1.37)
children.translated_text: from worshipping it, and from giving it away — a sixfold fruit is seen. (RA 1.37)

children.text: kedārādīni liṅgāni | pṛthivyā yāni kāni ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅgas</s> such as <s>Kedāra</s> and whichever others exist on earth —

children.text:
tāni dṛṣṭvā tu yatpuṇyaṃ | tatpuṇyaṃ rasadarśanāt ||
                    (RA_1.38)
children.translated_text: the merit obtained from seeing them — that same merit [comes] from seeing <s>rasa</s>. (RA 1.38)
Mercury mixed with sandalwood, <s>aguru</s>, camphor, and saffron,
swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>) — for the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, for the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>'s presence. (RA 1.39)
From consuming [it], O supreme goddess, <s>rasa</s> destroys the three [kinds of] sin.
Likewise it destroys the three afflictions (<s>tāpatraya</s>), and diseases arising from the three <s>doṣas</s>. (RA 1.40)
That which is difficult for those devoted to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — the supreme abode is attained
by <s>Rasendra</s> (the lord of mercury) established within the lotus of the heart-space, O great goddess. (RA 1.41)
Through remembering [it], one is freed from sins accumulated in previous births. (RA 1.42)
The fruit that comes from the proper worship of a thousand self-manifested <s>liṅgas</s> —
that fruit, multiplied ten million times, comes from the worship of a <s>rasa-liṅga</s> (mercury <s>liṅga</s>). (RA 1.43)

children.text: adhamaḥ khagavādas tu | vilavādas tu madhyamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Inferior is the practice of alchemy with birds (<s>khagavāda</s>); middling is the practice with earths (<s>vilavāda</s>);
superior is the practice with <s>mantras</s>; but the practice of <s>rasa</s> (mercury alchemy) is the most excellent. (RA 1.44)
Those who, [merely] knowing <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>, disparage the practice of <s>rasa</s> —
they all go to hell, having destroyed their stock of merit. (RA 1.45)
The science of <s>rasa</s> is the supreme science, extremely difficult to obtain even in the three worlds.
Since it bestows both enjoyment and liberation, therefore it should be given by those who possess [its] qualities. (RA 1.46)
Some say 'it exists'; some say 'it does not exist.'

children.text:
āstike tu bhavetsiddhiḥ | tasya sidhyati bhūtale ||
                    (RA_1.47)
children.translated_text: For the believer, there is <s>siddhi</s> (success) — for him, it becomes efficacious on earth. (RA 1.47)
For the disbeliever, by the force [of disbelief], who says 'it does not exist, it does not exist' —

children.text: tasya nāsti priye siddhir | janmakoṭiśatair api || (RA_1.48)
children.translated_text: for him there is no <s>siddhi</s>, O beloved, even in hundreds of millions of births. (RA 1.48)
Even if liberated through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, the sinner who disparages <s>rasa</s> —

children.text: nāhaṃ trātā bhave tasya | janmakoṭiśatair api || (RA_1.49)
children.translated_text: I am not his protector in [this] existence, even in hundreds of millions of births. (RA 1.49)
He is born as a dog, O goddess, for as long as a thousand births.
For thirty million births, he is born as a cat [because of disrespecting] <s>rasa</s>;
as a donkey for a hundred thousand births; as a crow for a hundred thousand births. (RA 1.50)
As a worm for a hundred thousand births; as a rooster for a hundred thousand births;
as a vulture for a hundred thousand births — [such is the fate of] the sinner who disparages <s>rasa</s>. (RA 1.51)
One who converses with or has bodily contact with those who disparage <s>rasa</s> —
for a thousand births, that person is afflicted with suffering. (RA 1.52)
In its potency, digestion, and post-digestive effect, mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>) is like nectar.
Therefore, mercury removes birth, old age, and disease, O beloved. (RA 1.53)
One should first propitiate the <s>guru</s> with a purified inner self.
When the <s>guru</s> is pleased, the rays [of knowledge, i.e., the lineage-holders] bestow the tradition. (RA 1.54)

children.text: gurusevāṃ vinā karma | yaḥ kuryān mūḍhacetanaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who performs actions without service to the <s>guru</s>, a fool —

children.text:
sa yāti niṣphalaṃ karma | svapnalabdhaṃ dhanaṃ yathā ||
                    (RA_1.55)
children.translated_text: his action becomes fruitless, like wealth obtained in a dream. (RA 1.55)

children.text: yaḥ karma kurute dṛṣṭaṃ | tasya lābhaḥ pade pade |
children.translated_text: One who performs action that has been seen [i.e., properly demonstrated] — for him, profit at every step.

children.text: kārayed rasavādaṃ tu | tuṣṭena guruṇā priye || (RA_1.56)
children.translated_text: One should have the practice of <s>rasavāda</s> (mercury alchemy) carried out by a <s>guru</s> who is pleased, O beloved. (RA 1.56)
This is the teaching of the means to <s>siddhi</s>, bestowing both enjoyment and liberation.
This <s>Rasārṇava</s>, the great <s>tantra</s>, is supremely difficult to obtain. (RA 1.57)
It is to be kept secret; obtained by the grace of the <s>guru</s>, it brings the fruit of <s>siddhi</s>.
Having obtained the procedures of <s>rasa</s> here, one should not act with egoism. (RA 1.58)

children.text: anujñātaś ca guruṇā | labdhvā cājñāṃ rasāṅkuśīm |
children.translated_text: Authorized by the <s>guru</s>, having received the command that is the goad of <s>rasa</s>,
taking refuge in the body of <s>Bhairavī</s>, one should accomplish <s>Rasabhairava</s>. (RA 1.59)
Thus the origin and the greatness of <s>rasa</s> have been told, O queen of the gods.

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_1.60)
children.translated_text: Tell me now, O queen of gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 1.60)
Second Chapter [The Procedure of Initiation]
The blessed Goddess said:

children.text: rasopadeśadātā ca | kathaṃ syādvada me prabho |
children.translated_text: Who may be a teacher of the science of <s>rasa</s>? Tell me, O lord.
And who may be a disciple, O god, devoted to the practice of <s>rasa</s>? (RA 2.1)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
One who is free from desire, free from ego, devoid of greed and deceit,
always devoted to the <s>Kula</s> path, and devoted to the worship of the <s>guru</s> — (RA 2.2)
self-controlled, skilled in instructing disciples, powerful, free from jealousy,

children.text:
dharmajñaḥ satyavāk dakṣaḥ | śīlavān guṇavān śuciḥ ||
                    (RA_2.3)
children.translated_text: a knower of <s>dharma</s>, truthful in speech, capable, virtuous, possessed of good qualities, pure — (RA 2.3)
a knower of many treatises on <s>rasa</s>, expert in the <s>rasa</s>-laboratory (<s>rasamaṇḍapa</s>),
a knower of the procedure of <s>rasa</s>-initiation, [and of] apparatus (<s>yantra</s>), herbs, and great mercurial preparations — (RA 2.4)
the [proper] sequences of coloring agents, the division of seeds, the pairing and combination [of substances], <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline agents),

children.text: rañjanaṃ sāraṇaṃ tailaṃ | dalāni krāmaṇāni ca || (RA_2.5)
children.translated_text: dyeing (<s>rañjana</s>), flowing (<s>sāraṇa</s>), oils, leaves (<s>dala</s>), and processes of sequential transmutation (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) — (RA 2.5)
enhancement of color, softening, and calcination (<s>jāraṇā</s>) of the young and the bound [mercury],

children.text: khecarīṃ bhūcarīṃ caiva | yo vetti sa gururmataḥ || (RA_2.6)
children.translated_text: the <s>khecarī</s> [process] and the <s>bhūcarī</s> [process] — one who knows these is considered a [true] <s>guru</s>. (RA 2.6)
A knower of place, time, and procedure, endowed with compassion and generosity,
free from greed and deceit, devoted to the practice of <s>mantras</s> — (RA 2.7)
possessing the marks of [reading] physiognomy, profound, devoted to the <s>guru</s>,
always devoted to the worship of the <s>devas</s>, the fire, the <s>yoginī</s> circle, and the <s>Kula</s> —
the disciple [should be] humble, a knower of the <s>tantras</s>, truthful, and firm in his vows. (RA 2.8)
Those persons whose hands bear the marks of a water-pot, a spade, a banner, a conch, and the like —

children.text: karair adhiṣṭhitā devi | yojyās te nidhisādhane || (RA_2.9)
children.translated_text: they, O goddess, are to be employed in the quest for [alchemical] treasures. (RA 2.9)
Strong, of great courage, with dark or red eyes,
with curved noses, always fierce — [these are] commended for the quest of [underground] cavities. (RA 2.10)
Those with lean flesh on the tops of their heads, red-haired, free from laziness —
Those who are hard [in constitution] and hot-footed — one should employ in the practice of metallurgy. (RA 2.11)
First, O Goddess, one should examine the practitioners with great care —
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>, in due order. (RA 2.12)
Those who have conquered the senses, who endure hardship, who are constantly diligent,

children.text:
śūrāś ca kṛtavidyāś ca | praśastāḥ sādhakāḥ priye ||
                    (RA_2.13)
children.translated_text: who are brave, and who are learned — such practitioners are commended, O Beloved. (RA 2.13)
Those who lack initiation in mercury (<s>rasa-dīkṣā</s>) and are devoid of the stated characteristics,
who are ruinous, devoted to sin — one should carefully avoid them. (RA 2.14)
A woman who is of bad conduct, ill-behaved, harsh, quarrelsome,

children.text: bahvāśinī ca duścittā | koṭarākṣī ca nirdayā |
children.translated_text: gluttonous, ill-minded, hollow-eyed, and merciless,

children.text: rasanindākarī yā ca | tāṃ nārīṃ parivarjayet || (RA_2.15)
children.translated_text: and who disparages mercury (<s>rasa</s>) — such a woman one should shun. (RA 2.15)
The surface of the earth is filled with such women, O Beautiful-hipped One,
but there is no woman like one who can bind mercury (<s>rasabandhakī</s>). (RA 2.16)
The [types of women are:] <s>Kākiṇī</s>, <s>Kīkaṇī</s>, and also <s>Kāñcikācinī</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe ṛtumatī | sā nārī kākiṇī smṛtā || (RA_2.17)
children.translated_text: A woman who menstruates during the dark fortnight is known as a <s>Kākiṇī</s>. (RA 2.17)

children.text: ubhayapakṣe ṛtumatī | sā nārī kīkaṇī matā || (RA_2.18)
children.translated_text: A woman who menstruates during both fortnights is considered a <s>Kīkaṇī</s>. (RA 2.18)
A woman who menstruates during the bright fortnight is a <s>Kāñcikācinī</s>. (RA 2.19)
Endowed with fresh youth, beautiful, with a charming smile,

children.text: sūkṣmakeśā tu yā nārī | kṣīrāhārapriyā sadā || (RA_2.20)
children.translated_text: a woman with fine hair, who always delights in a diet of milk — (RA 2.20)
who always speaks sweetly, who loves discourse on the teachings of <s>Śiva</s>,
whose face is lotus-shaped, whose gaze resembles the blue lotus — (RA 2.21)
whose teeth are like diamonds, whose lower lip resembles coral,

children.text: yasyāḥ payodharau devi | tuṅgapīnau samāv ubhau || (RA_2.22)
children.translated_text: whose breasts, O Goddess, are high, full, and symmetrical — (RA 2.22)
whose vulva resembles an <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) leaf, whose genitalia are symmetrical,
whose feet are fleshy, smooth, and rounded with spiraling hair — (RA 2.23)

children.text: śyāmā ca madhye kṣāmā ca | tanvī bhaktiparā śive |
children.translated_text: who is dark-complexioned, slender in the waist, lean, devoted to [<s>Śiva</s>]-worship, O <s>Śiva</s>'s consort —

children.text: padminī sā tu vijñeyā | prasannā mṛgalocanā || (RA_2.24)
children.translated_text: she should be known as a <s>Padminī</s> (lotus-woman), serene and deer-eyed. (RA 2.24)
She who menstruates on the full moon or the new moon day, every fortnight,
[is one of] the six varieties of <s>Kākiṇī</s> by name, described earlier — she who yields mercury. (RA 2.25)

children.text: yasya tuṣṭo mahādevas | tasya siddho rasāyane |
children.translated_text: He with whom <s>Mahādeva</s> is pleased — for him, success in the mercurial science (<s>rasāyana</s>) [is assured].
Through her alone, O Queen of the Gods, one should perform the operations with mercury. (RA 2.26)

children.text: tasya hi nirmalā buddhir | niścitā rasasādhane |
children.translated_text: For his intellect is pure and resolute in the accomplishment of mercury.

children.text:
tasmādguruś ca śiṣyaś ca | pūrvoktaḥ siddhibhāgbhavet ||
                    (RA_2.27)
children.translated_text: Therefore, the teacher and the disciple, as described above, shall be partakers of success. (RA 2.27)
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: īdṛśair lakṣaṇaiḥ nārīṃ | kutaḥ prāpnoti sādhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: With such characteristics, how does the practitioner obtain [such] a woman?

children.text: yatra rūpaṃ mahādeva | lakṣaṇaṃ nātra vidyate || (RA_2.28)
children.translated_text: Where beauty exists, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, [the required] characteristics are not found there. (RA 2.28)

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ vidyate yatra | bhāvanā nātra vidyate |
children.translated_text: Where the characteristics are found, the [proper] disposition is not present there;
or else, how can beauty be conferred upon one who lacks beauty? (RA 2.29)
Where have you seen the triad of characteristics [together], O <s>Maheśvara</s>?
Tell me the means by which that [combination] arises, O Lord. (RA 2.30)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu devi paraṃ guhyaṃ | yat surair api durlabham |
children.translated_text: Listen, O Goddess, to the supreme secret, which is difficult to obtain even for the gods.
One who was born from the father <s>Sadāśiva</s>, whose birth was in the womb of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> — (RA 2.31)
Her intellect becomes pure, O Goddess, in the accomplishment of mercury.
One should give her the <s>Tvaritā</s> mantra; she should recite it, free from pride. (RA 2.32)

children.text: lakṣamantraṃ japedyā tu | jāyate sā sulakṣaṇā |
children.translated_text: A woman who recites [that] mantra a hundred thousand times becomes endowed with [all] auspicious marks.

children.text:
baddhvā tu khecarīṃ mudrāṃ | japet pheṭkārabhairavīm ||
                    (RA_2.33)
children.translated_text: Having assumed the <s>khecarī mudrā</s>, she should recite [the mantra of] <s>Pheṭkāra-Bhairavī</s>. (RA 2.33)

children.text: mameyaṃ caṇḍikā mātā | janma ca tripurāntakāt |
children.translated_text: '<s>Caṇḍikā</s> is my mother, and my birth is from <s>Tripurāntaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).

children.text:
kālikāhaṃ samudbhūtā- | smīdṛśaṃ saṃsmaret tu sā ||
                    (RA_2.34)
children.translated_text: I am <s>Kālikā</s>, thus born' — she should contemplate in this manner. (RA 2.34)

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca | trailokye kathayet tu sā |
children.translated_text: Past, present, and future — she shall declare [all] in the three worlds.
Such helpers [come to] him as [his] destiny requires. (RA 2.35)
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:
O God of gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, vessel of all knowledge,

children.text: rasadīkṣāṃ tu pṛcchāmi | sādhakānāṃ hitāya vai || (RA_2.36)
children.translated_text: I ask about the initiation for mercury (<s>rasa-dīkṣā</s>), for the benefit of practitioners. (RA 2.36)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu bhairavi yadbhāvam | apūrvaṃ varṇayāmi te |
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, I shall describe to you an unprecedented matter.
Hear, then, the procedure for the initiation of mercury, as I declare it. (RA 2.37)
Where there is a king devoted to righteous policy, powerful, dedicated to <s>dharma</s>,
and a minister who knows the essence of <s>dharma</s>, endowed with devotion and faith — (RA 2.38)
There one should perform this work — the binding of mercury and the mercurial elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>).

children.text: janā māheśvarā yatra | tatra sthāne tu kārayet || (RA_2.39)
children.translated_text: Where there are devotees of <s>Maheśvara</s>, in such a place one should perform [the work]. (RA 2.39)

children.text: kārayed vijane sthāne | paśuryatra na vidyate |
children.translated_text: One should perform [it] in a secluded place where no animal is present,
in a well-hidden, well-leveled place, free from all disturbances. (RA 2.40)
Enclosed by walls and moats, guarded by doors and bolts,
in a solitary, clean, pleasing [spot], surrounded by various flowering trees — (RA 2.41)
frequented by swans and water-birds, adorned with <s>cakravāka</s> birds,
furnished with divine medicinal plants, with water and dark-green grass — (RA 2.42)
adorned with groves of night-lotuses, blue lotuses, white water-lilies, and plantain trees,
in a variegated house-garden — one should perform [the work], O Supreme Goddess. (RA 2.43)
In the midst of that [garden], O Queen of the Gods, [build a laboratory] furnished with an intoxicated elephant,
equipped with windows, with smoke-vents rising upward — (RA 2.44)
furnished with red banners, properly equipped with implements,
with medicines, chaff, firewood, and forest-lotuses arranged in separate compartments — (RA 2.45)
with the guardians of the directions drawn [on the walls], with <s>Vināyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) properly worshipped,
consecrated by <s>Umā</s> and <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and protected by the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians). (RA 2.46)
One should construct a one-storied or two-storied pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>).
Then, in the bright fortnight, O Goddess, when the moon, stars, and strength [of the planets] are favorable — (RA 2.47)

children.text: puṇye tithau muhūrte ca | lagne saumyagrahekṣite |
children.translated_text: on an auspicious <s>tithi</s> and <s>muhūrta</s>, when the ascendant is aspected by benefic planets,
having bathed, wearing white garments, with white garlands and unguents — (RA 2.48)
having worshipped young girls with honey, ghee, curd, milk, and sesame seeds,
on [ground] smeared with the dung of a tawny cow, surrounded by golden water-pots — (RA 2.49)
strewn with barley and white mustard seeds, adorned with fragrance and garlands,
there, on a pedestal (<s>karapīṭha</s>) constructed of bricks, O Goddess of the gods — (RA 2.50)
having carved out a stone slab [and] a stone bolt, O Beloved,
having performed the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual installation) with the <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> [mantra] on the fingers, heart, and other [places] — (RA 2.51)

children.text: rasaliṅgaṃ nyasettatra | hemnā ca sahitaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: one should install the mercury-<s>liṅga</s> there, together with gold, O Beloved.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sūtarājasya | mūlamantra udāhṛtaḥ || (RA_2.52)
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ</s> — the root mantra of the King of Mercury (<s>Sūtarāja</s>) is declared. (RA 2.52)
On that [<s>liṅga</s>], one should invoke the goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> with the root [mantra], O Beloved.

children.text: caturasre tu dikpālān | pūjayitvā bahiḥ kramāt || (RA_2.53)
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the guardians of the directions outside in the four corners, in sequence — (RA 2.53)
<s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgirīṭa</s>, <s>Mahābala</s>,

children.text:
kumbhakarṇaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ | bhṛṅgīkaṃ ca dṛḍhāyudham ||
                    (RA_2.54)
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgīka</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhāyudha</s> — (RA 2.54)
placing [them] fourfold at the doors, one should worship [them] on the right and left.
Having worshipped <s>Śukra</s> in the east, <s>Skanda</s> in the southeastern quarter — (RA 2.55)

children.text: dakṣiṇasyāṃ tato rudraṃ | pavanaṃ nairṛte tathā |
children.translated_text: then <s>Rudra</s> in the south, <s>Pavana</s> (Wind) in the southwest,

children.text: śivaṃ paścimabhāge tu | pāvakaṃ vāyave nyaset |
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> in the western quarter, <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire) in the northwest,
<s>Umā</s> in the northern quarter, and <s>Vyāpaka</s> (the Pervader) in the northeast. (RA 2.56)

children.text: lepikā kṣepikā caiva | kṣārikā rañjikā tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Lepikā</s> (the Anointer), <s>Kṣepikā</s> (the Projector), <s>Kṣārikā</s> (the Alkalizer), <s>Rañjikā</s> (the Colorer),
<s>Lohaṭī</s> (the Metal-eater), <s>Bandhakārī</s> (the Binder), <s>Bhūcarī</s> (the Earth-mover), <s>Mṛtyunāśinī</s> (the Death-destroyer), (RA 2.57)

children.text: vibhūtiḥ khecarī caiva | daśa dūtyaḥ krameṇa ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhūti</s> (Splendor), and <s>Khecarī</s> (the Space-mover) — these ten female messengers (<s>dūtīs</s>), in order,

children.text:
pūjyāstvaṣṭadale padme | ūrdhvādhas tu daleṣu ca ||
                    (RA_2.58)
children.translated_text: are to be worshipped on an eight-petaled lotus, on the upper and lower petals. (RA 2.58)
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>Vimala</s> (stainless [ore]), <s>Śaila</s> (mountain [ore]), <s>Capala</s> (quicksilver [ore]), <s>Rasaka</s> (zinc ore),
<s>Sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol), and the two [kinds of] <s>Gandha-tāla</s> (orpiment) — in order from the east. (RA 2.59)
The <s>Rudras</s> with eighteen arms, five faces, three eyes,
with crowns adorned by the crescent moon, blue-throated, bearing the bull banner — (RA 2.60)
all bearing their respective colors, and likewise the eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>,
are to be worshipped, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, on the second eight-petaled lotus. (RA 2.61)
In the pericarp, from the east onward, first the four <s>Śaktis</s>:

children.text: mālinī hemaśaktiś ca | parā śaktirbalā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: <s>Mālinī</s>, <s>Hemaśakti</s> (Golden Power), <s>Parā Śakti</s> (Supreme Power) [also called] <s>Balā</s>,
and <s>Aparā Vajraśakti</s> (Lower Adamantine Power) — whose radiance is called <s>parāpara</s> (the supreme-and-non-supreme). (RA 2.62)

children.text: madhye tāsāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ | sarvajñaṃ rasabhairavam |
children.translated_text: In the center of those <s>Śaktis</s>, [one should worship] the omniscient <s>Rasa-Bhairava</s>,
resembling pure crystal, with five faces and three eyes — (RA 2.63)
with blazing tawny and fierce eyes, with flaming tongue and mouth,
with blazing brows and blazing hair, terrible to behold, seated on a corpse-throne — (RA 2.64)
wearing a crown of matted locks, with the crescent moon at its crest,
clad in a tiger skin, with a serpent as sacred thread, bearing the bull banner — (RA 2.65)
the god with eighteen arms, with a slightly smiling face —
one should worship the complete <s>Śiva</s> with the thirty-two-syllable mantra. (RA 2.66)

children.text:
raseśvarasya mantraṃ ca | kathyamānaṃ nibodha me ||
                    (RA_2.67)
children.translated_text: Now hear from me the mantra of <s>Raseśvara</s> (the Lord of Mercury) as it is declared: (RA 2.67)

children.text:
oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ raseśvarāya mahākālāya mahābalāyāghorabhairavāya vajravīra
                    krodhakaṅkāla kṣlauḥ kṣlaḥ || Ras_2.68 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ Raseśvarāya Mahākālāya Mahābalāya Aghorabhairavāya Vajravīra Krodhakaṅkāla kṣlauḥ kṣlaḥ</s>. (RA 2.68)
On His lap, [one should worship] <s>Mahādevī</s>, adorned with jeweled ornaments,
radiant as molten gold, wearing yellow garments, three-eyed — (RA 2.69)
flanked by two white fly-whisks, resplendent under a pearl-[studded] parasol,
holding a goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) and a rosary (<s>akṣamālā</s>) in her right hands — (RA 2.70)
and a noose (<s>pāśa</s>) and the gesture of fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>) in her left [hands], with the crescent moon as her crest —
<s>Rasāṅkuśī Mahādevī</s>, blue-throated, full of compassion. (RA 2.71)
One should worship [her] for the success of mercury, with the five-seed (<s>pañcabīja</s>) <s>vidyā</s>:

children.text: vāgbhavaṃ bhuvaneśīṃ ca | śrībījaṃ ca sureśvari || (RA_2.72)
children.translated_text: <s>Vāgbhava</s> [<s>aiṃ</s>], <s>Bhuvaneśī</s> [<s>hrīṃ</s>], and the <s>Śrī</s>-seed [<s>śrīṃ</s>], O Goddess of the gods — (RA 2.72)
the <s>Mādana</s> [seed, <s>klīṃ</s>] and the <s>Śakti</s>-seed [<s>hauṃ</s>] — a <s>vidyā</s> supremely difficult to obtain.
With incense, lamps, food offerings, flowers, betel, and sandalwood — (RA 2.73)
with the sounds of peace-recitations (<s>śānti-pāṭha</s>), hymns of praise, and auspicious chants,
accompanied by the clanging of bells — having performed the worship according to the prescribed method — (RA 2.74)
one should give the sacrificial offering (<s>bali</s>) with the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra], for the pacification of all obstacles,
to the <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s>, with care. (RA 2.75)
Endowed with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, beginning with <s>Oṃ</s> and ending with <s>Namaḥ</s>,
[this mantra is] the accomplisher of all rites, O Goddess, the destroyer of obstacles and calamities. (RA 2.76)
Having recited to the extent of one's ability the <s>Rasāṅkuśī vidyā</s>,
having prepared a fire-pit, O Goddess of gods, [and] a <s>yoni-cakra</s> (ritual diagram) with a girdle — (RA 2.77)
having performed the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) there with ghee and sesame seeds, in sequence,
one should set up a water-pot, O Goddess, filled with milk and fruits — (RA 2.78)
furnished with the five gems, wrapped in cloth,
consecrated separately by the eighteen <s>vidyās</s> — (RA 2.79)
filled with fragrance, flowers, and the like, adorned with leaves,
and having worshipped the <s>arghya</s>-vessel (offering-bowl), one should sprinkle the practitioner with the <s>vardhanī</s> water. (RA 2.80)
One hundred and eight [times], thus, with the water from the <s>arghya</s>-vessel —
the knower of mantras should consecrate [the practitioner] with the water from the pot, according to the prescribed method. (RA 2.81)
One should impart the <s>vidyā</s>, O Goddess, and instruct the mercury-practitioner,
as well as the <s>kumāras</s>, <s>yoginīs</s>, <s>yogins</s>, and <s>sādhakas</s>, with appropriate [initiations]. (RA 2.82)

children.text: tarpayed annapānaiś ca | jāgaraṃ tatra kārayet |
children.translated_text: One should satisfy [them] with food and drink, and keep a vigil there.
The practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), thus properly initiated, [should proceed] with the razor-like [technique] (<s>kṣuranāyikā</s>). (RA 2.83)
There, [one should contemplate] the <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) consisting of the five great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>), endowed with the five syllables (<s>varṇapañcaka</s>),
having the five seed-syllables (<s>bīja</s>) as its essence, within the thread of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control). (RA 2.84)
Having formed the <s>Rasāṅkuśī mudrā</s> (Mercury-goad seal), one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, O beloved.
For that [practitioner], O Goddess of Gods, <s>Rasabhairava</s> (the mercury-deity) is accomplished without obstacles. (RA 2.85)
Beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, after the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), the supreme recitation [is performed].
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is the sandalwood, truth (<s>satya</s>) is the flower, non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>) is the incense. (RA 2.86)
Celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is the great lamp, non-acceptance of gifts (<s>apratigraha</s>) is the bell.
The food-offering of milk-rice, O great Goddess, is imbued with compassion for all beings. (RA 2.87)
One should worship the Goddess in secret — such a one becomes a vessel of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).

children.text:
sahasraṃ vā śataṃ vāpi | trisaṃdhyaṃ saṃjapedimām ||
                    (RA_2.88)
children.translated_text: One should recite this [mantra] a thousand times, or a hundred, at the three junctures of the day (<s>trisaṃdhya</s>). (RA 2.88)
By the grace of her command, the mercury becomes <s>khecara</s> (sky-moving, i.e., sublimated).
And divine herbs (<s>divyauṣadhi</s>) too are accomplished for him, O one praised by the gods. (RA 2.89)
Just as one who mounts a maddened elephant in the forest without a goad [comes to grief],
so one who knows not the <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> (mercury-goad [mantra]), having obtained mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), comes to ruin. (RA 2.90)

One who desires accomplishment in all respects should deliberate [on mercury operations] together with the <s>vidyā</s>, [as received] from a teacher belonging to an authentic lineage (<s>satsampradāya</s>),
regarding the procedures born of mercury practice (<s>rasaprayoga</s>). (RA 2.91)
Now, for the descent of the oracular inquiry (<s>praśnāvatāra</s>), one should meditate with a concentrated mind on the previously described <s>Rasabhairava</s>,
and practice [the rites] while absorbed in That. (RA 2.92)
Having placed the mind in the <s>Anāhata</s> [center] and the <s>Brahmarandhra</s> (crown aperture), free from affliction,
having first performed the hand-installation (<s>karanyāsa</s>), then the limb-installation (<s>aṅganyāsa</s>),
one should recite the mantra of <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury-lord) with concentration, according to one's capacity. (RA 2.93)
Having made a square, and within it a hexagonal <s>maṇḍala</s>,

children.text:
hastamātraṃ dvihastaṃ vā | taṇḍulair vimalair likhet ||
                    (RA_2.94)
children.translated_text: one cubit or two cubits [in size], one should draw it with pure rice grains. (RA 2.94)
In a place anointed with fragrant [substances], one should worship with sandalwood and the like. (RA 2.95)
On the pericarp [of the maṇḍala], O Goddess, one should place the previously described <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
In the hexagon, one should install the group of six deities beginning with <s>Mahākāla</s>. (RA 2.96)
<s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Mahābala</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Vajravīraka</s>,

children.text:
nyaset krodhaṃ ca kaṅkālaṃ | mālāmantraiḥ samarcayet ||
                    (RA_2.97)
children.translated_text: one should install <s>Krodha</s> and <s>Kaṅkāla</s>, and worship [them] with the garland-mantras (<s>mālāmantra</s>). (RA 2.97)

children.text:
oṃ hrīṃ krauṃ kṣlaiṃ kṣlaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrūḥ huṃ phaṭ raseśvarāya
                    mahākālabhairavāya raudrarūpāya kṛṣṇapiṅgalalocanāya |
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ krauṃ kṣlaiṃ kṣlaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrūḥ huṃ phaṭ — to <s>Raseśvara</s> (Lord of Mercury), to <s>Mahākālabhairava</s>, to the one of terrifying form, to the one with dark-tawny eyes —

children.text:
avatara 2 avatāraya 2 jalpa 2 jalpaya 2 śubhāśubhaṃ kathaya 2 kathāpaya 2
                    mahārakṣāṃ kuru 2 rasasiddhiṃ dehi |
children.translated_text: descend, descend; make descend, make descend; speak, speak; make speak, make speak; tell the auspicious and inauspicious, tell, tell; make tell, make tell; grant great protection, grant; bestow the <s>siddhi</s> of mercury, bestow!
These are the garland-mantras (<s>mālāmantra</s>).
Oṃ, to <s>Mahākālabhairava</s>, to the Heart, <s>namaḥ</s>.
Oṃ, to <s>Mahābalabhairava</s>, to the Head, <s>svāhā</s>.
Oṃ, to <s>Aghorabhairava</s>, to the Crest-lock, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.
Oṃ, to <s>Vajravīrabhairava</s>, to the Armor, <s>hum</s>.
Oṃ, to <s>Krodhabhairava</s>, to the Eye, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.
Oṃ, to <s>Kaṅkālabhairava</s>, to the Weapon, <s>phaṭ</s>.
Everywhere [the mantra ends with] <s>svāhā</s>.
Thus are the limb-installations (<s>aṅganyāsa</s>).
Thus one should perform the finger-installations (<s>aṅgulīnyāsa</s>) first.
These are the root-mantras (<s>mūlamantra</s>) for the six-limbed worship.
Having thus [performed] the installation of syllables (<s>nyāsākṣara</s>) with groups [of mantras], one should worship with fragrant [substances] and flowers.
One should place a full water-pot (<s>pūrṇakumbha</s>) in the center, together with a saucer and rice grains. (RA 2.98)

children.text:
tasyopari ghṛtadīpaṃ | vartīṃ mantraiś ca mantrayet ||
                    (RA_2.99)
children.translated_text: Upon it, a ghee-lamp — one should consecrate the wick with mantras. (RA 2.99)

children.text: samānīya kumārīṃ tu | kumāraṃ vā suśobhanam |
children.translated_text: Having brought a maiden (<s>kumārī</s>) or a handsome boy (<s>kumāra</s>),
one, two, three, four, or five — as available — one should bring [them],
and worship [them] with fragrant substances, flowers, incense, lamps, and food-offerings (<s>naivedya</s>). (RA 2.100)
For each one, one should install the mantra, along with the Heart-deity and the other [limb-deities]. (RA 2.101)
Then, gazing at that lamp, all the maidens there

children.text: paśyanti devatā dīpe | kumārāś ca śubhāśubham |
children.translated_text: see the deities in the lamp; and the boys [see] the auspicious and inauspicious.
The maidens tell [whether there will be] accomplishment or non-accomplishment. (RA 2.102)
Having thus ascertained the descent of the oracular inquiry (<s>praśnāvatāra</s>), one should proceed with the mercury operations. (RA 2.103)
He who, O Goddess of Gods, with mind absorbed in <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury-lord) previously,

children.text: saptajanma mṛto jāto | na tyajed rasabhāvanam || (RA_2.104)
children.translated_text: having died and been born [again] through seven births, does not abandon the contemplation of mercury. (RA 2.104)
Having thus ascertained the auspicious and inauspicious, endowed with the grace of the deity,
in the pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>), one should worship the Goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> as before. (RA 2.105)
Having also worshipped the preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>) with incense, garlands, sandalwood, and the like,

children.text: aghoreṇa baliṃ dattvā | tataḥ karma samācaret || (RA_2.106)
children.translated_text: having offered a <s>bali</s> (sacrificial offering) with the <s>Aghora</s> [mantra], one should then commence the operation. (RA 2.106)
Herbs [should be placed] in the eastern [quarter] of the pavilion; the sweating of mercury (<s>rasasveda</s>) [should be done] in the domain of fire [i.e., the southeast].
In the southern [quarter], the killing of metals (<s>lohamāra</s>); in the southwest, grinding (<s>peṣaṇa</s>) and the like. (RA 2.107)

children.text: drutikriyā tu vāruṇyāṃ | vāyavye dhamanaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: The melting operation (<s>drutikriyā</s>) in the western [quarter]; in the northwest, the bellowing (<s>dhamana</s>), O beloved.
The enhancement of color (<s>varṇotkarṣa</s>) in the northern [quarter]; in the northeast, the transmutation of mercury (<s>rasavedhana</s>). (RA 2.108)

children.text: āsanaṃ tu guror madhye | niveśya suranāyike |
children.translated_text: The teacher's seat should be installed in the center, O leader of the gods.
The operations from restraining (<s>niyāmana</s>) and so forth up to <s>krāmaṇa</s> (making [mercury] traverse [metals]),
should be performed by the practitioner with the <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> mantra, O fair-faced one. (RA 2.109)
The <s>Rasabhairava</s> previously described, O Goddess of Gods —

children.text: sadyojātaṃ tasya jānu | vāmadevaṃ tu guhyakam || (RA_2.110)
children.translated_text: <s>Sadyojāta</s> is his knee; <s>Vāmadeva</s> is the secret [part]. (RA 2.110)

children.text: aghoraṃ hṛdayaṃ tasya | vaktraṃ tatpuruṣaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: <s>Aghora</s> is his heart; the face is said to be <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Up to the mid-brow is <s>Īśāna</s>; the forehead is the crescent moon (<s>Ardhacandra</s>). (RA 2.111)

children.text: bindur deveśi tasyordhve | bindorūrdhve sthito nadaḥ |
children.translated_text: Above that, O Goddess, is the <s>Bindu</s> (point); above the <s>Bindu</s> abides <s>Nāda</s> (resonance).
Between the forehead and the crown of the head, <s>Śakti</s> is established there. (RA 2.112)
<s>Vyāpinī</s> (the Pervading one) abides at the <s>Brahmarandhra</s>; above that is <s>Unmanā</s> (the Transmental).
<s>Unmanā</s>, the state of <s>Unmanī</s> (transmental consciousness), the imperishable station of <s>Unmanā</s>. (RA 2.113)
Above that is the supreme truth, abiding in the void (<s>vyoman</s>), higher than the highest,

children.text:
śūnyaṃ śūnyaṃ punaḥ śūnyaṃ | triśūnyaṃ ca nirāmayam ||
                    (RA_2.114)
children.translated_text: void upon void upon void — the triple void, free from affliction. (RA 2.114)

children.text: nabhaś ca gaganaṃ vyoma | khamākāśaṃ ca kevalam |
children.translated_text: Sky (<s>nabhas</s>), firmament (<s>gagana</s>), space (<s>vyoman</s>), ether (<s>kha</s>), <s>ākāśa</s> (space), and the Absolute (<s>kevala</s>),
without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), without impurity (<s>nirmala</s>), eternal (<s>nitya</s>), without waves (<s>nistaraṅga</s>), free from affliction (<s>nirāmaya</s>). (RA 2.115)
Without phenomenal expansion (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), without support (<s>nirādhāra</s>), without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), [yet] within the range of [manifest] qualities (<s>guṇa</s>).
One should always meditate on <s>Rasabhairava</s> in this form within one's own body. (RA 2.116)

children.text: yadā ca niścalaṃ dhyāyet | yadā ca niścalaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: When one meditates motionlessly, when the mind is steady,
then mercury (<s>sūta</s>), [placed] in the midst of fire, is bound (<s>baddhyate</s>) — likewise motionless. (RA 2.117)

children.text:
yadā ca calati dhyānaṃ | raso vahnau na tiṣṭhati ||
                    (RA_2.118)
children.translated_text: When meditation wavers, the mercury does not remain stable in the fire. (RA 2.118)
Outside the <s>maṇḍala</s>, at night, with liquor, fish, meat, and the like,
one should worship the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. (RA 2.119)
Obstacles to the operation and obstacles to the fruit [arise] by the millions.

children.text: sambhavanti tathā tattac | chāntyai ca vaṭukeśvaram |
children.translated_text: For the pacification of each of those, [one should worship] <s>Vaṭukeśvara</s>,
and having first worshipped the group of six grace-bestowing [deities], one should then commence. (RA 2.120)
At the conclusion of the operation, one should again worship the child [deity], the eight-times-eight grace-bestowing [deities],

children.text:
sampūjya viniyuñjyāt tat | siddhadravyaṃ tu siddhidam ||
                    (RA_2.121)
children.translated_text: and having worshipped [them], should consecrate the accomplished substance (<s>siddhadravya</s>) that bestows <s>siddhi</s>. (RA 2.121)

children.text: siddhas tu nāśayed vādaṃ | taddeśaṃ tu parityajet |
children.translated_text: One who has attained <s>siddhi</s> should abandon disputation, leave that place,
and wander begging food like a bee (<s>mādhukārī bhikṣā</s>), when the great mercury is perfectly accomplished. (RA 2.122)
If an obstacle arises from carelessness after the binding of mercury has been accomplished,
the pacification of mercury should be performed — one should not agitate the mercury. (RA 2.123)

children.text: rasaṃ na darśayed devi | nārīhaste na pātayet |
children.translated_text: One should not show the mercury, O Goddess; one should not let it fall into a woman's hand.

children.text:
nāryai guhyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ | dravyaṃ tābhyo hi gopayet ||
                    (RA_2.124)
children.translated_text: The secret should not be told to a woman; the substances should be concealed from them. (RA 2.124)
One should not perform [operations] with others' substances; one should not touch others' wives.

children.text:
parānnaṃ naiva bhuñjīta | parāṃścaiva na viśvaset ||
                    (RA_2.125)
children.translated_text: One should not eat others' food; one should not trust others. (RA 2.125)
One should not give [the accomplished mercury] to those of wicked intent, nor to one who begs under the guise of a gathering. (RA 2.126)
On the eighth [lunar day], on the full moon, on the new moon, on the beginnings of <s>Yugas</s>,
at the solstices, at the equinoxes, and especially on the fourteenth [lunar day],
one should celebrate a festival of mercury (<s>rasotsava</s>) according to one's means. (RA 2.127)
Thus, O Goddess, one who celebrates the mercury festival with devotion —
various sins including the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmahatyā</s>) are destroyed. (RA 2.128)

children.text: anena vidhinā yatra | pūjāṃ kurvanti sādhakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where practitioners (<s>sādhaka</s>) perform worship according to this procedure,

children.text:
na tatra rogadaurgatyaṃ | netayaḥ prabhavanti ca ||
                    (RA_2.129)
children.translated_text: there neither disease nor misfortune prevails, nor do [hostile] forces have power. (RA 2.129)
Having established worship of mercury in this manner according to the proper rites,

children.text:
paścāt karma vidhātavyam | ātmanaḥ śubham icchatām ||
                    (RA_2.130)
children.translated_text: thereafter the operation should be performed by those who desire their own well-being. (RA 2.130)

children.text: anyathā kurute yas tu | tasya siddhir na jāyate |
children.translated_text: But one who does otherwise — for him, <s>siddhi</s> does not arise;

children.text: apāyaḥ pāpaśaṅkā ca | buddhibhaṅgo hi jāyate || (RA_2.131)
children.translated_text: calamity, fear of sin, and breakdown of intellect arise. (RA 2.131)

children.text: avajñā rogajātaṃ ca | saṃdehaś ca pade pade |
children.translated_text: Contempt, diseases, and doubt at every step —

children.text: ālasyād gurulobhāc ca | parasya kathanena ca |
children.translated_text: from laziness, from the greed of the teacher, and from telling others,

children.text: utpannam api vijñānaṃ | haranti kulakāḥ priye || (RA_2.132)
children.translated_text: even knowledge that has arisen is carried away by the <s>kulakas</s> (obstructing spirits), O beloved. (RA 2.132)
One who is initiated should perform mercury operations knowing the mantra-installations (<s>mantranyāsa</s>).

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_2.133)
children.translated_text: Tell me about that, O Goddess of Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 2.133)
Third Chapter [Mantra-Installations]
The blessed Goddess spoke:
O Lord, God of Gods, Protector of the World, Master of the Universe,
describe the mantra-installations (<s>mantranyāsa</s>) that are auxiliary to the mercury operations. (RA 3.1)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> spoke:
I shall declare yet another [form] — the mantra-embodied <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>,

children.text: pañcamaṃ tu gṛhaṃ devi | durlabhaṃ devadānavaiḥ || (RA_3.2)
children.translated_text: the fifth house (<s>gṛha</s>), O Goddess, which is difficult to obtain [even] for gods and demons. (RA 3.2)
There are four principal houses; the fifth is the <s>Haṃsa</s>-house.

children.text: yatra siddhir makārādiḥ | tiṣṭhate pañcame gṛhe || (RA_3.3)
children.translated_text: Where the <s>siddhi</s> beginning with the letter 'ma' abides — in the fifth house. (RA 3.3)

children.text: liṅgāśrayaṃ yathā rūpaṃ | liṅgimāyā tu liṅginī |
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>liṅga</s> has a form dependent on its support, the <s>māyā</s> of the <s>liṅga</s>-bearer is the <s>liṅginī</s>.

children.text: gaganena tu sā jñeyā | bhagarekhā tu pañcame || (RA_3.4)
children.translated_text: She is to be known through the void (<s>gagana</s>); the <s>yoni</s>-mark [is placed] in the fifth [house]. (RA 3.4)
Having first uttered the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), then the supreme seed-syllable (<s>bīja</s>),
<s>hrīṃkāra</s> and <s>krīṃkāra</s>, followed by <s>Haṃsa</s>-awareness. (RA 3.5)
The great mantra of the noose of time (<s>Kālapāśa</s>) — the master-practitioner should receive [it].
For the great undertaking, that mantra — the <s>Pratīhāra</s> (door-keeper) — is [identified with] <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>. (RA 3.6)
One who recites it one hundred thousand times — great <s>siddhi</s> comes about.
Then, with the dung of a calf, one should make [the mercury] seize [its substrate]. (RA 3.7)
With the ash of a cremation fire, one should make [it] seize, O Supreme Goddess.
That is the supreme place, the [sacred] field (<s>kṣetra</s>); <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury-lord) abides there. (RA 3.8)
One should sweep the place with a broom; [the mantra here is] the <s>Khecarī</s> called <s>Kubjikā</s>,
having thirty-two syllables, O Goddess, established in the five <s>Nādas</s> (resonances). (RA 3.9)

children.text: tataḥ siddhāś ca catvāraḥ | puruṣāṣṭādaśa smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, the four <s>Siddhas</s>; and eighteen <s>Puruṣas</s> are mentioned.
Endowed with the five meanings (<s>arthapañcaka</s>); and again, the fivefold meditation. (RA 3.10)
Conjoined with the six <s>Yoginīs</s>, with the sequence of twenty-seven [stages],
endowed with eighty-one stations, with the five coverings (<s>pañcāvaraṇa</s>). (RA 3.11)
By this sequential method, one should worship the broom (<s>mārjanī</s>).

children.text:
anena mārjayet kṣetraṃ | rasendro yatra tiṣṭhati ||
                    (RA_3.12)
children.translated_text: With this [mantra] one should sweep the area where <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) is situated. (<s>RA</s> 3.12)

children.text: upalepaṃ tu tatraiva | caṇḍaghaṇṭāṃ tu kārayet |
children.translated_text: One should apply a coating there, and should make [an image of] <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s>.

children.text: pūrve gṛhe tu sā devī | caṇḍaghaṇṭā vyavasthitā || (RA_3.13)
children.translated_text: In the eastern chamber, that goddess <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s> is stationed. (<s>RA</s> 3.13)
<s>Caṇḍabhairavikā</s> goddess is stationed in the southern chamber.
With that [mantra], one should take cow-dung for the purpose of smearing, O beautiful-faced one. (<s>RA</s> 3.14)
<s>Caṇḍakāpālinī</s> goddess is stationed in the northern chamber.
Having taken water with that [mantra], one should smear the ground surface. (<s>RA</s> 3.15)
One should place the seventeen-syllabled <s>Kālī</s> [mantra] upon the grinding stone (<s>khallapāṣāṇa</s>).
The thirty-two-syllabled fierce [mantra] should be applied to the grinding implement (<s>mardaka</s>). (<s>RA</s> 3.16)
One should take the sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), O goddess, consecrated with the <s>Kālapāśa</s> mantra.
Thus, the family of <s>Khecarīs</s> performs the conjunction of auspicious work. (<s>RA</s> 3.17)
Eighty-eight thousand divine <s>Khecarīs</s> who are stationed [in the sky],

children.text:
tāḥ sarvāḥ kiṃkarāstasya | auṣadhaṃ peṣayanti tāḥ ||
                    (RA_3.18)
children.translated_text: all of them become his servants — they grind the medicines. (<s>RA</s> 3.18)
The mantra of all of them is one, consisting of four syllables:
'<s>So'haṃ Haṃsaḥ</s>'.

children.text: sā vidyā khecarīṇāṃ tu | nāmnāṃ tu kulakhecarī || (RA_3.19)
children.translated_text: That is the <s>vidyā</s> of the <s>Khecarīs</s>, known by name as <s>Kulakhecarī</s>. (<s>RA</s> 3.19)

children.text: rājikāṃ saindhavaṃ nyasya | sā vidyā kulakhecarī |
children.translated_text: Having placed mustard seed and rock salt, that <s>vidyā</s> [is called] <s>Kulakhecarī</s>.
One should consecrate the sour gruel there; the king of mantras is <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>. (<s>RA</s> 3.20)
One should recite the missile-knowledge (<s>astravidyā</s>) there, which was known in the earlier [work of] <s>Bhārgava</s>.

children.text:
guḍeṣṭakāṃ tu saṃmardya | priye tanmarditaṃ rasam ||
                    (RA_3.21)
children.translated_text: Having ground the jaggery brick, O beloved, [one obtains] the ground mercury. (<s>RA</s> 3.21)

children.text: kā kathā mantrarājasya | na vākyaṃ triśirasya ca |
children.translated_text: What need to speak of the king of mantras? Not even the words of <s>Triśiras</s> [can describe it].

children.text:
ṣaḍaṅgaṃ yojayet tāṃ tu | tvaritaṃ dhārayet tataḥ ||
                    (RA_3.22)
children.translated_text: One should apply the six-limbed [<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> mantra] to it and quickly perform the holding [ritual]. (<s>RA</s> 3.22)
The great mantra called <s>Ḍāmara</s> should be applied to the bellows (<s>dhamanī</s>).
The great <s>vidyā</s> of <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> should be applied to the protective armors (<s>kavaca</s>). (<s>RA</s> 3.23)

children.text: caṇḍikāyā mahāmantraṃ | taṃ tu pātre niyojayet |
children.translated_text: The great mantra of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> should be applied to the vessel (<s>pātra</s>).
The nine <s>vidyās</s>, O beautiful-hipped one, should be placed upon the husk-and-cowdung [fuel]. (<s>RA</s> 3.24)
The goddess <s>Tripurābhairavī</s> should be placed upon the mustard-seed and sour gruel.
<s>Kālarātri</s> should be placed upon the jaggery, O one praised by heroes. (<s>RA</s> 3.25)

children.text: trikūṭākṣaṃ trinetraṃ tu | analasya tu vinyaset |
children.translated_text: The three-peaked, three-eyed [mantra] should be placed upon the fire.
Upon the water, O goddess, one should place the eighty-four <s>Caṇḍikās</s>. (<s>RA</s> 3.26)
The <s>Kṣetrapāla Aghora</s> missile should be placed upon the container (<s>koṣṭhaka</s>), O beloved.
The great <s>Pāśupata</s> missile should be applied to the crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>). (<s>RA</s> 3.27)
This group of mantras, O goddess, should be applied to the mercury-working place.

children.text:
tadā tu sidhyate tasya | sādhakasya phalaṃ priye ||
                    (RA_3.28)
children.translated_text: Then the fruit is attained for that practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), O beloved. (<s>RA</s> 3.28)
The great mantra <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> should be recited within the heart.

children.text: anye ye yoginīmantrāḥ | sarvānnārīś ca jāpayet || (RA_3.29)
children.translated_text: The other <s>yoginī</s> mantras and all the female [mantras] should also be recited. (<s>RA</s> 3.29)
Secretly, with that very [method], [one should recite] the king of mantras, <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s>.
And the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) should be secretly protected from women,
as [revealing it would cause] the great violation of the covenant — [guarded] like the hearts of women. (<s>RA</s> 3.30)

children.text: kubjikādyāstu ye mantrā | mayā te saṃprakāśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The mantras beginning with <s>Kubjikā</s> and the others that have been revealed by me —

children.text:
trailokyaṃ kṣobhitāste tu | na manyante mama priye ||
                    (RA_3.31)
children.translated_text: they agitate the three worlds, yet they do not heed me, O beloved. (<s>RA</s> 3.31)
By the knowledge of <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s>, the three worlds come under control. (<s>RA</s> 3.32)
Having known the placement of mantras, the apparatus (<s>yantra</s>), the crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), the fire, and the measurements,
the practitioner, performing the alchemical operations (<s>rasakarma</s>), attains perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). (<s>RA</s> 3.33)
Fourth Chapter [Description of Apparatus, Crucibles, and Fires]
The glorious Goddess said:
Without knowing the apparatus, crucibles, fires, and measurements — even one who knows the mantras,

children.text: kiṃ karoti mahādeva | tāni me vaktumarhasi || (RA_4.1)
children.translated_text: what can he accomplish, O great God? Please tell me those [details]. (<s>RA</s> 4.1)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Mercury, subsidiary metals (<s>uparasa</s>), metals (<s>loha</s>), cloth, sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), alkali reagent (<s>viḍa</s>),
bellows (<s>dhamanī</s>), metal apparatus (<s>lohayantra</s>), grinding stone (<s>khallapāṣāṇa</s>), and pestle (<s>mardaka</s>), (<s>RA</s> 4.2)
furnace (<s>koṣṭhikā</s>), curved tube (<s>vakranāla</s>), cow-dung, fuel-wood (<s>sāra</s>), and kindling (<s>indhana</s>),
earthen apparatus, pestles (<s>musala</s>), and mortars (<s>ulūkhala</s>), (<s>RA</s> 4.3)
tongs (<s>saṇḍasī</s>), flat plate (<s>paṭṭa</s>), pincers (<s>saṃdaṃśa</s>), earthen pots, and iron bowls (<s>kaṭoraka</s>),
standard measures, balances, cutting instruments, and touchstones (<s>kaṣopala</s>), (<s>RA</s> 4.4)
bamboo tubes, metal tubes, alkali powder (<s>ūṣā</s>), charcoal, and also herbs,
oils, acids, salts, alkalis, poisons, and subsidiary poisons. (<s>RA</s> 4.5)
Having thus gathered all the materials, one should commence the operational procedure. (<s>RA</s> 4.6)
With liquid substance, [filling] half the belly of a vessel,

children.text: mukhe tiryakkṛte bhāṇḍe | rasaṃ sūtreṇa lambitam |
children.translated_text: with the vessel's mouth turned sideways, the mercury suspended by a thread,
one should steam it placed at the bottom — this is known as the swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.7)
Having made a pair of metal crucibles, twelve finger-breadths in measurement,
one [crucible] with a slight hole, containing sulfur therein, (<s>RA</s> 4.8)
the mercury-filled crucible should be inserted into the other one.
Water should be below the mercury; fire should be ignited above and below. (<s>RA</s> 4.9)
The juice of garlic (<s>rasonaka</s>), O auspicious one, carefully filtered through cloth,
should be applied abundantly and carefully, immersing the mercury and sulfur. (<s>RA</s> 4.10)

children.text: sthālikāyāṃ nidhāyordhvaṃ | sthālīm anyāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Having placed [it] in a pan (<s>sthālikā</s>), place another firm pan above.

children.text:
saṃdhiṃ vilepayed yatnāt | mṛdā vastreṇa caiva hi ||
                    (RA_4.11)
children.translated_text: One should carefully seal the joint with clay and cloth. (<s>RA</s> 4.11)
Within the [enclosed] pan, [one applies] the pigeon-grade (<s>kapota</s>) heating with fire of one <s>karṣa</s> [weight of fuel] constantly.
Below the apparatus, one should give cow-dung fire or even intense fire. (<s>RA</s> 4.12)

children.text: evaṃ tu tridinaṃ kuryāt | tato yantraṃ vimocayet |
children.translated_text: One should do this for three days, then release the apparatus.

children.text:
taptodake taptacullyāṃ | na kuryāc chītale kriyām ||
                    (RA_4.13)
children.translated_text: In hot water and a heated furnace — one should not perform the operation in cold conditions. (<s>RA</s> 4.13)

children.text: na tatra kṣīyate sūto | na ca gacchati kutracit |
children.translated_text: There, the mercury is not diminished, nor does it go anywhere.
By this sequential method, one should perform the sulfur-assimilation (<s>gandhakajāraṇa</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.14)
Fire above, water below, and collection of mercury in the middle —
this is the crucible-apparatus (<s>mūṣāyantra</s>), O goddess; with it one should assimilate mica (<s>gagana</s>) and the like. (<s>RA</s> 4.15)
I shall describe the womb-apparatus (<s>garbhayantra</s>), [used] for making cakes (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) and calcination (<s>bhasman</s>).
A crucible of clay, firm, four finger-breadths long, (<s>RA</s> 4.16)
three finger-breadths in the middle width, with a round mouth —

children.text: lohasya viṃśatirbhāgā | eko bhāgas tu gugguloḥ || (RA_4.17)
children.translated_text: twenty parts of metal and one part of <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium). (<s>RA</s> 4.17)

children.text: suślakṣṇaṃ peṣayitvā tu | toyaṃ dadyāt punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having ground [it] very finely, one should add water again and again.

children.text:
mūṣālepaṃ tataḥ kuryāt | tale piṣṭīṃ ca nikṣipet ||
                    (RA_4.18)
children.translated_text: Then one should coat the crucible and place the cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>) at the bottom. (<s>RA</s> 4.18)
On the ground, with a fire of husk [measuring] one <s>karṣa</s>, one should apply gentle steaming.

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā | rasendro bhasmatāṃ vrajet ||
                    (RA_4.19)
children.translated_text: In one day and night, or three nights, the mercury lord (<s>Rasendra</s>) becomes calcined (<s>bhasma</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.19)
For assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>), for calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>), and for the coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) of the king of mercury,
the apparatus is the one supreme secret — where herbs [provide] great power. (<s>RA</s> 4.20)
Without herbs, this [mercury] is bound forcibly by the apparatus alone.
Mercury goes everywhere, except when it has the character of earth [i.e., is fixed]. (<s>RA</s> 4.21)
Attracted by the deities [i.e., mantric powers], even when placed on a clod of earth, it moves.
Therefore, the power of the apparatus alone should not be transgressed by one who knows. (<s>RA</s> 4.22)
Through the combination of mantras and herbs, this [mercury] becomes perfectly accomplished.
The <s>Aghora</s> mantra should be recited here; at the end of recitation, one should worship the mercury. (<s>RA</s> 4.23)

children.text:
ekānte tu kriyā kāryā | dṛṣṭān yair viphalā bhavet ||
                    (RA_4.24)
children.translated_text: The operation should be performed in solitude; it becomes fruitless [if] seen by those [who should not see it]. (<s>RA</s> 4.24)

children.text: gandhakasya kṣayo nāsti | na rasasya kṣayo bhavet |
children.translated_text: There is no loss of sulfur, nor does mercury diminish.

children.text: kṣayo yantrasya vijñeyaḥ | yantre vikriyate kriyā |
children.translated_text: The loss should be understood as [pertaining to] the apparatus; in the apparatus, the operation is modified.
In the absence of loadstone (<s>kānta</s>) metal, the apparatus should be made of [ordinary] metal. (<s>RA</s> 4.25)
Without knowing the fire-mark, half the mercury may be lost.
For one who knows the method of apparatus-loss, [only] a quarter is lost. (<s>RA</s> 4.26)
In two months, one-half [is processed]; the third portion in three [months].

children.text: mahāgniṃ sahate hy eṣa | sārito yatra tiṣṭhati || (RA_4.27)
children.translated_text: This [mercury] endures great fire wherever it is placed in fixed form. (<s>RA</s> 4.27)
Having filled a potsherd (<s>kharpara</s>) with sand, one should place [the mercury] upon it.

children.text:
aparaṃ kharparaṃ tatra | śanair mṛdvagninā pacet ||
                    (RA_4.28)
children.translated_text: Another potsherd [is placed] on top of that, and [it is] cooked gently with mild fire. (<s>RA</s> 4.28)

children.text: pañcakṣāraistathā mūtrair | lavaṇaiś ca viḍaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: With five alkalis, with urines, and with salts — that is the alkali reagent (<s>viḍa</s>).
This is known as the goose-cooking (<s>haṃsapāka</s>) by those skilled in the science of apparatus. (<s>RA</s> 4.29)

children.text: kṛṣṇā raktā ca pītā ca | śuklavarṇā ca mṛttikā |
children.translated_text: Black, red, yellow, and white — [these are the types of] clay.

children.text:
ādyā śreṣṭhā kaniṣṭhāntyā | madhyamā madhyamā matā ||
                    (RA_4.30)
children.translated_text: The first is the best, the last is the lowest, and the middle ones are middling. (<s>RA</s> 4.30)
Clay mixed with burnt grain-husks — for the making of furnaces (<s>koṣṭhikā</s>),
or made with a curved tube — this is praised, O beautiful goddess. (<s>RA</s> 4.31)

children.text: gārā dagdhā tuṣā dagdhā | dagdhā valmīkamṛttikā |
children.translated_text: Burnt gypite (<s>gārā</s>), burnt husks, burnt anthill clay,

children.text:
ajāśvānāṃ malaṃ dagdhaṃ | yāvattat kṛṣṇatāṃ gatam ||
                    (RA_4.32)
children.translated_text: burnt dung of goats and horses — until it has become black. (<s>RA</s> 4.32)

children.text: vāsakasya ca pattrāṇi | valmīkasya mṛdā saha |
children.translated_text: The leaves of <s>Vāsaka</s> [<s>Adhatoda vasica</s>], together with anthill clay,
should be ground with fire-water [hot water] until it has become fine. (<s>RA</s> 4.33)

children.text:
mardayet tena badhnīyāt | vakranālaṃ ca koṣṭhikām ||
                    (RA_4.34)
children.translated_text: One should grind [it further] and with that bind the curved tube and the furnace. (<s>RA</s> 4.34)

children.text: gārā dagdhā tuṣā dagdhā | dagdhā valmīkamṛttikā |
children.translated_text: Burnt gypite, burnt husks, burnt anthill clay,
bark-charcoal and slag — [a crucible made of these] cannot be broken even by a thunderbolt. (<s>RA</s> 4.35)
Six parts of burnt charcoal and one part of black clay,
bark-charcoal and slag — this is declared to be the diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.36)
Husks and cloth burnt equally, and four parts of clay,
combined with <s>kupī</s>-stone — this is declared to be the excellent crucible (<s>varamūṣā</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.37)

children.text: prakāśā cāndhamūṣā ca | mūṣā tu dvividhā smṛtā || (RA_4.38)
children.translated_text: The crucible is of two kinds: open (<s>prakāśā</s>) and closed (<s>andhā</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.38)
The open crucible, O queen of gods, is shaped like a saucer (<s>śarāva</s>).
It is highly praised by alchemists (<s>vādika</s>) for the extraction of substances. (<s>RA</s> 4.39)
The closed crucible should be made in the shape of a cow's udder (<s>gostana</s>),
equipped with a lid, with a slightly raised top. (<s>RA</s> 4.40)
For leaf-coating (<s>pattralepa</s>), for coloring (<s>raṅga</s>), and for combining pairs (<s>dvaṃdvamelāpaka</s>),
the same [crucible], when provided with holes, shallow and deep, is suitable for the sāraṇa process. (<s>RA</s> 4.41)
Two parts of sesame-ash, combined with one part of brick [powder],
this is known as the ash-crucible (<s>bhasmamūṣā</s>) — useful for the purification of silver (<s>tārā</s>). (<s>RA</s> 4.42)
Two parts of <s>mokṣa</s>-alkali, combined with one part of brick [powder],
and parts of clay — for the purpose of purifying silver, this is the best, O beautiful lady. (<s>RA</s> 4.43)
Mixed with the red group [of reagents], saturated with the red group,
coated with the red group — [this crucible is] excellent for all purifications. (<s>RA</s> 4.44)
Mixed with the white group, saturated with the white group,
coated with the white group — [this crucible is] excellent for white [metal] purifications. (<s>RA</s> 4.45)
Mixed with the alkali-reagent (<s>viḍa</s>) group, [the crucible] requires firmness for assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>).
The extraction should be performed with [a crucible] coated with the red group. (<s>RA</s> 4.46)
With poison (<s>viṣa</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and <s>guñjā</s> [<s>Abrus precatorius</s>] seeds, one should make the crucible coating.
In the open [crucible], one should apply the charcoal coating. (<s>RA</s> 4.47)
Having placed [the substance] in that crucible, the wise one should rotate the material.
The coating [for] color-heating (<s>varṇapuṭa</s>), O goddess, [is made] of red earth, <s>sindhūra</s>, earth, and <s>bhūkhaga</s> [mica?]. (<s>RA</s> 4.48)

children.text: āvartamāne kanake | pītā tāre sitā prabhā |
children.translated_text: When gold is being rotated [in the crucible], a yellow glow [appears]; in silver, a white glow;
in copper, a blue-like [glow]; in lead (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), a black color, O queen of gods. (<s>RA</s> 4.49)

children.text: śaile tu dhūsarā devi | āyase kapilaprabhā || (RA_4.50)
na visphuliṅgo na ca budbudaś ca | yadā na rekhāpaṭalaṃ na śabdaḥ |

mūṣāgataṃ ratnasamaṃ sthiraṃ ca | tadā viśuddhaṃ pravadanti
                    loham || (RA_4.52)
chādanaṃ tu pratīvāpaḥ | niṣekaṃ majjanaṃ viduḥ |
abhiṣekaṃ tadicchanti | snapanaṃ kriyate tu yat || (RA_4.53)
vāpo niṣekaḥ snapanaṃ | drute nirmalatāṃ gate |
uṣṇenaiva hi vāñchanti | śītalaṃ na ca vāñchati || (RA_4.54)
śukladīptiḥ saśabdaś ca | yadā vaiśvānaro bhavet |

lohāvartaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ | sattvaṃ patati nirmalam ||
                    (RA_4.55)

bakagalasamamānaṃ vaṅkanālaṃ vidheyaṃ | śuṣiranalinikā syānmṛnmayī dīrghavṛttā ||
                    Ras_4.58 ||
sa ca lohamayaḥ śailo | hy ayaskāntamayo 'thavā || (RA_4.60)

mantreṇa racayec chuddhiṃ | bhūmiṃ tenaiva śodhayet ||
                    (RA_4.61)
indhanāni ca sarvāṇi | dravyāṇi ca viśeṣataḥ |

dāhakaṃ jvālayet tena | khallaṃ tenaiva śodhayet ||
                    (RA_4.62)
rasaṃ viśodhayet tena | vinyaset divase śubhe |

tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_4.65)
yayā sampadyate hy eṣām | oṣadhīṃ vaktumarhasi || (RA_5.1)
tittiḍī kṣīriṇī rāsnā | meṣaśṛṅgī ca kukkuṭī || (RA_5.6)
kṛṣṇaparṇī ca tulasī | śvetā ca girikarṇikā |
śṛgālajihvā bṛhatī | vajrā cakrī ca rājikā || (RA_5.9)
kāñcanī vanarājī ca | kākamācī ca keśinī |
gojihvā kākajaṅghā ca | mahākālī ca śambarī |
sūryāvartaś ca kadalī | vandhyā kośātakī tathā |
doṣān haranti yogina | dhātūnāṃ pāradasya ca || (RA_5.23)
tāmbūlī nāginī brahmī | haṃsapādī ca lakṣaṇā |
bhūpāṭalī ca kaumārī | siṃhavallī ca śūkarī |
hemaparṇī paṭolī ca | nāgavallī ca bhṛṅgarāṭ |

ityaṣṭa mūlikāḥ proktāḥ | pañcaratnaṃ śṛṇu priye ||
                    (RA_5.27)
indirā ca kṣamāpālī | pañcamī tu niśācarī |

sauvarcalaṃ ca kācaṃ ca | lavaṇāḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ ||
                    (RA_5.32)
saktukaṃ kālakūṭaṃ ca | sitamustā tathaiva ca |
śṛṅgī kṛṣṇaviṣaṃ caiva | pañcaite tu mahāviṣāḥ || (RA_5.33)
pañcaivopaviṣā mukhyāḥ | tailāni hy uttamāni vai |
sarve malaharāḥ kṣārāḥ | sarve cāmlāḥ prabodhakāḥ |

kriyāṃ kurvanti tadyogāt | śaktayaś ca mahārasāḥ ||
                    (RA_5.44)

tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_5.45)

pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā śuklaṃ | raktaṃ bhūmeś ca saṃgamāt ||
                    (RA_6.2)
pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ | vajraṃ cābhraṃ caturvidham |

pināke 'gniṃ praviṣṭe tu | śabdaś ciṭiciṭir bhavet ||
                    (RA_6.4)
agniṃ praviṣṭaṃ nāgaṃ tu | phūtkāraṃ devi muñcati || (RA_6.5)

agniṃ praviṣṭaṃ vajraṃ tu | vajravattiṣṭhati priye ||
                    (RA_6.6)

nāgaṃ dehagataṃ nityaṃ | vyādhiṃ kuryād bhagaṃdaram ||
                    (RA_6.7)
rase rasāyane caiva | yojyaṃ vajrābhrakaṃ priye |
raktaṃ pītaṃ ca hemārthe | kṛṣṇaṃ hemaśarīrayoḥ |
children.translated_text: The red and yellow [<s>abhraka</s>] are for the purpose of gold-making; the black is for [transmuting] gold and the body;

children.text: tārakarmaṇi śuklaṃ ca | kācakiṭṭaṃ sadā tyajet || (RA_6.9)
children.translated_text: The white is for silver-making; <s>kācakiṭṭa</s> (glassy residue) should always be discarded. (RA 6.9)
The <s>abhraka</s> (mica) previously made into a single sheet, O queen of the gods,
[should be processed] with the juice of <s>agastya</s> flowers and with the juice of night-lotuses (<s>kumuda</s>). (RA 6.10)
With <s>kapitinduka</s>, lemon (<s>jambīra</s>), <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>punarnava</s>;
with barley (<s>yava</s>), tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>), sour gruel (<s>ranālāmla</s>), oleander (<s>karavīra</s>), and red lotus (<s>aruṇotpala</s>); (RA 6.11)
with wild yam (<s>vanasūraṇa</s>), <s>bhūdhātrī</s>, <s>bhiṇḍī</s> root, and sour date (<s>āmlavetasa</s>);
with <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, hare fat (<s>śaśavasā</s>), horn-oil (<s>śṛṅgataila</s>), and <s>śamī</s> juice; (RA 6.12)
with <s>vajravallī</s>, milk-tuber (<s>kṣīrakanda</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>), and <s>sumukha</s> —
one should steam [the mica] for three days, O Goddess — it becomes free of defects. (RA 6.13)
Having first made grain-[processed] <s>abhraka</s>, very smooth like fresh butter,
[take] thirty <s>palas</s> of mica powder and two <s>palas</s> of small fish. (RA 6.14)
One <s>pala</s> of sesame (<s>tila</s>) powder, three <s>palas</s> of <s>guñjā</s> [<s>Abrus precatorius</s>], and a quarter [<s>pala</s>] of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>);
a lump bound with wheat (<s>godhūma</s>), saturated with the five cow-products (<s>pañcagavya</s>). (RA 6.15)
By blowing [bellows] in a <s>koṣṭhikā</s> furnace with the two bellows and intense fire,
the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of <s>abhraka</s> falls down, as do all [other] essences. (RA 6.16)
Rolled with the exudates of steaming herbs and heated (<s>puṭita</s>) repeatedly,
[the mica is] killed (<s>mṛta</s>) by five <s>nicula</s>-hearth firings with abundant cow-dung cakes. (RA 6.17)

children.text: piṇḍitaṃ vyoma niṣkledaṃ | dattvā sattvaṃ nirañjanam |
children.translated_text: The mica, formed into a lump, free of moisture, having yielded its pure essence,
[is processed] with <s>umā</s> fruits and flowers, soaked in <s>ṣaṣṭikā</s> rice-sour [water];
by grinding with a pestle of <s>umā</s>-[plant] wood, it clearly melts and flows. (RA 6.18)
Having placed <s>agnijāra</s> [fire-calcined substance] in a new pot, sealed with clay,
the mica melts quickly, [becoming] lustrous like pearls. (RA 6.19)
[Take] a hundredfold the powder of <s>kañcukī</s> [skin-shedding plant], saturated with <s>kañcukī</s> juice;

children.text: drāvayed gaganaṃ devi | lohāni sakalāni ca || (RA_6.20)
children.translated_text: [with this] one can melt mica, O Goddess, and all metals as well. (RA 6.20)
Soaked in stale sour gruel (<s>dhānyāmlaka</s>), [then] placed in water of <s>nicula</s> alkali —
it attains fluidity, [becoming] like pure liquid mercury. (RA 6.21)
Having ground [the mica] with <s>agastya</s> flower-water in a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber [vessel],
[and kept it] buried in the ground of the furnace for a month — it becomes like liquid mercury. (RA 6.22)
Sprinkled with goat's urine, [mixed] with <s>kapitinduka</s> powder,
the <s>abhraka</s>, thus sublimated (<s>vāpita</s>), O Goddess, becomes like water. (RA 6.23)
[Take] the powder of <s>abhraka</s> essence, ground with <s>kākinī</s> seed powder;

children.text:
snuhikṣīreṇa saptāhaṃ | siktaṃ dhmātaṃ drutaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_6.24)
children.translated_text: sprinkled with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (spurge) for seven days and blown [in the furnace], it becomes fluid. (RA 6.24)
[Take] all five parts of the <s>apāmārga</s> plant and <s>abhraka</s>, well ground;

children.text:
sthāpayen mṛnmaye pātre | tadbhavet salilaṃ yathā ||
                    (RA_6.25)
children.translated_text: place [them] in an earthen vessel — it becomes like water. (RA 6.25)
The ground <s>abhraka</s> powder, [processed] with <s>kapālī</s> [<s>Kāravellaka</s>] and pepper (<s>marica</s>),
sublimated on a stone slab, again combined with <s>agastya</s> juice, (RA 6.26)
ground with the juice of roots and fruits of <s>mārjārapādī</s>,
placed in a citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) fruit, stored in a bed of rice —
it melts in a mere fortnight, combined with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and stone. (RA 6.27)
The [mica] made into a single sheet, thrown into <s>muni</s> [<s>agastya</s>] juice for seven days,
mixed with <s>dārvī</s> [turmeric] and pepper, soaked in <s>maurvī</s> [bowstring-hemp] juice; (RA 6.28)
the mica combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, soaked in <s>vajravallī</s> juice,
blown [in the furnace] in a covered dish (<s>śarāva-saṃpuṭa</s>) — it becomes like water. (RA 6.29)
The <s>abhraka</s> powder mixed equally with the powder of <s>vegā</s>-fruit,
saturated in <s>vajra</s> (euphoria) milk, blown in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) — it melts instantly. (RA 6.30)
