Having ground the mica with <s>vajravallī</s> juices, combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> salt,
[and] cooked in a covered dish — it melts, becoming like water. (RA 6.31)
With cow-flesh, rock salt, <s>arka</s> [<s>Calotropis</s>], and combined again with <s>muni</s>-water,
placed inside a plantain (<s>kadalī</s>) stem, [heated] with cow-dung fire for three days — it melts. (RA 6.32)
Taking a black mica sheet, smear it with <s>pīlu</s> oil;
heat it in the sun for seven days, then throw it into sour [liquid] for three days. (RA 6.33)
[Take] the alkalis of <s>vajra</s> [<s>Euphorbia</s>], <s>arka</s>, and <s>citraka</s>; the alkali of bottle-gourd (<s>tumbī</s>); and likewise <s>arjuna</s>;
the alkali of <s>sarja</s> [<s>Vateria indica</s>], the alkali of barley (<s>yava</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) as the eighth. (RA 6.34)
And the juice of the milk-bulb (<s>kṣīrakanda</s>), and likewise the juice of the <s>vajra</s>-bulb,
combined with the three <s>vṛhatī</s> [nightshade plants] — smear [the mica] with this alkali group. (RA 6.35)
That sheet-mica, coated with this paste,
[placed] in a bronze vessel — by the heat of the sun, it becomes fluid in three days. (RA 6.36)
Alternatively, a mica sheet [placed] inside <s>kañcukī</s> milk,

children.text:
bhāvayec ca tathā tena | yāvaccūrṇaṃ tato bhavet ||
                    (RA_6.37)
children.translated_text: should be soaked with that [liquid] until it becomes a powder. (RA 6.37)
One should take the mica sheets, immerse [them] in sour [liquid] for three days,
coat [them] with that paste, place [them] in a bronze vessel;
by the heat of the sun for seven days, fluidity is produced instantly. (RA 6.38)
With the powder of <s>kākāṇḍī</s> fruit, and with the five melting agents (<s>drāvakas</s>),

children.text:
abhrakasya yutaṃ cūrṇaṃ | dhmātaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dravat ||
                    (RA_6.39)
children.translated_text: the <s>abhraka</s> powder, combined [with them] and blown in a crucible, melts. (RA 6.39)

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ cumbakaṃ caiva | karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: The revolving [type] (<s>bhrāmaka</s>), the attracting [type] (<s>cumbaka</s>), the pulling [type] (<s>karṣaka</s>), and the melting [type] (<s>drāvaka</s>) —
thus lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) is of four kinds, with <s>romakānta</s> as the fifth. (RA 6.40)
One-faced, two-faced, three-faced, four-faced, five-faced, and all-faced —

children.text:
pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā raktaṃ | trivarṇaṃ syāt pṛthak pṛthak ||
                    (RA_6.41)
children.translated_text: yellow, black, and red — [lodestone] is of three colors, each separately. (RA 6.41)
The presiding deities there are, in order, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>. (RA 6.42)

children.text: sparśavedhi bhavet pītaṃ | kṛṣṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rasāyane |
children.translated_text: The yellow is touch-transmuting (<s>sparśavedhi</s>); the black is best for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation);
the red-colored one, O great lady, is praised for mercury-binding (<s>rasabandha</s>). (RA 6.43)

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ tu kaniṣṭhaṃ syāt | cumbakaṃ madhyamaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: The <s>bhrāmaka</s> (revolving) is the lowest; the <s>cumbaka</s> (attracting) is middling, O beloved;
the <s>karṣaka</s> (pulling) is superior, O Goddess; and the <s>drāvaka</s> (melting) is the most excellent. (RA 6.44)
That which causes a metal to revolve — that lodestone is the <s>bhrāmaka</s>, O beloved;

children.text:
cumbayec cumbakaṃ kāntaṃ | karṣayet karṣakaṃ priye ||
                    (RA_6.45)
children.translated_text: that which causes [metal] to adhere is the <s>cumbaka</s>; that which draws [metal] is the <s>karṣaka</s>, O beloved. (RA 6.45)
That which directly melts metal — that lodestone is the <s>drāvaka</s>;
the <s>romakānta</s> is [so called because] from the split [stone], hair-like [filaments] emerge. (RA 6.46)
One-faced is the lowest; two- and three-faced are middling;
four- and five-faced are superior; all-faced (<s>sarvatomukha</s>) is the best. (RA 6.47)
The <s>bhrāmaka</s> and <s>cumbaka</s> are praised for the destruction of diseases;

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva | karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ hitam || (RA_6.48)
children.translated_text: for mercury [operations] and rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>), the <s>karṣaka</s> and <s>drāvaka</s> are beneficial. (RA 6.48)
Mercury (<s>sūta</s>) is [like] a maddened elephant in rut; lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) is said to be the goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>);
[lodestone] should be obtained by digging the earth, with great effort. (RA 6.49)
That [lodestone] which has been exposed to wind and heat should be discarded, O beauty of the gods;
the lodestone found on the surface should be soaked in goat's blood. (RA 6.50)
It should be wrapped in cloth smeared with goat's blood,
covered with goat skin, and placed in the earth as before. (RA 6.51)
After extracting it [from the earth] after seven months, throw it into a pot of water. (RA 6.52)
It should always be worshipped with red flowers, red garlands, and red unguents;
worshipped with liquor and meat, it should be employed in mercury and rejuvenation [operations]. (RA 6.53)
The <s>bhrāmaka</s>, consecrated with goat's blood, becomes a <s>cumbaka</s>;
by this sequential procedure, it becomes a <s>drāvaka</s>, O beloved. (RA 6.54)
I shall describe the processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of mercury-metal (<s>sūtaloha</s>), which gives great comfort,
and which, upon entering the living body, bestows bodily comfort and strength. (RA 6.55)

children.text: kāntalohaṃ vinā sūto | dehe na krāmati kvacit |
children.translated_text: Without lodestone-metal, mercury never penetrates the body;
[but with it,] it transmutes and pervades quickly — like a drop of oil on water. (RA 6.56)

children.text: na sūtena vinā kānto | na kāntaḥ sūtavarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without mercury, lodestone is [useless]; without lodestone, mercury is [useless];
the combination of lodestone and mercury is the preparation that sustains the body. (RA 6.57)
Taking barley alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>), store it in a greased vessel;
with mica and pepper powder, form it into a lump;
the lodestone-metal, when blown [in the furnace], melts — no deliberation is needed here. (RA 6.58)
Thirty [<s>palas</s> of] <s>cumbaka</s>-lodestone, ground with <s>triphalā</s> water —

children.text:
tenaiva kṣālanaṃ kāryyaṃ | pañcaniṣkaṃ tu ṭaṅkaṇam ||
                    (RA_6.59)
children.translated_text: washing should be done with that same [liquid]; [add] five <s>niṣkas</s> of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). (RA 6.59)
Wrapping in worn cloth, fire [the preparation] with honey and ghee;
storing it for the duration of a month — there purification is achieved, O beloved. (RA 6.60)
The root of <s>sināḍikā</s>, measured at ten <s>niṣkas</s>, combined [with the lodestone],
[and processed in] a decoction of the three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>) — grind in a mortar. (RA 6.61)
It should be placed equally in three crucibles (<s>mūṣās</s>), each eight <s>aṅgulas</s> [in height];
the inner coating of the crucible should be done with one <s>niṣka</s>'s measure of that root. (RA 6.62)
The <s>Śiva</s> five-faced [arrangement] should be made for each crucible;
[then,] binding securely in the apparatus-arm (<s>yantrahasta</s>), [place] the alloy (<s>khoṭaka</s>) on a stone surface. (RA 6.63)
Having mixed with oil, one obtains <s>kānta-nāga</s> (lodestone-lead);
by the same sequential procedure as for mica, one should achieve the melting and pouring. (RA 6.64)
When the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods and demons with Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) was drunk by the gods, [and they] attained immortality. (RA 6.65)
O Goddess, drops [of nectar that] fell upon the surface of the earth as they drank,
dried up and became diamonds (<s>vajra</s>) — of various colors and great power. (RA 6.66)
Some drops became [diamonds that are] seeded (<s>sasyaka</s>) and pure;
[classified as] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s> — thus in many ways. (RA 6.67)
White, red, yellow, and black — [they are] of four kinds;
[they are] male, female, and neuter, in order. (RA 6.68)
Round, with full facets, lustrous, and very large —
those should be known as male [diamonds] — free from lines and spots. (RA 6.69)
Those with lines and spots, and those that are broken, are female [diamonds];
triangular, flat, and elongated ones should be known as neuter [diamonds]. (RA 6.70)
Those possessing essence (<s>sattva</s>), endowed with strength, capable of penetrating metals,
and quickly effecting the binding of mercury — [these are] male diamonds, O one praised by the gods. (RA 6.71)
Those producing bodily luster are female diamonds — of slight power;

children.text:
napuṃsakāḥ sattvahīnāḥ | kaṣṭaṃ lohe kramanti ca ||
                    (RA_6.72)
children.translated_text: the neuter [diamonds] are devoid of essence and penetrate metal with difficulty. (RA 6.72)
The <s>Kṣatriya</s> [diamonds] should be avoided in all operations and in mercury work;
the [remaining three] are proclaimed as superior, middling, and inferior. (RA 6.73)
Coarse, very coarse, medium, fine, and very fine, O beloved —
[those] that withstand striking, burning, and splitting, that are unblemished and free of defects,

children.text:
vīryyavantaś ca te jyeṣṭhā | nirmalā balavattarāḥ ||
                    (RA_6.74)
children.translated_text: that are potent, pure, and very strong — those are the best. (RA 6.74)
The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [diamond] in rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) bestows the <s>aṇimā</s> and other powers;
the <s>Kṣatriya</s> [diamond serves] for the destruction of death, and removes wrinkles, grey hair, and disease. (RA 6.75)

children.text: dravyakāro tathā vaiśyaḥ | śarīraṃ dṛḍhatāṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśya</s> [diamond] is for making wealth, and brings firmness to the body;
the <s>Śūdra</s> [diamond] appeases diseases and effects the arrest of aging. (RA 6.76)

children.text:
klībe klīvāḥ striyaḥ strīṇāṃ | sarbbeṣāṃ puruṣā hitāḥ ||
                    (RA_6.77)
children.translated_text: For impotent [diamonds], impotent [substances are used]; for female [diamonds], female [substances]; for all [types], male [substances] are beneficial. (RA 6.77)

children.text: yathā jātistathotsāhaṃ | yathā sattvaṃ tathā guṇān |
children.translated_text: According to the caste [of the diamond], so is the vigor; according to the essence (<s>sattva</s>), so are the qualities;

children.text: yathā rucistathā śīlaṃ | yathā śīlaṃ tathā varam |
children.translated_text: according to the taste, so is the disposition; according to the disposition, so is the excellence;

children.text:
yathā varastathā varṇaṃ | kurvanti kuliśāḥ priye ||
                    (RA_6.78)
children.translated_text: according to the excellence, so is the color — thus do the diamonds [respond], O Beloved. (RA 6.78)
<s>Śyāmā</s> (dark plant), <s>śamī</s> (acacia), <s>ghanarava</s> (a plant), <s>vaṣā</s>, wild millet (<s>kodrava</s>),
<s>ākhukarṇī</s> (mouse-ear plant), <s>munitaru</s> (ascetic's tree), horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>), and sour tamarind (<s>amlavetasa</s>) — (RA 6.79)
<s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> (goat's horn plant), the juice of these, and the bulb of the <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant-foot yam) —
one should purify the diamond for three days — it attains purity, O Goddess of the Gods. (RA 6.80)
<s>Meṣaśṛṅga</s> (goat's horn), serpent bone, tortoise shell, <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch),
the sap of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) plant, breast milk, and lodite (<s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s>) — (RA 6.81)

children.text: vajrakaṃ cāpi vaikrāntaṃ | tanmadhye prakṣipet priye |
children.translated_text: and also the diamond [fragment] and <s>vaikrānta</s> — one should put [these] within that [crucible], O Beloved.

children.text: tīvrānale puṭaṃ dattvā | puṭāntaṃ yāvad āgatam || (RA_6.82)
children.translated_text: Having given a heating-cycle (<s>puṭa</s>) in intense fire, until the cycle is complete — (RA 6.82)
one should grind horse gram and wild millet with horse urine,
and quench the heated [diamond] on [the grinding] slab until it turns to ash. (RA 6.83)
This is the <s>Kāpālika</s> method — the supreme process for killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) diamond. (RA 6.84)
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>meṣaśṛṅga</s>, <s>śilā</s> (realgar), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
<s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) — soaked in the milk of <s>vajrī</s> (euphorbia) — (RA 6.85)

children.text: lepaṃ mūṣodare dattvā | samāvarttaṃ tu kārayet |
children.translated_text: having applied the paste inside the crucible and sealed it completely,
the diamonds are killed therein, and in the pair [of metals], they merge properly. (RA 6.86)

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca śilādhātuṃ | bhrāmakasya mukhaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>śilā</s> mineral, the face [powder] of <s>bhrāmaka</s>,

children.text: śaśakasya ca dantāṃś ca | vetasāmlena peṣayat || (RA_6.87)
children.translated_text: and the teeth of a hare — one should grind [these] with sour tamarind juice. (RA 6.87)
With this prepared paste, one should coat the inside of the crucible.

children.text:
andhamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ | vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_6.88)
children.translated_text: Smelted in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>), the diamond is killed instantly. (RA 6.88)

children.text: tenaiva militaṃ vajraṃ | tārahemni na saṃśayaḥ || (RA_6.89)
children.translated_text: The diamond thus fused merges into silver and gold — there is no doubt. (RA 6.89)
<s>Tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), camphor, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
tamarind seed, <s>meṣaśṛṅga</s> — ground with menstrual blood,

children.text:
mūṣālepagataṃ dhmātaṃ | vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_6.90)
children.translated_text: applied as a crucible-coating and smelted — the diamond is killed instantly. (RA 6.90)
The five parts of the <s>śarapuṅkha</s> (arrow-plume) plant should be ground with menstrual blood; or else
the seed of <s>peṭārī</s> (box-thorn) should be ground with rice-water. (RA 6.91)
Or one should grind three <s>karṣas</s> of cotton-root with rice-water;
or the root of <s>ārakta-rākā</s>, ground with breast milk. (RA 6.92)
Or one should grind <s>vajrakanda</s> (diamond-bulb) with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> (euphorbia), O virtuous one.

children.text:
tatkalkapuṭitaṃ dhmātaṃ | vajraṃ caiva mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_6.93)
children.translated_text: Sealed with that paste and smelted — the diamond becomes killed. (RA 6.93)
Soaked for one day in the white shell of a great river-[creature],
with the milk of the northern <s>vāruṇī</s> [plant] and with this paste, O virtuous one — (RA 6.94)

children.text: tālena meṣaśṛṅgyā ca | vajravallyā ca veṣṭitam |
children.translated_text: wrapped with <s>tāla</s> (palm), <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>vajravallī</s> (diamond-creeper),

children.text:
andhamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ | vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_6.95)
children.translated_text: smelted in a sealed crucible — the diamond is killed instantly. (RA 6.95)
One should place the diamond inside a lodestone cake, O Goddess,
and grind [it] with <s>gandha-taila</s> (fragrant oil) — the diamond is killed, O Supreme Goddess. (RA 6.96)
In a decoction of horse gram, with green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum), and orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),
combined with the alkali of <s>apāmārga</s> (chaff-flower) — the diamond, when quenched, becomes killed. (RA 6.97)
Wrapped in the bulb of <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), the seeds of <s>timira</s> (dark plant), bark, and milk,
placed inside a <s>meṣaśṛṅga</s> [container], coated with clay — the diamond is killed by heating-cycles. (RA 6.98)

children.text: peṭārī haṃsapādī ca | vajravallī ca sūraṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>Peṭārī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s> (goose-foot plant), <s>vajravallī</s>, and <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant-foot yam),
and sprouts of the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), O Goddess — all ground with breast milk. (RA 6.99)
With this prepared paste, wrapped in the fruit of <s>bṛhatī</s> (nightshade),

children.text:
kṣiptaṃ bahirmṛdā liptaṃ | mriyate saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
                    (RA_6.100)
children.translated_text: placed outside, coated with clay — [the diamond] is killed by seven heating-cycles. (RA 6.100)
With the flower-water of <s>śveta-indurekhā</s> (white moon-mark plant), the three [forms of] <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) —

children.text:
veṣṭitaṃ kuliśaṃ devi | puṭapākāt mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_6.101)
children.translated_text: the diamond, O Goddess, when wrapped [with these] and baked in a heating-cycle, becomes killed. (RA 6.101)
<s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>badarī</s> (jujube), <s>bhiṇḍī</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), and crab shell —
ground with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia), by a heating-cycle, the <s>vipra</s> (Brāhmaṇa-class diamond) is killed. (RA 6.102)
With the milk of oleander (<s>karavīra</s>) and crown-flower (<s>arka</s>), <s>meṣaśṛṅga</s> with cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>),
combined with <s>udumbara</s> (fig) juice — by a heating-cycle, [this is] the killing of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> [-class diamond]. (RA 6.103)

children.text: bālā cātibalā caiva | gandhakaṃ karkaṭāsthi ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Bālā</s> and <s>Atibālā</s> [plants], <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and crab shell,
with the milk of the northern <s>vāruṇī</s> — by a heating-cycle, [this is] the killing of the <s>Vaiśya</s> [-class diamond]. (RA 6.104)
With the itching yam (<s>kaṇḍūla-sūraṇa</s>), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and garlic,
with the milk of the banyan (<s>nyagrodha</s>) and conch — the <s>Śūdra</s> [-class diamond] is killed instantly. (RA 6.105)
Thick [diamonds] are destroyed by many large heating-cycles;
they become as if well-softened, and malleability arises. (RA 6.106)
Having ground the five parts of the <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) [and] the fair-colored <s>indravāruṇī</s> —

children.text:
anena veṣṭitaṃ vajraṃ | mriyate saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
                    (RA_6.107)
children.translated_text: the diamond, wrapped with this, is killed by seven heating-cycles. (RA 6.107)
One should place the diamond inside the living body of a <s>mātṛvāhaka</s> (mother-carrier insect);
in a swing-apparatus steam-bath (<s>dolāsveda</s>) for three days, O Goddess — it becomes like a [thin] leaf of metal. (RA 6.108)
One should insert the diamond into the trunk of a castor-oil (<s>eraṇḍa</s>) tree, O Goddess.
After one month, O Goddess, it becomes like a [thin] metal leaf. (RA 6.109)
One should insert the diamond inside a lodestone cake, O Goddess,
with cotton and neem leaves, combined with <s>badarī</s> (jujube) leaves. (RA 6.110)
One should grind all of this together, wrapped in a lodestone ball,
outside [wrapped] with a betel leaf, and place it between the knees. (RA 6.111)
Within two watches (<s>yāmas</s>), that diamond certainly becomes soft.

children.text:
tatkṣaṇānmriyate vajraṃ | tāre hemni na saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_6.112)
children.translated_text: The softened diamond is killed in that instant — [it merges] into silver and gold, without doubt. (RA 6.112)
Placed inside a citron (<s>jambīra</s>) fruit, wrapped in a cloth bundle,
one should boil [it] in a decoction of wild millet by this method for three days.

children.text:
tad vajraṃ jāyate khoṭaṃ | hemnā milati tatkṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_6.113)
children.translated_text: That diamond becomes a lump (<s>khoṭa</s>) and merges with gold instantly. (RA 6.113)

children.text: nāgavallyā praliptaṃ tu | tat pattreṇaiva veṣṭitam |
children.translated_text: Smeared with <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) [juice] and wrapped with its leaf,

children.text:
jānumadhye sthitaṃ yāmaṃ | mṛdu saṃjāyate dhruvam ||
                    (RA_6.114)
children.translated_text: placed between the knees for one watch (<s>yāma</s>) — it certainly becomes soft. (RA 6.114)
At the root of the <s>vajra-latā</s> (diamond-creeper), one should insert the softened diamond.
Applying a heating-cycle carefully — it turns to ash instantly. (RA 6.115)

children.text: sukhādbandhakaraṃ hy āśu | sattvaṃ muñcati tatkṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: It readily produces binding; the essence (<s>sattva</s>) is released instantly.
These [processes] pacify all [types of] death and bestow all <s>siddhis</s>. (RA 6.116)
Having placed the diamond perforated [and threaded] inside a chain of bones,

children.text:
jalabhāṇḍe tu tat svinnaṃ | saptāhaṃ dravatāṃ vrajet ||
                    (RA_6.117)
children.translated_text: steamed in a water vessel for seven days — it attains liquefaction. (RA 6.117)
The three alkalis (<s>kṣāra-traya</s>), <s>rāmaṭha</s> (rock salt), <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpea), sour tamarind,
add the milk of <s>jvālāmukhī</s> (flame-mouth plant), and the juice of the land-tortoise (<s>sthala-kumbhīra</s>) — (RA 6.118)
the diamond pressed with these, and with the milky sap of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (crown-flower),

children.text: dolāyāṃ svedayed devi | jāyate rasavad yathā || (RA_6.119)
children.translated_text: should be steamed in a swing-apparatus, O Goddess — it becomes like mercury. (RA 6.119)
Or else, steamed mica (<s>abhraka</s>), pearl, and coral,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ nīlapuṣpaṃ ca | pītaṃ marakataṃ mahat |
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), blue sapphire (<s>nīlapuṣpa</s>), yellow [stone], and great emerald (<s>marakata</s>),
<s>vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye), crystal, and the like — they liquefy like water. (RA 6.120)

children.text: lohajātaṃ tathā dhmātam | agnivarṇaṃ tu dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: Metal-born [substance], when smelted, appears fire-colored;

children.text: vāpitaṃ sakṛd ekena | mṛtaṃ jalasamaṃ bhavet || (RA_6.121)
children.translated_text: quenched once with that [liquid] — the killed [metal] becomes like water. (RA 6.121)
A pearl, soaked for seven days in sour tamarind juice,
placed inside a citron fruit, should be stored in a heap of grain.
By a heating-cycle, it becomes powder — [dissolving] like water. (RA 6.122)
Listen, O greatly fortunate Goddess, about the great mineral (<s>mahārasa</s>) called <s>vaikrānta</s>. (RA 6.123)
The demon-lord <s>Mahiṣa</s>, the accomplished one, born from the body of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —

children.text: durgā bhagavatī devī | taṃ śūlena vyamardayat || (RA_6.124)
children.translated_text: the blessed Goddess <s>Durgā</s> crushed him with [her] trident. (RA 6.124)

children.text: tasya raktaṃ tu patitaṃ | yatra yatra sthitaṃ bhuvi |
children.translated_text: His blood, wherever it fell and remained on the earth —

children.text:
tatra tatra tu vaikrānto | vajrākāro mahārasaḥ ||
                    (RA_6.125)
children.translated_text: there, in those places, [arose] <s>vaikrānta</s>, diamond-shaped, a great mineral. (RA 6.125)

children.text: vindhyasya dakṣiṇe cāsti | uttare nāsti sarvathā |
children.translated_text: It exists to the south of the <s>Vindhya</s> [mountains]; to the north it is entirely absent.
Because it cuts (<s>vikṛntayati</s>) metals, it is known as <s>vaikrānta</s>. (RA 6.126)
White, yellow, red, blue, dove-colored,
resembling a peacock's tail, and another with emerald lustre — (RA 6.127)

children.text: dehasiddhikaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ | pīte pītaḥ site sitaḥ |
children.translated_text: the black one bestows bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>); the yellow [is effective] on yellow [metals], the white on white.
The red one grants all aims; likewise the emerald-lustered one.

children.text:
śeṣe dve niṣphale varjye | vaikrāntamiti saptadhā ||
                    (RA_6.128)
children.translated_text: The remaining two are fruitless and should be avoided — thus <s>vaikrānta</s> is sevenfold. (RA 6.128)

children.text: yatra kṣetre sthitaṃ devi | vaikrāntaṃ tatra bhairavam |
children.translated_text: In whichever field the <s>vaikrānta</s> is found, O Goddess, there [one should worship] <s>Bhairava</s>
and <s>Vināyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), and then the foremost practitioner should collect [it]. (RA 6.129)
The <s>vaikrānta</s>, finely powdered, honored by gods and demons,
placed inside the bulb of <s>vyāghrī</s> (tiger-plant), and smelted in a heating-cycle — (RA 6.130)
should be steamed with horse urine over gentle fire for seven days.
Then it should be dried in the shade — this is the supreme <s>vaikrānta</s>. (RA 6.131)
Or else, with salt, alkali, urine, sour [substances], and black sesame oil,
one should steam [it] in a decoction of horse gram and wild millet for seven days. (RA 6.132)

children.text: vandhyācūrṇaṃ tu vaikrāntaṃ | samāṃśena tu cūrṇayet |
children.translated_text: The barren-[tree] powder and <s>vaikrānta</s> should be powdered in equal parts;
soaked with goat's urine, dried in the shade,

children.text: andhanāle dhamitvā tu | mūṣāsattvaṃ tu jāyate || (RA_6.133)
children.translated_text: and smelted in a closed tube — the metallic essence (<s>mūṣā-sattva</s>) is produced. (RA 6.133)
Soaked with the alkali of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation-plant), <s>moraṭa</s>, and <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) in cow's urine,
combined with the paste of <s>vajrakanda</s> root, lac, and borax — (RA 6.134)
the <s>vaikrānta</s>-derived powder, mixed with the juice of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,
formed into a ball and smelted in a sealed crucible — releases its metallic essence. (RA 6.135)
<s>Vaikrānta</s> and <s>vajrakanda</s> should be ground with <s>vajra</s>-water (<s>vajra-vāri</s>);

children.text: māhiṣe navanīte ca | sakṣaudraṃ piṇḍitaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: then formed into a ball with buffalo butter and honey,
purified and smelted — the essence falls out, resembling a firefly (<s>indragopa</s>). (RA 6.136)
The juice of <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, the stone from a [pearl-]churning, with <s>khecara</s> (an ingredient) —
by steaming, O Goddess, the <s>vaikrānta</s> becomes mercury-like. (RA 6.137)

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ | kāntalohasya vā rajaḥ |
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, or the powder of lodestone (<s>kānta-loha</s>) —
by this steaming method, [all] liquefy like water. (RA 6.138)
Thus have been described the characteristics and the like of the four [minerals] beginning with mica (<s>abhraka</s>).

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_6.139)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 6.139)

children.text:
iti śrīpārvatīparameśvarasaṃvāde rasārṇave rasasaṃhitāyām
                    abhrakādilakṣaṇasaṃskāranirṇayo nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ paṭalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the dialogue between <s>Śrī Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, the <s>Rasa-saṃhitā</s>, [ends] the sixth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) named 'Determination of the Characteristics and Processing of Mica and the Like.'
7. [Determination of the Characteristics, Processing, Gem-Liquefaction, and Killing of the Great Minerals, Sub-minerals, and Metals]
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:
Together with their characteristics and processing, instruct [me on] the great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>);
and whatever else, O God, is auxiliary to the science of mercury. (RA 7.1)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> spoke:
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>Vimala</s> (iron vitriol), <s>Śaila</s> (bitumen/shilajit), <s>Capala</s> (bismuth), <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc ore), likewise
<s>Sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol), <s>Darada</s> (cinnabar), and <s>Srotoñjana</s> (antimony/galena) — these are the eight.
Thus are the eight great minerals (<s>mahārasa</s>); hear of them first. (RA 7.2)
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (Viṣṇu), having heard the <s>Bhārata</s> [war], entered the sleep of <s>Yoga</s> (<s>yoganidrā</s>).
His foot-sole was pierced by a hunter who mistook [him] for a deer. (RA 7.3)
Those drops of blood that fell to the ground from the wound
became, in the shape of <s>neem</s> fruits, the stones of <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite). (RA 7.4)
<s>Mākṣika</s> is of two kinds, distinguished as yellow and white.

children.text: vimalastrividho devi | śuklaḥ pītaś ca lohitaḥ || (RA_7.5)
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> is of three kinds, O Goddess: white, yellow, and red. (RA 7.5)
In oil, sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>), buttermilk (<s>takra</s>), cow's urine, banana juice,
and decoctions of horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>) and <s>kodrava</s> [millet] — <s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>Vimala</s> likewise,
placed repeatedly in an elephant-yam tuber (<s>sūraṇakanda</s>), should be sweated, O woman of excellent complexion. (RA 7.6)
Endowed with alkalies (<s>kṣāra</s>), acids (<s>amla</s>), salts (<s>lavaṇa</s>), egg, oil, and ghee,
three firings (<s>puṭa</s>) should be given — [thereby] those two become purified. (RA 7.7)
<s>Mākṣika</s>, powdered, treated with breast milk, <s>snuhī</s> (cactus) milk, and <s>arka</s> (milkweed) milk,
when well-smelted with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, yields its essence (<s>sattva</s>). (RA 7.8)
Soaked in the juices of banana tuber, <s>tulasī</s> (basil), and sour orange (<s>nāraṅga</s>),
subjected to seven-times-seven firings (<s>puṭa</s>), combined with the five fluxes (<s>pañcadrāvaka</s>),
treated with breast milk and smelted, <s>Mākṣika</s> yields its essence (<s>sattva</s>). (RA 7.9)
With honey-oil (<s>kṣaudra</s>) and <s>gandharvataila</s> (castor oil), with cow's urine and ghee,
and with the extract of banana tuber — <s>Mākṣika</s>, treated repeatedly,

children.text:
mūṣāyāṃ muñcati dhmātaṃ | sattvaṃ śulvanibhaṃ mṛdu ||
                    (RA_7.10)
children.translated_text: when smelted in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), yields a soft essence resembling copper. (RA 7.10)
Having added the juice of <s>devadālī</s>, with a quarter-portion of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text:
prakaṭāṃ mūṣikāṃ kṛtvā | dhamet sattvam apekṣitam ||
                    (RA_7.11)
children.translated_text: having made an open crucible, one should smelt — the desired essence [is obtained]. (RA 7.11)
What is remarkable here? <s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), well-cooked with banana juice in an elephant-yam tuber container,

children.text:
vātāritailena puṭena tāpyaṃ | puṭena dagdhaṃ varaśuddhim eti ||
                    (RA_7.12)
children.translated_text: [heated] with castor oil (<s>vātāritaila</s>) by a firing — when burnt by a firing, attains excellent purification. (RA 7.12)
With cow's urine, <s>snuhī</s> milk, and castor oils,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ dinam ekaṃ tu | marditaṃ vaṭakīkṛtam |
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, ground for one day and made into cakes,
should be smelted like mica (<s>abhra</s>) — this procedure applies to <s>Sasyaka</s> as well. (RA 7.13)
<s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite) is a mineral; <s>āvartaka</s> is <s>dhātumākṣika</s>; <s>madhudhātu</s> (honey-mineral) [is another name].
<s>Mākṣika</s> is bitter-sweet; it cures diabetes (<s>meha</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>), consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>), and skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>).
It removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is strengthening (<s>balya</s>), a carrier of medicinal potency (<s>yogavāhī</s>), and a rejuvenative (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 7.14)
Fever, combined afflictions (<s>saṃnipāta</s>), and poverty — by the mere utterance of its name,
[these] are destroyed [even] at a distance of a hundred <s>yojanas</s> — who then [could doubt] its power to transmute metals? (RA 7.15)
<s>Vimala</s>, [treated] with <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree) water, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and borax,
combined with <s>vajrakanda</s>, treated with banana juices, (RA 7.16)
combined with the alkali of <s>mokṣaka</s> [plant], smelted in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>),
it yields an essence resembling the moon and sun — without doubt. (RA 7.17)
<s>Śaila</s> (bitumen/shilajit) is of two kinds, O Goddess: 'fallen' (<s>patita</s>) and 'not-fallen' (<s>apatita</s>).
It is praised in other treatises as well, extolled by many gods. (RA 7.18)
In summer, the mountains, heated by the [sun's] warmth, exude
the essence of minerals as a resin — that is declared to be <s>Śilājatu</s> (shilajit). (RA 7.19)
'That which is from rock' (<s>śilāvad dhātuka</s>), 'rock-born' (<s>śailaja</s>), 'mountain's companion' (<s>girisānuja</s>),
'mineral resin' (<s>jatvadri</s>), 'mountain' (<s>giri</s>), 'rock' (<s>śaila</s>) — these are the names as declared and recounted by you. (RA 7.20)
Smelted with alkaline liquids, cow's urine, and acids, <s>Śilājatu</s> is purified.
Or with cow's ghee, with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s> (three myrobalans) and fresh ginger (<s>dvyārdraka</s>),

children.text: lohapātre vinikṣipya | śodhayet tat tu yatnataḥ || (RA_7.21)
children.translated_text: placing it in an iron vessel, one should carefully purify it. (RA 7.21)
Having powdered <s>Śaila</s> (bitumen), with fermented grain acid (<s>dhānyāmla</s>), <s>upaviṣa</s> (semi-poisons), and poisons,

children.text:
piṇḍaṃ baddhvā tu vidhivat | pātayec capalaṃ yathā ||
                    (RA_7.22)
children.translated_text: having bound it into a pellet properly, one should make it fall [i.e., distill] like <s>Capala</s> (bismuth). (RA 7.22)

children.text: gauraḥ śveto 'ruṇaḥ kṛṣṇaś | capalas tu praśasyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Capala</s> (bismuth) is praised [in varieties of] fair, white, reddish, and dark.
That which resembles gold, and that which resembles silver, are especially [effective as] binders of mercury. (RA 7.23)

children.text: śeṣau madhyau ca lākṣāvat | śīghradrāvau tu niṣphalau |
children.translated_text: The remaining two [varieties], which are medium, resemble lac, melt quickly, and are ineffective.
It melts in fire like tin — hence it is called <s>Capala</s> ('the fickle one'). (RA 7.24)

children.text: vastreṇa baddhvā capalaṃ | laṅghayed yadi sāgaram |
children.translated_text: If one binds <s>Capala</s> in cloth and takes it across the ocean,

children.text:
vastraṃ ca veṣṭayet sadyaḥ | tenāsau capalaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.25)
children.translated_text: the cloth immediately wraps around [it, dissolving] — for this reason too it is called <s>Capala</s> ('the restless one'). (RA 7.25)
One should extract <s>Capala</s> by the firing method (<s>puṭapāka</s>) on a mountaintop.
It accomplishes the binding of the body [i.e., bodily immortality], and especially the binding of mercury. (RA 7.26)
<s>Capala</s>, restless like a cloud, effects the transmutation of <s>Capala</s> [itself].
<s>Capala</s> is scraping, unctuous, and is considered to produce bodily [immortality] and [transmutation of] metals. (RA 7.27)
<s>Rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc ore) is of three kinds, distinguished as earth-like, jaggery-like, and stone-like. (RA 7.28)
The yellow, earth-like <s>Rasaka</s> is the best.
The jaggery-colored one is known as middling; the stone-colored one is the lowest. (RA 7.29)
Having stirred <s>Rasaka</s> in the exudate of bitter gourd (<s>kaṭu alābu</s>), one should cook it.
It becomes purified, free from defects, and turns yellow in color. (RA 7.30)

children.text: kimatra citraṃ rasakaṃ rasena | rajasvalāyāḥ kusumena bhāvitam |
children.translated_text: What is remarkable here? <s>Rasaka</s>, treated with mercury and the menstrual blood of a woman,

children.text:
krameṇa kṛtvā uragena rañjitaṃ | karoti śulbaṃ tripuṭena
                    kāñcanam || (RA_7.31)
children.translated_text: gradually tinged with serpent [venom] — it turns copper into gold by three firings. (RA 7.31)
It does not diminish when placed in fire — it is in the form of [pure] essence, of great potency. (RA 7.32)

children.text: rasakaṃ cūrṇayitvā tu | baddhvā vastre vicakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having powdered <s>Rasaka</s>, the discerning one should bind it in cloth
and immerse it in women's urine for seven nights, O Goddess. (RA 7.33)

children.text:
puṣpāṇāṃ raktapītānāṃ | rasaiḥ pattraiś ca bhāvayet ||
                    (RA_7.34)
children.translated_text: One should treat it with the juices and leaves of red and yellow flowers. (RA 7.34)

children.text: kṣāraiḥ snehaistathā cāmlaiḥ | bhāvitaṃ rasakaṃ muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, treated repeatedly with alkalies, oils, and acids,
combined with wool (<s>ūrṇā</s>), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>bhūlatā</s> (a creeper), and smoke, (RA 7.35)
placed in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>) and smelted with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),
it yields an essence resembling <s>kuṭila</s> (antimony/tin) — without doubt. (RA 7.36)
<s>Gobhadda</s> (cow-pierced), <s>Rasaka</s>, <s>Tuttha</s> (blue vitriol), <s>Kṣitikiṭṭa</s> (earth-rust), <s>Rasodbhava</s> (born of rasa),
<s>Kharpara</s> (calamine) — enemy of eye diseases, maker of brass (<s>rīti</s>), colorer of copper — [these are its names]. (RA 7.37)
<s>Rasaka</s> is coloring, rough (<s>rūkṣa</s>), aggravates <s>vāta</s>, and destroys <s>kapha</s>.
But its essence (<s>sattva</s>) destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> and cures eye diseases. (RA 7.38)
<s>Garuḍa</s>, having drunk the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison, was unable to endure it;
he vomited even the nectar (<s>sudhā</s>), having consumed the immortality-giving venom of the serpent.

children.text:
svayaṃ vinirgate cañcvoḥ | sasyako 'bhūt sa kālikaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.39)
children.translated_text: What fell spontaneously from his beak became <s>Sasyaka</s> — that is [its origin-myth], O dark one. (RA 7.39)
<s>Sasyaka</s> of the first kind — one should treat its powder in women's urine,
or immerse it in hare's blood for one day. (RA 7.40)
Its powder, O great Goddess, combined with a quarter-part of <s>saubhāgya</s> (good-fortune mineral),
placed in <s>karañja</s> (pongamia) oil, should be immersed for one day. (RA 7.41)
Placed in the middle of a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>), one should smelt with three [charges of] bellows-blowing.
A beautiful essence resembling the <s>indragopaka</s> (cochineal insect) falls out. (RA 7.42)
Thus <s>Sasyaka</s> of the first kind, when smelted, falls out [as essence],
freed from [its] dark [impurity], red, resembling a peacock's neck in appearance. (RA 7.43)
<s>Sasya</s> [i.e., <s>Sasyaka</s>] is [also called] <s>Mayūratuttha</s> (peacock-vitriol); it produces [digestive] fire, destroys death,

children.text:
rasāyane tu yogyaḥ syād | vayaḥstambhakaro bhavet ||
                    (RA_7.44)
children.translated_text: is suitable for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>), and arrests aging (<s>vayaḥstambhakara</s>). (RA 7.44)
<s>Sasyaka</s> attains purity when treated with the red group [of substances]. (RA 7.45)
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar) is declared to be of three kinds: <s>Carmāra</s> (leather-like), <s>Śukatuṇḍaka</s> (parrot-beak[-colored]),
and the third, <s>Haṃsapāda</s> (goose-foot) — each successively superior in quality. (RA 7.46)
<s>Darada</s> is again of two kinds, distinguished as powder and [liquid] mercury. (RA 7.47)
In cow meat, buffalo urine, in curd, acids, sesame, and oil,
cooking [it] in each for three days, one should then treat it with peacock bile. (RA 7.48)
One should distill <s>Darada</s> in a distillation apparatus (<s>pātanāyantra</s>) into a water receptacle.

children.text: sattvaṃ tu sūtasaṃkāśaṃ | jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ || (RA_7.49)
children.translated_text: An essence resembling mercury (<s>sūta</s>) is produced — of this there is no doubt. (RA 7.49)
<s>Laghu</s> (light), <s>kandarasa</s> (cave-juice), <s>Mleccha</s>, <s>Hiṅgula</s> (vermilion), <s>Cūrṇapārada</s> (powdered mercury),
<s>Maṇirāgaja</s> (born of gem-color) — these are the names; [also] <s>Carmāragandhika</s> (leather-like sulfide). (RA 7.50)
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar/vermilion) is pungent and hot, divine, born of mercury and sulfur.
It cures metal[-caused] diseases and skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>); it is a divine strengthener, enhancer of intellect, and kindler of [digestive] fire. (RA 7.51)

children.text: kimatra citraṃ daradaḥ subhāvitaḥ | kṣīreṇa meṣyā bahuśo 'mlavargaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What is remarkable here? <s>Darada</s>, well-treated with ewe's milk and with many acid substances,
turns white gold, heated with much fire, into the color of excellent saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) — visibly. (RA 7.52)
Shaped like the peak of an anthill, in fracture having the luster of a blue lotus,
when rubbed, having the hue of red ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — [this is] <s>Srotoja</s> (stream-born [antimony]), O one praised by the gods. (RA 7.53)
Treated repeatedly with cow dung juice, cow's urine, ghee, honey, and fat,

children.text:
bhāvitaṃ bahuśastac ca | kṣipraṃ badhnāti sūtakam ||
                    (RA_7.54)
children.translated_text: it swiftly binds mercury. (RA 7.54)
Thus the great minerals (<s>mahārasa</s>) have been described; now hear of the subsidiary minerals (<s>uparasa</s>), O beloved. (RA 7.55)
<s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>Tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>Śilā</s> (realgar), <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum from Saurashtra), <s>Khagagairika</s> (red ochre),

children.text: rājāvartaś ca kaṅkuṣṭham | aṣṭā uparasāḥ smṛtāḥ || (RA_7.56)
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), and <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> — these eight are known as the subsidiary minerals (<s>uparasa</s>). (RA 7.56)
On the White Island (<s>Śvetadvīpa</s>), O Goddess, long ago, adorned with all gems,
on that delightful [shore], fulfilling all desires, on the bank of the Ocean of Milk (<s>Kṣīrasāgara</s>), (RA 7.57)
with foremost <s>Vidyādharī</s> women, with beautiful ladies,
with beloved <s>Siddha</s> women, and with hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), (RA 7.58)
with divine women and others, sporting, O beloved,
with varied songs, dances, and manifold musical instruments, (RA 7.59)
while [You were] thus sporting, Your menstrual flow (<s>rajas</s>) issued forth.
That menstrual blood, O beautiful-hipped one, was exceedingly fragrant and enchanting. (RA 7.60)
Due to the abundance of that menstrual flow, Your garment became red.

children.text: tatra tyaktvā tu tadvāsaḥ | susnātā kṣīrasāgare || (RA_7.61)
children.translated_text: Having discarded that garment there, having bathed well in the Ocean of Milk, (RA 7.61)
You, surrounded by divine women and gods, went to the city.
The waves carried Your blood-stained garment into the midst of the ocean. (RA 7.62)

children.text: evaṃ te śoṇitaṃ bhadre | praviṣṭaṃ kṣīrasāgare |
children.translated_text: Thus, O auspicious one, Your blood entered the Ocean of Milk.
During the churning of the Milk Ocean, this [substance] arose together with the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>),
delighting all gods and demons with its own fragrance. (RA 7.63)
Then the hosts of gods declared: 'Let this be called <s>Gandhaka</s> ("the fragrant one").' (RA 7.64)
'Let this serve for the binding of mercury and for its calcination (<s>jāraṇā</s>).',

children.text:
ye guṇāḥ pārade proktās | te caivātra bhavantviti ||
                    (RA_7.65)
children.translated_text: 'The qualities that are attributed to mercury — let those same [qualities] be in this [substance] as well.' (RA 7.65)

children.text: iti devagaṇaiḥ prītaiḥ | purā proktaṃ sureśvari |
children.translated_text: Thus was it formerly declared by the pleased hosts of gods, O Goddess.
Therefore, this is renowned in the terrestrial sphere by the name <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur). (RA 7.66)

children.text: sa cāpi trividho devi | śukacañcunibho varaḥ |
children.translated_text: And it is of three kinds, O Goddess: that resembling a parrot's beak [in color] is the best;
the yellow-colored one is middling; the white-colored one is the lowest, O beloved. (RA 7.67)
Having melted it with <s>karañja</s> [seeds], egg-oil, in goat's milk,
one should pour it into the exudate of <s>Unmatta</s> (datura) — three times, each separately. (RA 7.68)
One should treat it with the seed-powder of <s>Jvālinī</s> [plant] and with fish bile.
Or, having been macerated for seven days in the juice of <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> [<s>Eclipta alba</s>], washed with water, (RA 7.69)
heated over jujube (<s>badara</s>) charcoal in a ghee-anointed metal vessel,
and rotated over mild fire on a ghee-anointed cloth — (RA 7.70)

children.text:
kṣipraṃ bhṛṅgasya niryāse | kṣālito gandhako hitaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.71)
children.translated_text: quickly washed in the juice of <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> — the sulfur becomes beneficial. (RA 7.71)
Sulfur, by its very nature, is of the form of mercury in its essential nature.
One should purify sulfur in milk, or in the juice of ginger (<s>śṛṅgavera</s>), (RA 7.72)

children.text: rase ca bhṛṅgarājasya | nimbukasya rase tathā |
children.translated_text: or in the juice of <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s>, or in the juice of lemon (<s>nimbuka</s>).
Purified seven times, the sulfur becomes immaculate. (RA 7.73)

children.text: tālakaḥ paṭalaḥ piṇḍo | dvidhā tatrādya uttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>) is [found as] sheet, lump, or powder — of these, the first is the best.

children.text:
kuṣmāṇḍe tu śataṃ vārān | tālakaṃ svedayed budhaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.74)
children.translated_text: In a pumpkin (<s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>), the wise one should steam orpiment a hundred times. (RA 7.74)
In the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s> [<s>Euphorbia</s>] and in the juice of bitter gourd (<s>kaṭukālābu</s>), separately seven times each,
[adding] sesame, mustard, drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), salt, and jaggery,

children.text:
ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca yutair hyetaiḥ | tālakaṃ bhūdhare dravet ||
                    (RA_7.75)
children.translated_text: and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) — combined with these, the orpiment should be melted in a mountain [furnace]. (RA 7.75)
The alkali of the <s>Vyādhighāta</s> fruit, and pumpkin-honey (<s>madhukuṣmāṇḍaka</s>),
with freshly produced liquids — the wise one should grind [the orpiment] for seven days. (RA 7.76)
Adding a quarter-portion of all [these], then [placing it] in the distillation apparatus (<s>pātanayantraka</s>),

children.text:
dadyāt puṭaṃ gajākāraṃ | patet sattvaṃ sutālakāt ||
                    (RA_7.77)
children.translated_text: one should apply elephant-grade (<s>gajākāra</s>) heating — the essence (<s>sattva</s>) will fall from the orpiment. (RA 7.77)

children.text: raktā śilā tu gomāṃse | luṅgāmlena vipācitā |
children.translated_text: Red realgar (<s>śilā</s>), cooked with beef and tamarind acid (<s>luṅgāmla</s>),

children.text:
tāṃ raktapītapuṣpāṇāṃ | rasaiḥ pittaiś ca bhāvayet ||
                    (RA_7.78)
children.translated_text: should be macerated with the juices of red and yellow flowers and with biles. (RA 7.78)

children.text:
sitā kṛṣṇā ca saurāṣṭrī | cūrṇakhaṇḍātmikā ca sā ||
                    (RA_7.79)
children.translated_text: White and black [are the two varieties]; and the <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> [variety comes] in powder and lump forms. (RA 7.79)

children.text: gopittena śataṃ vārān | saurāṣṭrīṃ bhāvayet tataḥ |
children.translated_text: With cow's bile, one should macerate the <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> [earth] a hundred times.
Having blown [in the furnace], one should extract the essence — the transmutation process is extremely secret. (RA 7.80)

children.text:
kāsīsaṃ trividhaṃ śuklaṃ | kṛṣṇaṃ pītamiti priye ||
                    (RA_7.81)
children.translated_text: Green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>) is of three kinds: white, black, and yellow, O beloved. (RA 7.81)
Having powdered the vitriol, one should macerate it with the juice of cough-plant (<s>kāsamarda</s>),
with the water of wild gourd (<s>rājakośātakī</s>), and with biles. (RA 7.82)
Red ochre (<s>gairika</s>) is of three kinds: [differentiated as] red, golden, and plain.
With decoctions of the red group of [reagents], and with biles, one should macerate each separately. (RA 7.83)
By this sequential method, one should blow the ochre [until] pure;

children.text:
kramāt sitaṃ ca raktaṃ ca | sattvaṃ patati śobhanam ||
                    (RA_7.84)
children.translated_text: successively, white and red essences fall, resplendent. (RA 7.84)
Lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>) is of two kinds, O goddess: in pellet and powder forms. (RA 7.85)
That powder, O queen of gods, combined with buffalo milk,
should be cooked in an iron vessel, mixed with cow's ghee. (RA 7.86)
That powder, O queen of gods, mixed with <s>Kunaṭī</s> [<s>Solanum</s>] ghee,
and with <s>Saubhāgya</s>-<s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow), should be formed into a ball.
When blown with <s>khadira</s> [acacia] charcoal, it releases a resplendent essence. (RA 7.87)

children.text:
kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ vidrumacchāyaṃ | tac ca sattvamayaṃ priye ||
                    (RA_7.88)
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> [is] coral-colored — and that is indeed of the nature of essence, O beloved. (RA 7.88)
With [the juices of] <s>sūryāvarta</s>, water, hailstones, <s>Agni</s> [plant], drumstick root,
the core of plantain stem, [and] the juices of barren gourd (<s>vandhyākośātakī</s>), (RA 7.89)
the juices of <s>Kākamācī</s> [<s>Solanum nigrum</s>], <s>Devadālī</s>, and <s>Vajrakanda</s>,
with these — individually or combined — together with alkalis, acids, oils, and rock salt,
the great ores (<s>mahārasa</s>) and subsidiary ores (<s>uparasa</s>) attain purity when macerated. (RA 7.90)
Lac, salt, <s>saubhāgya</s>, smoke-extract, and the three pungents (<s>kaṭutraya</s>),
drumstick root, beeswax (<s>madhūcchiṣṭa</s>), <s>Pathyā</s> [<s>Terminalia chebula</s>], bdellium (<s>guggulu</s>), [and] metallic preparations, (RA 7.91)
<s>sarjikā</s> alkali, resin of <s>Sarjā</s> [<s>Vateria indica</s>], combined with <s>piṇyāka</s> [oil-cake] and wool,
pigeon-excrement, five minor animal fluids (<s>kṣudra matsya drāvaka pañcaka</s>), (RA 7.92)
sesame, mustard, wheat, black gram (<s>māṣa</s>), flat beans (<s>niṣpāva</s>), and chickpea,
combined with goat's milk — this is declared to be the <s>vajrapiṇḍī</s> (diamond-ball preparation). (RA 7.93)
With this <s>vajrapiṇḍī</s>, combined with the five buffalo products (<s>pañcamāhiṣa</s>),
the great ores are pleased [i.e., processed] — macerated with the five cow products (<s>pañcagavya</s>). (RA 7.94)

children.text: koṣṭhe kharāgninā dhmātāḥ | sattvaṃ muñcanti suvrate |
children.translated_text: Blown in the furnace with fierce fire, they release their essences, O virtuous one.

children.text:
evaṃ śilābhyo jīvebhyo | mṛdbhyaḥ sattvaṃ prajāyate ||
                    (RA_7.95)
children.translated_text: Thus, from minerals, from living [substances], and from earths, essence is produced. (RA 7.95)

children.text: evaṃ coparasāḥ proktāḥ | śṛṇu lohānyataḥ param || (RA_7.96)
children.translated_text: Thus the subsidiary ores have been described. Now hear about the metals hereafter. (RA 7.96)

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ | tīkṣṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ bhujaṃgamam |
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and lead (<s>bhujaṅgama</s>) —

children.text:
lohaṃ tu ṣaḍvidhaṃ tac ca | yathā pūrvaṃ tadakṣayam ||
                    (RA_7.97)
children.translated_text: metals are of six kinds, and in order from the first, they are [progressively] inferior. (RA 7.97)
Of these, O queen of gods, the first two — [gold and silver] — are considered 'essential' (<s>sāra</s>) metals.
[Copper and iron are] 'ordinary' (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>); tin and lead are 'foul' (<s>pūtika</s>). (RA 7.98)
Born from mercury, born from the earth, and born from the mixing of metals —
gold is of three kinds; a fourth is not found. (RA 7.99)

children.text: raktābhaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ca | dvividhaṃ devi kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: Red-hued and yellow-colored — gold is of two kinds, O goddess.

children.text:
dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede | nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham ||
                    (RA_7.100)
children.translated_text: Red when heated, white when cut, and of saffron luster on the touchstone. (RA 7.100)
Heavy, soft, unctuous, and free from silver and copper —
gold rich in sixteen <s>varṇas</s> [of purity] is praised for [use in] the body and metals. (RA 7.101)
Clay macerated for five days with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) acid,
together with ash and salt — one should purify gold by means of sealed heating (<s>puṭapāka</s>). (RA 7.102)

children.text: śuklaṃ ca tārakṛṣṇaṃ ca | dvividhaṃ rajataṃ priye |
children.translated_text: White and dark — silver is of two kinds, O beloved.
Heavy, unctuous, soft, and white — such silver is considered the best. (RA 7.103)
Melted with lead and alkali-king [<s>yavakṣāra</s>], it seeks purity.
Silver, immersed three times in <s>Piśācī</s>-oil — [becomes purified]. (RA 7.104)

children.text: tāmraṃ ca dvividhaṃ proktaṃ | raktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sureśvari |
children.translated_text: Copper is said to be of two kinds: red and black, O queen of gods.
That which endures hammering, is unctuous, has red leaves, and is soft — that is the best. (RA 7.105)
Coated with the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s> and <s>Arka</s> [<s>Calotropis</s>], salt, and alkali-acid,

children.text:
tāmrapattraṃ ca nirguṇḍī- | rasamadhye tu ḍhālayet ||
                    (RA_7.106)
children.translated_text: the copper sheet should be quenched (<s>ḍhālana</s>) in the juice of <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> [<s>Vitex negundo</s>]. (RA 7.106)

children.text: rohaṇaṃ vājaraṃ caiva | tṛtīyaṃ ca paḍālakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Rohaṇa</s>, <s>Vājara</s>, and the third, <s>Paḍālaka</s> —

children.text:
iti tīkṣṇaṃ tridhā tac ca | kāntalohamiti smṛtam ||
                    (RA_7.107)
children.translated_text: thus iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) is of three kinds, and it is known as lodestone-metal (<s>kāntaloha</s>). (RA 7.107)
Blue-black, unctuous, with fine grain — that is the auspicious [iron].
<s>Guḍūcī</s> [<s>Tinospora</s>], <s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>Naktamāla</s> [<s>Pongamia</s>], and the three fruits (<s>phalatraya</s>), (RA 7.108)
<s>Gopālakī</s>, cow products, <s>Tumburu</s>, and <s>Lohanighnaka</s> —
in the juice of these, one should quench it — for the removal of earth-defects. (RA 7.109)
Tin (<s>trapu</s>) is to be known as of two kinds, distinguished as white and black.

children.text:
śvetaṃ laghu mṛdu snigdham | uttamaṃ vaṅgamucyate ||
                    (RA_7.110)
children.translated_text: White, light, soft, and unctuous — that is said to be the best tin (<s>vaṅga</s>). (RA 7.110)
Lead (<s>nāga</s>) is of one kind alone, O goddess — quick to melt, soft, and heavy. (RA 7.111)
With the bone-powder of a buffalo, and by sprinkling with its urine,

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ śuddhaṃ bhavet tadvat | nāgo nāgāsthimūtrataḥ ||
                    (RA_7.112)
children.translated_text: tin becomes pure; likewise, lead [is purified] with the bones and urine of an elephant. (RA 7.112)
Fruits of <s>Gaurī</s> [plant], <s>Kṣuraka</s>, turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>), and <s>Tumburu</s>,
seeds of <s>Kuberākṣa</s>, and jasmine (<s>mallikā</s>), O beautiful one — (RA 7.113)
combined with the alkali of <s>Palāśa</s> [<s>Butea</s>] dried [bark], <s>Apāmārga</s> [<s>Achyranthes</s>],
and the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s> — through seven [rounds of] quenching, they purify lead (<s>bhujaṅgama</s>). (RA 7.114)
Combined with the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s>, one should also quench tin. (RA 7.115)
With the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s> and <s>Arka</s>, <s>Halinī</s>, <s>Kañcukī</s>-bulb, <s>Citraka</s>,
<s>Guñjā</s>, <s>Karañja</s> [<s>Pongamia</s>], thorn-apple (<s>dhuttūra</s>), <s>Hayagandhā</s> [<s>Ashwagandha</s>], and <s>Aṅghritālaka</s>, (RA 7.116)
combined with <s>Naktamāla</s>, <s>Iṅgudī</s> [<s>Balanites</s>], and <s>Indra Vāruṇī</s> roots —
ground into a paste and steeped in buffalo buttermilk for seven nights,

children.text:
niṣekaḥ sarvalohānāṃ | malaṃ hanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.117)
children.translated_text: [this] sprinkling [quench-preparation] destroys the impurities of all metals — no doubt. (RA 7.117)
The pollen and juices of the <s>Devadālī</s> fruit, macerated repeatedly —

children.text:
drāvayet kanakaṃ vāpāt | bhūyo na kaṭhinaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_7.118)
children.translated_text: by quenching, gold is melted [and rendered] such that it becomes no longer hard. (RA 7.118)
All metallic essences can be melted by the power of this [preparation]. (RA 7.119)
Equal parts of [the powder of] <s>Suragopa</s> [cochineal beetle] and of <s>Suradālī</s> —
by quenching with that, O goddess, gold becomes water-like [in fluidity]. (RA 7.120)
With frog-bone fat, borax, horse-saliva, and <s>Indragopa</s> [cochineal] —
by the quenching additive (<s>prativāpa</s>), gold remains fluid for a long time. (RA 7.121)
The ash of <s>Jvālinī</s> [plant], filtered twenty-one times in cow's urine,

children.text:
śoṣayet tasya vāpena | tīkṣṇaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dravet ||
                    (RA_7.122)
children.translated_text: dried — by quenching with this, iron placed in a crucible melts. (RA 7.122)
Macerated twenty-one times with the ash of <s>Nicula</s> [<s>Barringtonia</s>],
and with the juices of <s>Ketakī</s> [<s>Pandanus</s>] — by quenching, iron becomes fluid. (RA 7.123)
With the juice of ripe <s>Dhātrī</s> [<s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Emblica officinalis</s>] fruit, macerated in a conch for seven days,
and again macerated for seven days in <s>Kañcukī</s>-water, (RA 7.124)
placed between a pair of saucers, firmly sealed and heated —
that iron powder, O queen of gods, becomes mercury-like in form. (RA 7.125)
Orpiment, arsenic (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>), realgar, pyrites (<s>mākṣika</s>), ochre,
vitriol, crystalline <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s>, blue vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), and mica, (RA 7.126)
the excrement of dogs, jackals, and hyenas, and of roosters,
the droppings of peacocks, vultures, and cats — in equal parts, (RA 7.127)
macerated three times in the milky latex of <s>Snuhī</s> and the juice of <s>Devadālī</s>,
with that paste, at one-eighth the quantity, one should coat the metal sheets. (RA 7.128)

children.text: dhamed drutaṃ bhavelloham | etair eva niṣecayet |
children.translated_text: One should blow [the furnace]; the metal becomes fluid. One should quench with those very [liquids].
The roots of <s>Aṅkola</s> [<s>Alangium</s>] should be ground with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>);

children.text:
lohalepaṃ tato dadyāt | agnisthaṃ dhārayet priye ||
                    (RA_7.129)
children.translated_text: then one should apply the metal-coating and hold it in fire, O beloved. (RA 7.129)
Then one should apply a coating again, with the juice of <s>Paricchinnā</s> [plant],
and with fish-bile, O queen of gods; one should hold it in fire, O beloved. (RA 7.130)
Again one should make a coating, produced from the bulb of <s>Lāṅgalī</s> [<s>Gloriosa</s>].
With three coatings, the metal becomes fluid — clear like pure water. (RA 7.131)
Powdered tortoise-bone, ram's horn, and mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>) —
by quenching additive, [the metal] becomes firm like water [i.e., solid yet lustrous] — strong as a thunderbolt. (RA 7.132)
<s>Arka</s>, <s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>Musalī</s>, <s>Nicula</s>, and <s>Citraka</s>,

children.text: kadalī potakī dālī | kṣārameṣāṃ tu sādhayet || (RA_7.133)
children.translated_text: plantain, <s>Potakī</s>, <s>Dālī</s> — the alkali of these should be prepared. (RA 7.133)
Filtered in buffalo urine six times, O one praised by gods,
by quenching, one should melt the powder produced from mica-essence and the like. (RA 7.134)
Especially with <s>Dantī</s>-tooth [plant], it melts [metal] like water. (RA 7.135)
The powder derived from <s>Vaikrānta</s> [tourmaline], soaked in the juice of <s>Uttara Vāruṇī</s>,
by quenching additive, melts metals [making them] water-like. (RA 7.136)

children.text:
ratnānāṃ drāvaṇaṃ vakṣye | gaganasya drutiṃ tathā ||
                    (RA_7.137)
children.translated_text: I shall describe the melting of gems, and also the liquefaction of mica. (RA 7.137)
The three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>), the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), the three alkalis (<s>trikṣāra</s>), and the five sharps (<s>paṭupañcaka</s>),

children.text: balā cātibalā caiva | tṛtīyā ca mahābalā || (RA_7.138)
children.translated_text: <s>Balā</s>, <s>Atibalā</s>, and the third, <s>Mahābalā</s>, (RA 7.138)
<s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>Cavī</s>, <s>Nārī</s>, <s>Bhūlatā</s>, <s>Mātṛvāhaka</s>,
<s>Gopendramaṇḍalī</s>, <s>Ṣaḍbindu</s>, and <s>Dvimukhī</s>. (RA 7.139)

children.text: dhīrā sūraṇakandaś ca | kañcukī ca punarnavā |
children.translated_text: <s>Dhīrā</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>punarnava</s>,
<s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>unmatta</s> [datura], <s>halinī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>; (RA 7.140)
lodestone (<s>ayaskānta</s>), <s>gokṣura</s>, soft <s>dūrvā</s> grass, sour date (<s>āmlavetasa</s>),
mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>), <s>sauvīra</s>, poison, sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). (RA 7.141)
All [these ingredients should be taken] separately at ten <s>palas</s> each, and ground to a fine powder;
two pots of horse-gram (<s>kulattha</s>) [decoction], with the wood of <s>tiniśa</s> [tree]; (RA 7.142)
boil on a gentle fire until one pot [of liquid] remains;
with that decoction, soak that powder twenty-one times. (RA 7.143)

children.text: ratnāni tena liptāni | tatkvāthasthaṃ dhamet punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Gems coated with that [paste], placed in that decoction and blown [in the furnace] —
within a day and night, they quickly melt like water. (RA 7.144)
Mica and other metals melt without hesitation,
and become pure, resembling <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) seed. (RA 7.145)
They unite with mercury quickly, and being fire-stable, they are imperishable;

children.text:
tair drutaiḥ sparśamātreṇa | kṣaṇād badhyeta sūtakaḥ ||
                    (RA_7.146)
children.translated_text: with those melted [substances], by mere touch, mercury is bound instantly. (RA 7.146)
I shall describe the killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) of metals — listen with concentrated mind.
With the milk of <s>snuhī</s> [spurge], [one kills] red lead (<s>sindūra</s>), gold, and silver; (RA 7.147)
with the same, [one kills] pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) and copper; with goat's milk, sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>);
with breast-milk, cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and <s>palāśaka</s>; (RA 7.148)
lead (<s>nāga</s>) [is killed] with the milk of <s>śilā</s> [lithophyte] and <s>arka</s> [<s>Calotropis</s>], having been made into thin sheets, O beloved;
kill [them] by the <s>puṭapāka</s> [sealed heating] method — an ash that does not revive is produced. (RA 7.149)

children.text: na so 'sti lohamātaṃgo | yaṃ na gandhakakesarī |
children.translated_text: There is no metal-elephant that the lion of sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>)
cannot slay by its mere smell — or [alternatively] the lion of pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>). (RA 7.150)
Metals, when killed, become mercurial (<s>rasībhūta</s>), O one praised by the gods;

children.text: haranti rogān sakalān | rasayuktāni kiṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: they destroy all diseases — how much more so when combined with mercury!
By regular use, they destroy wrinkles, grey hair, disease, and old age. (RA 7.151)
Diamond (<s>vajra</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), and mica (<s>abhra</s>) are recommended for bodily applications;

children.text:
nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ suvīraṃ ca | dravyakarmaṇi yojayet ||
                    (RA_7.152)
children.translated_text: lead (<s>nāga</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and <s>suvīra</s> should be employed for material operations (<s>dravyakarman</s>). (RA 7.152)

children.text: paribālaṃ tu yallohaṃ | tathā ca malayodbhavam |
children.translated_text: The metal called <s>paribāla</s> and that which is born of the <s>Malaya</s> [mountains] —
this pair of metals, O Goddess, is especially for the protection of the body. (RA 7.153)
Having known the coloring power (<s>rāga</s>) of the great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>) and the like, one should prepare the seeds (<s>bījas</s>).

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum arhasi ||
                    (RA_7.154)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 7.154)
8. [<s>Bījasādhana</s> (Preparation of Seeds)
The Glorious Goddess said:
Of the great minerals, metals, and gems, O Lord of the Gods,

children.text:
rāgasaṃkhyāṃ tathā bīja- | sādhanaṃ ca vada prabho ||
                    (RA_8.1)
children.translated_text: tell me the enumeration of coloring powers (<s>rāga</s>) and the preparation of seeds (<s>bīja</s>), O Lord. (RA 8.1)
The Glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said:
In the great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>), the copper-coloring power is doubled, O Queen of the Gods;

children.text: giridoṣe kṣayaṃ nīte | sūtakaṃ rañjayanti te || (RA_8.2)
children.translated_text: when the defect of mineral origin (<s>giridoṣa</s>) is removed, they color (<s>rañjayanti</s>) mercury. (RA 8.2)
<s>Sasyaka</s> (green vitriol), <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite),

children.text: vimalo gairikaṃ caiṣām | ekaikaṃ dviguṇaṃ bhavet || (RA_8.3)
children.translated_text: <s>vimala</s> (iron pyrites), and <s>gairika</s> (ochre) — each successive one has double [the coloring power]. (RA 8.3)

children.text: bhrāmakādiṣu kānteṣv apy | ekadvitriguṇo hi saḥ |
children.translated_text: Among the lodestones beginning with <s>bhrāmaka</s>, the [coloring power] is one-, two-, and three-fold;
in each [type of] mica — white, yellow, red, and pale — [it increases] individually. (RA 8.4)
Eighteen thousand coloring powers reside in sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>);
ten thousand in cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), O Goddess; two thousand in realgar (<s>śilā</s>). (RA 8.5)
In <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), seven thousand; in <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, four thousand;
they manifest in the womb of mercury — if calcination (<s>jāraṇa</s>) takes place. (RA 8.6)

children.text: dvādaśāgraṃ śataṃ pañca | nāge rāgā vyavasthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Five hundred and twelve [i.e., 1,260] coloring powers are established in lead (<s>nāga</s>);

children.text: śatahīnaṃ sahasraṃ tu | vaṅge rāgā vyavasthitāḥ || (RA_8.7)
children.translated_text: nine hundred are established as coloring powers in tin (<s>vaṅga</s>). (RA 8.7)
One hundred and fifty coloring powers are established in copper (<s>śulva</s>);

children.text: raktapītāś ca śuklāś ca | hemni rāgāś ca ṣoḍaśa || (RA_8.8)
children.translated_text: red, yellow, and white — sixteen coloring powers [are established] in gold (<s>hema</s>). (RA 8.8)
Sixty thousand coloring powers are established in blue sapphire (<s>śakranīla</s>);

children.text: mahānīle ca deveśi | te rāgā dviguṇāḥ sthitāḥ || (RA_8.9)
children.translated_text: and in the great sapphire (<s>mahānīla</s>), O Queen of the Gods, those coloring powers are doubled. (RA 8.9)
In ruby (<s>māṇikya</s>), O Lady of the Gods, [there are] thirteen <s>lakṣas</s> (1,300,000) of coloring powers;
the gem known as pearl (<s>muktāphala</s>) is born from elephants and water [oysters]. (RA 8.10)
In [pearls from] elephants, three thousand; in [those from] water [oysters], six thousand;
nine <s>lakṣas</s> (900,000) of coloring powers are established in <s>padmarāga</s> (red corundum). (RA 8.11)

children.text: bhedayet sarvalohāni | yac ca kena na bhidyate |
children.translated_text: That which splits all metals, and which nothing can split —

children.text:
tadvajraṃ tasya deveśi | rāgaṃ lakṣadvayaṃ viduḥ ||
                    (RA_8.12)
children.translated_text: that is diamond (<s>vajra</s>); its coloring power, O Queen of the Gods, is known as two <s>lakṣas</s> (200,000). (RA 8.12)
Sixteen thousand [coloring powers] are established in topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>);
three-quarters of a <s>lakṣa</s> (75,000) of coloring powers are stated for emerald (<s>marakata</s>), O beloved. (RA 8.13)

children.text: rāgasaṃkhyāṃ na jānāti | saṃkrāntasya rasasya tu |
children.translated_text: One who does not know the enumeration of coloring powers of transmitted mercury
will kill too much metal when [the power is] excessive, and [only] reveal [it] when deficient. (RA 8.14)

children.text: mānavendraḥ prakurvīta | yo hi jānāti pārvati |
children.translated_text: One who knows [this], O <s>Pārvatī</s>, would become a lord of measures;
he should calculate the enumeration of coloring powers in units of one hundred <s>koṭis</s>;
thus observing the touch[-test], he transmutes (<s>vidhyate</s>) [to the measure of] one hundred <s>koṭis</s>. (RA 8.15)

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi | bījānāṃ sādhanaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: Hereafter I shall describe the preparation of seeds (<s>bījas</s>), O beloved — listen.
The seed is of two kinds — for gold and for silver — O Goddess. (RA 8.16)
The gold-seed is [made] from yellow and red [substances]; the silver-seed from white ones;

children.text:
kalpitaṃ rañjitaṃ pakvam | iti bhūyastridhā bhavet ||
                    (RA_8.17)
children.translated_text: [each seed is] further of three kinds: prepared (<s>kalpita</s>), colored (<s>rañjita</s>), and matured (<s>pakva</s>). (RA 8.17)
The prepared [seed] is again of two kinds — pure (<s>śuddha</s>) and mixed (<s>miśra</s>). (RA 8.18)
The preparation of seeds from mercurial substances (<s>rasas</s>), auxiliary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>), and metals (<s>lohas</s>) is done separately;

children.text:
śuddhaṃ miśraṃ tu saṃyogāt | yathālābhaṃ sureśvari ||
                    (RA_8.19)
children.translated_text: [the seed is] pure or mixed according to the combination — as available, O Queen of the Gods. (RA 8.19)
The essence (<s>sattva</s>) of mica (<s>vyoman</s>), revolved (<s>āvartita</s>), purified with glass (<s>kāca</s>) and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),
[treated] with sprinkling of the paste of tamarind (<s>ciñcāphala</s>), sour [juice], and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves —
when matured and solidified, O Goddess, it becomes fit to be a mercury-pellet (<s>rasapiṣṭi</s>). (RA 8.20)
With the groups of oils (<s>sneha</s>), alkalis (<s>kṣāra</s>), and sour substances (<s>āmla</s>), and from three firings (<s>puṭas</s>) of realgar (<s>śilā</s>),
when killed, [placed] in a fumigation apparatus (<s>dhūpanāyantra</s>) with [appropriate] fumigation, anointing, and scenting —
[this applies] also to the process of tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), or of killed orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>); (RA 8.21)
or also of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) and cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), or of killed <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) —
in the womb of mercury, the black sheet of gold and silver melts. (RA 8.22)
The [alloy] called <s>saṃkara</s> (impure alloy), which is difficult to unite, O beloved — called soft-hard (<s>mṛdukhara</s>);
then when ground together, O Goddess, the binary combination (<s>dvaṃdvamelāpana</s>) [takes place] quickly —

children.text: bhavet samarasaṃ garbhe | rasarājasya ca dravet || (RA_8.23)
children.translated_text: it becomes uniform in the womb [of mercury], and melts in the womb of the king of mercurial substances. (RA 8.23)
Hereafter I shall describe the binary combination (<s>dvaṃdvamelāpana</s>) — listen. (RA 8.24)
[Take] <s>varṣābhū</s>, plantain (<s>kadalī</s>) tuber, black nightshade (<s>kākamācī</s>), and <s>punarnava</s>;
powder of human skull (<s>narakapāla</s>), combined with <s>guñjā</s> and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>);
well-blown with milk and oil — gold-mica (<s>hemābhra</s>) unites, O beloved. (RA 8.25)
By this very procedure, silver-mica (<s>tārābhra</s>) also unites. (RA 8.26)
Having revolved tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), O Queen of the Gods, and then combined it with mercury,
grind it with plantain-tuber water, combined with borax;
placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) and blown — tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>) unites instantly. (RA 8.27)
Human skull powder, breast-milk, wild mustard (<s>vanaśigruka</s>),
combined with <s>guñjā</s> and borax — tin-mica unites instantly. (RA 8.28)
Having powdered mica, soaked in black nightshade (<s>kākamācī</s>) juice,
moistened with wood-apple (<s>kapittha</s>) water, combined with mercury and borax,
placed between tin sheets and blown — tin-mica unites. (RA 8.29)
Having revolved [the metal] with pungent oil, throw in ash of <s>apāmārga</s>;

children.text:
vaṅgābhraṃ haritālaṃ ca | nāgābhre tu manaḥśilāḥ ||
                    (RA_8.30)
children.translated_text: tin-mica [unites] with orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); lead-mica (<s>nāgābhra</s>) with realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>). (RA 8.30)
Gold-mica [is produced] from lead and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); silver-mica from tin and orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>);
copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>) with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>); iron-mica (<s>tīkṣṇābhra</s>) with <s>sindhu</s> and cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>);
tin-mica with orpiment; lead-mica unites with realgar (<s>śilā</s>). (RA 8.31)
[Take] <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>cāmarī</s> hair, cotton seed (<s>kārpāsāsthi</s>), and horse-gram (<s>kulattha</s>);
<s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>aśmadahanī</s>, breast-milk, and <s>suragopaka</s> (cochineal insect). (RA 8.32)
With [a crucible] coated with these [substances], and well-blown with intense fire,
lodestone-mica, stone, and <s>vimala</s> all unite instantly. (RA 8.33)
The flesh of the <s>latāchuchundarī</s> (musk-rat), combined with poison and borax,
[used as] crucible coating, effects unification in all binary [combinations]. (RA 8.34)

children.text: abhrakaṃ surasā śṛṅgaṃ | maṇḍūkasya vasā viṣam |
children.translated_text: Mica, holy basil (<s>surasā</s>), horn of a frog, fat, and poison,
combined with <s>guñjā</s> and borax — [effects] unification in all essences (<s>sattvas</s>). (RA 8.35)
With borax, wool, mineral pitch (<s>girijatu</s>), <s>karṇākhya</s>, and <s>karkaṭa</s> (crab),
ground with breast-milk — all binary [combinations] unite. (RA 8.36)
With <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>sarja</s> resin, barley (<s>yāva</s>), and borax,
ground with breast-milk — all binary [combinations are achieved] for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 8.37)
The essence of mica (<s>khasattva</s>), [made into] fine powder, combined with the aforesaid paste,
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — the impure alloy (<s>saṃkara</s>) unites instantly. (RA 8.38)
[Mica essence] sublimated with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>sasyaka</s> (vitriol), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>),

children.text:
khasattvaṃ syānnibaddhaṃ ca | dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ milettataḥ ||
                    (RA_8.39)
children.translated_text: the mica-essence becomes firmly bound; well-blown, it then unites. (RA 8.39)
All the mercurial substances (<s>rasas</s>), auxiliary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>), and metals (<s>lohas</s>) should be blown together;

children.text:
anyonyaṃ dvaṃdvatāṃ yānti | dravanti salilaṃ yathā ||
                    (RA_8.40)
children.translated_text: they mutually form binary [unions] and melt like water. (RA 8.40)
Seeds thus prepared — now hear about colored (<s>rañjita</s>) [seeds]. (RA 8.41)
Mica essence (<s>ghana</s>), colored with pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) powder and copper powder,
paired with <s>tāpya</s>-essence — [serves as] the coloring agent for the king of mercury. (RA 8.42)
With [preparations] soaked repeatedly in <s>āraktavallī</s> and cow-urine,
with <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s> (arsenic stone), gold, pyrite, and cinnabar; (RA 8.43)

children.text: vāpitaṃ sevitaṃ rakta- | gaṇaiḥ snehair mṛtaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: sublimated, treated with the red group [of substances] and oils, then killed —
[this becomes] the coloring agent of the king of mercury — iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) and copper especially. (RA 8.44)

children.text: kevalaṃ vimalaṃ tāmraṃ | vāpitaṃ daradena ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> [iron pyrites] and copper alone, sublimated with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>),

children.text:
kurute triguṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ | lākṣābhaṃ nirmalaṃ rasam ||
                    (RA_8.45)
children.translated_text: when digested (<s>jīrṇa</s>) threefold, produce a pure mercury resembling lac (<s>lākṣā</s>). (RA 8.45)
Adding double the amount of <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), copper is well-blown, O Goddess;

children.text:
kṛṣṇābhrakasya cūrṇaṃ ca | raktavargair muhuḥ puṭaiḥ ||
                    (RA_8.46)
children.translated_text: with black mica powder, [processed] with the red group, [and] with repeated firings; (RA 8.46)

children.text: tāpyena vā mṛtaṃ hema | triguṇena nivāpitam |
children.translated_text: or gold killed with <s>tāpya</s>, sublimated threefold,
[placed] in a container with <s>rasaka</s> combined with <s>tāpya</s> and rock salt; (RA 8.47)
until [it becomes] like a <s>indragopa</s> [firefly] — all by double calcination (<s>jāraṇā</s>);

children.text: drutaṃ hemanibhaṃ sūtaṃ | kurute nātra saṃśayaḥ || (RA_8.48)
children.translated_text: the melted mercury becomes gold-like — there is no doubt in this. (RA 8.48)

children.text: abhrakaṃ hema tāmraṃ ca | śilayā mākṣikeṇa ca |
children.translated_text: Mica, gold, and copper, with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>),

children.text: gairikeṇa ca mukhyena | rasakena ca rañjayet || (RA_8.49)
children.translated_text: and with the foremost ochre (<s>gairika</s>) and <s>rasaka</s> — one should color [the seed]. (RA 8.49)
Seeds thus colored — now hear about matured (<s>pakva</s>) seeds. (RA 8.50)
One should add the great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>), the auxiliary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>), and the sharp metals (<s>tīkṣṇalohas</s>),
in equal parts with an equal [portion of] pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), by the process of sulphur-sublimation (<s>gandhakāvāpa</s>). (RA 8.51)
One should sublimate this a hundred times — [the mercury remains] undiminished, with a residue;
[add] an equal part of the king of mercury — in the womb, it melts assuredly. (RA 8.52)
This very [preparation] is recommended for brick-solidification (<s>viṣṭikāstambha</s>), for calcination (<s>jāraṇā</s>), O Queen of the Gods,
for coloring the king of mercury, and for extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>). (RA 8.53)

children.text: tadeva śataśo rakta- | gaṇaiḥ snehair niṣecitam |
children.translated_text: That very [preparation], sprinkled a hundred times with the red group [of substances] and oils,
is especially recommended among those — it transmutes at a ratio of one to a thousand. (RA 8.54)
[The seed], purified from lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), in the operation for gold and silver,
The essence of mica (<s>kha-sattva</s>) should be combined with sun[-gold]; the pair would serve in the mercurial elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 8.55)
With oil, alkalis, the five sours, those [herbal] juices, orpiment and the like —
in equal, double, or triple proportions, one should carry tin and lead into copper. (RA 8.56)
That, saturated with red oil, is known as the extraction of mercury (<s>rasākṛṣṭi</s>). (RA 8.57)
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s> (fragrant stone / realgar), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar),
<s>vaikrāntaka</s>, the best <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), <s>sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol), <s>vimala</s> collyrium,

children.text:
rasakaṃ vāpitaṃ śaśvac- | cūrṇitaṃ hemni vāhayet ||
                    (RA_8.58)
children.translated_text: and <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore) — each quenched [in herbal liquids] and pulverized, should be carried into gold. (RA 8.58)
With metal flakes (<s>loha-parpaṭikā</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and mica,
killed copper, the essence of <s>śilā</s> (realgar), milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and cinnabar —

children.text: nāgo nirjīvatāṃ yāti | puṭayogaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ || (RA_8.59)
children.translated_text: lead is rendered lifeless (<s>nirjīva</s>) by repeated heating-cycles. (RA 8.59)
With mercury, orpiment, conch-shell, mica, and tamarind alkali, likewise tin;

children.text: mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ | śulvaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca vā mṛtam |
children.translated_text: killed lead, killed tin, killed copper, and killed iron —
each one individually should be carried into the finest gold, O one honored by the gods. (RA 8.60)

children.text: nirutthe pannage hemni | nirvyūḍhe śataśo gaṇe |
children.translated_text: When lead has been expelled and the [metal] driven into gold a hundredfold —
it attains a radiance like <s>gorocanā</s> (bright yellow pigment) in gold, and like silver in the sun-[metal]. (RA 8.61)
Iron, mica, sun-metal in equal parts, and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) in double quantity,
