children.text:
āvartitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ ca | māritaṃ saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
                    (RA_8.62)
children.translated_text: reversed, pulverized, and killed by seven heating-cycles — (RA 8.62)

children.text: vyūḍhe śataguṇe hemni | tadbījaṃ jārayet samam |
children.translated_text: when driven into gold a hundredfold, one should add (<s>jārayet</s>) that seed equally.
With a coating of moon-and-sun leaf (<s>candrārka-pattara</s>), one should transmute in one-hundredth proportion. (RA 8.63)

children.text: ūrdhvādho mākṣikaṃ dattvā | śulvaṃ hemasamaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Placing <s>mākṣika</s> above and below, the copper becomes equal to gold.
Thus, driven tenfold, the seed resembles the [original] cause. (RA 8.64)
<s>Rasaka</s> (zinc), mica, lodestone, and copper — adding [these] in increasing proportions, one should smelt.

children.text: mākṣikeṇa hataṃ tac ca | bīje nirvāhayet priye || (RA_8.65)
children.translated_text: That, killed with <s>mākṣika</s>, should be carried forth into the seed, O Beloved. (RA 8.65)

children.text: dvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ hemni | nāgaṃ tāpyaṃ hataṃ vahet |
children.translated_text: Lead, driven into gold in thirty-two-fold proportion, and killed <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) should be carried;
with realgar added in thirtyfold proportion — this is declared the gold-seed (<s>nāga-bīja</s>). (RA 8.66)
With the addition of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), the essence of yellow mica —
this should be carried forth into the seed; it transmutes that which is polished by women (<s>yoṣā-mṛṣṭa</s> = silver). (RA 8.67)

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ | nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatām |
children.translated_text: Lead produces softness; when expelled, it [produces] redness.

children.text:
vāpitaṃ pītatāṃ tīkṣṇaṃ | kāntasthāṃ kālikāṃ viṣam ||
                    (RA_8.68)
children.translated_text: Iron, when quenched, [produces] yellowness; lodestone, stability; <s>kālikā</s>, poison. (RA 8.68)
Thus has been described the gold-seed; now hear about the silver-seed. (RA 8.69)
Iron, mica, <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), <s>vimala</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore) — in equal parts;
the portions of tin are four; all [is] smelted and pulverized. (RA 8.70)

children.text: puṭena nihataṃ kāryaṃ | vyūḍhaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet |
children.translated_text: It should be killed by a heating-cycle. The silver thus driven should transmute.

children.text: dvātriṃśatsadguṇaṃ tāre | vaṅge tāpyaṃ hataṃ vahet |
children.translated_text: In thirty-two-fold [proportion] in silver, killed <s>tāpya</s> should be carried with tin;
from the addition of orpiment in thirtyfold proportion — this is declared the tin-seed (<s>vaṅga-bīja</s>). (RA 8.71)

children.text: kuṭilaṃ vimalaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ | khasattvaṃ cāpi vāhayet |
children.translated_text: One should also carry <s>kuṭila</s> (antimony), <s>vimala</s>, iron, and the essence of mica (<s>kha-sattva</s>);
tin-mica, or the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, with the addition of orpiment and <s>mākṣika</s>;
one should perform quenching with collections of white flowers combined with oil. (RA 8.72)
Thus have been described the silver-seeds; now hear about the coloring of the seeds. (RA 8.73)
Iron, <s>mākṣika</s>, and copper, and lead killed with quicksilver —
until it resembles cinnabar (<s>sindūra</s>) — with that, one should color the seeds. (RA 8.74)
Placing lead on a shallow pan (<s>kharpara</s>) together with the leaves of <s>brahmabīja</s> (castor),
burning it over fire placed below — when it attains fire-color — (RA 8.75)
with <s>vāsaka</s> (Malabar nut), <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia), <s>śāka</s> (teak), <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame tree), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick),
the flower of <s>koraṇḍaka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, and <s>arjuna</s> tree — (RA 8.76)
<s>ahimāra</s> (snake-killer plant), <s>nāginī</s>, <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>nāgakanyā</s>,
and <s>śilā</s> (realgar) in triple proportion — boiled in goat's water (<s>ajavāriṇā</s>) — (RA 8.77)

children.text: bhāvitaṃ kharparasthaṃ ca | plāvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: soaked [while] on the pan, flooding [it] repeatedly —
within seven days, it is killed, O one honored by the gods. (RA 8.78)
First, one should heat-treat with sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), then with sours.
This [preparation], for the coloring of the leaf-seeds [and] of the King of Mercury,
should be employed in opening (<s>udghāṭa</s>), stepping-up (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), and especially in solidification of the cake (<s>piṣṭī-stambha</s>). (RA 8.79)
Madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), <s>kiṃśuka</s> juice, catechu (<s>khadira</s>), red sandalwood,
oleander (<s>karavīra</s>), <s>devadāru</s> (deodar), <s>sarala</s> (pine), and the two types of turmeric (<s>rajanī-dvaya</s>) — (RA 8.80)
other red flowers as well — having ground [them] with lac juice,

children.text: tailaṃ vipācayed devi | tena bījāni rañjayet || (RA_8.81)
children.translated_text: one should cook the oil, O Goddess — with that, one should color the seeds. (RA 8.81)
In double [quantity of] red flowers and the collection of red-and-yellow [flowers],
a decoction four times [the quantity], milk [as the base], and oil — one [portion], O Goddess of the Gods. (RA 8.82)
Oil derived from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (staff tree), <s>karañja</s> (Indian beech), and bitter gourd (<s>kaṭu-tumbī</s>),
combined with the juice of <s>pāṭalī</s> (trumpet flower), long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>), and <s>kāma-kākatuṇḍī</s> — (RA 8.83)
with the fat of frog, pig, ram, snake, fish, tortoise, and leech —
combined individually, in one-sixteenth proportions, well-ground — (RA 8.84)
with <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry), <s>mākṣīka</s>, and the combining herbs of the pair (<s>dvaṃdva-melāpana</s>) —
cooked and filtered — this is called the extracting oil (<s>sāraṇā-taila</s>). (RA 8.85)

children.text: rasatulyaṃ yathā bījaṃ | gataṃ garbhadrutiṃ priye |
children.translated_text: When the seed, equal to the mercury, has entered into the interior fluid (<s>garbha-druti</s>), O Beloved,
all [ingredients] are desired in equal parts by [their] pervading capacity. (RA 8.86)

children.text:
pakvaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ samaṃ garbhe | yaddravedrañjayec ca tam ||
                    (RA_8.87)
children.translated_text: When well-cooked, [it is] the best, uniform in the interior; whatever melts should be colored with it. (RA 8.87)
The seeds thus described should be digested (<s>jārayet</s>) by means of the auxiliary (<s>viḍa</s>).

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_8.88)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 8.88)
9. [Description of the Auxiliaries (<s>Viḍas</s>)
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: bījānāṃ kalanaṃ proktaṃ | viśeṣeṇa ca sādhanam |
children.translated_text: The preparation of the seeds has been described, and especially their accomplishment;

children.text: jāryante tāni yaiḥ sūte | tān viḍān vaktumarhasi || (RA_9.1)
children.translated_text: tell me about those <s>viḍas</s> (auxiliary preparations) by which they are digested in mercury. (RA 9.1)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>sauvīra</s> (a salt), the three pungents (<s>vyoṣa</s>), sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>),
<s>sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt), <s>sarjikā</s> (soda ash), and that produced from the nectar of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) —
sprinkled with the juice of <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root — this <s>viḍa</s> is the universal digestive (<s>sarva-jāraṇa</s>). (RA 9.2)
Calcined conch-shell powder, saturated a hundred times with the milk of <s>ravi</s> (crown-flower / <s>arka</s>),
and heated in cycles many times, O Goddess — is an excellent digestive <s>viḍa</s>. (RA 9.3)

children.text:
śataśo vā plutaṃ cūrṇaṃ | gandhakasya gavāṃ jalaiḥ ||
                    (RA_9.4)
children.translated_text: Or, sulfur powder saturated a hundred times with cow's water (<s>gavāṃ jala</s> = cow urine). (RA 9.4)
Calcined conch-shell powder, soaked with <s>śigru</s>-root water,
combined a hundred times with <s>viṣa</s> (aconite) and <s>sindhūttha</s> (a salt) — [this is called] <s>vaḍavā-mukha</s> (submarine-fire [<s>viḍa</s>]). (RA 9.5)
Borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), O Goddess, should be saturated a hundred times with <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-tree) juice.
This <s>viḍa</s> called '<s>Vahnimukha</s>' (fire-mouth) [is used] in the digestion of metals, O Beloved. (RA 9.6)

children.text: cūlikā gandhapāṣāṇaḥ | kāntasya ca mukhaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: <s>Cūlikā</s> (a preparation), <s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s> (fragrant stone), and the face-powder of <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), O Beloved —
each one alone is sufficient for the digestion of metal powder. (RA 9.7)
<s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>sindhūttha</s>, <s>cūlī</s>, borax, and <s>bhūkhaga</s> (earthworm) —

children.text: kṣārairmūtraiś ca vipaced | ayaṃ jvālāmukho viḍaḥ || (RA_9.8)
children.translated_text: cook [these] with alkalis and urines — this is the <s>viḍa</s> [called] '<s>Jvālāmukha</s>' (flame-mouth). (RA 9.8)
Alkali of <s>nicula</s> (barringtonia), saturated twenty-one times with the leaf-juice of <s>devadālī</s> —
[this] digests all metallic essences. (RA 9.9)
<s>Vāstuka</s> (lamb's quarters), egg-[plant], banana, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>punarnava</s> (spreading hogweed),
<s>vāsā</s> (Malabar nut), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), <s>nicula</s>, <s>tilaka</s> (sesame), gold, and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — (RA 9.10)
all parts, cut into pieces — not too dry — on a stone slab,

children.text:
dagdhakāṇḍais tilānāṃ tu | pañcāṅgaṃ mūlakasya ca ||
                    (RA_9.11)
children.translated_text: with burnt stalks of sesame, and the five parts of radish — (RA 9.11)
flood [these] with the group of urines; the liquid filtered from that
should be cooked in an iron vessel, in a distillation apparatus, by the <s>haṃsa-pāka</s> method — by one who knows the degrees of fire. (RA 9.12)
When the abundant rising of steam and bubbles [occurs],
then [add] green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum), the three alkalis, and the three pungents, (RA 9.13)

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca sitaṃ hiṅgu- | lavaṇāni ca ṣaṭ tathā |
children.translated_text: sulfur, white <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and also the six salts.
One should add the powder of these [while the liquid is] enclosed between two iron plates.

children.text:
saptāhaṃ bhūgataḥ paścād | dhānyasthaḥ pravaro viḍaḥ ||
                    (RA_9.14)
children.translated_text: Buried underground for seven days, then stored in grain — [this is] the supreme <s>viḍa</s>. (RA 9.14)
Cooking with citron-sour and with <s>śigru</s>-root juice;
<s>cūlikā</s> and sulfur sprinkled [on top] — these two <s>viḍas</s>, [prepared] a hundred times in sequence. (RA 9.15)
With the leaf-juice of <s>koṣātakī</s> (sponge gourd), or alkalis from <s>nicula</s> (barringtonia),
<s>devadālī</s>, <s>śiva</s>-seed, <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), rock salt, and borax —
saturated with the group of sours — this <s>viḍa</s> is the gold-digestive (<s>hema-jāraṇa</s>). (RA 9.16)
With the alkalis of radish, ginger, and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), filtered through cow's urine —
sulfur should be saturated a hundred times — this <s>viḍa</s> [is used] in gold-digestion. (RA 9.17)
Orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), alkali, salt, conch-shell, and oyster-shell —
cooked by the <s>haṃsa-pāka</s> method — this <s>viḍa</s> is for gold-digestion. (RA 9.18)
Having thus gathered the materials, one should perform the mercury-work.

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_9.19)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 9.19)
10. [Purification of Mercury
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: rasasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃvā | rasakarma ca kīdṛśam |
children.translated_text: What are the characteristics of mercury? And what is the nature of mercury-work?
I do not know that, O Lord of the Gods — please describe it truly. (RA 10.1)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
The origin of mercury has been previously described; now hear its characteristics. (RA 10.2)
Its names number thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds of millions.

children.text:
śakyate na mayā vaktuṃ | saṃkṣepāt kathyate śṛṇu ||
                    (RA_10.3)
children.translated_text: I am unable to enumerate [them all]; hear them described in brief. (RA 10.3)

children.text: raso rasendraḥ sūtaś ca | pāradaścātha miśrakaḥ || (RA_10.4)
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, <s>Rasendra</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Pārada</s>, and also <s>Miśraka</s>. (RA 10.4)
One should know the [mercury from a] <s>siddha-kṣetra</s> (accomplished field) as '<s>rasa</s>' — the accomplished mercury.

children.text: nāśayet sakalān rogān | valīpalitam eva saḥ || (RA_10.5)
children.translated_text: It destroys all diseases, and [cures] wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 10.5)
Now hear about <s>Rasendra</s> — pure, the transformer of body and metal;

children.text: śarīre hemni kartā ca | jāraṇe sāraṇāsu ca || (RA_10.6)
children.translated_text: an agent [of transformation] in the body and in gold, [useful] in digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) and extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>) processes. (RA 10.6)

children.text: īṣatpītaś ca rūkṣāṅgo | doṣayuktaś ca sūtakaḥ || (RA_10.7)
children.translated_text: Slightly yellowish, with a rough body, and endowed with defects — that is <s>Sūtaka</s>. (RA 10.7)
That which is white both externally and internally, extensively covered with a film (<s>kañcuka</s>) —

children.text:
taṃ vidyāt pāradaṃ devi | tārakarmaṇi yojayet ||
                    (RA_10.8:1)
children.translated_text: know that as <s>Pārada</s>, O Goddess — it should be employed in silver-work. (RA 10.8a)
Just as a milk-vessel is ruined by the contact of fermented gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),

children.text: tathā hema śarīraṃ ca | pāradena vinaśyati || (RA_10.8:2)
children.translated_text: so gold and the body are ruined by <s>pārada</s>. (RA 10.8b)
That which has the luster of a peacock's feather — the wise know it as <s>Miśraka</s> (mixed [mercury]).
Seeing mercury of smoky color, it is especially recognized;
one should know <s>Miśraka</s> as the agent of the raising-up (<s>udvāha</s>) operation. (RA 10.9)
Thus, O Goddess, the five varieties of mercury have been determined. (RA 10.10)

children.text: svedanaṃ mardanaṃ caiva | cāraṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Steaming (<s>svedana</s>), grinding (<s>mardana</s>), propelling (<s>cāraṇa</s>), digesting (<s>jāraṇa</s>),

children.text: drāvaṇaṃ rañjanaṃ caiva | sāraṇaṃ krāmaṇaṃ kramāt |
children.translated_text: liquefying (<s>drāvaṇa</s>), coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), extracting (<s>sāraṇa</s>), and stepping-up (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) — in sequence:

children.text:
iti yo vetti tattvena | tasya sidhyati sūtakaḥ ||
                    (RA_10.11)
children.translated_text: one who knows these truly — for him, mercury is accomplished. (RA 10.11)

children.text: tīvratvaṃ jāyate svedāt | amalatvaṃ ca mardanāt |
children.translated_text: From steaming arises intensity; from grinding, purity;
from propelling, strength is produced; from digesting, binding occurs. (RA 10.12)
From liquefying, oneness [with the metal]; from red-coloring (<s>rakta-kāñjana</s>), redness;
from extracting, pervading capacity; from stepping-up, the stepping-up [quality]. (RA 10.13)
Impurity-ridden, in the form of impurity — [mercury], if hastened, attains the <s>haṃsa</s>-course (volatile ascent).
Impurity-ridden, in the form of impurity — smoky, it attains the smoke-course. (RA 10.14)
Another is the living course (<s>jīva-gati</s>), O Goddess — the living [mercury] emerges as if from an egg.

children.text: sa tāvajjīvayejjīvaṃ | tena jīvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ || (RA_10.15)
children.translated_text: It enlivens the living [body] for that long — hence mercury is called '<s>jīva</s>' (living). (RA 10.15)
Its fourfold course is obtained by the skilled [practitioner];

children.text: catasro gatayo dṛśyā | adṛśyā pañcamī gatiḥ || (RA_10.16)
children.translated_text: the four courses are visible; the fifth course is invisible. (RA 10.16)
by <s>mantra</s>-recitation, meditation, and the like, its fifth motion is destroyed. (RA 10.17)
Smoke (<s>dhūma</s>), crackling (<s>ciṭiciṭi</s>), frog-leap (<s>maṇḍūkapluti</s>),

children.text:
akampaś ca vikampaś ca | pañcāvasthā rasasya tu ||
                    (RA_10.18)
children.translated_text: steadiness (<s>akampa</s>), and trembling (<s>vikampa</s>) — these are the five states of mercury. (RA 10.18)
When churned with paste, three motions arise:
water-motion (<s>jalagati</s>), impurity-motion (<s>malagati</s>), and then swan-motion (<s>haṃsagati</s>). (RA 10.19)

children.text: hema dattvā tataḥ śuddhaṃ | tat tu stambhen niyāmake |
children.translated_text: Then, having added gold, the purified [mercury] should be [placed] in the restraining apparatus (<s>niyāmaka</s>);
with the restraining group of herbs, having added the mercury, one should cook [it]. (RA 10.20)

children.text: niyamito na prayāti | tathā dhūmagatiṃ śive || (RA_10.21)
children.translated_text: Once restrained, it does not go into smoke-motion, O <s>Śiva</s> (Goddess). (RA 10.21)
Free from granule-movement, devoid of bubbles,
the restrained [mercury] becomes capable of withstanding crucible-fire as well. (RA 10.22)
When one heats unrestrained mercury in a vessel of sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),

children.text:
jāyate niścitaṃ bhadre | tadā tasya gatitrayam ||
                    (RA_10.23)
children.translated_text: then certainly, O auspicious one, three motions arise in it. (RA 10.23)
By swing-steaming (<s>dolāsveda</s>), necessarily steamed for three days,
with <s>vasubhaṇṭā</s> and other [herbs], O Goddess, the king of mercury is not diminished. (RA 10.24)

children.text: akṣīṇaṃ tu rasaṃ dṛṣṭvā | dadyādvyomādikaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing that the mercury is undiminished, one should then add <s>vyoma</s> (mica) and the like;

children.text:
svedanaṃ ca tataḥ karma | dīyamānasya mardanam ||
                    (RA_10.25)
children.translated_text: then steaming, and the process of grinding while [substances are] being added. (RA 10.25)
The food embraced by mercury is called a pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>);
that [pellet], when liquefied within the womb of mercury, is called <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion). (RA 10.26)
That is called <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion) — and thus it is observed.
At the end of digestion, coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) should be performed with the group of red substances. (RA 10.27)

children.text: jīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ tu saṃraktaṃ | samahemnā tu sārayet |
children.translated_text: What has been digested again and again and made red, should be extracted (<s>sārayet</s>) with gold;
by means of the extraction-apparatus (<s>sāraṇāyantra</s>), the extracted mercury becomes bound (<s>baddha</s>). (RA 10.28)
Having been extracted again and again, the mercury becomes such [that]

children.text: krāmaṇena samāyuktaṃ | taṃ ca vedhe niyojayet || (RA_10.29)
children.translated_text: when endowed with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmuting power), it should be employed for <s>vedha</s> (transmutation). (RA 10.29)

children.text: āroṭaḥ pārado brahmā | mūrchitas tu janārdanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Mercury in the <s>āroṭa</s> state is <s>Brahmā</s>; when mūrchita (swooned/solidified), it is <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>);
when bound (<s>baddha</s>), it assumes the form of <s>Rudra</s> — [such is] mercury by the power of <s>karmayoga</s> (alchemical practice). (RA 10.30)
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the details of <s>karmayoga</s> (alchemical practice). (RA 10.31)

children.text: pāradasya trayo doṣā | viṣaṃ vahnirmalas tathā |
children.translated_text: Mercury has three defects: poison (<s>viṣa</s>), fire (<s>vahni</s>), and impurity (<s>mala</s>).

children.text: viṣeṇa saviṣaṃ vidyāt | vahnau kuṣṭhī bhavennaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Through poison, one should know [mercury as] poisonous; through fire, a man becomes leprous;
through impurity, one gets abdominal disease; and [mercury with these defects] causes death in <s>rasāyana</s> [practice]. (RA 10.32)

children.text: ṣaṭtruṭyaścaikalikṣā syāt | ṣaḍlikṣā yūka eva ca |
children.translated_text: Six <s>truṭis</s> make one <s>likṣā</s>; six <s>likṣās</s> make one <s>yūka</s>;
six <s>yūkas</s> are called a <s>rajas</s> — thus have [the measures] been told to you, O virtuous one. (RA 10.33)

children.text: ṣaḍrajaḥ sarṣapaḥ sākṣāt | siddhārthaḥ sa ca kīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Six <s>rajas</s> equal one <s>sarṣapa</s> (mustard seed), which is also called <s>siddhārtha</s>;
six <s>siddhārthas</s>, O Queen of the Gods, are declared to be one <s>yava</s> (barley grain). (RA 10.34)
Six <s>yavas</s> make one <s>guñjā</s> (berry); six <s>guñjās</s> make one <s>māṣaka</s>;

children.text:
māṣā dvādaśa tolaḥ syāt | aṣṭau tolāḥ palaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_10.35)
children.translated_text: twelve <s>māṣas</s> make one <s>tola</s>; eight <s>tolas</s> make one <s>pala</s>. (RA 10.35)
Thirty-two <s>palas</s>, O Goddess, are declared to be one <s>śubha</s> (an auspicious [measure]);

children.text:
śubhasya tu sahasre dve | bhāra ekaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
                    (RA_10.36)
children.translated_text: two thousand <s>śubhas</s> are declared to be one <s>bhāra</s> (load). (RA 10.36)

children.text: dve sahasre palānāṃ tu | sahasraṃ śatameva vā |
children.translated_text: Two thousand <s>palas</s>, or [alternatively] a hundred, or a thousand,

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśat palānāṃ tu | daśa pañcakameva vā || (RA_10.37)
children.translated_text: or twenty-eight <s>palas</s>, or ten, or five — (RA 10.37)
with half a <s>pala</s> itself, the processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of mercury should be performed. (RA 10.38)
<s>Mahābalā</s>, <s>Nāgabalā</s>, <s>Meghanādā</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>,
<s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s> — with their essences, combined with <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac),
the mercury, O Queen of Gods, should be steamed for three days. (RA 10.39)
<s>Girikarṇī</s>, <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, <s>Sahadevī</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>,
<s>Uragā</s>, <s>Triphalā</s>, <s>Kāntā</s>, <s>Laghuparṇī</s>, <s>Śatāvarī</s> — (RA 10.40)

children.text: tuṣavarje tu dhānyāmle | sarvaṃ saṃkṣubhya nikṣipet |
children.translated_text: all [these] should be agitated and placed in sour grain-water (<s>dhānyāmla</s>) free from husks;
[mercury] in eleven parts of that sour [liquid], ground with a sixteenth part [of herbs]. (RA 10.41)
With <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), salt, <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents),
<s>citraka</s>, ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), and radish (<s>mūlaka</s>), one should steam [mercury] in a swing-apparatus, O Goddess, for three days over gentle fire. (RA 10.42)

children.text: aṅkolas tu viṣaṃ hanti | vahnimāragvadhaḥ priye |
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅkola</s> destroys the poison; <s>āragvadha</s> (cassia) [destroys] the fire, O beloved;

children.text:
citrakas tu malaṃ hanyāt | kumārī saptakañcukam ||
                    (RA_10.43)
children.translated_text: <s>citraka</s> destroys the impurity, and <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) [removes] the seven sheaths. (RA 10.43)

children.text:
tasmād ebhiḥ samopetair | mardayet pātayed budhaḥ ||
                    (RA_10.44)
children.translated_text: Therefore, endowed with all these, the wise one should grind and precipitate [the mercury]. (RA 10.44)
With the <s>vidyādhara</s>-apparatus, one should process [it] until free from defects;
then, placed in a triple-layered cloth, that mercury, O Goddess, [should be] filtered. (RA 10.45)
Because of having <s>triphalā</s> and <s>vahni</s>-root (leadwort), combined with the juice of <s>gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe),

children.text: nirudgāre tu pāṣāṇe | mardayet pātayet punaḥ || (RA_10.46)
children.translated_text: one should grind and precipitate [mercury] again on a non-porous stone. (RA 10.46)
With <s>dhūmasāra</s> (sublimate of smoke), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents),
<s>rajanī</s> (turmeric), <s>sita</s> (sugar), and mustard seeds,
with brick [powder], sour gruel, and <s>ūrṇā</s> (wool), one should grind for three days — then the mercury becomes free from impurity, manifesting my power. (RA 10.47-48)
With <s>vāsaka</s> (Malabar nut) and <s>vibhīta</s> (marking nut), one should grind and precipitate again;
the defects arising from lead (<s>nāga</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and the like — those adventitious defects — are destroyed. (RA 10.49)
Seven times with <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), one should grind [it] until freed from defects;
precipitating seven times, the mercury sheds its mountain-born defect (<s>giridoṣa</s>). (RA 10.50)
The mercury sheds its field-born defect (<s>kṣetradoṣa</s>), O Goddess, when processed with <s>gokarṇa</s> juice. (RA 10.51)
Steamed in the juice of cotton (<s>kārpāsa</s>) leaves with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>),
the mercury becomes freed from [its] seven sheaths after seven days. (RA 10.52)
<s>Kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Gāṅgerī</s>, red <s>citraka</s>,
<s>Maṇḍūkī</s>, <s>Mudgaparṇī</s>, ginger (<s>śṛṅgavera</s>), <s>rasāṅkuśa</s>, (RA 10.53)
<s>Devadālī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>Kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>Śatāvarī</s>,
<s>Kumārī</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>Grīṣmasundara</s>, (RA 10.54)
<s>Śūlinī</s>, <s>Śūrpaparṇī</s>, <s>Gojihvā</s>, <s>Kṣīrakañcuka</s> —

children.text:
tadrasair marditaḥ pātyaḥ | saptadhā nirmalo bhavet ||
                    (RA_10.55)
children.translated_text: ground with their juices and precipitated seven times, [the mercury] becomes free from impurity. (RA 10.55)
Having made a pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) with copper, one should precipitate [it] by upward distillation (<s>ūrdhvapātana</s>);
abandoning tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and lead (<s>nāga</s>), the mercury becomes purified. (RA 10.56)
Ground with <s>triphalā</s>, drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), mustard (<s>rājikā</s>), <s>paṭu</s> (sharp substances), and <s>citraka</s>,
placed in the upper vessel, it should be heated with blazing coals below. (RA 10.57)
By blocking the moisture-outlet (<s>sṛṣṭyambuja</s>), the mercury is mostly recovered.
Combined with [the juices of] <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>bimbī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and lotus (<s>ambuja</s>), (RA 10.58)

children.text: rasaṃ niyāmake dadyāt | tejasvī nirmalo bhavet |
children.translated_text: the mercury, placed in the restraining apparatus (<s>niyāmaka</s>), becomes lustrous and free from impurity.
Thus purified, the mercury, dried with one-eighth [its weight of] <s>bhadrā</s> (turmeric), (RA 10.59)
with small sour [substances], salt, alkali, <s>bhūkhaga</s> (earthworm?),
cow urine, drumstick (<s>śigru</s>),

mustard (<s>rājikā</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), steamed in sour rice-water (<s>āranāla</s>) for three days — the mercury is ignited (<s>dīpita</s>), O Goddess, and becomes hungry for food (<s>grāsa</s>). (RA 10.60)
<s>Vyoma</s>-essence (mica-essence) and other seed-substances — [these are] for the purification and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of mercury.

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_10.61)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 10.61)
11. [<s>Bālajāraṇā</s> — Preliminary Digestion
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ śodhanaṃ caiva | pāradasya śrutaṃ mayā |
children.translated_text: The characteristics and purification of mercury have been heard by me;
I wish to hear about <s>cāraṇa</s> (mobile application) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), O <s>Bhairava</s>. (RA 11.1)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said:
When all sins are destroyed, the [ability for] <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion) of mercury is obtained;
upon obtaining that, the <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge) which is the cause of <s>mukti</s> (liberation) is as good as obtained. (RA 11.2)
<s>Jāraṇa</s> (digestion) is the revealer of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) for the practitioner, O Goddess;

children.text: yāvanna jāryate sūtaḥ | tāvat tu na ca nirvṛtiḥ || (RA_11.3)
children.translated_text: as long as mercury is not digested (<s>jārya</s>), so long there is no bliss (<s>nirvṛti</s>). (RA 11.3)

children.text: khallas tu pīṭhikā devi | rasendro liṅgamucyate |
children.translated_text: The mortar (<s>khalla</s>) is the seat (<s>pīṭhikā</s>), O Goddess; the king of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) is the <s>liṅga</s>;

children.text: mardanaṃ vandanaṃ tasya | grāsaḥ pūjā vidhīyate || (RA_11.4)
children.translated_text: grinding is its worship (<s>vandana</s>); the food (<s>grāsa</s>) is the offering (<s>pūjā</s>) — thus it is ordained. (RA 11.4)

children.text: yāvad dināni vahnistho | jāryate dhāryate rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: For as many days as the mercury is kept on fire and digested,
for that many thousands of <s>yugas</s> one is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>. (RA 11.5)
He who gives fire to the king of mercury for even a single day —

children.text: dravanti tasya pāpāni | kurvannapi na lipyate || (RA_11.6)
children.translated_text: his sins melt away; even while acting, he is not tainted. (RA 11.6)
<s>Jāraṇā</s> (digestion) is twofold: <s>bālajāraṇā</s> (preliminary digestion) and <s>baddhajāraṇā</s> (bound digestion).
Of these, first, O Supreme Goddess, <s>bālajāraṇā</s> will be described. (RA 11.7)
One should first digest <s>gagana</s> (mica); then all [other] mineral-essences (<s>sattva</s>);
then purified <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite); and then gold. (RA 11.8)

children.text: garbhasthaṃ drāvayitvā tu | tato bāhyadrutiṃ dravet |
children.translated_text: Having liquefied [the substance] within the interior (<s>garbha</s>), then one should liquefy the external fluid (<s>bāhyadruti</s>);

children.text: sitaṃ sitena dravyeṇa | raktaṃ raktena rañjayet || (RA_11.9)
children.translated_text: the white [mercury] should be colored with a white substance; the red, with a red one. (RA 11.9)

children.text:
sāraṇaṃ krāmaṇaṃ jñātvā | tato vedhaṃ prayojayet ||
                    (RA_11.10)
children.translated_text: Having learned extraction (<s>sāraṇa</s>) and transmuting application (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), then one should employ <s>vedha</s> (transmutation). (RA 11.10)

children.text: oṃ namo 'mṛtalohāya parāmṛtarasodbhavāya huṃ svāhā || Ras_11.11 ||
children.translated_text: Oṁ, salutation to the immortal metal, born from the supreme nectar — <s>Huṃ Svāhā</s>. (RA 11.11)
For the benefit of all beings, O Lord, with your permission,

children.text:
jāraṇaṃ kartumicchāmi | grāsaṃ gṛhṇa mama prabho ||
                    (RA_11.12)
children.translated_text: I wish to perform <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) — accept [this] food (<s>grāsa</s>), O Master. (RA 11.12)
'Proceed' — thus said by <s>Śiva</s>, [the sign] should indeed be taken by the wise one. (RA 11.13)
Listen, O Goddess, I shall describe the excellent digestion of <s>vyoma</s> (mica).
That is twofold: digestion of leaf-mica (<s>pattrābhrajāraṇa</s>) and digestion of [mica-]essence (<s>sattvajāraṇa</s>). (RA 11.14)
Without-mouth (<s>nirmukha</s>), with-mouth (<s>samukha</s>), and flavoring-mouth (<s>vāsanāmukha</s>) —

children.text:
ekaikaṃ trividhaṃ tac ca | tad vakṣyāmy ānupūrvaśaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.15)
children.translated_text: each of these is threefold. I shall describe them in order. (RA 11.15)
By contact with <s>vaikrānta</s>-diamond or by the power of divine herbs,

children.text:
nirmukho bhakṣayed devi | kṣaṇena gaganaṃ rasaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.16)
children.translated_text: by the mouthless [method], mercury devours <s>gagana</s> (mica) in an instant, O Goddess. (RA 11.16)

children.text: hemakarmaṇi hemaiva | tāre tāro mukhaṃ bhavet || (RA_11.17)
children.translated_text: In gold-work, gold is the mouth (<s>mukha</s>); in silver-[work], silver becomes the mouth. (RA 11.17)
A pellet (<s>piṣṭi</s>) made in a heated mortar (<s>taptakhalla</s>), [with] mica finely [ground] in small quantities,
[processed] with [the juices of] <s>amlavetasa</s> (sour tamarind), citron (<s>jambīra</s>), <s>bījapūra</s>,
sour <s>bhūkhaga</s> — ground [thus], it moves (is digested), O Goddess — this is the with-mouth (<s>samukha</s>) digestion. (RA 11.18)
Three alkalis (<s>kṣāratraya</s>), five sharp [substances] (<s>pañcapaṭu</s>), <s>kākṣī</s>, green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>),
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), combined with sour [liquid] — one should digest [them] in a copper vessel. (RA 11.19)
This divine [preparation], having been produced by pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>), the discerning one [should use]

children.text:
jāraṇārthaṃ ca bījānāṃ | vajrāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ||
                    (RA_11.20)
children.translated_text: for the purpose of digesting seed-substances (<s>bīja</s>) and diamonds (<s>vajra</s>) in particular. (RA 11.20)
In that [preparation], lead (<s>nāga</s>) or tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), O one honored by the gods,
should be quenched a hundred times — [but this preparation is] not [to be used] in <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir-making). (RA 11.21)

children.text: anena sakalaṃ devi | cāraṇāvas tu bhāvayet |
children.translated_text: With this, one should process all <s>cāraṇā</s> operations, O Goddess.

children.text:
kṣārāmle bhāvitaṃ vyoma | rajasā prathamena ca ||
                    (RA_11.22)
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>vyoma</s>), treated (<s>bhāvita</s>) with alkaline sour [liquid] and with the first <s>rajas</s> (menstrual blood / mineral powder), (RA 11.22)
ground with the drops (<s>kaṇā</s>) of the three-creation water (<s>sṛṣṭitraya-udaka</s>) and <s>tumburu</s> juice,
should be made to move [i.e. digested] or alternatively smelted in a heating-cycle with barley and tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) juice. (RA 11.23)
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Gadā</s>, <s>Rambhā</s> (plantain), <s>Meghanādā</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>,

children.text:
śigruko yavaciñcā ca | bhāvitaṃ tadrasaiḥ kramāt ||
                    (RA_11.24)
children.translated_text: drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), and <s>yavaciñcā</s> — [mica should be] treated (<s>bhāvita</s>) with their juices in sequence. (RA 11.24)
The root of <s>Hilamucā</s>, and the root of <s>Kauverī</s>,
plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), <s>Musalī</s>, drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), betel (<s>tāmbūlī</s>), bamboo (<s>vāṇa</s>), <s>Pīluka</s>, (RA 11.25)
<s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>Balā</s>, jujube (<s>kola</s>), <s>Āsphoṭa</s>, <s>Kharamañjarī</s>,
<s>Tumburu</s>, or bitter greens (<s>tiktaśāka</s>) — with the juice of any one of these,
combined with mustard (<s>rājikā</s>) and the three pungents (<s>vyoṣa</s>), mica should be steamed for three days. (RA 11.26)
Combined with green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), <s>tuvarī</s>, rock salt (<s>sindhu</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>),
By the previously described consecration method (<s>abhiṣavayoga</s>), mercury moves [i.e., becomes active] instantly. (RA 11.27)
It quickly becomes a globule (<s>golaka</s>), bestowing all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments). (RA 11.28)
Taking fermented grain-acid (<s>dhānyāmla</s>), O Goddess, combined with the acid group,
having boiled mica (<s>abhraka</s>) [therein], one should grind it with <s>snuhī</s> (cactus) milk. (RA 11.29)
Then, with wild cow dung, [give it] a dove-[grade] firing (<s>kapotapuṭa</s>). (RA 11.30)
With the exudate of banana tuber and with radish juice,
<s>Kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, <s>Apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower), and <s>Muni</s> (agati), (RA 11.31)
castor plant (<s>Eraṇḍa</s>), fresh ginger (<s>Ārdraka</s>), <s>Meghanāda</s> (thunder-plant), and <s>Punarnavā</s> (spreading hogweed) —
with the juice of each one separately, one should give one firing each. (RA 11.32)
Combined with <s>vajrī</s> (euphorbia) milk, one should cook it in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>).
Then, having dried it in the shade, combined with gram-acid (<s>caṇakāmla</s>), (RA 11.33)

children.text: navasāraṃ ca kāsīsaṃ | vacāṃ nimbaṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: sal ammoniac (<s>navasāra</s>), green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), and <s>nimba</s> (neem) likewise —
each in one-sixteenth proportion to the mica — one should add. (RA 11.34)

children.text: nidhāya tāmrapātre tu | gharṣayet tac ca suvrate |
children.translated_text: Placing [the mixture] in a copper vessel, one should grind it, O virtuous one.

children.text: navavāraṃ tato devi | lohapātre tu jārayet || (RA_11.35)
children.translated_text: Nine times, O Goddess, one should then calcine it in an iron vessel. (RA 11.35)
Together with mercury, O Goddess, [and] sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) with gram-acid,
it should be decocted on a mild fire — it is accomplished in half a <s>prahara</s> (1.5 hours). (RA 11.36)
Having ground it with <s>Somavallī</s> (moon-creeper) juice, the mica combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt),

children.text:
śanaiḥ śanair haṃsapādyā | dāpayec ca puṭatrayam ||
                    (RA_11.37)
children.translated_text: gradually, with <s>Haṃsapādī</s> [plant], one should give three firings. (RA 11.37)
With <s>Somavallī</s> juice itself, one should give seven firings.

children.text: pātayen mṛnmaye bhāṇḍe | rasena saha saṃyutam || (RA_11.38)
children.translated_text: One should make [the mica] fall [i.e., calcine it] in an earthen vessel, combined with mercury. (RA 11.38)
The root of <s>Siteṣupuṅkhā</s> [plant] — one should grind it with cow's milk.

children.text:
kalkena lepayet sūtaṃ | gaganaṃ ca tadūrdhvagam ||
                    (RA_11.39)
children.translated_text: With the paste, one should coat the mercury, and the mica [placed] above it. (RA 11.39)
Heating by sun-heat, the [mica], without opening [the vessel], is swallowed [by the mercury] instantly.

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ | nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || (RA_11.40)
children.translated_text: A cake (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) is quickly formed — there should be no doubt about this. (RA 11.40)
With <s>Tilaparṇī</s> (sesame-leaf plant) juice alone, one should treat the mica, O beloved.
By grinding, a cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>) is formed — there should be no doubt about this. (RA 11.41)
One should repeatedly pour lead (<s>nāga</s>) into the exudate of <s>Muṇḍī</s> [plant].

children.text:
tenābhrakaṃ tu saṃplāvya | bhūyobhūyaḥ puṭe dahet ||
                    (RA_11.42)
children.translated_text: Then, flooding the mica with that, one should burn it in successive firings. (RA 11.42)
With the [juices of] <s>Citraka</s> (leadwort) and fresh ginger roots, each separately seven times,
the powder of sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) and mica (<s>abhraka</s>) should be carefully flooded. (RA 11.43)
Treated with <s>Nāgaśuṇḍī</s> juice, breast milk, menstrual blood, and <s>Luṅga</s>-acid,
wrapped [in mica] at one-sixteenth proportion, the mercury should be processed in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolā</s>). (RA 11.44)
In sixty-four-fold proportion, O Goddess, or in thirty-two-fold,
or in sixteen-fold, or likewise in eight-fold,

children.text:
caturguṇaṃ vā dviguṇaṃ | samaṃ vā cārayet priye ||
                    (RA_11.45)
children.translated_text: or four-fold, or two-fold, or equal proportion — one should process, O beloved. (RA 11.45)
Hear, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, the calcination of the supreme essence of mica. (RA 11.46)
The essence of mica (<s>vyomasattva</s>) in equal proportion, combined with the essence of pyrite (<s>tāpyasattva</s>) —
thus processed, O Goddess, the mercury becomes one that melts the interior (<s>garbhadrāvī</s>). (RA 11.47)
Lead-mica (<s>nāgābhra</s>), O Goddess, tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>), iron-mica (<s>tīkṣṇābhra</s>), sun-mica (<s>bhāskarābhra</s>),
silver-mica (<s>tārābhra</s>), O Goddess, gold-mica (<s>hemābhra</s>) — one should calcine [them all] with mercury-interior (<s>rasagarbha</s>). (RA 11.48)
By the previously described consecration method, [the mica] melts inside [the mercury] by grinding. (RA 11.49)
The first feeding (<s>grāsa</s>) is one-sixty-fourth; the second is one-thirty-second;

children.text:
tṛtīyaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśas tu | caturtho 'ṣṭāṃśa eva ca ||
                    (RA_11.50)
children.translated_text: the third is one-sixteenth; and the fourth is one-eighth. (RA 11.50)

children.text: pañcamas tu caturthāṃśaḥ | ṣaṣṭho dvyaṃśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The fifth is one-fourth; the sixth is declared to be one-half.
The feeding is to be given to the mercury — of mica together with its essence. (RA 11.51)
At the one-sixty-fourth feeding, the mercury becomes rod-like (<s>daṇḍadhārī</s>).
At the second feeding, [it becomes] like a leech, O Goddess. (RA 11.52)
With the third feeding, it becomes like crow's dung.
With the fourth feeding, it becomes like whey (<s>dadhimaṇḍa</s>). (RA 11.53)
When the fifth feeding is accomplished, it becomes like fresh butter (<s>navanīta</s>).
At the sixth, it takes a globular form — these are the signs of progressive digestion (<s>jīrṇa</s>). (RA 11.54)
Red mica, bathed a hundred times in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),
should be processed in a mortar, together with the coating of copper. (RA 11.55)

children.text: hema tāraṃ ca saṃghṛṣya | khalle tatra rasaṃ nyaset |
children.translated_text: Having rubbed gold and silver in the mortar, one should place the mercury there.
With <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) mixed with sour gruel and rock salt (<s>sindhu</s>) — the mercury processes [them]. (RA 11.56)

children.text: hema sīsaṃ tu saṃghṛṣya | rasaṃ tatra pradāpayet |
children.translated_text: Having rubbed gold and lead together, one should add the mercury.
Mica combined with lead and gold, when equally digested, becomes fluid.
It swiftly processes mica and subsidiary minerals through its mouth [i.e., by absorption]. (RA 11.57)

children.text: tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ ca saṃghṛṣya | rasaṃ tatra pradāpayet |
children.translated_text: Having rubbed silver and tin together, one should add the mercury.
Mica combined with lead and gold, when equally digested, becomes fluid.
It processes mica through its mouth — this is recommended for silver-making operations. (RA 11.58)

children.text:
samukhaṃ nirmukhaṃ vāpi | yatnataś cārayen nabhaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.59)
children.translated_text: Whether with opening (<s>samukha</s>) or without opening (<s>nirmukha</s>), one should carefully process the mica. (RA 11.59)
Having thus performed the threefold processing (<s>cāraṇā</s>), producing interior-melting (<s>garbhadruti</s>) in the mercury,
one should calcine, sweat, and pelletize the mass through the three stages of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). (RA 11.60)
Smeared with [a mixture of] sharp acids (<s>paṭvamla</s>), alkalies (<s>kṣāra</s>), cow's urine, and <s>snuhī</s> milk,

children.text: bahiś ca baddhaṃ vastreṇa | bhūyo grāsaṃ niveditam |
children.translated_text: bound externally in cloth, with another feeding offered,
it should be sweated in alkaline solutions, sour gruel, and oils over a mild fire. (RA 11.61)
By this method, O Goddess, it is calcined in three days.

children.text:
yantrād uddhṛtamātraṃ tu | lohapātre sthitaṃ rasam ||
                    (RA_11.62)
children.translated_text: As soon as it is removed from the apparatus, the mercury [is placed] in an iron vessel. (RA 11.62)
First washed with warm sour gruel and strained through cloth,
one should grind it in a vessel with a comfortably warm hand until [the impurities] are exhausted. (RA 11.63)

children.text: caturguṇena vastreṇa | pīḍito nirmalaś ca saḥ || (RA_11.64)
children.translated_text: Pressed through cloth folded four times, it becomes pure. (RA 11.64)
Through the straining process, when [impurities] exit from the feeding by pressing,
it becomes rod-like (<s>daṇḍadhārī</s>) — [this is] the mercury with digested feeding. (RA 11.65)

children.text: ajīrṇe pācayet piṣṭīṃ | svedayen mardayet tathā |
children.translated_text: If undigested, one should cook the cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>), sweat it, and grind it.
With the application of cane-acid (<s>vetasāmla</s>), when digested, one should give [the next] feeding. (RA 11.66)
With [powders of] brick, jaggery, burnt wool, indigo (<s>rājī</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), and smoke-born [substances],

children.text:
ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ sa dhānyāmlaiḥ | mardyaḥ svedyaś ca pāradaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.67)
children.translated_text: each in one-sixteenth proportion, with fermented grain-acid — the mercury should be ground and sweated. (RA 11.67)

children.text: nirmalīkaraṇārthaṃ tu | grāse grāse punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the purpose of purification, at each and every feeding,
when the mica is digested and the seed [metal] is digested, [the mercury] — now pure — takes on colors. (RA 11.68)
By this method, four feedings should be given in the swing-apparatus (<s>dolā</s>).
Then, with the tortoise-apparatus (<s>kacchapāyantra</s>), [comes] ignition and binding in sequence. (RA 11.69)
With one-eighth [proportion] of alkaline preparation (<s>viḍa</s>), applied above and below, one should calcine.
Mercury with equally digested mica becomes one that transmutes a hundred-fold, O beloved. (RA 11.70)
A thousand-fold transmuter with double [mica]; a ten-thousand-fold transmuter with triple.
A hundred-thousand-fold transmuter with quadruple — that mercury becomes an earth-rover (<s>bhūcara</s>). (RA 11.71)
When quintuple [mica] is digested, O Goddess, the mercury attains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
With sextuple, the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 11.72)
All defects of mercury, by sextuple mica
when digested, are destroyed — there should be no doubt about this. (RA 11.73)

children.text: rasarāje yadā jīrṇaṃ | ṣaḍguṇaṃ gaganaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: When sextuple mica is digested in the king of mercuries, O beloved,

children.text: tadā grasati lohāni | tyajec ca gatimātmanaḥ || (RA_11.74)
children.translated_text: then it devours metals and abandons its own mobility. (RA 11.74)
Smoke, crackling (<s>ciṭiciṭi</s>), frog-leap (<s>maṇḍūkapluti</s>),

children.text:
sakampaś ca vikampaś ca | pañcāvasthā rasasya tu ||
                    (RA_11.75)
children.translated_text: trembling (<s>sakampa</s>), and violent shaking (<s>vikampa</s>) — these are the five stages of mercury. (RA 11.75)
It becomes tawny (<s>kapila</s>), ceases to emit sparks,
and stands motionless in fire — these are the signs of [mercury with] digested mica. (RA 11.76)
With equally digested [mica], it is a 'child' (<s>bāla</s>); with fourfold, it is in 'youth' (<s>yauvana</s>).

children.text:
vṛddhas tu ṣaḍguṇaṃ jīrṇaḥ | kuryāt karma pṛthak pṛthak ||
                    (RA_11.77)
children.translated_text: With sextuple digested [mica], it is 'old' (<s>vṛddha</s>) — each performs different operations. (RA 11.77)
The 'child' [performs] by leaf-smearing (<s>pattralepa</s>); the 'youth' by paste-application (<s>kalkayoga</s>).
The 'old' one pierces metals — whether calcined (<s>jārita</s>) or processed (<s>sārita</s>). (RA 11.78)

children.text: kumāras tu raso devi | na samartho rasāyane |
children.translated_text: The 'boy' mercury, O Goddess, is not capable of rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>).

children.text: yauvanastho raso devi | kṣamo dehasya rakṣaṇe || (RA_11.79)
children.translated_text: The mercury in 'youth,' O Goddess, is capable of protecting the body. (RA 11.79)

children.text: jarāvastho raso yaś ca | dehe lohena saṃkramet |
children.translated_text: The mercury in 'old age' — that one enters the body along with metal.
In the absence of mica-essence, one should add magnetite-essence (<s>kāntasattva</s>). (RA 11.80)

children.text: kāntasya cāpyabhāve tu | tīkṣṇalohaṃ tu dāpayet |
children.translated_text: And in the absence of magnetite, one should add iron (<s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>).
By this sequential method, one should calcine all essences. (RA 11.81)
Even one [portion of mercury], combined with gold, instantly makes [base metals into] gold.
Among [all] mercuries, mineral essences, and subsidiary minerals, nothing surpasses sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>). (RA 11.82)
By the previously described apparatus-method, sixteen-fold sulfur,
or twelve-fold, or sextuple — one should calcine [it in mercury]. (RA 11.83)
Taking the essence of <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), one should calcine it in one-quarter proportion.
Then, all other essences too should be melted within the mercury-interior. (RA 11.84)
Gold and fire are friends; likewise gold and mercury.
Fire and mercury are enemies — through the friend of each, their friendship [is established]. (RA 11.85)

children.text: agniko yavaciñcā ca | vasuhaṭṭaś ca rāgiṇī |
children.translated_text: <s>Agnika</s> (fire-plant), <s>Yavaciñcā</s> (barley-tamarind), <s>Vasuhaṭṭa</s>, and <s>Rāgiṇī</s> —
cooked by swing-apparatus sweating (<s>dolāsveda</s>) — this is the best gold-calcination method. (RA 11.86)
<s>Palāśa</s> (butea) ash, <s>Apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower), barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>), sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),

children.text:
sauvarcalaṃ ca kāsīsaṃ | sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ tathā ||
                    (RA_11.87)
children.translated_text: black salt (<s>sauvarcala</s>), green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), (RA 11.87)
mustard (<s>āsurī</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), sal ammoniac (<s>navasāra</s>) likewise,
camphor (<s>karpūra</s>), and <s>Mākṣīka</s> (pyrite) — one should make these in equal portions. (RA 11.88)
With <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> (milkweed) milks, O Goddess, one should make a crucible-coating.

children.text:
viḍacūrṇaṃ tato dattvā | kanakaṃ jārayet priye ||
                    (RA_11.89)
children.translated_text: Then, adding alkaline powder (<s>viḍacūrṇa</s>), one should calcine the gold, O beloved. (RA 11.89)

children.text:
śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi | bhūcarākhyaṃ tu jāraṇam ||
                    (RA_11.90)
children.translated_text: Hear, O Goddess — I shall declare the calcination called 'earth-roving' (<s>bhūcara</s>). (RA 11.90)

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ pītaṃ raktamabhraṃ | śulve tīkṣṇe ca melayet ||
                    (RA_11.91)
children.translated_text: Black, yellow, and red mica — one should combine with copper and iron. (RA 11.91)

children.text: śulve tīkṣṇaṃ yadā cūrṇaṃ | dvāviṃśatiguṇaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: When iron powder [is combined] with copper in twenty-two-fold proportion, O beloved,

children.text:
gandhanāgaṃ tato 'rdhaṃ tu | krameṇaiva tu melayet ||
                    (RA_11.92)
children.translated_text: then half of that in sulfur-lead (<s>gandhanāga</s>) — one should combine progressively. (RA 11.92)

children.text: hemnā tu saha dātavyaṃ | sūtakaikena ṣoḍaśa |
children.translated_text: Together with gold, it should be given — for one [part] mercury, sixteen [parts total].

children.text: gandhanāgaṃ yadā jīrṇaṃ | tadā baddho bhavedrasaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the sulfur-lead is digested, then the mercury becomes bound (<s>baddha</s>).
When the gold is digested, with half that [proportion] of killed metal (<s>mṛtaloha</s>), one should color [it]. (RA 11.93)
Copper killed with sulfur, pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and iron —

children.text:
puṭena mārayec chuddhaṃ | hema dadyāt tu ṣaḍguṇam ||
                    (RA_11.94)
children.translated_text: one should kill by firing and give pure gold in sextuple [proportion]. (RA 11.94)

children.text: sūtake hemabījaṃ ca | yadā jīrṇaṃ caturguṇam |
children.translated_text: When four-fold gold-seed is digested in the mercury,
one should know it as having bound color (<s>baddharāga</s>) — the mercury becomes gold-hued. (RA 11.95)
[Place the mercury] in the extraction apparatus (<s>sāraṇāyantra</s>) and extract it together with that [substance];
having extracted one-third, calcine it again therein. (RA 11.96)
Calcined and extracted, then calcined and extracted again —
by the sevenfold chain procedure (<s>saptaśṛṅkhalikā</s>), the mercury becomes a <s>koṭi</s>-transmuter. (RA 11.97)

children.text: bhūcarī jāraṇā proktā | khecarīṃ jāraṇāṃ śṛṇu || (RA_11.98)
children.translated_text: The terrestrial (<s>bhūcarī</s>) calcination has been described; now hear the aerial (<s>khecarī</s>) calcination. (RA 11.98)
[Take] gems headed by diamond (<s>hīra</s>), made into mercury-residue;
the seeds of bitter gourd (<s>kaṭutumba</s>) — [add] half that amount. (RA 11.99)
This is called the great calcination (<s>mahājāraṇa</s>); the skilled practitioner should make a paste,
and in the mouth of a diamond crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>), he should place the mercury in its center. (RA 11.100)

children.text: katakaṃ kanakaṃ caivam | ekīkṛtya ca mardayet |
children.translated_text: Having made <s>kataka</s> and gold into one [mass] and ground it,

children.text:
padmarāgaṃ prayatnena | rase grāsaṃ tu dāpayet ||
                    (RA_11.101)
children.translated_text: he should carefully feed ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) as a morsel to the mercury. (RA 11.101)
Until eleven times the amount of ruby [is fed] into the mercury —
when the coloring [substance] is digested, O Queen of the Gods, the mercury takes on a <s>liṅga</s>-form. (RA 11.102)
It should be carefully protected with the eight world-guardians (<s>lokapālas</s>);
one-sixth of the king of mercury should be administered to each of them. (RA 11.103)
It should be consumed carefully, after bowing to the <s>guru</s> and the deity,
having saluted all the <s>Siddhas</s> and the deities especially. (RA 11.104)

children.text: mūrchāṅgadāhaś ca tato | jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Fainting (<s>mūrchā</s>), bodily burning, and the like then arise — there is no doubt;
[but] one sees oneself risen up, [possessed of] divine radiance and great strength. (RA 11.105)
Accompanied by the sounds of conches and kettledrums, together with <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
he wanders through the worlds at will, assuming any form, traveling in aerial vehicles (<s>vimāna</s>). (RA 11.106)

children.text:
devāś ca yatra līyante | siddhastatraiva līyate ||
                    (RA_11.107)
children.translated_text: Where the gods dissolve, the <s>Siddha</s> too dissolves there. (RA 11.107)
Now I shall describe another excellent calcination procedure. (RA 11.108)
Well-ground and purified mercury, freed from all defects,
[treated] with the juice of <s>śāka</s> tender leaves and with the juice of <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>; (RA 11.109)
sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), saturated with <s>palāśa</s> flower-water, in equal parts,

children.text:
samaṃ kṛṣṇābhrasattvaṃ ca | rasakaṃ cāṣṭakaṃ guṇam ||
                    (RA_11.110)
children.translated_text: equal [parts of] black mica essence, and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) in eightfold proportion; (RA 11.110)
iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), copper (<s>śulva</s>), and <s>uraga</s> [nāga/lead] — calcine with the tortoise apparatus (<s>kūrmāyantra</s>);
afterwards, calcine gold with the <s>viḍa</s> (flux) method, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 11.111)

children.text: tataḥ siddhaṃ vijānīyāt | dvaidhaṃ śulvasya dāpayet |
children.translated_text: Then one should know [the mercury] is accomplished; feed it half the copper;
according to the prescribed measure of the operation — lead becomes gold. (RA 11.112)
Hereafter I shall describe the excellent procedure of stepwise calcination. (RA 11.113)
Having soaked the seed-powders in oil repeatedly,
[give] a morsel at one-sixteenth [the amount], and grind gently with the finger. (RA 11.114)
Then, by the procedure with fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>) and the like, [the morsel] should be given at one-sixteenth;

children.text:
bhūrje dattvā tato deyaṃ | dolāyantre vinikṣipet ||
                    (RA_11.115)
children.translated_text: having placed [it] on birch bark (<s>bhūrja</s>), put [it] in the swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>). (RA 11.115)
Within a day and night, the mercury swallows that seed, O beloved;

children.text:
tamuddhṛtya rasaṃ devi | khalle saṃmardayet tataḥ ||
                    (RA_11.116)
children.translated_text: having extracted that mercury, O Goddess, grind it in a mortar. (RA 11.116)
Then, having placed [it] in the apparatus, [heat] with steady fire for a day and night;
having heated and extracted it from the apparatus, grind it in a heated mortar. (RA 11.117)

children.text: mardayitvābhrake piṇḍaṃ | kṣiptvā tatra puṭaṃ dadet |
children.translated_text: Having ground [it], throw the lump into mica and apply a firing (<s>puṭa</s>) therein;

children.text:
tato garbhe patatyāśu | jārayet tat sukhena tu ||
                    (RA_11.118)
children.translated_text: then [the seed] falls into the womb quickly — calcine it comfortably. (RA 11.118)
Then, having placed [it] in the swing-apparatus, combined with a wet lump,

children.text: tṛtīye divase sūto | jarate grasate tataḥ || (RA_11.119)
children.translated_text: on the third day the mercury calcines and swallows [it]. (RA 11.119)
[Continue] until evenly digested in the swing-apparatus — [so says] the skilled one;
afterwards, [continue to] even digestion with the tortoise-apparatus, O <s>Pārvatī</s>;
that morsel at one-twelfth, calcine with the tortoise [apparatus]. (RA 11.120)
As before, [apply] the fresh-ginger procedure and the womb-melting [technique];
afterwards, O Goddess, having placed [it], the skilled one should apply a firing. (RA 11.121)

children.text: aṣṭāṃśena tato grāsaṃ | garbhadrāvaṃ ca pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: Then a morsel at one-eighth, and womb-melting as before;
having placed that mercury in the belly of a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber,

children.text:
puṭet tu jāritastāvat | yāvat kando na dahyate ||
                    (RA_11.122)
children.translated_text: fire it — calcining until the tuber does not burn. (RA 11.122)

children.text: pādāṃśena tu mūṣāyā | grāsaḥ sūte vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: A morsel at one-quarter in the crucible is prescribed for mercury;

children.text:
pūrvavac ca viḍaṃ dadyāt | garbhadrāvaṇameva ca ||
                    (RA_11.123)
children.translated_text: give the flux (<s>viḍa</s>) as before, and the womb-melting too. (RA 11.123)

children.text: evaṃ caturguṇe jīrṇe | sūtako balavān bhavet |
children.translated_text: Thus, when fourfold [the amount] is digested, the mercury becomes powerful;

children.text:
tataḥ śalākayā grāsān | agnistho grasate rasaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.124)
children.translated_text: then, with a rod (<s>śalākā</s>), the mercury swallows the morsels while in the fire. (RA 11.124)
Then gems should be calcined by the procedure to be described. (RA 11.125)

children.text: abhrakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ caiva | śaṅkhanābhiṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Mica, <s>bhrāmaka</s> [lodestone], and conch-center (<s>śaṅkhanābhi</s>) likewise,
having added the mercurial substances and auxiliary minerals combined with the great calcination [paste]; (RA 11.126)
<s>vajrakanda</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and treated iron (<s>amṛtāyasa</s>),
seeds of bitter gourd (<s>kaṭutumba</s>), and killed metals — cook [all these]. (RA 11.127)
All in equal parts, measured with peacock's blood;

children.text:
tāvattaṃ mardayet prājño | yāvat karma dṛḍhaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_11.128)
children.translated_text: the skilled one should grind until the preparation becomes firm. (RA 11.128)
A crucible in the shape of a lute (<s>vallākṛti</s>) should be made, with covers;
place the mercury in its center and blow [the bellows] from below. (RA 11.129)
First, therein should be given [the gem] coated with the diamond-herbal [paste];

children.text:
gṛhyate ko 'tra saṃdeho | yathā tīvre hutāśane ||
                    (RA_11.130)
children.translated_text: it is swallowed — what doubt is there? — as if in an intense fire. (RA 11.130)

children.text: kuliśena puṭe dagdhe | karṣvagnau tena mardayet |
children.translated_text: When the diamond is burnt by firing, grind it in the fire of a pit;
calcine the diamond up to eleven times [the amount] again. (RA 11.131)
Well-burnt conch-center, soaked in citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice —

children.text:
muktāphalaṃ tato deyaṃ | vajrajīrṇe tu sūtake ||
                    (RA_11.132)
children.translated_text: then pearl (<s>muktāphala</s>) should be given, once the diamond is digested by the mercury. (RA 11.132)
By this sequential procedure, [the gems fed] become eleven times [the amount of mercury];
only peacock bile, mixed with indigo (<s>nīlī</s>) exudate, (RA 11.133)
and blue lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>), coated [with this mixture] and thrown into the mercury —
[one should] prepare great coloring [substances] in the mercury and discard those with weak coloring. (RA 11.134)
Red [substances] and peacock bile, combined with great gems;
coat the gem-bearing [mercury] with that — it melts in the midst of the mercury. (RA 11.135)
Turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>) and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, saturated with <s>Brahma</s>-exudate;
[this is] the calcination [agent] for topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>) — administer it together with that [mercury]. (RA 11.136)
When many gems are digested — with <s>bhṛṅga</s>-coloring, O pious one —
the king of mercury is seen, O Goddess, with a blue-yellow-red hue. (RA 11.137)
Coat pure gold sheets at one-hundredth [the proportion];
kill them by firing — [the mercury] becomes like a firefly (<s>indragopa</s>). (RA 11.138)
By mere touch it transmutes everything — this gold is 'killed,' O beloved;
[take] one-third of the king of mercury, extract it with that [gold]. (RA 11.139)
With [the mercury] placed in the crucible, calcine again with that [substance];
[it becomes] a smoke-transmuter (<s>dhūmavedhin</s>), O Goddess, when extracted and calcined again. (RA 11.140)
By this sequential procedure, if the threefold chain [is digested],
it transmutes — there is no doubt — mountains, nether-worlds, and the earth's surface. (RA 11.141)

children.text: pārśvajyotiḥ pradṛśyeta | cordhvaṃ naiva tu dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: If light is seen at the sides but not above,

children.text:
bhūcaraṃ taṃ vijānīyāt | rasendraṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.142)
children.translated_text: one should know that king of mercury to be a 'terrestrial one' (<s>bhūcara</s>) — there is no doubt. (RA 11.142)
With that, [having] tireless motion, O Goddess, one can travel a hundred <s>yojanas</s>;
[one becomes] of divine radiance, great body, divine sight, and great strength. (RA 11.143)
Freed from all diseases, one lives as long as the moon and stars [endure];
even his urine and feces transmute all metals. (RA 11.144)

children.text: samajīrṇena vajreṇa | hemnā ca sahitena ca |
children.translated_text: With evenly digested diamond and combined with gold,
[the mercury], placed in the fire, calcines metals — the mercury attains binding. (RA 11.145)

children.text: sārayet tena bījena | sahasram api vedhayet |
children.translated_text: Extract with that seed — it transmutes even a thousand [times];

children.text:
sāritaṃ jārayet paścāt | lepyaṃ kṣepyaṃ sahasraśaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.146)
children.translated_text: having extracted, calcine afterwards — coat and throw [the substance] a thousand times. (RA 11.146)
Extract with that seed — one obtains transmutation of a <s>lakṣa</s> [hundred thousand];
by this sequential procedure, the mercury becomes a <s>koṭi</s>-transmuter. (RA 11.147)

children.text: kevalaṃ tu yadā vajraṃ | samajīrṇaṃ tu jārayet |
children.translated_text: When diamond alone, evenly digested, is calcined,
the mercury is then to be known as 'bound' — immovable and free from defects. (RA 11.148)

children.text: agnistho jāyate sūtaḥ | śalākāṃ grasate kṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: The mercury, placed in fire, arises — it swallows the rod instantly;
when blown with forced fire (<s>haṭhāgni</s>), it swallows everything carefully. (RA 11.149)
The mercury moves, calcines, and becomes a giver of life-substances;

children.text:
mūṣāsthaṃ dhamayet sūtaṃ | haṭhāgnau naiva kampate ||
                    (RA_11.150)
children.translated_text: blow the mercury placed in a crucible — in forced fire, it does not tremble. (RA 11.150)
[When it] calcines all gems, the bound [mercury] leads to the aerial state (<s>khecaratā</s>);
thus, when eightfold metal is digested, the binding of mercury is [achieved]. (RA 11.151)

children.text: lohāni sattvaṃ triguṇaṃ | dviguṇaṃ kanakaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Metals' essence at threefold, gold at twofold —
[the mercury] becomes a smoke-and-gaze transmuter and bestows <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (RA 11.152)
At first, eightfold mica-essence and great mineral should be calcined;
equal [parts] with one-tenth gold — calcine diamond-gems. (RA 11.153)

children.text: sarvaṃ ca jārayed vajraṃ | tadāsau khecaro rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: When all the diamond is calcined, then that mercury becomes 'aerial' (<s>khecara</s>);
it revolves clockwise and becomes a <s>koṭi</s>-transmuter. (RA 11.154)

children.text: same tu pannage jīrṇe | daśavedhī bhavedrasaḥ |
children.translated_text: When an equal [amount of] <s>pannaga</s> (nāga/lead) is digested, the mercury becomes a ten-transmuter;

children.text:
dviguṇe śatavedhī syāt | triguṇe tu sahasrakam ||
                    (RA_11.155)
children.translated_text: at double, a hundred-transmuter; at triple, a thousand. (RA 11.155)
At fourfold, ten thousand, O Goddess — increase by this progression;
by successive increase, calcine the <s>pannaga</s> therein. (RA 11.156)

children.text: kuṭilaṃ pannagaṃ jāryaṃ | tatra saṃkhyākrameṇa tu |
children.translated_text: Crooked (serpentine) <s>pannaga</s> should be calcined, therein by the enumeration procedure;
that [mercury], O Queen of the Gods, becomes a <s>koṭi</s>-transmuter. (RA 11.157)
By the demon lord <s>Ruru</s>, ash-mercury was consumed;
wherein iron was calcined twelvefold, O Queen of the Gods. (RA 11.158)
Having consumed one <s>pala</s>, the demon, proud of his strength,
uprooted the world — even <s>Kailāsa</s> was pulverized by him. (RA 11.159)

children.text: tatra mayā kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā | dṛṣṭvā tanmāyayā kṛtam |
children.translated_text: Then, by me, having meditated for a moment and seen that [his power] was produced by <s>māyā</s>,

children.text:
jāritaṃ pannage sūtaṃ | samāṃśaṃ śilayā hatam ||
                    (RA_11.160)
children.translated_text: mercury was calcined in <s>pannaga</s> (lead), in equal parts, killed with realgar (<s>śilā</s>). (RA 11.160)
With that mercury, the trident was coated, O daughter of the snow-mountain;
by that trident, the demon proud of his strength was slain. (RA 11.161)

children.text: hema śulvaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ | vājaraṃ ca paḍālakam |
children.translated_text: Gold, copper, iron, <s>vājara</s>, and <s>paḍālaka</s>,
<s>rohaṇa</s>, and lodestone-metal — calcine according to the [prescribed] enumeration of principles. (RA 11.162)
With each one [digested], this king of mercury, bound, leads to the aerial state (<s>khecaratā</s>).

children.text:
gandhanāge drute devi | jāraṇāṃ sukarāṃ śṛṇu ||
                    (RA_11.163)
children.translated_text: O <s>Devī</s>, hear the easy method of calcination (<s>jāraṇā</s>) when lead-sulfide (<s>gandhanāga</s>) is melted. (RA 11.163)
First, purified mercury, combined with turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>) powder,
should be ground until black, [then] washed with hot sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). (RA 11.164)
Thus, ground repeatedly, the lead-sulfide melts into liquid. (RA 11.165)

children.text: nāgasya mūtre deveśi | vatsasya mahiṣasya vā |
children.translated_text: O Queen of the Gods, in the urine of a lead[-fed] cow, or of a calf, or of a buffalo,
having repeatedly revolved the serpent [mercury], one should quench it seven times. (RA 11.166)
O Beautiful One, having made its leaves [foils] pierced with thorns,
one should combine sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) in the proportion of one-fourth. (RA 11.167)
Spreading a layer of lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), then hair (<s>romāṇi</s>) on top of that,

children.text:
ūrdhvaṃ gandhakacūrṇaṃ ca | tato nāgadalaṃ tathā ||
                    (RA_11.168)
children.translated_text: then sulfur powder above, then lead foil likewise. (RA 11.168)
Sulfur, human hair, a layer of lac — in sequence,

children.text:
ūrdhvaṃ prasārya saṃsthāpya | sūtrair vartiṃ tu kārayet ||
                    (RA_11.169)
children.translated_text: spreading and placing above, one should make a wick [roll] tied with threads. (RA 11.169)
One should immerse it in <s>karañja</s> oil for ten nights;

children.text:
dīptāgrabhāgāṃ tāṃ vartiṃ | saṇḍaśyā tu vidhārayet ||
                    (RA_11.170)
children.translated_text: that wick, with its tip ignited, should be held with tongs. (RA 11.170)
One should drop that melted liquid into a vessel containing antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>) and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text:
kācakūpyāś ca madhye tu | tattailaṃ sthāpayet priye ||
                    (RA_11.171)
children.translated_text: and in the middle of a glass bottle, one should place that oil, O Beloved. (RA 11.171)
Having placed mercury in a cow-udder crucible (<s>gostanamūṣā</s>) coated with calciumite (<s>śilā</s>),
knowing the strength and weakness [of mercury] by the proportion of one-sixty-fourth etc., O <s>Devī</s>, (RA 11.172)
having added the melted lead-sulfide into that crucible, O One Worshipped by the Gods,
having placed [the crucible] in a pit filled with cow-dung,
one should give sealed heating (<s>puṭapācana</s>) with two handfuls (<s>prasṛti</s>) of cow-dung cakes and rice husks. (RA 11.173)
If there is suspicion of indigestion [incomplete absorption], one should add

children.text:
caturbindūn puṭe prāgvad | evaṃ pratidinaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_11.174)
children.translated_text: four drops of <s>siṃhavallī</s> juice in the sealed heating as before — thus it should be done daily. (RA 11.174)
After threefold calcination, the mercury becomes the color of a <s>jambū</s> [rose-apple] fruit. (RA 11.175)
Pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) essence in small increments, combined with killed lead,
should remain in the crucible until, adding glass above and below,
thus blown twelve times, it becomes colored (<s>rañjita</s>). (RA 11.176)
The seed-powder cooked by that [process], in mercury at one-fourth proportion,
ground with gram-sour-liquid (<s>caṇakāmla</s>), instantly melts in the womb [internally]. (RA 11.177)
If internal melting (<s>garbhadruti</s>) does not occur, O <s>Devī</s>, from two [portions of] mineral coloring agents and sulfur,
with red <s>sindhu</s>-born, <s>alarka</s> [calotropis],

children.text:
kalkena liptaṃ puṭitaṃ | bījaṃ garbhe drutaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_11.178)
children.translated_text: borax, and the feathers [iron filings] — with a paste [of these], the sealed-heated seed melts internally. (RA 11.178)

children.text: bīje pādārdhatulyāṃśe | jīrṇe vedhaṃ karoti saḥ |
children.translated_text: When [the seed is] digested in one-fourth, half, or equal proportion in the seed, it effects transmutation (<s>vedha</s>),
at [ratios of] one-to-ten, one-to-sixteen, one-to-twenty-two, in sequence. (RA 11.179)
Combining triple the amount of brass (<s>rīti</s>), with silver (<s>tāra</s>) leaving silver as remainder,
coating with this <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> [silver-destroying compound], one should transmute with that mercury. (RA 11.180)

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ tu saṃskāraṃ | vakṣye nāgābhrajāraṇam |
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the further procedure — the calcination of lead-mica (<s>nāgābhra</s>).
O <s>Devī</s>, having powdered realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) [which is] red like oleander (<s>karavīra</s>), (RA 11.181)
one should steep [it] twenty times in the juice of tamarind (<s>yavaciñcā</s>);
with that paste, having carefully coated a lead foil,
one should cook it over a trench-fire (<s>karṣvānala</s>) until it becomes powdered. (RA 11.182)

children.text: rasakasya ca bhāgāṃs trīn | bhāgaikaṃ daradasya ca |
children.translated_text: Three parts of zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) and one part of cinnabar (<s>darada</s>),
ground with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice, one-fourth sulfur, and realgar (<s>śilāviṣa</s>). (RA 11.183)
With this paste coated in a crucible, sealed-heated,

children.text:
taṃ nāgaṃ dhamayed evaṃ | saptadhā hemavadbhavet ||
                    (RA_11.184)
children.translated_text: that lead, thus blown seven times, becomes like gold. (RA 11.184)

children.text: pītābhrakaṃ tv ekadalaṃ | liptāyāṃ maricena tu |
children.translated_text: Yellow mica (<s>pītābhraka</s>), single-layered, in a crucible coated with pepper (<s>marica</s>),
blown [until] fire-colored, should be dropped into drumstick (<s>saubhāñjana</s>) juice. (RA 11.185)
One should precipitate by the previous method — that essence [becomes] gold-lustrous. (RA 11.186)
A foil of colored lead, and the essence of yellow mica,
with woman's breast-milk, glass, smoke-born [soot], <s>guñjā</s>, lodestone, and borax,
combined with vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>) — this [constitutes] the lead-mica binary [combination]. (RA 11.187)
Or, with <s>ranāla</s> [rancid water], mustard (<s>siddhārtha</s>), sublimate (<s>dhūmasāra</s>), brick-powder, and jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>),

children.text:
mardayet tridinaṃ sūtaṃ | dolāyāṃ svedayet tryaham ||
                    (RA_11.188)
children.translated_text: one should grind the mercury for three days, [then] steam it in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolā</s>) for three days. (RA 11.188)
Combined with the paste of <s>punarnava</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>sarpākṣī</s>,
and also <s>āsurī</s> [mustard], <s>sindhuviṣa</s> [rock salt], ground with pepper (<s>marica</s>),
in a swing-apparatus again, one should steam for three days. (RA 11.189)
Having assimilated lead-mica at one-eighth proportion, O Queen of the Gods,
two parts of realgar (<s>śilā</s>) and one part of <s>sindhusauvarcala</s> [rock salt]; (RA 11.190)
half [a part] borax, one-quarter poison, and alkali-salt (<s>viḍa</s>) at one-eighth of the lump;

children.text:
tridine kacchape jāryam | evaṃ jāryaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam ||
                    (RA_11.191)
children.translated_text: in three days, in a tortoise-apparatus (<s>kacchapa</s>), it should be calcined — thus calcined sixfold. (RA 11.191)
<s>Śaila</s> [rock], vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), serpent [mercury], copper, iron, <s>ghoṣāraka</s>, and gold,
in progressively increasing [proportions] — this vitriol, from precipitating the essence of <s>tāpya</s> [pyrite]; (RA 11.192)
leaving gold as residue, that seed, at one-fourth portion, with citron juice,
one should assimilate [into] the king of mercury; one should calcine with gold-bearing [substances]: (RA 11.193)
pyrite, rock salt (<s>sauvarcala</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), vitriol (<s>āsīsa</s>), and borax;
having placed in a lotus-apparatus (<s>padmayantra</s>), and inserting the peg, O Queen of the Gods, (RA 11.194)

children.text: dhameddinatrayaṃ mandaṃ | yāvad bījaṃ drutaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: one should blow gently for three days until the seed melts;

children.text:
tameva samajīrṇaṃ tu | vahnau niṣkampanaṃ rasam ||
                    (RA_11.195)
children.translated_text: that very [mercury], having evenly digested [the seed], remains steady in fire. (RA 11.195)
Then, with sixfold seed, extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>) by the graduated method;
one should transmute silver, iron, and copper at one-thousandth ratio. (RA 11.196)
Poison, sulfur, <s>tāpya</s>-mica, crow-dung (<s>kākaviṣṭhā</s>), tin-ore (<s>ghanadhvani</s>),
<s>sahadevī</s>, <s>vahniśikhā</s> — with this paste, the mercury penetrates (<s>kramate</s>). (RA 11.197)

children.text: mūrchito mṛtasūtaś ca | jalūkābandha eva ca |
children.translated_text: Stupefied (<s>mūrchita</s>), killed (<s>mṛta</s>) mercury, and leech-bound (<s>jalūkābandha</s>),

children.text: caturtho mūrtibandhas tu | paṭṭabandhas tu pañcamaḥ |
children.translated_text: the fourth is solid-bound (<s>mūrtibandha</s>), and the fifth is foil-bound (<s>paṭṭabandha</s>),

children.text:
bhasmasūtaś ca khoṭaś ca | saṃskārāt saptadhā rasaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.198)
children.translated_text: ash-mercury (<s>bhasmasūta</s>) and ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) — by processing, mercury becomes sevenfold. (RA 11.198)
When mercury, abandoning fluidity and volatility, acquires the color of lead,

children.text:
lakṣaṇaṃ dṛśyate yasya | mūrchitaṃ taṃ vadanti hi ||
                    (RA_11.199)
children.translated_text: [and] those characteristics are seen — they call that stupefied (<s>mūrchita</s>). (RA 11.199)
Moistness, fluidity, luster, heaviness, and volatility —
when these are not seen in it, one should know it as killed mercury (<s>mṛtasūtaka</s>). (RA 11.200)

children.text: nānāvarṇaṃ tathā svacchaṃ | drutaṃ yonau jalūkavat |
children.translated_text: Multi-colored, clear, [and] when melted in the receptacle [it behaves] like a leech —
that binding of mercury is the characteristic of leech-binding (<s>jalūkābandha</s>). (RA 11.201)
Heaviness, reddish color, luster resembling the sun,
[and] when held in the middle of fire it remains [stable] — this is the characteristic of solid-binding (<s>mūrtibandha</s>). (RA 11.202)
Or, by calcination with a rod (<s>śalākā</s>), solid-binding is also obtained. (RA 11.203)

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ guru tathā | mṛdu sikthakasaṃnibham |
children.translated_text: White, yellow, heavy, soft like beeswax (<s>sikthaka</s>),
when it remains in the middle of fire — this is the characteristic of foil-binding (<s>paṭṭabandha</s>). (RA 11.204)

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ śvetaṃ tathā pītaṃ | nīlaṃ bhasmanibhaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Black, white, yellow, blue, or ash-colored —
when volatility is destroyed, this is the characteristic of ash-mercury (<s>bhasmasūta</s>). (RA 11.205)
When mercury [becomes] like a hen's egg, and breaks salt,
the mercury so revolves — this is the characteristic of ingot (<s>khoṭaka</s>). (RA 11.206)

children.text: athavā chedane snigdhaṃ | raśminā mṛdunā dravet |
children.translated_text: Or, when cut it is unctuous, melts with a gentle flame,
imperishable, hard, and white — this is the characteristic of ingot-binding (<s>khoṭabandha</s>). (RA 11.207)

children.text: khoṭādayas tu ye pañca | vihāya jalukākṛti |
children.translated_text: The five [forms] beginning from ingot, excluding leech-form,

children.text:
haṭhāgnau dhāmitāḥ santi | na tiṣṭhatyeva mūrchitaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.208)
children.translated_text: when blown in intense fire, they remain [stable] — but the stupefied [form] does not remain. (RA 11.208)
Resembling the young sun, multi-colored, O Queen of the Gods,
[mercury] transmutes body-metals — [this is] the colored (<s>rañjita</s>) <s>Rasabhairava</s> [mercury-lord]. (RA 11.209)
First, purification of mercury, then assimilation (<s>grāsamāna</s>),
then calcination of mica-essence (<s>vyomasattva</s>), then calcination of all essences. (RA 11.210)
After that, internal and external melting (<s>druti</s>), then calcination of gold,
then divine-herb sealed-heating (<s>puṭa</s>), then gem-binding (<s>ratnabandha</s>). (RA 11.211)

children.text: rañjanaṃ ca tato devi | jāraṇā cānusāraṇā |
children.translated_text: Then coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), O <s>Devī</s>, then calcination and extraction (<s>anusāraṇā</s>),

children.text:
krāmaṇaṃ ca tato deyaṃ | sūtakasya vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
                    (RA_11.212)
children.translated_text: then penetration (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) should be given to the mercury by the wise. (RA 11.212)

children.text:
evaṃ kramaṃ tu yo vetti | tasya siddhirna saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.213)
children.translated_text: One who knows this sequence — success is certain for him, without doubt. (RA 11.213)

children.text: vedhakaṃ yas tu jānāti | dehe lohe rasāyane |
children.translated_text: One who knows transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) — in the body, in metals, and in rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) —

children.text:
tasya janma jarā vyādhir | naśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.214)
children.translated_text: birth, old age, and disease are destroyed for him, without doubt. (RA 11.214)

children.text: dehe tu pañcaratnāni | nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ tathāyasam |
children.translated_text: In the body, the five gems are lead, tin, and iron;
the penetration of the king of mercury is the medicine that destroys disease. (RA 11.215)
