Through herbs, mercury penetrates; through the power of yoga it gradually
penetrates the mass of diseases and devours the corrupt ailment. (RA 11.216)

children.text: tasya tu krāmaṇaṃ jñātvā | tato vaidyair upācaret |
children.translated_text: Knowing its penetration, physicians should then treat [the patient];

children.text: krāmaṇena vinā sūto | na kramet na ca vedhayet |
children.translated_text: without penetration, mercury neither penetrates nor transmutes

children.text:
dehalohāmayān sarvān | vṛthā syāt kevalaṃ śramaḥ ||
                    (RA_11.217)
children.translated_text: the diseases of body and metals — it would be merely fruitless labor. (RA 11.217)

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogas | tenaiva saha yojayet |
children.translated_text: For whichever disease whichever formulation [is indicated], one should combine with that very one;
the lord of mercury destroys diseases of humans, elephants, and horses. (RA 11.218)
In sublimated form (<s>āroṭa</s>) it confers strength; stupefied, it destroys diseases;
when bound, [it gives] <s>khecarī</s>-<s>siddhi</s> [aerial powers]; when killed, [it grants] freedom from old age and death. (RA 11.219)
Especially disease-allaying [is mercury] stupefied with sulfur;

children.text:
oṣadhyā ghātitaḥ sūto | yathā bhūyo na jīvati ||
                    (RA_11.220)
children.translated_text: mercury killed by herbs, such that it does not revive again, (RA 11.220)
that indeed penetrates metals — with that one should prepare rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>).

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi | kim anyac chrotum icchasi ||
                    (RA_11.221)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 11.221)
Chapter 12
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said:
O Lord, what kind of herb is the auspicious one that stupefies mercury?

children.text:
kena vā bhasmasūtaḥ syāt | kena vā khoṭabandhanam ||
                    (RA_12.1)
children.translated_text: By what [means] does mercury become ash-mercury? By what [means] is ingot-binding [achieved]? (RA 12.1)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Hear attentively, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, the secret of mercury-binding,
unknown to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and other gods, O One Worshipped by Heroes. (RA 12.2)
Between [the rivers] <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, there is a demon (<s>rākṣasa</s>) named <s>Prayoga</s>;
in its vicinity, O Fair-Hipped One, mercury is bound instantly. (RA 12.3)
The best practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) should take the leaves of the night-roamer [the rākṣasa plant];

children.text: adho niṣpīḍitaṃ devi | raso bhavati cottamaḥ || (RA_12.4)
children.translated_text: Pressed downward, O Goddess — the mercury becomes excellent. (RA 12.4)

children.text: rasaṃ saṃmardya tenaiva | dināni trīṇi vārttikaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having ground the mercury with that [preparation] for three days, the skilled practitioner

children.text:
āroṭaṃ bandhayet kṣipraṃ | gaganaṃ tatra jārayet ||
                    (RA_12.5)
children.translated_text: should quickly bind [it into] a solidified mass (<s>āroṭa</s>); therein, one should digest mica (<s>gagana</s>). (RA 12.5)
With that leaf-mercury itself, one should again process mica.
Treated seven times with that [mica], together with the three pungents (<s>tryūṣaṇa</s>),

children.text: yantre vidyādhare devi | gaganaṃ tatra jārayet || (RA_12.6)
children.translated_text: in the <s>Vidyādhara</s> apparatus, O Goddess — one should digest mica therein. (RA 12.6)

children.text: māsamātreṇa deveśi | jīryate tat samaṃ same |
children.translated_text: Within one month, O Goddess of the Gods, it is digested — equal in equal [proportion].
When [mica] is digested equally in mercury, O Goddess, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold transmuter. (RA 12.7)
In the juice of the night-wanderer [plant] (<s>niśācara</s>), O Goddess, one should then treat sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>);

children.text: bhāvayet saptavāraṃ tu | dvipadyāś ca rasena tu || (RA_12.8)
children.translated_text: one should treat [it] seven times with the fluid of the bipedal [creature] (woman's menstrual blood). (RA 12.8)
With a coating of silver leaf, half-and-half with the finest gold —
when the sulfur is equally digested in this, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold transmuter. (RA 12.9)

children.text: punas taṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā | pattralepe raviṃ haret |
children.translated_text: Again, having added that sulfur, one should transmute gold through leaf-coating.

children.text:
taṃ raviṃ tāramadhye tu | triguṇaṃ vāhayet tataḥ ||
                    (RA_12.10)
children.translated_text: That gold should then be carried into silver in triple proportion. (RA 12.10)
Gold combined with half-gold attains equality with the mother-[substance].

children.text:
punas taṃ gandhakaṃ sākṣād | drāvayitvā drutaṃ kuru ||
                    (RA_12.11)
children.translated_text: Again, having directly liquefied that sulfur, make it fluid. (RA 12.11)

children.text: rasendraṃ mardayet tena | gatadehaṃ tu kārayet |
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) with that; one should render [it] bodiless (<s>gatadeha</s>).
By mere application of that, O Beloved, the eighteen types of skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>),

children.text:
arśo bhagaṃdaraṃ lūtāṃ | śirorogāṃś ca nāśayet ||
                    (RA_12.12)
children.translated_text: hemorrhoids (<s>arśa</s>), fistula (<s>bhagaṃdara</s>), spider-bite [ulcers] (<s>lūtā</s>), and head diseases are destroyed. (RA 12.12)
In the juice of the night-wanderer [plant], orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>) should be treated seven times.

children.text:
tenaiva ghātayed vaṅgaṃ | vaṅgaṃ tāre tu nirvahet ||
                    (RA_12.13)
children.translated_text: With that, one should kill tin (<s>vaṅga</s>); [that] tin should be carried into silver. (RA 12.13)

children.text: taṃ tāraṃ jārayet sūte | tatsūtaṃ bandhanaṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: That silver should be digested in mercury; that mercury attains binding.
By mere application of that, it becomes [effective] in one sixty-fourth [proportion]. (RA 12.14)
At the sixty-fourth proportion, one should make it transmute copper.

children.text: śulvaṃ tu dāpayet tāre | tattāraṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: The copper should be carried into silver; that silver becomes gold.
That silver becomes excellent — granting <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation. (RA 12.15)
The flowers of the night-wanderer [plant] should be made into fine powder.

children.text:
palāni daśa cūrṇasya | rasair dhātryāstu bhāvayet ||
                    (RA_12.16)
children.translated_text: Ten <s>palas</s> of the powder should be treated with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (Indian gooseberry). (RA 12.16)
Mixed with ghee and honey, it should be placed in a new vessel;
it should be stored in a heap of grain for three weeks, O Goddess of the Gods. (RA 12.17)
By merely consuming that, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 12.18)

children.text: valkalaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu | madhunā sahitaṃ lihet |
children.translated_text: The bark, finely powdered, should be licked with honey.
By application for half a month, the result becomes directly perceptible, O Beloved. (RA 12.19)
From his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
By application for one month, lead becomes gold. (RA 12.20)
Or, one should extract its fruit-oil in the apparatus called <s>Pātāla</s> (subterranean).

children.text: tena tailena deveśi | rasaṃ saṃkocayed budhaḥ || (RA_12.21)
children.translated_text: With that oil, O Goddess of the Gods, the wise one should contract (solidify) the mercury. (RA 12.21)
Instantly, O Goddess, the great mercury becomes bound as a solid cake (<s>paṭṭabaddha</s>). (RA 12.22)
A pungent bracelet (<s>kaṅkaṇa</s>) should be prepared; on the mercury-<s>liṅga</s>, O Beautiful-faced One,
having contracted [it], the killing [of mercury] should be done with that — [it is] supremely wonderful. (RA 12.23)
Gold (<s>bhāskara</s>) placed in the juice of the night-wanderer [plant] seven times —
becomes free from tarnish (<s>kālikā</s>), and attains a golden radiance. (RA 12.24)

children.text: tattāreṇa samaṃ bāhyaṃ | tena siktaṃ tu vāpitam |
children.translated_text: That [gold], equal to silver externally, quenched and sprinkled with that,

children.text:
daśāṃśaṃ vedhayet sūtaṃ | daśa pītaṃ śatena ca ||
                    (RA_12.25)
children.translated_text: one should transmute mercury in one-tenth [proportion]; ten [transmutes] the yellow [metal]; and a hundred [transmutes more]. (RA 12.25)
A hundred transmutes a hundred thousand; a thousand is a transmuter of ten million.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ koṭivedhi syāt | koṭivedhi samena ca || (RA_12.26)
children.translated_text: In one-tenth proportion, it transmutes ten million; in equal proportion, it transmutes ten million. (RA 12.26)
Now I shall declare another mercury-binding, exceedingly rare. (RA 12.27)
She who is the mother of the three worlds — the herb <s>Ajanāyikā</s> —
by mere contact with her, mercury stands bound. (RA 12.28)
Ground for seven days with the juice of that great herb,
by transmutation in one-hundredth proportion, it produces divine gold. (RA 12.29)
By grinding in the juice for two weeks, O Beautiful-colored One,

children.text:
lakṣavedhī rasaḥ sākṣād | aṣṭau lohāni kāñcanam ||
                    (RA_12.30)
children.translated_text: the mercury directly becomes a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter — [converting] the eight metals into gold. (RA 12.30)
In three weeks, O Goddess of the Gods, it transmutes ten hundred-thousands.
In the fourth week, the great mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 12.31)
Steamed, heated, and rubbed with the juice of the great herb,
[mercury] bestows the <s>khecarī siddhi</s> (power of flying through space) — with unobstructed range. (RA 12.32)
One can enjoy a thousand women within a single day.

children.text:
naṣṭacchāyo hy adṛśyaś ca | trailokyaṃ ca bhramedrasaiḥ ||
                    (RA_12.33)
children.translated_text: With shadow vanished, invisible, one may roam the three worlds through [the power of] mercury. (RA 12.33)
With the juice of the great herb, the revivification of the dead becomes possible.

children.text:
anena ghātayet sūtaṃ | pañcāvasthaṃ kuru priye ||
                    (RA_12.34)
children.translated_text: With this, one should kill mercury and bring it to the fifth stage, O Beloved. (RA 12.34)

children.text: mṛtasya dāpayen nasyaṃ | hastapādau tu mardayet |
children.translated_text: One should administer the nasal application (<s>nasya</s>) to the dead person; one should massage the hands and feet.
Life enters into him — even of one who is dead, O Beautiful-faced One. (RA 12.35)
Now I shall declare another mercury-binding, exceedingly rare.
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> (sal ammoniac / a plant), mercury is bound in an instant. (RA 12.36)
Having added the juice of <s>narasāra</s> together with the fluid of the biped (woman's menstrual blood),
at the end of the day, binding is attained; it colors all metals. (RA 12.37)
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone, when lead is digested in sixfold [proportion],

children.text:
tāre tāmre 'pi vā devi | bhāvayet taṃ manaḥśilām ||
                    (RA_12.38)
children.translated_text: [whether] in silver or in copper, O Goddess — one should treat realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) with that. (RA 12.38)

children.text: nirgandhā jāyate sā tu | ghātayet tadrasāyanam |
children.translated_text: It becomes odorless; with that, one should kill [it] as an elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>).
Together with the fluid of the biped [woman], lead becomes devoid of essence. (RA 12.39)
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone, when lead is digested in sixfold [proportion],

children.text:
tāre tāmre 'pi vā devi | koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.40)
children.translated_text: in silver or copper, O Goddess — the mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 12.40)
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> and breast-milk, treated seven times separately,
one should give <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) its food (<s>grāsa</s>) in the apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>. (RA 12.41)

children.text: jīryate gaganaṃ devi | nirmukhaṃ ca varānane |
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>gagana</s>) is digested, O Goddess — mouthless (<s>nirmukha</s>), O Beautiful-faced One.
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> and the juice of <s>kīṭamārī</s> (insect-killer plant),

children.text:
drāvayed gaganaṃ devi | tīkṣṇaṃ lohaṃ ca pannagam ||
                    (RA_12.42)
children.translated_text: one should liquefy mica, O Goddess, as well as iron and lead. (RA 12.42)
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> and the juice of <s>hanūmatī</s> (a plant),
divine gold is produced — by pouring (<s>niṣeka</s>), O sun-beloved One. (RA 12.43)
Having added madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>) and red sandalwood to the juice of <s>narasāra</s>,

children.text:
svarase mardayet paścāt | pannagaṃ devi secayet ||
                    (RA_12.44)
children.translated_text: one should grind [them] in their own juice; then, O Goddess, one should pour [it] on lead. (RA 12.44)
Instantly, divine gold [results]. Poured seven times,

children.text:
ravighṛṣṭaṃ tu taṃ devi | pannagaṃ triguṇaṃ priye ||
                    (RA_12.45)
children.translated_text: rubbed with gold, that lead, O Goddess, [becomes gold] in triple [proportion], O Beloved. (RA 12.45)
That copper, gold-resembling, combined with one-fifth silver,
[and] gold combined with one-eighth — [this is] the remedy in gold-work. (RA 12.46)
In the juice of <s>narasāra</s>, cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>) should be treated seven times.
With that, one should kill iron — it should be directed to the state of ash. (RA 12.47)

children.text:
tadbhasma tāmrapiṣṭaṃ tu | triguṇaṃ tena nirvahet ||
                    (RA_12.48)
children.translated_text: That ash, with a copper cake (<s>tāmra-piṣṭa</s>), should be carried out in triple [proportion]. (RA 12.48)
That copper, gold-resembling, combined with one-eighth silver —

children.text:
tārahema samāṃśaṃ tu | dviguṇaṃ pittalaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.49)
children.translated_text: silver-gold in equal proportion, doubled, becomes brass (<s>pittala</s>). (RA 12.49)
In the juice of <s>narasāra</s>, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore) should be treated seven times.

children.text:
taṃ rasaṃ rasakaṃ caiva | tīkṣṇaṃ lohaṃ ca pannagam ||
                    (RA_12.50:1)
children.translated_text: That mercury and <s>rasaka</s>, and iron and lead — (RA 12.50a)
with the juice of <s>narasāra</s> itself, one should grind all together.
Instantly, the binding of both the mercury and the <s>rasaka</s> occurs. (RA 12.50b)

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ nāgaṃ tathā śulvaṃ | rasakena tu rañjayet |
children.translated_text: Iron, lead, and copper — one should color [them] with <s>rasaka</s>.
All becomes gold, with the radiance of a pumpkin flower. (RA 12.51)
Now I shall declare another mercury-binding, exceedingly rare. (RA 12.52)
The herb called <s>Kaṅkāla-khecarī</s>, O Supreme Goddess —
having collected its oil, combined with <s>Māgha-khecarī</s>,
one should treat [it] for one day in a vessel made of gold (<s>bhāskara</s>). (RA 12.53)

children.text: dvitīye vāsare prāpte | vajraratnaṃ tu ghātayet |
children.translated_text: When the second day arrives, one should kill a diamond gem.
One should heat it in fire — [until it becomes] intensely hot and blazing. (RA 12.54)
In the oil of <s>Kaṅkāla-khecarī</s>, one should quench the diamond gem.

children.text: daśavāraṃ niṣiktaṃ tu | bhasmākāraṃ hi jāyate || (RA_12.55)
children.translated_text: Quenched ten times, it takes on the form of ash. (RA 12.55)
That gold-cooked seed (<s>hema-pakva-bīja</s>), combined equally with that ash,
[with] one-third borax added, should be smelted in a sealed crucible.
Instantly, the pair merges — the diamond gem and the gold. (RA 12.56)
Moon-gold, O Beautiful-hipped One — if [one] digests [it] in equal [proportion],

children.text: koṭivedhī raso devi | lohānyaṣṭau ca vidhyati || (RA_12.57)
children.translated_text: the mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter, O Goddess — it transmutes the eight metals. (RA 12.57)
Now I shall declare another mercury-binding, exceedingly rare. (RA 12.58)

children.text: sabījā cauṣadhī grāhyā | kācid gulmalatā priye |
children.translated_text: A certain seeded herb, a shrub-creeper, should be collected, O Beloved;
the second, named <s>Mantra-siṃhāsanī</s>, O Goddess, [is] a <s>khecarī</s> [herb].
Its oil should be extracted in the <s>Pātāla</s> apparatus, [and stored] in a copper vessel. (RA 12.59)

children.text: tasya tailasya madhye tu | prakṣipet khecarīrasam |
children.translated_text: In the midst of that oil, one should add the juice of the <s>Khecarī</s> [herb].
One should place [it] within the <s>Medinī</s> apparatus, O Beautiful-faced One. (RA 12.60)
With the first herb, O Goddess, mica [processed] on the <s>Medinī</s> surface —
then, having given [it as] food to mercury, make a ball by grinding. (RA 12.61)

children.text: baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tena | gaganaṃ tena jārayet |
children.translated_text: Having tied it in a cloth bundle, one should digest mica with that.

children.text:
same tu gagane jīrṇe | baddhastiṣṭhati sūtakaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.62)
children.translated_text: When mica is equally digested, mercury stands bound. (RA 12.62)
When blown with bellows-blasts, [the mercury] does not disappear.
The appearance of the equally-digested [mercury] becomes like crow's excrement. (RA 12.63)

children.text: dviguṇe gagane jīrṇe | aṣṭau lohāni saṃharet || (RA_12.64)
children.translated_text: When mica is digested in double proportion, it assimilates the eight metals. (RA 12.64)
Now I shall declare another mercury-binding, exceedingly rare. (RA 12.65)
Born from the body of <s>Śiva</s> — the herb <s>Turasiṃhanī</s>.

children.text:
jārayed gandhakaṃ sā tu | jārayet sāpi tālakam ||
                    (RA_12.66)
children.translated_text: She digests sulfur; she also digests orpiment. (RA 12.66)

children.text: kāñcanaṃ jārayet sāpi | rasendraṃ sā ca baddhayet |
children.translated_text: She also digests gold; she also binds <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury).

children.text: pravālaṃ jārayet sā tu | gaganaṃ drāvayet tathā |
children.translated_text: She digests coral; she likewise liquefies mica.

children.text:
vajraṃ ca ghātayet sā tu | sarvasattvaṃ ca pātayet ||
                    (RA_12.67)
children.translated_text: She also kills diamond; she also precipitates all metallic essences. (RA 12.67)
She digests all metals and also refines essences.
Having placed [it] in the juice of <s>harīṃdarī</s>, in a cow's horn, O Beautiful-faced One,
[and] stored in a heap of grain — mercury stands killed. (RA 12.68)
With the juice of the divine herb, <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury), O one honored by the gods —

children.text: same tu kanake jīrṇe | daśakoṭīstu vedhayet || (RA_12.69)
children.translated_text: when gold is digested equally, it transmutes ten tens-of-millions. (RA 12.69)
At the fifth [stage], a hundred-thousand-times-ten-million; at the sixfold [stage], a touch-transmuter.

children.text: saptame dhūmavedhī syāt | aṣṭame tv avalokataḥ |
children.translated_text: In the seventh [degree], it becomes a smoke-transmuter (<s>dhūmavedhī</s>); in the eighth, [it transmutes] by sight (<s>avalokataḥ</s>);

children.text:
navame śabdavedhī syād | ata ūrdhvaṃ na vidyate ||
                    (RA_12.70)
children.translated_text: in the ninth, it becomes a sound-transmuter (<s>śabdavedhī</s>) — beyond that, nothing [higher] exists. (RA 12.70)
Deluded beings wander about, devoid of <s>kulauṣadhi</s> (clan-herbs);
from the juices of grass-herbs (<s>tṛṇauṣadhi</s>), perfection is never born. (RA 12.71)
Therefore, with every effort, the <s>kulauṣadhī</s> (clan-herb) must be known. (RA 12.72)
Sixty-four divine herbs (<s>divyauṣadhī</s>) are established within the clan (<s>kula</s>);
the deluded ones do not know them, bewildered by divine delusion. (RA 12.73)
Non-divine grass-herbs grow in mountain-caves. (RA 12.74)

children.text: tṛṇauṣadhyā rase sūtaṃ | naiva baddhaṃ kadācana |
children.translated_text: By the juice of grass-herbs, mercury is never bound;

children.text: akṣayaṃ ca varārohe | vahnimadhye na tiṣṭhati || (RA_12.75)
children.translated_text: and [it is] perishable, O beautiful-hipped one — it does not withstand fire. (RA 12.75)

children.text: na khoṭo na ca vā bhasma | naiva dravyaṃ karoti saḥ |
children.translated_text: It produces neither an alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) nor a calx (<s>bhasma</s>), nor does it create [any useful] substance.

children.text:
kiṃ tat dravyaṃ prakurvīta | dhāmyamāno na tiṣṭhati ||
                    (RA_12.76)
children.translated_text: How could that substance be made [useful] — [when] it does not withstand being blown [in fire]? (RA 12.76)

children.text: pattre pāke kaṭe chede | naiva tiṣṭhati kāñcane |
children.translated_text: In leaf-smearing (<s>pattralepa</s>), in cooking (<s>pāka</s>), in cutting (<s>kaṭa</s>), in cleavage (<s>cheda</s>) — it does not withstand gold;

children.text:
na vedhaṃ ca śatād ūrdhvaṃ | karoti sa rasaḥ priye ||
                    (RA_12.77)
children.translated_text: nor does that mercury perform transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) beyond a hundredfold, O beloved. (RA 12.77)

children.text: yāvanna baddhamekaṃ tu | vikrītaṃ tat tu kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: Until even one [piece of] bound [mercury] has been sold as gold,

children.text:
dharmārthakāmamokṣārthaṃ | naiva dadyāt tu tat priye ||
                    (RA_12.78)
children.translated_text: for the purposes of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>, one should never give it away, O beloved. (RA 12.78)
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: nirjīvatvaṃ gataḥ sūtaḥ | kathaṃ jīvaṃ dadāti ca |
children.translated_text: Mercury that has become lifeless (<s>nirjīva</s>) — how can it give life?

children.text: nirjīvena tu nirjīvaḥ | kathaṃ jīvati śaṃkara || (RA_12.79)
children.translated_text: Through the lifeless, the lifeless — how does one live, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>? (RA 12.79)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said:

children.text: divyauṣadhyā yadā devi | rasendro mūrchito bhavet |
children.translated_text: When, O Goddess, the king of mercury is swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>) by a divine herb,
the mercury becomes free from blackness (<s>kālikā</s>), O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 12.80)
Mercury free from blackness destroys another's death (<s>kāla</s>),

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ caiva lohānāṃ | malaṃ śamayati kṣaṇāt || (RA_12.81)
children.translated_text: and instantly pacifies the impurities of [all] eight metals. (RA 12.81)

children.text: mahāmūrchāgataṃ sūtaṃ | ko vāpi kathayen mṛtam |
children.translated_text: Mercury that has attained the great swoon (<s>mahāmūrchā</s>) — who would call it dead?
Through the juice of a divine herb, [it], though having lost consciousness, is reborn. (RA 12.82)
Mercury, consisting of the five elements, abides as <s>Sadāśiva</s> eternally. (RA 12.83)
I shall now describe another method of mercury-binding (<s>rasabandhana</s>), O Goddess. (RA 12.84)

children.text: kṣmāpālena hataṃ vajram | anenaiva tu kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: Diamond killed by <s>kṣmāpāla</s> (loadstone), and gold [killed] by the same —
diamond-calx and gold-calx — those two should be bound together. (RA 12.85)
It should be calcined in the juice of <s>niśācara</s> (night-roaming [plant]); one should calcine with <s>narajīva</s> (human-life plant).
That mercury, O auspicious one, should be killed with <s>gajāri</s> (lion-plant), a divine <s>kulauṣadhī</s>. (RA 12.86)

children.text: bhakṣitaḥ sa raso yena | so 'pi sākṣāt sadāśivaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who consumes that mercury — he himself becomes <s>Sadāśiva</s> incarnate.
When consumed [even in] one <s>tolaka</s>, a man becomes a touch-transmuter (<s>sparśavedhī</s>). (RA 12.87)
From the sweat of his body, the king of mercury is transmuted;
from [his] sweat and even urine, [all] eight metals [become] gold. (RA 12.88)
That foremost practitioner lives for a hundred thousand years.
<s>Prajāpati</s> [plant], of dark brilliance, binds mercury in an instant. (RA 12.89)
By the touch of <s>gajāri</s>, O Goddess, it is bound by <s>kṣmāpāla</s> (loadstone). (RA 12.90)
Mica (<s>gagana</s>) treated with the juice of <s>vajravallī</s>, O beloved,
should be calcined in a sand-bath apparatus — it becomes an alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) instantly. (RA 12.91)
One <s>māṣa</s> of killed-mercury ball and one <s>māṣa</s> of gold ball —
having combined and ground together with lime-sour [juice] for three days,
one should smear one <s>karṣa</s> of lead sheets with mercury-paste. (RA 12.92)

children.text: veṣṭayed vṛścikālyā ca | tatpiṇḍaṃ lepayet tataḥ |
children.translated_text: One should wrap [it] with <s>vṛścikālī</s> (scorpion-plant) and then coat that ball;
the lead is killed, O Goddess — it becomes like a firefly (<s>śakragopa</s>). (RA 12.93)
One should smear one <s>karṣa</s> of silver (<s>tāra</s>) sheets with killed lead;

children.text:
vṛścikālyā ca tat pattraṃ | lepitaṃ veṣṭayet tataḥ ||
                    (RA_12.94)
children.translated_text: that sheet, coated with <s>vṛścikālī</s>, should then be wrapped. (RA 12.94)
That silver is killed, O Goddess — it becomes vermilion-dawn colored.
With a thousandth part of that, one should effect the transmutation of copper. (RA 12.95)
Divine gold is produced — [worthy of being] ornaments for the gods. (RA 12.96)
Endowed with milky sap, many fruits, and knots, O <s>Pārvatī</s> —
the one known by the name <s>Caṭulaparṇī</s> is praised for mercury-binding. (RA 12.97)
In the juice of <s>Ekavīrā</s>-tuber, mercury placed in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>),
blown with mouth-bellows — the bound [mercury] is recommended for consumption. (RA 12.98)
The tuber of red <s>kañcukī</s>, ground with woman's breast-milk,
in a crucible by the previously described method, effects mercury-binding. (RA 12.99)
The seed of <s>vṛścikā</s>-leaf, combined with woman's milk —
[the mercury] should be blown as before — the skilled one [uses this] for the purpose of consumption. (RA 12.100)
Taking <s>vajrakanda</s> (diamond-tuber), one should place it in the midst of mercury;

children.text:
gajendrākhyaṃ puṭaṃ dattvā | saptadhā baddhatāṃ nayet ||
                    (RA_12.101)
children.translated_text: giving a <s>gajendra</s> (elephant-grade) heating-cycle seven times, it reaches the state of being bound. (RA 12.101)

children.text:
bhakṣayet taṃ rasaṃ prājñaḥ | ṣaṇmāsādamaro bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.102)
children.translated_text: The wise one should consume that mercury — within six months, he becomes immortal. (RA 12.102)
Taking the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s> and the tuber of <s>karkoṭī</s>,
placing mercury in their midst, one should steam and grind again. (RA 12.103)
It is killed, there is no doubt — blown with intense fire.
Mercury placed in a parrot-beak [vessel] (<s>śukacañcu</s>) should be heated in a cycle and then blown. (RA 12.104)
This [mercury], transmuting a hundredth part, becomes a bestower of bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>). (RA 12.105)
Mercury [treated with] the juice of <s>haṃsapādī</s> (goose-foot plant), placed inside a <s>śūkakanda</s> tuber —
given a <s>gajendra</s> heating-cycle — it is killed, of this there is no doubt. (RA 12.106)

children.text: haṃsāṅghriṃ śukatuṇḍīṃ ca | gṛhītvā mardayed rasam |
children.translated_text: Taking <s>haṃsāṅghri</s> (goose-foot) and <s>śukatuṇḍī</s> (parrot-beak plant), one should grind mercury [with them];
placed inside a <s>krauñcapāda</s> (crane-foot) [vessel], then given three heating-cycles. (RA 12.107)
It is killed, there is no doubt — [this] great mercury transmutes a hundred-thousand-fold. (RA 12.108)
Hear about the divine herb known as <s>Tṛṇajyoti</s> (grass-light), O beloved.
At night it blazes always; in the daytime it does not blaze, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text:
tasyā mūle tu nikṣiptaṃ | kṣīraṃ raktaṃ bhavet priye ||
                    (RA_12.109)
children.translated_text: When milk is placed at its root, it becomes red, O beloved. (RA 12.109)
With its root-juice, sulfur (<s>gandha</s>), and mica (<s>abhra</s>), ground with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice,
copper sheets smeared [with this] become gold after three heating-cycles. (RA 12.110)
Combined with the powder of its root, the king of mercury, O Queen of the Gods,
ground in citron juice — mica is digested in an instant. (RA 12.111)
Now I shall describe <s>Uccaṭī</s>, the mercury-binder, O beloved.

children.text:
ekameva bhavennālaṃ | tasya roma tu veṣṭanam ||
                    (RA_12.112)
children.translated_text: It has a single stalk; its hairs form its covering. (RA 12.112)

children.text: tasyāgre ca bhavet puṣpaṃ | śukatuṇḍasya saṃnibham |
children.translated_text: At its tip there is a flower, resembling a parrot's beak;
its leaves, O Queen of the Gods, resemble parrot feathers;
its tuber has the shape of <s>kuṣṭha</s>; its milk is vermilion-colored, very beautiful. (RA 12.113)
Its sap oozes like beeswax — taking that, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
one should transmute all metals — they become gold. (RA 12.114)
Mercury, orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and blue vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>) — [these] should be ground with the juices of <s>Uccaṭī</s>;
heated in sunlight, the mercury is killed by the power of the divine herb. (RA 12.115)
It transmutes seven metals with a hundred-thousandth part, O beautiful-faced one. (RA 12.116)
Now I shall describe the procedure of red <s>snuhī</s> (spurge), O divine beauty.
With <s>snuhī</s>-milk, one should smear copper sheets. (RA 12.117)
One should heat again with [the] milk seven times, O beautiful-faced one;
when repeatedly [treated], [the copper] becomes like <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold in lustre. (RA 12.118)
Then, with sesame oil (<s>tilatailena</s>), one should cook for three days.

children.text:
tathā śulvasya pattrāṇi | vedhyaṃ jāmbunadaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.119:1)
children.translated_text: Likewise, the copper sheets become gold fit for transmutation. (RA 12.119)
Mercury, red <s>snuhī</s>-milk, <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), mica (<s>abhraka</s>),
cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and metals — [all these, it] transmutes with a thousandth part. (RA 12.119:2)
Taking <s>snuhī</s>-milk, half-[portion of] <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), and gold — both [together],
<s>kunaṭī</s> and sulfur-powder — one should grind all together. (RA 12.120)
By this very method, one should purify gold with half-[portion of] <s>niśā</s> (turmeric);
making it into a pill, with that, one transmutes lead (<s>nāga</s>) instantly. (RA 12.121)
Now hear the procedure of the divine herb <s>Sthalapadminī</s> (land-lotus). (RA 12.122)

children.text: padminīsadṛśī pattraiḥ | puṣpair api ca tādṛśī |
children.translated_text: With leaves resembling a lotus, and flowers also similar,

children.text:
bhaṅge caiva bhavet kṣīraṃ | raktavarṇaṃ suśobhanam ||
                    (RA_12.123)
children.translated_text: when broken, a milk oozes — red-colored, very beautiful. (RA 12.123)
Stepping with the left foot [on it], one should gaze at the sky;
one should behold the circle of stars, planets, and constellations.
From a distance of a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, O Goddess — that is to be known as <s>Sthalapadminī</s>. (RA 12.124)
Taking its five parts (<s>pañcāṅga</s>), combined with <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and <s>Gaurī</s>,
combined with realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), together with pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), (RA 12.125)

children.text: mardayet saptarātraṃ tu | tena śulvaṃ ca vedhayet |
children.translated_text: one should grind for seven nights; with that, one should transmute copper.
With a thousandth part, O Queen of the Gods, the transmuted [copper] becomes gold. (RA 12.126)
Taking its five parts, by the previously stated method, O beloved,
one should make the king of mercury move [digest]; placed in a sealed crucible, one should blow. (RA 12.127)
It is killed within the crucible — by contraction, without doubt.
With that very [mercury], one should transmute all metals with a thousandth part. (RA 12.128)
Now I shall describe the procedure of <s>Kumudinī</s> (night-lily), O beloved.
Having split a Kashmiri stone, one should prepare [it] on the full-moon day. (RA 12.129)

children.text: tasyāḥ pañcāṅgam ādāya | bhāvayet tu manaḥśilām |
children.translated_text: Taking its five parts, one should treat realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) [with them];

children.text:
kharpare dhārayitvā tu | bhāvayet tu punaḥ punaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.130)
children.translated_text: placing [it] in a saucer (<s>kharpara</s>), one should treat again and again. (RA 12.130)

children.text: kharpare drāvitaṃ nāgaṃ | tatkalkena yutaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) melted in a saucer — make [it] combined with that paste.
Equal to Kashmiri saffron in [color], gold is certainly produced. (RA 12.131)
How <s>Citraka</s> (leadwort) should be gathered — I shall tell briefly. (RA 12.132)
<s>Citraka</s> is known to be threefold: red and black for <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir-making),
white for pacifying diseases — the best, middle, and least [respectively]. (RA 12.133)

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ sitaṃ vāpi | hemante noddharedbudhaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.134)
children.translated_text: Black, red, or white — the wise one should not uproot [them] in winter (<s>hemanta</s>). (RA 12.134)
Having uprooted black <s>citraka</s> not smelled by cows, O Goddess —
milk placed within [its] milk becomes black-colored instantly. (RA 12.135)
With the powder of its five parts, one should grind mercury;

children.text:
dhamec ca mūkamūṣāyāṃ | khoṭo bhavati tatkṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_12.136)
children.translated_text: blown in a sealed crucible — it becomes an alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) instantly. (RA 12.136)
Having donned red garments, with red garlands and unguents,
on the fifth [day] of the dark fortnight, with rice cooked with red grain (<s>raktaśāli</s>) —
Having offered a <s>bali</s> (sacrificial offering), O great Goddess, one should uproot the red <s>Citraka</s> (leadwort). (RA 12.137)
With the powder of red <s>Citraka</s>, tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), through three firings each,
becomes freed from all defects and instantly attains rigidity (<s>stambha</s>). (RA 12.138)
Its root and mercury in acid, with the application of <s>Kaṅguṇī</s> (celastrus) oil,
through twenty-one times [of treatment], copper becomes pure. (RA 12.139)
Red <s>Citraka</s> — smeared with <s>bhallāta</s> (marking nut) oil and [subjected to] a firing,
a silver-and-gold leaf, O Goddess, becomes beautiful gold. (RA 12.140)
<s>Nāginī</s> tuber, mercury-lord, combined with red <s>Citraka</s> —
in the measure of leaf-smearing, silver-and-gold [alloy] becomes [pure] gold. (RA 12.141)
Mercury combined with red <s>Citraka</s> becomes all-giving. (RA 12.142)
I shall describe the oil-method of <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> (malkangani) — hear, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 12.143)

children.text: jyotiṣmatī nāma latā | yā ca kāñcanasaṃnibhā |
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> — a creeper that resembles gold,
abundant in vine-canopy, with golden-colored fruits, auspicious. (RA 12.144)
In the bright half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> [month], having collected the excellent seeds,

children.text: tilavat kvāthayitvā tu | hastaiḥ pādair athāpi vā |
children.translated_text: boiling them like sesame, by hand or by foot,

children.text:
tasya tailaṃ samādāya | kumbhe tāmramaye kṣipet ||
                    (RA_12.145)
children.translated_text: one should take its oil and place it in a copper pot. (RA 12.145)
The pot, buried in the ground, should be heated gradually from above with chaff-fire.

children.text:
ṣaṇmāse tu vyatikrānte | sa ghaṭaḥ kāñcanaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.146)
children.translated_text: When six months have passed, that pot becomes gold. (RA 12.146)
Having made that into gold, [one should take] the oil mixed with pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>).

children.text:
prativāpe niṣiñcet tat | hema tāmrasamaṃ bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.147)
children.translated_text: One should pour it as a quenching medium (<s>prativāpa</s>) — gold becomes equal to copper [in quantity]. (RA 12.147)
And thus it would be a hundred-fold transmuter — an unsurpassed gem of knowledge. (RA 12.148)
I shall describe <s>Dagdhārohā</s> (the 'burnt-sprouter'), O beloved, which accomplishes the binding of mercury.
It should be known for touch-transmutation (<s>sparśavedha</s>), accomplishing the purpose of all undertakings. (RA 12.149)

children.text: śastracchinnā mahādevi | dagdhā vā pāvakena tu |
children.translated_text: Cut with a weapon, O great Goddess, or burnt by fire,
this divine great herb sprouts again instantly — whether burnt or cut. (RA 12.150)

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ | tasyāḥ puṣpaṃ prajāyate |
children.translated_text: Its flowers appear in red, yellow, white, and black.
Its leaves, like those of the chickpea plant, should be recognized as well-produced. (RA 12.151)

children.text: sā sthitā gomatītīre | gaṅgāyām arbude girau |
children.translated_text: It is found on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s> [river], on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, on Mount <s>Arbuda</s> (Abu),
to the south of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, and in the margins of forests. (RA 12.152)
Its divine tuber-juice, accompanied by dark streaks,

children.text:
tāmbūlena samaṃ kṛtvā | guṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.153)
children.translated_text: the wise one should make into a pill, [prepared] together with betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>). (RA 12.153)
Of all metals melted in the midst of fire,

children.text:
sahasraṃ vedhayitvā tu | kāñcanaṃ kurute kṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_12.154)
children.translated_text: having transmuted a thousand [parts], it makes [them] gold instantly. (RA 12.154)
Likewise, mercury dies [i.e., is killed/fixed] when combined with magnetite, gold, and mica.
It makes divine gold, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods. (RA 12.155)
Hear about the divine herb known as <s>Kaṭutumbī</s> (bitter gourd), O Goddess. (RA 12.156)
Having collected its seeds, one should make them into fine powder. (RA 12.157)
One should treat [the mercury] twenty-one times with <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalakī/gooseberry) juice,
combined with milk and with <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> (ginger, the 'universal medicine'). (RA 12.158)

children.text: bījaṃ yantre vinikṣipya | tailaṃ saṃgṛhya paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having placed the seed in an apparatus, the learned one should collect the oil.
With that, one should cause the mercury to faint (<s>mūrchā</s>), and grind it with <s>Cakramarda</s> (ringworm cassia). (RA 12.159)
Cow bile, peacock bile, combined with <s>kāṅkṣī</s> and <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) —
these in equal proportion to silver — the mercury [renders them all] equal. (RA 12.160)
It should be stored in a ram's horn for one month continuously.
Sprinkled with an iron rod, it transmutes all metals. (RA 12.161)
Sulfur treated twenty-one times with an iron rod,
combined with this iron, mixed with lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) juice — (RA 12.162a)
with seed, accompanied by mercury, placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>),

children.text:
bhūgataṃ māsamekaṃ tu | tāraṃ kāñcanatāṃ nayet ||
                    (RA_12.162:2)
children.translated_text: buried in the ground for one month — it turns silver into gold. (RA 12.162b)
One part of the [transmuting] pellet, five parts of silver,

children.text:
śulvasya pañcabhāgaṃ ca | bījasyaikaṃ ca yojayet ||
                    (RA_12.163)
children.translated_text: five parts of copper, and one part of the seed — one should combine [them]. (RA 12.163)

children.text: ete dvādaśa bhāgāḥ syuḥ | sarvaṃ taddhārayet kṣitau |
children.translated_text: These become twelve parts [in total]; all of this should be buried in the ground.

children.text:
sthānasyāsya niṣekaṃ tu | bhūdaṇḍena tu kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.164)
children.translated_text: The sprinkling of this site should be done with an earth-rod. (RA 12.164)
At the end of twenty-five days, the best gold is produced. (RA 12.165)
I shall describe the method of <s>Kṣīrakanda</s> (milk-tuber), the supreme bestower of all <s>siddhis</s>.
There, among the four colored varieties, the red tuber is praised. (RA 12.166)
When broken, it oozes a milk of red color, very beautiful. (RA 12.167)
Adorned with [leaves] that arise at the rumbling of clouds,
with seven leaves, unctuous like [those of] <s>snuhī</s> (cactus), of splendid golden luster —
[this herb effects] the binding of the king of mercuries, subjugating all beings. (RA 12.168)

children.text: tasya kṣīraṃ tu saṃgṛhya | tāraṃ nirvāpayed budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having collected its milk, the wise one should quench silver [in it].
Then smelting with chaff-fire, beautiful gold is produced. (RA 12.169)
With the exudate of tamarind leaves, slightly mixed with copper dust,
the wise one should grind mercury — mercury-binding will result. (RA 12.170)
Placed in water, the pill becomes [hard] like a diamond (<s>vajra</s>). (RA 12.171)
Of the teak tree (<s>Śākavṛkṣa</s>), O Goddess, having pressed out the excellent juice,
combined with red sandalwood (<s>raktacandana</s>), it calcines all metals. (RA 12.172)
With the fragrance of <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s> (sulfur-stone), applied to iron —
all metals merge, melting like water. (RA 12.173)
Sulfur, calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), mercury, and red sandalwood,
combined with the juice of the weeping [plant] (<s>rudantī</s>) — silver becomes gold. (RA 12.174)

children.text: śākavṛkṣasya niryāsaṃ | pattre tasya ca gālayet |
children.translated_text: The exudate of the teak tree — one should strain it through its own leaf.
The powder of <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root should be ground with that juice. (RA 12.175)
Having coated copper leaves [with the paste] and placed them in a firing, one should cook [them].
That melted [product] becomes divine gold, endowed with [all proper] characteristics. (RA 12.176)
One should collect the ripe fruits of the teak tree.

children.text:
tadrasena yutaṃ prājñaḥ | saptarātraṃ tu bhāvayet ||
                    (RA_12.177)
children.translated_text: The wise one should treat [the substance] for seven nights with that juice. (RA 12.177)
Combined with that juice, mixed with <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder),
one should coat silver leaves — when smelted, it becomes gold. (RA 12.178)
Of <s>Devadālī</s> (divine creeper), the great herb, I shall describe the supreme method.

children.text:
sā śvetā vyādhināśe ca | kṛṣṇā pītā rasāyane ||
                    (RA_12.179)
children.translated_text: The white [variety] is for destruction of diseases; the black and yellow are for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 12.179)
On the full moon, on the thirteenth [lunar day], during a solar eclipse by <s>Rāhu</s>,
or on the fifth of the dark fortnight — one should uproot this [plant] according to the proper rites. (RA 12.180)
The fruit of <s>Devadālī</s>, O Goddess, and <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s> (butterfly pea) — [these] cause mercury

children.text:
mūrchayed bandhayet kṣipraṃ | śulvaṃ hema karoti ca ||
                    (RA_12.181)
children.translated_text: to faint and bind it quickly; and [they] turn copper into gold. (RA 12.181)
The fruit and root of <s>Devadālī</s>, along with <s>Īśvarī</s> juice,

children.text:
toyena marditaṃ kṛtvā | vaṅgaṃ stambhayati kṣaṇāt ||
                    (RA_12.182)
children.translated_text: ground with water — [this] rigidifies tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) instantly. (RA 12.182)
Hereafter, I shall describe the method of white <s>Guñjā</s> (abrus seeds), O beloved. (RA 12.183)
On the fourteenth or the eighth of the dark fortnight, O one worshipped by the gods,

children.text:
kapāle mṛttikāṃ nyasya | secayet salilena tu ||
                    (RA_12.184)
children.translated_text: having placed earth in a skull-bowl, one should moisten it with water. (RA 12.184)
One should sow the seeds of white <s>Guñjā</s> with flower-offerings,
and perform the collection with the mantra about to be stated. (RA 12.185)

children.text:
namo bhagavati śvetavalli śvetaparvatavāsini sarvakāryāṇi kuru kuru apratihate
                    namo namaḥ svāhā |
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage, O blessed White Creeper, dweller of the white mountain, accomplish all tasks, accomplish, accomplish — O invincible one, homage, homage, <s>svāhā</s>!
By this mantra alone, <s>siddhi</s> arises — not otherwise.
For six months, one should protect the creeper with mantra-purification. (RA 12.186)

children.text: śuddhaśulvaṃ tu saṃgṛhya | mūṣāmadhye tu saṃsthitam |
children.translated_text: Having taken purified copper, placed in a crucible,
in the amount of fifteen <s>palas</s>, with half a <s>karṣa</s> of white <s>Guñjā</s> — (RA 12.187)
together, it becomes silver, free from any [copper] smell.
Combined with <s>Brahmarīti</s> (divine brass) and <s>Guñjā</s> powder together,

children.text:
devānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ devi | jāyate hema śobhanam ||
                    (RA_12.188)
children.translated_text: beautiful gold fit for the ornaments of gods is produced, O Goddess. (RA 12.188)
With moon-water (<s>candrodaka</s>), O Goddess, I shall describe the binding of mercury. (RA 12.189)
On the full moon of the bright fortnight, having beheld the full moon-disc,
[certain substances] emerge, breaking through the earth — moon-waters in various forms. (RA 12.190)
Some are earth-colored, some saline in taste,
some moon-like, some shining like the sky.
They wax with the waxing of the moon and wane with its waning. (RA 12.191)
Having seen the moon-water, the mantrin [should collect it] on the full moon especially.
It emerges breaking through the earth, growing with the growth of the moon. (RA 12.192)
Having first performed the demarcation of the field (<s>kṣetrabandha</s>), having worshipped the god <s>Śaṃkara</s> (Śiva),
on the fourteenth [lunar day], having worshipped that field, the discerning one,
having fasted for a day and a night, should offer a <s>bali</s> there. (RA 12.193)

children.text: pūrṇamāsyāṃ ca rātrau ca | gatvā tasya samīpataḥ |
children.translated_text: On the full moon night, going near it,
having collected the moon-water, empowered with mantras, well-consecrated,
having stirred it with honey and ghee, one should drink it with concentration. (RA 12.194)
Merely upon drinking it, a faint (<s>mūrchā</s>) occurs instantly.

children.text: candrodaye tato dṛṣṭe | kṣīraṃ tasya tu dāpayet |
children.translated_text: Then, upon seeing the moon rise, one should give [the person] milk.
Through application for seven nights, one becomes pure like the moon. (RA 12.195)
Through twenty-one nights [of use], one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Through application for one month, that person attains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>. (RA 12.196)

children.text: candrodakena gaganaṃ | rasaṃ hema ca mardayet |
children.translated_text: With moon-water, one should grind mica, mercury, and gold.
Placed in a crucible and smelted, it becomes a pill instantly. (RA 12.197)

children.text:
ayaṃ ca sparśamātreṇa | lohānyaṣṭau ca vedhayet ||
                    (RA_12.198)
children.translated_text: This, by mere touch, transmutes all eight metals. (RA 12.198)
With that juice, the mercury should be treated, calcined together with diamond (<s>vajra</s>).
In one-sixty-fourth proportion in a pellet, and with double — a thousand-fold [transmuter]. (RA 12.199)
A man [should take] a <s>guñjā</s>-measure of mercury, bound with a tenfold chain,
wrapped in three metals, and holding it in the mouth, he attains invisibility. (RA 12.200)

children.text:
oṃ namo rudrāya daṃṣṭrotkaṭāya vighnanāśāya diśāṃ rakṣa rakṣa vidiśāṃ rakṣa rakṣa
                    rudro vijñāpayati huṃ phaṭ svāhā |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, salutation to <s>Rudra</s>, the one with terrible fangs, the destroyer of obstacles — protect the directions, protect, protect the intermediate directions, protect — <s>Rudra</s> commands — <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text:
oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya triśūlahastāya amṛtodbhavāya rakṣa rakṣa phaṭ svāhā
                    |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, salutation to the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, trident in hand, born of nectar — protect, protect — <s>phaṭ svāhā</s>.
Now I shall describe the binding of scissors-mercury (<s>kartarīrasa</s>). (RA 12.201)
In the encounter with the demons (<s>asuras</s>), with a mind filled with wrath,
the great discus <s>Sudarśana</s> was hurled by the enemy of <s>Mura</s> [i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. (RA 12.202)
From the frontal plate of that [discus], drops of sweat fell;

children.text:
te bhūmau patitā divyāḥ | saṃjātāḥ kartarīrasaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.203)
children.translated_text: those divine [drops], having fallen to the earth, became scissors-mercury (<s>kartarīrasa</s>). (RA 12.203)

children.text: rakṣārthaṃ sthāpitaṃ tatra | viṣṇunā ca sudarśanam |
children.translated_text: For protection, <s>Sudarśana</s> was established there by <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
it revolves like a discus and cuts down weapons. (RA 12.204)

children.text: kurute garjitaṃ nādaṃ | dhūmaṃ jvālāṃ vimuñcati |
children.translated_text: It produces a thundering sound and emits smoke and flames;
[there is] the sight-scissors (<s>kartarī</s>) — by mere glance; and another, the sound-scissors; (RA 12.205)
the touch-scissors, the shadow-scissors, the smoke-scissors,
the flame-scissors — and [these are all] the powers of the terrible scissors. (RA 12.206)
For the welfare of the worlds, the terrible power (<s>ghoraśakti</s>) is established;
in the form of mercury, supremely terrible — cutting down the unaccomplished. (RA 12.207)

children.text: tasyāḥ kṣetraṃ yadā gacchet | aghorāstraṃ japettadā |
children.translated_text: When one goes to its territory (<s>kṣetra</s>), one should then recite the <s>Aghora</s>-weapon [mantra];
again one should place the <s>Ghora</s> [mantra] there, and then the wise one should establish the weapon. (RA 12.208)
Establishing the scissors-[mercury] in the body by the forward and reverse [procedure],

children.text:
mudrayā mudrayet tāṃ tu | aghorāstreṇa yojitām ||
                    (RA_12.209)
children.translated_text: one should seal it with the <s>mudrā</s>, conjoined with the <s>Aghora</s>-weapon. (RA 12.209)

children.text: dīpenārādhayet tāṃ tu | stambhayed dhūpanena ca |
children.translated_text: One should worship it with a lamp and immobilize it with fumigation;
with the <s>viṣṭarā</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one should establish it in the proper position. (RA 12.210)

children.text: kañcukī tu śilā krāntā | kumārī vajrakandakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Kañcukī</s>, realgar (<s>śilā</s>), <s>krāntā</s> [<s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>], <s>kumārī</s> [aloe], <s>vajrakandaka</s>,
a woman's menstrual blood, cow's urine — and a <s>tilaka</s> [mark] that subjugates all. (RA 12.211)
Now I shall describe the binding of poison-water mercury (<s>viṣodaka-rasabandha</s>). (RA 12.212)
Poison-water is like poison [in potency]; ghee-water is like ghee;
rich in colors — white, yellow, and so forth — this, O Goddess, is the best of mercuries. (RA 12.213)
Having gone there, to a forest region, one should recite the <s>Ghora</s> [mantra] a thousand times;

children.text:
keśāḥ kṣiptāḥ sphuṭantyasmin | ātmacchāyā na dṛśyate ||
                    (RA_12.214)
children.translated_text: hairs thrown [into the water] split open; one's own shadow is not seen. (RA 12.214)

children.text: tailaṃ ca golakākāraṃ | ghṛtaṃ caiva visarpati |
children.translated_text: Oil [placed in it] takes a spherical form; ghee spreads out;
it takes away the smell of sulphur; saltiness and sourness arise. (RA 12.215)
Having obtained [it], [place] on a <s>palāśa</s> leaf and throw into a bitter gourd (<s>kaṭukālābu</s>) [vessel];

children.text:
viṣodakaṃ gandhakaṃ ca | harabījaṃ ca tatsamam ||
                    (RA_12.216)
children.translated_text: poison-water, sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) seed — in equal parts. (RA 12.216)
Having ground with goat's milk, coat copper sheets [with it];
fire that by the <s>puṭa</s> method, O Queen of the Gods — [it becomes] like red lead (<s>sindūra</s>) in color;
at one-hundredth [ratio], O Queen of the Gods, it transmutes all metals. (RA 12.217)

children.text: anena vidhinā devi | nāgaḥ sindūratāṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: By this procedure, O Goddess, lead attains the state of red lead;
at one-thousandth [ratio], one should give it transmutation of silver (<s>tāra</s>). (RA 12.218)
Red, yellow, and black — each progressively more effective in [its] operation. (RA 12.219)
Three <s>palas</s> [of the preparation], in a lodestone vessel or in a gourd vessel,

children.text:
gṛhītvā pūrvavat pattraiḥ | pālāśair veṣṭayed bahiḥ ||
                    (RA_12.220)
children.translated_text: having taken [it], wrap it externally with <s>palāśa</s> leaves as before. (RA 12.220)
Store it in a heap of grain for twenty-one days;
in the midst of buffalo's milk, prepare a single drop [of the mercury]. (RA 12.221)

children.text: pāyasaṃ bhakṣayed yas tu | madhvājyena tu saṃyutam |
children.translated_text: One who eats rice-pudding (<s>pāyasa</s>) combined with honey and ghee —
for as many <s>palas</s> of powder [consumed], O Goddess, one lives for that many [years] by the count of drops. (RA 12.222)
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, house-soot (<s>gṛhadhūma</s>), red lead (<s>sindūra</s>), the two turmerics (<s>rajanīdvaya</s>),

children.text:
meṣaśṛṅgīṃ ca śṛṅgīṃ ca | kṛṣṇonmattaṃ ca mārakam ||
                    (RA_12.223:1)
children.translated_text: <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, black datura (<s>kṛṣṇonmatta</s>), and the killing-agent (<s>māraka</s>); (RA 12.223:1)
mercury with its seed, ground with poison-water;
the wise one should soak [it] seven times with poison-water. (RA 12.223:2)

children.text: athavā bhāvayet tat tu | yāvaccūrṇaṃ tu tadbhavet |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one should soak it until it becomes a powder;
casting that upon lead at one-sixteenth [ratio], it is accomplished. (RA 12.224)

children.text: mūṣākhye veṇuyantre ca | trivāram api bhāvayet |
children.translated_text: In a bamboo apparatus called a crucible (<s>mūṣākhya veṇuyantra</s>), soak it even three times;
one should avoid its smoke — it is supremely harmful to the body. (RA 12.225)
Store the lead-red-lead (<s>nāgasindūra</s>) then in a gourd vessel;
that powder, at one-hundredth [ratio], transmutes silver sheets. (RA 12.226)
Having taken the poison-water, rolled [the preparation] in barley gruel,

children.text:
niṣiktaṃ tac ca varte 'yaṃ | tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
                    (RA_12.227)
children.translated_text: and having sprinkled it on the rolled [preparation] — this becomes fine silver. (RA 12.227)
Having taken the poison-water, throw [it] into the excellent mercury;
<s>kunaṭī</s>, arsenic-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>), poison, borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and <s>lāṅgalī</s>; (RA 12.228:1)
ground to a destroyed-paste in a mortar — coat silver sheets;
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — seedless (pure) gold is produced. (RA 12.228:2)
<s>Oṃ</s>, to the Glorious Blue-Throated One (<s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>) — <s>ṭha ṭhaḥ</s>.
One should recite this ten thousand times.
I shall describe the poison-grass (<s>viṣatṛṇa</s>) procedure — listen with concentrated mind. (RA 12.229)
Sulphur (<s>gandha</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), combined with <s>kunaṭī</s> and mercury,
combined with poison-grass, ground with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice. (RA 12.230)

children.text: etat kalkaṃ palamātraṃ | cauṣadhyā lepanaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: This paste, one <s>pala</s> in measure, coat with the herb;

children.text:
niryāse tu puṭaṃ kuryāt | trivāraṃ hema śobhanam ||
                    (RA_12.231)
children.translated_text: fire it in the exudate [medium] three times — beautiful gold [results]. (RA 12.231)
Now I shall describe the procedure for <s>saṃjīvanī</s> water (life-restoring water), O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 12.232)
O Goddess, I was worshipped previously by <s>Śukra</s> [the preceptor of the demons], O one praised by the gods,
for the welfare of the demons who had died in the battle with the gods. (RA 12.233)
By me, the <s>saṃjīvanī vidyā</s> (life-restoring knowledge) was given, in the form of water;

children.text: tayā saṃjīvitā daityā | ye mṛtā devasaṃgare || (RA_12.234)
children.translated_text: by that, the demons (<s>daityas</s>) who had died in the battle with the gods were revived. (RA 12.234)

children.text:
nikṣiptā martyaloke sā | samyak te kathayāmyaham ||
                    (RA_12.235)
children.translated_text: That [water] was deposited in the mortal world — I shall tell you about it properly. (RA 12.235)
In the mortal world, there is a supremely holy and sacred [river] in the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (Deccan);

children.text:
nadī godāvarī nāma | prasiddhā jāhnavī yathā ||
                    (RA_12.236)
children.translated_text: the river named <s>Godāvarī</s>, famous like the <s>Ganges</s>. (RA 12.236)

children.text: dakṣiṇe ca taṭe tasyāḥ | kadalīnagaraṃ param |
children.translated_text: On its southern bank is the excellent <s>Kadalīnagara</s> (Plantain City);
to its south is a mountain renowned in all the worlds. (RA 12.237)
Known by the name <s>Kṛṣṇagiri</s> (Black Mountain) — it is seen, O All-Auspicious One;
a village called <s>Suprasiddhāmbikā</s> is in its vicinity. (RA 12.238)
Having gone there, one should examine the water, O one worshipped by the gods. (RA 12.239)
Having taken a dry bamboo [stick] and thrown it into the midst of the water,
within a day and night, it assuredly becomes green and moist,
putting forth sprouts and leaves — and is seen to be beautiful. (RA 12.240)
With offerings of food, flowers, and oblations, one should then worship the Goddess,
the guardian of the field (<s>kṣetrādhipa</s>), <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and <s>Caṇḍa-Yonīśvara</s>. (RA 12.241)

children.text:
tasya mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi | triṣu lokeṣu durlabham ||
                    (RA_12.242)
children.translated_text: I shall describe the <s>mantra</s> for that — rare in the three worlds. (RA 12.242)

children.text: oṃ caṇḍāya pinākine śūlahastāya oṃ diśāṃ bandhaya vidiśāṃ bandhaya ṭhaṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, to <s>Caṇḍa</s>, to the one bearing the <s>Pināka</s>, trident in hand — <s>Oṃ</s>, bind the directions, bind the intermediate directions — <s>ṭha ṭhaḥ</s>.
Sesame seeds, rice grains, and mustard seeds,
having consecrated them seven times with this <s>mantra</s>, the practitioner should throw them in the [eight] directions. (RA 12.243)
The water [should be placed] in a bitter gourd [vessel]; the concentrated [practitioner], having performed the protection [rite],
having taken it carefully, should repair to his own abode. (RA 12.244)

children.text: oṃ namo 'mṛte 'mṛtarūpiṇi amṛtaṃ me kuru kuru evaṃ rudra ājñāpayati svāhā |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, salutation, O Immortal One, O one of immortal form, make me immortal — thus <s>Rudra</s> commands — <s>svāhā</s>.
Having consecrated that water seven times with this <s>mantra</s>,
for one day, mercury combined with two <s>māṣas</s> of gold,

children.text:
mardayet tena toyena | pibettat tu vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.245)
children.translated_text: should be ground with that water; the skilled one should drink that. (RA 12.245)
For twenty-one nights, on a milk-diet, with effort,
one lives for ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> and more — assuming any form, of great strength. (RA 12.246)
Having traveled a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, one returns again;

children.text:
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ | svec chācāraḥ sa khecaraḥ ||
                    (RA_12.247)
children.translated_text: invulnerable to all beings, moving at will — he becomes an aerial being (<s>khecara</s>). (RA 12.247)
Gold, mercury, and mica — combine in equal parts;

children.text:
mardayet tena toyena | saptavāraṃ tu svedayet ||
                    (RA_12.248)
children.translated_text: grind with that water and steam seven times. (RA 12.248)

children.text:
sa rasaḥ sarvalohāni | ṣaṣṭyaṃśena tu vedhayet ||
                    (RA_12.249)
children.translated_text: That mercury transmutes all metals at a sixtieth ratio. (RA 12.249)

children.text: athavā taṃ rasaṃ divyaṃ | madhunā saha bhakṣayet |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one should consume that divine mercury with honey;
by use for a mere month, one lives for ten thousand days of <s>Brahmā</s>. (RA 12.250)
By his urine, feces, and sweat, copper becomes gold. (RA 12.251)
Having taken the water in a windless [place], one should drink three handfuls;
immediately upon drinking, fainting occurs; recovery comes after three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours). (RA 12.252)
For twenty-one days thus, one should be on a milk-diet; then,
the wise one [attains] the appearance of an eight-year-old — assuming any form, of great strength. (RA 12.253)
He sees the entire earth as if perforated, together with the seven nether-worlds;
invulnerable to gods and demons, he is born with a lifespan of a <s>kalpa</s>. (RA 12.254)
Alternatively, having taken the water, mercury, and realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>),
grind on a stone mortar until it becomes a destroyed-paste. (RA 12.255)

children.text:
svedayet saptarātraṃ tu | trilohena ca veṣṭayet ||
                    (RA_12.256)
children.translated_text: Steam for seven nights and wrap with three metals. (RA 12.256)
One goes to invisibility instantly — one becomes a lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>;
surrounded by a hundred <s>Siddha</s>-maidens, for fourteen <s>kalpas</s>. (RA 12.257)

children.text: dineṣu teṣu sarveṣu | dadyāc chālyodanaṃ ghṛtam |
children.translated_text: On all those days, one should give boiled rice with ghee,

children.text:
payasā ca samāyuktaṃ | nityamevaṃ tu kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.258)
children.translated_text: combined with milk — one should always do this. (RA 12.258)
I shall describe the hot-water (<s>uṣṇodaka</s>) procedure — listen with concentrated mind.

children.text:
paśyed uṣṇodakaṃ yatra | vāsaṃ tatraiva kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.259)
children.translated_text: Where one sees hot water, one should take up residence right there. (RA 12.259)
There is [a river] named <s>Godāvarī</s>, very famous in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>;
in its northern part is <s>Sahyādri</s>, the holy mountain. (RA 12.260)
There is a well-known temple called <s>Mātāpura</s>.
To the north of that, O <s>Devī</s>, is the supreme city called <s>Kampā</s>. (RA 12.261)
There [resides] the god <s>Kampeśvara</s>; there exists perpetual hot water (<s>uṣṇodaka</s>),

children.text: praṇītākhyā nadī tatra | snātvā vai sādhakottamaḥ |
children.translated_text: and a river there called <s>Praṇītā</s>. Having bathed, the best practitioner
should then perform the procedure as prescribed in the hot-water pool. (RA 12.262)

children.text: śarvarīm uṣitastatra | dhanavāṃś ca dine dine |
children.translated_text: Having spent the night there, [becoming] wealthy day by day,
one should consume [it] for one month — one lives eight hundred years. (RA 12.263)
If one uses [it] for one year, one lives ten thousand years happily,
free from wrinkles and gray hair, an enjoyer, like <s>Indra</s> himself. (RA 12.264)
If one drinks the water for one year, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars;
by his urine and feces, copper becomes gold. (RA 12.265)
Hot water combined with vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>) and arsenic stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>),
with one-fourth part zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) — one should add ten parts [of copper]. (RA 12.266)

children.text: śulvaṃ ca mardayet sarvaṃ | naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ kṣaṇena tu |
children.translated_text: One should grind all the copper — [it becomes] a vanished paste instantly;
merely by coating with that, copper becomes gold. (RA 12.267)

children.text: niṣiktaṃ tena toyena | prativāpaṃ daded budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise one should give a supplementary charge (<s>prativāpa</s>) to [copper] quenched with that water;
copper becomes gold, having the luster of the young sun. (RA 12.268)
Quenched with that water, gold combined with seed-substance,

children.text:
tāraṃ cānena mārgeṇa | niṣiktaṃ hematāṃ vrajet ||
                    (RA_12.269)
children.translated_text: and silver by this method, when quenched, attains the state of gold. (RA 12.269)
With hot water, one should eat marking-nut (<s>bhallātaka</s>) and sesame paste;
by using [this] for two months, one lives three hundred years. (RA 12.270)
Mercury, sulfur, stone, zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>), vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>),
ground with hot water for three hours — one should coat silver foils [with this]. (RA 12.271)
Blown twice, O <s>Devī</s>, it becomes fourteen-<s>varṇa</s> [quality gold];
by this method, O Queen of the Gods, copper [becomes] sixteen-<s>varṇa</s>. (RA 12.272)
One part each of gold and silver, paired with lodestone and mica separately,
ground with hot water, by blowing, attains ingot-state. (RA 12.273)
If one holds that in the mouth for a month, a man becomes diamond-bodied (<s>vajrakāya</s>);
if one eats a grain-measure of that powder with honey and ghee,

children.text:
yāvat palaṃ tasya malaiḥ | śulvaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
                    (RA_12.274)
children.translated_text: with excretions up to one <s>pala</s>, copper becomes gold. (RA 12.274)
One should eat horse-gram (<s>kulattha</s>) cooked in hot water and become a milk-drinker [subsist on milk];
one should bathe with hot water — within a year, one attains a thousand-year lifespan. (RA 12.275)
One should cook milk with hot water and a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: pāyasaṃ kāntapātre tan | māsam ekaṃ tu bhakṣayet |
children.translated_text: [make] rice-pudding (<s>pāyasa</s>) in a lodestone vessel — one should eat that for one month;
having eaten, one lives a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, and a man attains the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (RA 12.276)
Now I shall describe the procedure for rock-water (<s>śailodaka</s>), O Beloved.
Mud-water, earth-rock, and stone — [these are the] four types. (RA 12.277)
Some [cause] transmutation in an instant, some in a day,
some [cause] transmutation in a fortnight, month, up to six months on this earth. (RA 12.278)

children.text: kṣiptaṃ yadā bhavet kāṣṭhaṃ | śailībhūtaṃ ca dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: When wood thrown [into it] is seen to become petrified,

children.text:
bahirantaś ca deveśi | vedhakaṃ tat prakīrtitam ||
                    (RA_12.279)
children.translated_text: both externally and internally, O Queen of the Gods — that is declared to be a transmuting [water]. (RA 12.279)

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ haritālaṃ ca | gandhakaṃ ca manaḥśilā |
children.translated_text: Cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) —

children.text:
eṣāṃ gandhāpahāraṃ yat | kurute tac ca vedhakam ||
                    (RA_12.280)
children.translated_text: whatever removes the odor of these — that too is a transmuting [water]. (RA 12.280)

children.text: gandhakaṃ tālakaṃ caiva | toyapūrṇe ghaṭe kṣipet |
children.translated_text: One should throw sulfur and orpiment into a water-filled pot;
when it [water] becomes bubble-shaped [effervescent], then it is rock-water;
otherwise it is merely covering (<s>veṣṭaka</s>), O <s>Devī</s> — that should not be taken, [being] worthless. (RA 12.281)
On <s>Śrīśaila</s>, at the edge of <s>Śrīvana</s> forest, on the rock-surface called <s>Paryaṅka</s>,
that [water] placed there transmutes in an instant; on the bank of the river <s>Bhagavatī</s>,

children.text:
ekāhe vedhakaṃ tatra | gokarṇe tu dinatrayam ||
                    (RA_12.282)
children.translated_text: it transmutes in one day; at <s>Gokarṇa</s>, in three days. (RA 12.282)
At <s>Bhadrāṅga</s> it transmutes in a day; at <s>Tristhalānta</s>, three days;
at <s>Dhāreśvara</s> it would be a fortnight; at <s>Varṣāpurī</s>, one day. (RA 12.283)

children.text: brahmeśvare māsikaṃ syāt | vyāghrapuryāṃ tu vāsaram |
children.translated_text: At <s>Brahmeśvara</s> it would be a month; at <s>Vyāghrapurī</s>, one day;

children.text: aghoreśe māsikaṃ tu | siṃhadvīpe tathā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: at <s>Aghoreśa</s>, a month; at <s>Siṃhadvīpa</s> likewise;
one day at <s>Brahmagiri</s>; at <s>Vindhya</s>, instant transmutation. (RA 12.284)
One day at <s>Mālyavanta</s>; instant [transmutation with] rock-water. (RA 12.285)
On the lovely mountain of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, on the bank of <s>Pampā</s>, [there is] grass-water;
to the west of that, O <s>Devī</s>, at a distance of two <s>yojanas</s>,
there is an earth-rock; on that mountain, [it effects] transmutation in three days. (RA 12.286)
On <s>Sahyācala</s>, in the city of the Goddess, in the vicinity of <s>Kṣīrakṣetra</s>,
rock-water transmutes at a crore[-fold ratio]; at <s>Durjadeśa</s> also, in one day;
at a lakh[-fold ratio is that] of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, in the city called <s>Gokula</s>. (RA 12.287)
Elsewhere also, wherever arises [water] born of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
there too [it is] ambrosia, there too [it is] the supreme virilifier (<s>vajrīkaraṇa</s>). (RA 12.288)
I shall now describe its origin — how practitioners know [it]. (RA 12.289)
From the body of <s>Varāha</s> [the Boar-form of Viṣṇu] who lifted the earth,

children.text:
yaḥ svedaḥ patitastasmāj | jātaṃ śailodakaṃ param ||
                    (RA_12.290)
children.translated_text: the sweat that fell from him — from that was born the supreme rock-water. (RA 12.290)

children.text: tanmukhe kṣaṇikaṃ jātaṃ | kroḍadeśe tu vāsaram |
children.translated_text: That [from] his face effects instant [transmutation]; from the chest-region, one day;

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ tryahavedhi syāt | māsavedhi tu pārśvayoḥ |
children.translated_text: from the two arms, three-day transmutation; from the sides, month-transmutation;
from the lower limbs, six months — all [ultimately] bear equal fruit. (RA 12.291)

children.text: aghorāstreṇa tatkṣetra- | rakṣāṃ kṛtvā diśāṃ balim |
children.translated_text: Having performed protection of that sacred site with the <s>Aghora</s>-weapon, and offering tribute to the directions,

children.text:
dattvā lakṣaṃ japitvā tu | gṛhṇīyādamṛtaṃ param ||
                    (RA_12.292)
children.translated_text: and having recited [mantras] a hundred thousand times, one should take the supreme ambrosia. (RA 12.292)
In autumn, summer, spring, or winter, O One Worshipped by the Gods,
in an iron or copper vessel, or in a vessel made of gourd,
one should place eight <s>palas</s> of rock-water and one <s>pala</s> of milk. (RA 12.293)
Having boiled down to the milk-remainder, a man should drink for twenty-one days;
he lives a thousand years, free from wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 12.294)
Or, eight <s>palas</s> of milk combined with one <s>pala</s> of [rock-]water,
one should take [when reduced to] the milk-remainder — one obtains the previously stated result. (RA 12.295)
One should cook horse-gram with eight times the water, reduced to one-eighth;
with four times that [liquid], one should cook ghee, reduced to ghee-remainder. (RA 12.296)
One should lick [this] combined with honey for twenty-one days, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;
within a month, attaining mastery of scriptures, knowing strength and weakness, O <s>Devī</s>,
[one becomes] having the appearance of a sixteen-year-old, with a thousand-year lifespan — no doubt. (RA 12.297)
The remaining horse-gram, at one-fourth portion with honey and ghee,
one should eat for one year — within a month, [one attains] a ten-thousand-year life. (RA 12.298)
With oil prepared from that [horse-gram], one should have anointing and massage performed;

children.text:
māsamekaṃ tato mardyaṃ | dehasiddhiṃ karoti ca ||
                    (RA_12.299)
children.translated_text: for one month one should be massaged — it effects perfection of the body (<s>dehasiddhi</s>). (RA 12.299)
It conquers suddenly scabs, eczema (<s>vicarcikā</s>), ringworm (<s>dadru</s>), and leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>);
one becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair and attains a thousand-year lifespan. (RA 12.300)
One who, rising in the morning, drinks three handfuls of rock-water,
in six months attains a thousand-year lifespan, free from wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 12.301)

children.text: athavā sūtakaṃ devi | vāriṇā saha mardayet |
children.translated_text: Or, O <s>Devī</s>, one should grind mercury with the [rock-]water;
in one month, O Queen of the Gods, it will become a vanished paste. (RA 12.302)
If one eats [that] for one month, one becomes free from old age and death. (RA 12.303)

children.text: athavā taṃ rasaṃ hemnā | hemabhasma tato balī |
children.translated_text: Or, that mercury with gold — then gold-ash, [made] potent,
one should grind with that water and blow with <s>khadira</s> [acacia] fire. (RA 12.304)
A pill [called] <s>Sundarī</s> [the Beautiful] — [it is] a repeller of all weapons;

children.text:
kartā hartā svayaṃ siddho | jīvec candrārkatārakam ||
                    (RA_12.305)
children.translated_text: [its possessor becomes] a creator, destroyer, self-perfected, and lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars. (RA 12.305)

children.text: kunaṭī cābhramākṣīkaṃ | hema tāraṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Kunaṭī</s>, mica, pyrite (<s>mākṣīka</s>), gold, and silver likewise,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ payasā kṣīrair | madyaṃ pācyaṃ dinatrayam |
children.translated_text: all that with milk — liquor should be cooked for three days;
by using for one month, [one becomes] free from wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 12.306)
Then with that very water, one should cook rice-pudding with half milk;
by using for one month, it destroys wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 12.307)

children.text: paktvā tenāmbhasā pathyāḥ | ṣaṣṭiṃ trīṇi śatāni ca |
children.translated_text: Having cooked with that water three hundred and sixty <s>pathyā</s> [<s>harītakī</s>] fruits,

children.text:
madhu saṃyojya bhāṇḍasthaṃ | bhūmau sarvaṃ nidhāpayet ||
                    (RA_12.308)
children.translated_text: combining with honey, placed in a vessel, one should bury everything in the ground. (RA 12.308)
Day by day, one at a time, one should eat [them] rising in the morning;
free from wrinkles and gray hair, one lives a thousand years. (RA 12.309)
One should eat petrified horse-gram with honey and ghee;
by consuming for six months, one lives a thousand years. (RA 12.310)

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ māritaṃ kṛtvā | yāni kāni phalāni ca |
children.translated_text: Having killed [prepared] a gourd (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>), and whatever fruits,
metals thrown into the water that become petrified — one should eat [them];
with a milk-diet after digestion, a man becomes diamond-bodied. (RA 12.311)
Grinding mica with that water, one should boil it, O Beloved;
eating [it] with the three pungents (<s>kaṭutraya</s>), one lives a thousand years. (RA 12.312)
Or, one <s>karṣa</s> of mercury — one should grind with that water,
place inside an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit, [immersed] in the midst of that rock-water;
in triple the time, hardness is produced in it. (RA 12.313)

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ tanmukhe dhāryaṃ | vajrakāyaṃ karoti ca |
children.translated_text: For six months, one should hold that in the mouth — it makes [one] diamond-bodied;
[one becomes] having the strength of ten elephants and rejoices with the gods. (RA 12.314)
Taking <s>triphalā</s>, one should immerse it in rock-water;

children.text:
yadā bhavati tacchailaṃ | gṛhītvā cūrṇayet tataḥ ||
                    (RA_12.315)
children.translated_text: when it becomes petrified, taking [it out], one should then powder it. (RA 12.315)
Mercury digested with lodestone, along with that [powder], saturated with ghee and honey,

children.text:
bhakṣayed varṣamekaṃ tu | tataḥ kṣīrāśano bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.316)
children.translated_text: one should eat for one year; then one should become a milk-subsister. (RA 12.316)
Resembling the rising sun, intelligent, pleasant to look upon,
with dark curly hair — one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars. (RA 12.317)

children.text: pāradaṃ haritālaṃ ca | śilā mākṣikameva ca |
children.translated_text: Mercury, orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>),

children.text:
daradaṃ ca viṣaṃ caiva | sarvamekatra kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.318)
children.translated_text: cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and poison — one should combine everything together. (RA 12.318)
One should grind on a mortar-stone with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice;
having made a ball (<s>golaka</s>), one should immerse it in water. (RA 12.319)

children.text:
tena tāraṃ ca śulvaṃ ca | kāñcanaṃ bhavati dhruvam ||
                    (RA_12.320)
children.translated_text: With that, silver and copper certainly become gold. (RA 12.320)
If one uses [it] for one month, free from wrinkles and gray hair,
a thousand years is his lifespan, [possessing] great strength and valor. (RA 12.321)
With petrified turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>) — merely by adding its powder,
lead attains gold-hood, having luster like the young sun. (RA 12.322)
Having placed [it] in mountain-water, or in earth-mountain mud,
knowing the measure of time, one should then bind the mercury. (RA 12.323)
Smelted with red alkali, and extracted with gold equally —
with a hundredth part, it makes all metals into gold. (RA 12.324)
Having attained the second extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>), one should consume [it] with honey and ghee.
At that time, the wind rises upward from those born of mind (<s>citta</s>). (RA 12.325)
Knowledge of time arises for him; he lives fifty thousand [years]. (RA 12.326)
Having attained the second extraction, it transmutes with a thousandth part.

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayed vaktre | divyatvaṃ labhate dhruvam ||
                    (RA_12.327)
children.translated_text: If one holds that alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) in the mouth, one certainly attains divinity. (RA 12.327)

children.text: nicule kakubhe caiva | kiṃśuke madhuke 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: In <s>nicula</s> (barringtonia), <s>kakubha</s> (arjuna tree), <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame tree), or <s>madhuka</s> (mahua),
or in the midst of an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit, or between the two turmerics — (RA 12.328)
one should grind mercury and sulfur into a pill-form;

children.text:
pācayed dinamekaṃ tu | hemnā saṃveṣṭya dhārayet ||
                    (RA_12.329)
children.translated_text: one should cook [it] for one day; wrapping [it] with gold, one should wear [it]. (RA 12.329)
Carefully wrapping [it] with a paste of <s>triphalā</s> and the three pungents (<s>vyoṣa</s>),

children.text: pādena kanakaṃ dattvā | pāradaṃ tatra yojayet |
children.translated_text: adding gold in one-quarter [proportion], one should combine mercury therein.
Placed in mountain-water, the pill becomes diamond-like. (RA 12.330)

children.text: pūrvavat sāraṇā kāryā | pūrvavat siddhidā bhavet |
children.translated_text: Extraction should be done as before; it becomes efficacious as before.

children.text:
dhāryamāṇā mukhe sā tu | sahasrāyuṣkarī bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.331)
children.translated_text: When held in the mouth, it grants a lifespan of one thousand years. (RA 12.331)
By the method of the second extraction, it transmutes ten thousand.
When held in the mouth, it grants a lifespan of ten thousand [years]. (RA 12.332)
By the method of the third extraction, it becomes a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter.

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayed vaktre | lakṣāyurjāyate naraḥ ||
                    (RA_12.333)
children.translated_text: If one holds that alloy in the mouth, the person attains a lifespan of a hundred thousand [years]. (RA 12.333)

children.text: caturthīṃ sāraṇāṃ prāpya | koṭivedho na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having attained the fourth extraction, it transmutes ten million — without doubt.
