His lifespan [extends to] ten million [years]; and the state of <s>khecara</s> (sky-wanderer) is attained. (RA 12.334)

children.text: pañcabhir daśakoṭiḥ syāt | ṣaḍbhiḥ koṭiśataṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: With the fifth, a hundred million; with the sixth, a billion.
[He lives] as long as the sun and moon endure — endowed with infinite strength and vigor. (RA 12.335)

children.text: dadāti saptamīṃ sāpi | sāraṇāṃ guṭikā parā |
children.translated_text: The supreme pill grants the seventh extraction as well.
[It is] renowned as <s>Khecarī</s> — impelled by <s>Bhairava</s> [himself]. (RA 12.336)

children.text: yas tu tadrājikāmātraṃ | māsamekaṃ tu bhakṣayet |
children.translated_text: One who consumes even a mustard-seed measure of that for one month —
he becomes a <s>Siddha</s> with a diamond-body, beloved of divine women.

children.text:
krīḍate khecarair bhogaiḥ | svec chayā śivatāṃ vrajet ||
                    (RA_12.337)
children.translated_text: He plays with the enjoyments of sky-wanderers, and by his own will attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 12.337)
Manifold are the fruits [obtainable] from its juices, seeds, and oils.

children.text:
tadbaddhaṃ pāradaṃ caiva | guṭikāṃ śṛṇu sundari ||
                    (RA_12.338)
children.translated_text: Now hear about that bound mercury and the pill, O Beautiful One. (RA 12.338)
The purely bound <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) — one should digest sulfur therein.

children.text:
triguṇe gandhake jīrṇe | tena hema tu kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.339)
children.translated_text: When sulfur is digested in triple [proportion], one should make gold with that. (RA 12.339)

children.text: kārayed bhasma sūtaṃ tu | kāñcanaṃ tatra sūtakam |
children.translated_text: One should reduce mercury to ash; that mercury [becomes] gold.

children.text:
tadbhasma sūtake jāryaṃ | rasendrasya same samam ||
                    (RA_12.340)
children.translated_text: That ash should be digested in mercury — equal to <s>Rasendra</s>, equally. (RA 12.340)
With that mercury in which [ash] is digested, one should digest a diamond gem.
That diamond becomes ash, resembling vermilion-red cinnabar. (RA 12.341)

children.text: tadbhasma jārayate sūte | triguṇe tu surārcite |
children.translated_text: That ash should be digested in mercury in triple [proportion], O one honored by the gods.

children.text:
hāṭake sārayet taṃ tu | guṭikāṃ tena kārayet ||
                    (RA_12.342)
children.translated_text: One should extract it in gold; with that, one should make a pill. (RA 12.342)

children.text: trilohāveṣṭitaṃ taṃ tu | mukhe prakṣipya sādhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Wrapped in the three metals, the practitioner should place that in the mouth.
With shadow vanished, he becomes invisible to gods and demons. (RA 12.343)

children.text: tat kṣaṇād vedhayed devi | sarvalohāni kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: In that instant, O Goddess, it transmutes all metals into gold.
For many thousands of years, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 12.344)
Bearing [an image of the] Trident-holder (<s>Śiva</s>) together with [his] <s>Śakti</s>, adorned with gems and other qualities —
one should wear [the pill] in the mouth or in the hand, for it wards off all weapons. (RA 12.345)
Mica (<s>vyoma</s>), the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), a silver-measure, the weapon of the gods (<s>surāyudha</s> = iron),
<s>vaikrānta</s>, orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), mercury — adorned with gem-qualities — (RA 12.346)
that pill, O Beautiful-hipped One, combined with the three sweets (honey, sugar, ghee),

children.text: vaktrasthā nāśayet sākṣāt | palitaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: placed in the mouth, directly destroys grey hair — there is no doubt in this.
O Goddess of the Gods, [it embodies] <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — just as gems and the like [contain the power of] <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 12.347)

children.text: hema tāraṃ tathā bhānuṃ | samabhāgāni kārayet |
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and sun[-gold] — make [them] in equal portions.
With menstrual blood, placed inside a tiger[-skin], wrap with a lotus-fiber. (RA 12.348)
Having wrapped it thus, pour [the preparation] and store in a secret place.

children.text: raṇe rājakule dyūte | divye kāmye jayo bhavet |
children.translated_text: In battle, in the royal court, in gambling, in divine and desired [endeavors] — victory results.

children.text:
yanmukhe caiva tadgolaṃ | sa sarvarañjako bhavet ||
                    (RA_12.349)
children.translated_text: In whose mouth is that ball — he becomes the charmer of all. (RA 12.349)
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, mica, lodestone, blue vitriol (<s>sasyaka</s>), and iron (<s>surāyudha</s>),
[combined with] the product of <s>vibhītaka</s> and the like — it becomes equal to fermented extract (<s>kāñcika</s>). (RA 12.350)
Then <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) should be combined with mercury in one-quarter proportion.
Rubbed with the juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), a single auspicious pill is made.
Placed in the mouth, it destroys disease, death, and old age — there is no doubt. (RA 12.351)
Five [parts] silver, O Beautiful-hipped One, and two of mercury,
three parts of mica, and one each of gold and lodestone — (RA 12.352)
with the method of half-copper — the pill, O Immortal Beauty,

children.text: akṣayo hy ajaraścaiva | bhavet tena mahābalaḥ |
children.translated_text: [grants that one becomes] imperishable, ageless, and greatly powerful,
freed from all diseases — one lives by holding [it] in the mouth. (RA 12.353)
One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury, one <s>pala</s> of killed lodestone,
one <s>pala</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and one <s>pala</s> of <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch); (RA 12.354)
one <s>pala</s> of <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), and one <s>pala</s> of <s>pathyā</s> (<s>harītakī</s>) powder —

children.text:
ekīkṛtyātha tat sarvaṃ | madhvājyena tu peṣayet ||
                    (RA_12.355)
children.translated_text: having combined all of these, one should grind [them] with honey and ghee. (RA 12.355)
One should make pills, O Goddess — three hundred and sixty.
One should consume one every day, continuously for one year. (RA 12.356)
One lives for thousands of years, mighty like <s>Rudra</s>. (RA 12.357)
Hereafter I shall describe the mercury-ash elixir (<s>rasa-bhasma-rasāyana</s>),
to be known as the supreme divine medicine, without drawbacks. (RA 12.358)

children.text: āmalakyādi kāntaṃ ca | pāradaṃ ca manaḥśilām |
children.translated_text: <s>Āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry) and the rest, lodestone, mercury, and realgar,
<s>vākucī</s> (Psoralea) in seven parts, ground with the juice of <s>kṣīriṇī</s> (a milky plant),
combined with the juice of <s>meghanāda</s> (thunder-plant), placed in a sealed crucible and heated. (RA 12.359)

children.text: māṣaṃ trimāṣaṃ triguṇaṃ | bhakṣayet tu krameṇa tu |
children.translated_text: One <s>māṣa</s>, three <s>māṣas</s>, tripled — one should consume progressively.
After three years, O Goddess, [the dose increases to] quarter-<s>niṣka</s>, half[-<s>niṣka</s>], progressively. (RA 12.360)

children.text: ṣaṭ saptāṣṭau ca varṣāṇi | kramān niṣkapramāṇataḥ |
children.translated_text: For six, seven, and eight years — progressively, in the measure of a <s>niṣka</s>.
One should eat divine food, free from old age and deformity. (RA 12.361)
Combined with some gold — a <s>niṣka</s> or half a <s>niṣka</s> —
one who consumes [it] for three years conquers all diseases fully. (RA 12.362)
In the eighth year, a thousand-year lifespan; in the twelfth, a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter.

children.text: ṣoḍaśe vatsare devi | divyarūpaḥ sa jāyate || (RA_12.363)
children.translated_text: In the sixteenth year, O Goddess, he attains a divine form. (RA 12.363)

children.text:
śatapalam abhayānām akṣadhātryos tathaiva | kvathitajalaśatāṣṭau
                    bhāgamaṣṭāvaśeṣam |
children.translated_text: A hundred <s>palas</s> of <s>abhayā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), and likewise of <s>akṣa</s> and <s>dhātrī</s> (the two myrobalans) — boiled [in] eight hundred [parts] water, reduced to an eighth;

children.text:
ghṛtamadhusitayāḍhyaṃ vyoṣacitraṃ daśāṃśaṃ | rasaphalarasasiddhaṃ lohajīrṇaṃ
                    mṛtaṃ ca || Ras_12.364 ||
children.translated_text: enriched with ghee, honey, and sugar, variegated with the three pungents and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) in one-tenth, perfected with the juice of mercury-fruit, [with metal-]digested and killed [mercury]. (RA 12.364)

children.text:
girijatusamamabhraṃ kāntabhṛṅgaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ | rasasahitasubhāvyaṃ taṇḍulair
                    divyamukhyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) in equal proportion, mica, lodestone, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia) — well-treated with mercury, with the finest divine rice-grains;

made into a paste with <s>ahimāra</s> (snake-killer plant), stored in an iron vessel for one <s>māṣa</s>, perfected [over] three days with thin [liquid] — this paste is the most excellent. (RA 12.365)
One who licks [it] at bedtime — devoted to the left eye[-ritual] — with firm, dense, and fine middle [body], with the pride of a maddened elephant,

children.text:
vigatasakaladoṣaḥ sarvadigdivyacakṣuḥ | madana iva sukāntiḥ kāminīnāṃ pravīraḥ ||
                    Ras_12.366 ||
children.translated_text: freed from all defects, with divine vision in all directions, with beauty like that of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), a champion among women — (RA 12.366)
With a body like a rain-cloud, with curling dark hair, pure like the preceptor of the gods, an excellent poet, a creator of marvels,

children.text:
vṛṣabhagativiceṣṭaḥ snigdhagambhīraghoṣaḥ | suragaja iva loke śrāntihantāśu
                    nityam || Ras_12.367 ||
children.translated_text: with the gait and movements of a bull, with a smooth and deep voice, like the divine elephant in the world — ever the dispeller of fatigue. (RA 12.367)

children.text:
prabhavati khalu loke somatārārkajīvī | kamalasadanasuśrīr nyāyaśāstrādivettā
                    |
children.translated_text: He truly flourishes in the world, living as long as the moon, stars, and sun endure, with the splendid beauty of one seated on a lotus, a knower of logic, <s>śāstra</s>, and the rest,

upholding the conduct of good people, an approver of <s>dharma</s>-initiation, profound like <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and [the cosmic] vastness, steadfast like the sun, the moon, and the ocean. (RA 12.368)
Lodestone, gold, sun[-gold], moon[-silver], and mica — [formed into] a ball and placed inside an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit,
[processed with] mountain-water — the excellent accomplished ball, beautiful, charming to the immortals, auspicious. (RA 12.369)
Lodestone, gold, sun[-gold], moon[-silver], mica, diamond gem, and a serpent-king ball —
placed inside a hollow in <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) wood, buried in mountain-earth and then retrieved,
having attained the nature of stone — when placed in the mouth, it makes the body diamond-like in a few days. (RA 12.370)
With orpiment, gold, fine copper, and mercury — a ball [prepared and] processed in <s>varaṇa</s> (Crataeva) wood apparatus,
with the juice of beautiful women made from mountain-water — this pill is called <s>Khecarī</s>. (RA 12.371)
A <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seed placed in mountain-water, rendered stone-like, should be eaten with honey and ghee,

children.text:
triḥsaptarātraṃ dinamekamekaṃ | sahasrajīvī vijayī naraḥ syāt
                    || (RA_12.372)
children.translated_text: for three-times-seven nights, one [pill] each day — [that] person becomes a thousand-year-liver, a conqueror. (RA 12.372)
Mercury and mica, combined with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> (euphorbia),
combined with gold — the pill becomes <s>Khecarī</s>. (RA 12.373)
Placed inside a <s>karañja</s> (Indian beech) fruit, one should deposit mercury therein.
[When] placed in ghee and mountain-water, it grants a lifespan of one thousand years. (RA 12.374)
In a <s>tinduka</s> (persimmon) — two thousand years; in a citron (<s>jambīra</s>) — three thousand;
in a <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) and in an orange (<s>nāraṅga</s>) — four and five thousand. (RA 12.375)
In a plantain fruit — six thousand; in a jackfruit (<s>panasa</s>) — seven thousand in number;
and in a <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia) fruit — ten thousand in number. (RA 12.376)
In a coconut, O Greatly Fortunate One — fourteen thousand.
In a lotus — thirty thousand; and in an <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) — a hundred thousand. (RA 12.377)
Mercury extracted from a decoction of mica leaf, [soaked] for one day and night in <s>śilā</s>-water (rock-water) —
the mercury drawn forth from that destroys death and poverty. (RA 12.378)
By the method of extraction and stepping-up, a new body is produced.

children.text:
rase rasāyane caiva | lakṣavedhī na saṃśayaḥ ||
                    (RA_12.379)
children.translated_text: In mercury and in the mercurial elixir — it becomes a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter, without doubt. (RA 12.379)

children.text: kardamaṃ ca kumāryāś ca | rasena kṛtagolakam |
children.translated_text: With the mud and juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), having formed a ball with mercury —

children.text: dhamanāt patate sattvaṃ | mukhe tad dhārayen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: From the blowing, the essence falls — a man should hold it in his mouth.
By [this] practice for six months, he attains agelessness and immortality. (RA 12.380)
The essence, blown with channel-collyrium (<s>srotoñjana</s>), mixed with mercury —

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayed vaktre | adṛśyo bhavati dhruvam ||
                    (RA_12.381)
children.translated_text: one should hold that alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) in the mouth — one becomes invisible, certainly. (RA 12.381)

children.text: yasya yo vidhir āmnāta | udakasya śivāgame |
children.translated_text: Whatever procedure has been taught for water in the <s>Śivāgama</s>,

children.text: rasenaiva tu kāle tu | kuryād eva rasāyanam || (RA_12.382)
children.translated_text: with mercury alone, at the [proper] time, one should perform <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (RA 12.382)
The glorious <s>Devī</s> said: (RA 13.1.1)

children.text: deva tvaṃ pāradendrasya proktā me bālajāraṇā / (RA_13.1.2)
children.translated_text: O God, you have taught me the <s>bālajāraṇā</s> (preliminary digestion) of the lord of mercury; (RA 13.1.2)
henceforth, describe properly the digestion of the bound [mercury]. (RA 13.1.3)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said: (13.2.1)
That which was described before is the inferior <s>bālajāraṇā</s> (preliminary digestion); (13.2.2)
the superior and rare one — hear [now about] <s>baddhajāraṇā</s> (bound digestion). (RA 13.2.3)

children.text:
abaddhaṃ jārayed yas tu jīryamāṇaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet /
                    (RA_13.3.1)
children.translated_text: He who would calcine unbound [mercury] — [that mercury,] being digested, goes to destruction; (RA 13.3.1)

children.text:
baddhasya jīryate grāso jīrṇasya ca mukhaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_13.3.2)
children.translated_text: but the food (<s>grāsa</s>) of the bound [mercury] is digested, and what is digested becomes its mouth (<s>mukha</s>). (RA 13.3.2)
The with-mouth (<s>sumukha</s>) and mouthless (<s>nirmukha</s>) [types] bear the characteristics of perfect excellence; (RA 13.4.1)
the ordinary [type], by [its] fire-resistance, digests great gems. (RA 13.4.2)

children.text: sāmānyaḥ prathamaṃ kāryaḥ sagrāsas tu susaṃmataḥ / (5.1)
children.translated_text: The ordinary [type] should be made first; with food, it is well-approved. (13.5.1)
The ordinary [type], O Goddess, becomes a bestower of golden bodies (<s>vasudeha</s>). (RA 13.5.2)

children.text: grāsahīnas tu yo baddho divyasiddhikaro bhavet // (RA_13.6)
children.translated_text: But bound [mercury] without food bestows divine perfection (<s>divyasiddhi</s>). (RA 13.6)
The best is root-binding (<s>mūlabandha</s>); the middling is mercury-binding (<s>rasabandhana</s>); (13.7.1)
the lowest is cooking-binding (<s>pākabandha</s>) — thus the threefold binding. (RA 13.7.2)

children.text:
mūlabandhana mūlabandhas tu yo bandho vāsanābandha ucyate /
                    (8.1)
children.translated_text: Root-binding: the binding that is root-binding is called fragrance-binding (<s>vāsanābandha</s>); (13.8.1)
from the sixty-four roots, binding [is effected] by some [particular] root. (RA 13.8.2)
The root-[substance] from the limbs of animals, demons, and the like — approved by the deities; (RA 13.9.1)

children.text:
pāṣāṇaṃ caiva siddhānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca pūjitam //
                    (RA_13.9.2)
children.translated_text: and the stone [substance] of the <s>siddhas</s> — [both are] honored among humans. (RA 13.9.2)
By pellet (<s>piṇḍikā</s>), fluid (<s>druti</s>), and contraction (<s>saṃkoca</s>), there are three types of binding. (RA 13.10.1)
With divine herbs (<s>divyauṣadhi</s>), the pure binding has been previously described. (13.10.2)
Instant-binding: mercury is bound by fluids — [this] is called instant-binding (<s>kṣaṇabandha</s>). (13.11)
Mica (<s>abhraka</s>) and <s>harabīja</s> (Śiva's seed = mercury), with gold in a sixteenth part, (13.12.1)
blown in an open crucible, should be purified with glass (<s>kāca</s>) and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). (RA 13.12.2)
Blown with rightward rotation, combined with <s>harabīja</s> (Śiva's seed), (RA 13.13.1)
having left the crucible, O beautiful-hipped one, the mercury stands as if bound. (RA 13.13.2)
With a mere half of half a <s>raktikā</s>, it would transmute even mountains. (RA 13.14.1)
By consuming it, O Queen of the Gods, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>. (RA 13.14.2)
He sports in the seven worlds, with prowess equal to <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 13.14.3)

children.text:
drutimelana mit divyauṣadhis drutīnāṃ melanaṃ devi
                    divyauṣadhiparaṃ śṛṇu // (15)
children.translated_text: Fluid-combination: listen, O Goddess, about the supreme [method of] combining fluids (<s>druti</s>) with divine herbs. (13.15)
<s>Vajrakanda</s> (diamond-tuber) and <s>lāṅgalī</s>, combined with <s>uccāṭa</s> (uprooting-plant) — (RA 13.16.1)

children.text:
abhrakaṃ kramate śīghram anyathā nāsti saṃkramaḥ //
                    (16.2)
children.translated_text: mica moves (is digested) quickly; otherwise, there is no transmutation (<s>saṃkrama</s>). (13.16.2)

children.text:
melana von druti und rasa
                    kṛṣṇāguruśaṅkhanābhīrasonasitarāmaṭhaiḥ / (17.1)
children.translated_text: Combining fluid and mercury: with black aloe (<s>kṛṣṇāguru</s>), conch-navel (<s>śaṅkhanābhi</s>), garlic (<s>rasona</s>), white <s>rāmaṭha</s>, (13.17.1)
combined with woman's menstrual fluid (<s>nārīkusuma</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (butea) and sesame oil, (RA 13.17.2)

children.text:
soṣṇair milanti kvathitā drutayaḥ sakalā rasaiḥ //
                    (RA_13.17.3)
children.translated_text: [when all are] warm and boiled, all the fluids (<s>druti</s>) combine with the mercury-juices. (RA 13.17.3)

children.text:
sarvadvandvamelāpana mākṣikaṃ ca viṣaṃ guñjā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ
                    strīrajastathā / (18.1)
children.translated_text: Combining all pairs: <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>guñjā</s> (abrus seed), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and woman's menstrual fluid (<s>strīrajas</s>) — (13.18.1)
smeared with woman's breast-milk, [this] combines all pairs (<s>dvandva</s>). (RA 13.18.2)
Combining metals and fluids: with <s>jīvāhi</s> (living-serpent plant), mica (<s>vyoma</s>), and minerals, well-treated with <s>kroṣṭujihvā</s> (jackal-tongue plant), (13.19.1)
[this is] the transmuting agent (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) for all metals and the combiner of fluids. (RA 13.19.2)
Ten-million-fold transmuting mercury: horse's saliva, garlic (<s>laśuna</s>), ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), and neem shoots (<s>nimbapallava</s>), (13.20.1)

children.text:
ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca rasaṃ vyoma vajraṃ cāpi praveśayet //
                    (RA_13.20.2)
children.translated_text: borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), mercury, mica (<s>vyoma</s>), and diamond (<s>vajra</s>) — one should introduce [them together]. (RA 13.20.2)
Mica, gold-fluid, and mercury — these three should be combined in one place. (RA 13.21.1)

children.text:
krāmaṇena tu mūṣāyāṃ lepaṃ dattvā vicakṣaṇaḥ /
                    (RA_13.21.2)
children.translated_text: With <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmuting agent), the discerning one should apply a coating in a crucible, (RA 13.21.2)
and by sweating with husk-fire on the ground, [they] combine instantly. (RA 13.21.3)
This becomes a hundred-fold transmuter in silver (<s>tāra</s>) and copper (<s>śulvaka</s>). (RA 13.22.1)

children.text:
tasya madhye tathā deyā abhrahemadrutiḥ punaḥ //
                    (RA_13.22.2)
children.translated_text: In its midst, one should add mica-gold-fluid again. (RA 13.22.2)
It should be sweated with husk-fire until only mercury remains; (RA 13.23.1)

children.text:
sahasravedhī sa bhavet nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
                    (RA_13.23.2)
children.translated_text: it becomes a thousand-fold transmuter — no deliberation is needed here. (RA 13.23.2)
With each successive binding (<s>saṃkala</s>), the transmutation increases tenfold. (RA 13.24.1)
Bound with seven successive bindings, the great mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 13.24.2)
When the discerning one would consume it for the body's sake — in the amount of one <s>guñjā</s>, (RA 13.25.1)
combined with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭu</s>) and three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>), with ghee and honey, (RA 13.25.2)

children.text:
jīrṇe jīrṇe tu saṃgrāhyaṃ yāvat syādaṣṭaraktikāḥ //
                    (25.3)
children.translated_text: as each [dose] is digested, one should take [the next], until [the dose reaches] eight <s>raktikās</s>. (13.25.3)
Mercury killed by successive bindings, from hundredfold to ten-million-fold — (RA 13.26.1)

children.text:
jīvet tena pramāṇena vajravallī yathā rasaḥ //
                    (RA_13.26.2)
children.translated_text: one lives in proportion to that [potency], like the <s>vajravallī</s>-mercury. (RA 13.26.2)
[Attaining <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood through fluids]
Mercury combined with the fluids of gold, mica, and copper, (13.27.1)
should transmute by the previously described method; consumed through all the [appropriate] combinations, (RA 13.27.2)
one attains the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, with prowess equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (RA 13.27.3)
[Rigidification of various metals]
The fluids from mica and gold, combined with mercury, (13.28.1)
by the addition of tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — rigidification (<s>stambhana</s>) [occurs] at a hundredth part, certainly. (RA 13.28.2)
Iron-calx (<s>tīkṣṇamāra</s>) and gold, combined with mercury, (RA 13.29.1)
by the addition of lead (<s>nāga</s>) — rigidification occurs at a hundredth part. (RA 13.29.2)

children.text:
tīkṣṇaṃ ghoṣaṃ tathā tāraṃ pāradena samanvitam /
                    (RA_13.30.1)
children.translated_text: Iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), bell-metal (<s>ghoṣa</s>), and silver (<s>tāra</s>), combined with mercury, (RA 13.30.1)
by the addition of tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — rigidification occurs at a hundredth part. (13.30.2)

children.text:
evaṃ hi drutiyogās tu vijñātavyā vidhānataḥ /
                    (RA_13.31.1)
children.translated_text: Thus, the fluid-combinations (<s>drutiyoga</s>) should be understood according to [proper] procedure. (RA 13.31.1)
By this fluid-combination, the mercury becomes a transformer of both body and metal. (RA 13.31.2)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said: (14.1.1)
I shall now describe another [method] — <s>vajrabandha</s> (diamond-binding), O Queen of the Gods. (RA 14.1.2)

children.text:
rasabandhana, -jāraṇa mit strīrajas gandhakaṃ bhakṣayen nārī
                    dinānāmekaviṃśatim / (2.1)
children.translated_text: [Mercury-binding and digestion with woman's menstrual fluid:] A woman should consume sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) for twenty-one days; (14.2.1)
her menstrual fluid (<s>rajas</s>) is beneficial for the binding and digestion of the king of mercury. (RA 14.2.2)

children.text: vajrabhasma tu bhāgaikaṃ bhāgāḥ śuddharasās trayaḥ / (3.1)
children.translated_text: One part diamond-calx (<s>vajrabhasma</s>) and three parts purified mercury — (14.3.1)

children.text:
dvipadī rajasāmardya yāvat tat kalkatāṃ gatam //
                    (RA_14.3.2)
children.translated_text: should be ground with the menstrual fluid of a <s>dvipadī</s> (woman) until it reaches a paste-like state. (RA 14.3.2)
With a quarter-part of gold, one should make a leaf-coating (<s>pattralepa</s>). (RA 14.4)
The juice of <s>vyomavallī</s> (sky-creeper), magnetite (<s>kānta</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), finely powdered, (RA 14.5.1)
with mica in an eighth part — placed in a mortar (<s>khalla</s>), one should grind. (RA 14.5.2)
The four [substances], ground to a vanished pellet (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>), having sealed [the crucible], one should then heat in a cycle; (RA 14.6.1)
blown in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>), combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmuting agent), (RA 14.6.2)

children.text: khoṭas tu jāyate devi śatavedhī mahārasaḥ // (RA_14.6.3)
children.translated_text: an alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) is produced, O Goddess — a great mercury, a hundred-fold transmuter. (RA 14.6.3)

children.text:
sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā viśodhayet /
                    (RA_14.7.1)
children.translated_text: Adding antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and glass (<s>kāca</s>) repeatedly, one should purify; (RA 14.7.1)

children.text: ajīrṇe milite hemnā samāvartas tu jāyate // (RA_14.7.2)
children.translated_text: when [the mercury] combines with gold without being fully digested, a circular form (<s>samāvarta</s>) is produced. (RA 14.7.2)
By successive bindings in increasing order, one should then apply <s>krāmaṇa</s>. (RA 14.8)
Successive bindings (<s>saṃkalikā</s>): with mercury equal [to the substance], one successive binding is called. (14.9.1)

children.text: triguṇena tu sūtena dvitīyā saṃkalī bhavet // (RA_14.9.2)
children.translated_text: With mercury in triple [proportion], the second successive binding occurs. (RA 14.9.2)

children.text: ṣaḍguṇena tu sūtena tṛtīyā saṃkalī bhavet / (RA_14.10.1)
children.translated_text: With mercury in sextuple, the third successive binding occurs. (RA 14.10.1)
With mercury in tenfold, the fourth successive binding occurs. (RA 14.10.2)
With fifteen-fold, O Goddess, the fifth successive binding occurs. (RA 14.11.1)
With twenty-one-fold, O Goddess, the sixth successive binding is recognized. (RA 14.11.2)
With twenty-eight-fold, O Goddess, the seventh successive binding is recorded. (RA 14.12.1)
Connected with thirty-six-fold, the eighth successive binding occurs. (RA 14.12.2)
With forty-five-fold, the ninth successive binding is recognized. (RA 14.13.1)
With fifty-five-fold, the tenth successive binding is recorded. (RA 14.13.2)
Thus, by progressive increase, [there are] ten successive bindings. (RA 14.14)

children.text:
vedhitva prathame daśavedhī syāt śatavedhī dvitīyake /
                    (15.1)
children.translated_text: Transmutation-power: In the first, it is a ten-fold transmuter; in the second, a hundred-fold transmuter. (14.15.1)
In the third, a thousand-fold transmuter; in the fourth, a ten-thousand-fold transmuter. (RA 14.15.2)

children.text:
pañcame lakṣavedhī syāt daśalakṣaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhake /
                    (RA_14.16.1)
children.translated_text: In the fifth, a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter; in the sixth, a million-fold. (RA 14.16.1)
In the seventh, a ten-million-fold transmuter; in the eighth, a hundred-million-fold. (RA 14.16.2)
In the ninth, [it transmutes by] smoke and sight; in the tenth, [it is] a sound-transmuter. (RA 14.17.1)

children.text:
saṃkalaiḥ saṃkalair baddho vedho daśaguṇo bhavet //
                    (17.2)
children.translated_text: With each successive binding, the transmutation becomes tenfold. (13.17.2)
Bound with ten successive bindings, the great mercury becomes a sound-transmuter. (RA 14.18.1)

children.text:
yathā lohe tathā dehe kramate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
                    (RA_14.18.2)
children.translated_text: As [it works] on metal, so [it works] on the body — there is no doubt about this. (RA 14.18.2)
One should transmute metals and the body in proportion to that [binding-level]. (RA 14.19.1)
One should make a divine pill the size of a jujube-stone. (14.19.2)
Having worshipped <s>Mahākālī</s>, the wise one should wear [it] constantly. (RA 14.20.1)

children.text:
tasya mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tridaśair api durlabham //
                    (20.2)
children.translated_text: I shall declare its mantra, difficult to obtain even for the gods. (14.20.2)
<s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), the seed of <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, then the seed of <s>Lakṣmī</s>. (RA 14.21)

children.text:
oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kālikā kāli mahākāli māṃsaśoṇitabhojini /
                    (22.1)
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kālikā Kāli Mahākāli</s>, O devourer of flesh and blood! (14.22.1)

children.text:
hrīṃ hrīṃ huṃ raktakṛṣṇamukhe devi rasasiddhiṃ dadasva me //
                    (22.2)
children.translated_text: <s>Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Huṃ</s>, O Goddess with a red-and-black face, grant me <s>rasasiddhi</s> (perfection in mercury)! (14.22.2)

children.text:
śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ramā śaktiś ca tārākhyo mantro'yaṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ
                    // (23)
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ</s> — <s>Ramā</s> [and] <s>Śakti</s>, and [that] called <s>Tārā</s> — this mantra bestows all perfections. (14.23)
Having worshipped the Goddess, and especially the <s>Siddhacakra</s> (circle of accomplished ones), (RA 14.24a)

children.text:
tāṃ kṣiped vaktramadhye tu guṭikāṃ divyarūpiṇīm //
                    (RA_14.24.2)
children.translated_text: one should place in the mouth that pill of divine form. (RA 14.24b)

children.text: śatavedhena yā baddhā rasena guṭikā priye / (RA_14.25.1)
children.translated_text: A pill bound with mercury at hundred-fold transmutation power, O beloved — (RA 14.25a)
kept in the mouth for one month, one lives to the end of a <s>Yuga</s>. (RA 14.25b)

children.text:
tathā sahasravedhena yā baddhā guṭikā śubhā /
                    (RA_14.26.1)
children.translated_text: Likewise, an auspicious pill bound at thousand-fold transmutation power — (RA 14.26a)
kept in the mouth for two months, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars [endure]. (RA 14.26b)
If a pill is bound at ten-thousand-fold transmutation power — (RA 14.27a)

children.text:
śakratulyaṃ tadāyuḥ syāt tribhir māsair varānane //
                    (27.2)
children.translated_text: then the lifespan becomes equal to <s>Śakra</s> (Indra's), in three months, O fair-faced one. (RA 14.27b)
A pill of divine form, bound at hundred-thousand-fold transmutation — (RA 14.28a)
kept in the mouth for four months, it grants the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>. (RA 14.28b)
A pill of divine form, bound at million-fold transmutation — (RA 14.29a)
kept in the mouth for five months, one obtains a lifespan equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s. (RA 14.29b)
A pill of divine form, bound at ten-million-fold transmutation — (RA 14.30a)

children.text:
ṣaṇmāsaṃ saṃsthitā vaktre sākṣādvai rudratāṃ nayet //
                    (30.2)
children.translated_text: established in the mouth for six months, it truly leads one to the state of <s>Rudra</s>. (RA 14.30b)
A pill of divine form, at the level of billion-fold transmutation — (RA 14.31a)

children.text:
saptamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā sa labhedaiśvaraṃ padam //
                    (31.2)
children.translated_text: kept in the mouth for seven months, one attains the station of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). (RA 14.31b)
A pill of <s>Śiva</s>'s form, bound at the level of smoke-perception (<s>dhūmāvalokana</s>) — (RA 14.32a)

children.text:
aṣṭamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā īśānasya phalaṃ labhet //
                    (RA_14.32.2)
children.translated_text: kept in the mouth for eight months, one attains the fruit of <s>Īśāna</s>. (RA 14.32b)
A pill of <s>Śiva</s>'s form, bound at the level of sound-transmutation (<s>śabdavedha</s>) — (RA 14.33a)

children.text:
navamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā sa bhavedvyāpako naraḥ //
                    (RA_14.33.2)
children.translated_text: kept in the mouth for nine months, that person becomes all-pervading. (RA 14.33b)
Bound by the nine <s>saṃkalikās</s> (chains), he becomes <s>Svayambhū</s> (self-born) or <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). (RA 14.34a)
He is the creator, the destroyer, the experiencer himself — the bestower of curses and blessings. (RA 14.34b)
Omniscient, the maker of all, of subtle form, untainted. (RA 14.35a)
By will he creates, by will he destroys the universe. (RA 14.35b)
Moving freely at will, that person becomes the universal form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>). (RA 14.36a)
He is worshipped by all the gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>. (RA 14.36b)
I shall now describe another [method] — the exceedingly rare diamond-binding (<s>vajrabandha</s>). (RA 14.37)

children.text:
vajrabandha samāṃśaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ hema śuddhasūtena kārayet /
                    (38.1)
children.translated_text: For the diamond-binding, one should make [the mercury] consume gold in equal proportion with pure mercury. (RA 14.38a)
Killed diamond (<s>mṛtavajra</s>), in one <s>pala</s>-proportion, should be ground with <s>Dvipadī</s> (bipedal plant) juice. (RA 14.38b)
The remainder, [prepared] as before and previously described, ground with <s>Haṃsapādī</s> [plant], (RA 14.39a)

children.text:
bhāvitaṃ puṭitaṃ ratnaiḥ pūrvavat saphalaṃ bhavet //
                    (39.2)
children.translated_text: treated and fired with gems as before — it becomes fruitful. (RA 14.39b)
One who is diamond-bound becomes accomplished, unconquerable by gods and demons. (RA 14.40a)
He becomes the leader of the twenty-four <s>Siddhas</s>, the bestower of all <s>siddhis</s>. (RA 14.40b)
Mercury equal in weight to diamond-powder should be ground with <s>Haṃsapādī</s> [plant]. (RA 14.41a)

children.text:
puṭitvā mārayet taṃ tu punas tulyaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet //
                    (41.2)
children.translated_text: Having fired it, one should kill it; then add equal [weight of] mercury again. (RA 14.41b)
When smelted, an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) quickly forms; purified with glass and borax, (RA 14.42a)
it becomes as resplendent as the rising [sun of] <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), O beloved. (RA 14.42b)

children.text:
vajrasattvaṃ ca gaganaṃ rasaṃ hema ca melayet /
                    (RA_14.43.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond-essence, mica, mercury, and gold should be combined. (RA 14.43a)
Kept in the mouth, one attains immortality, O chief of the gods. (RA 14.43b)

children.text: jārayitvā rasaṃ taddhi punas tenaiva jārayet / (44.1)
children.translated_text: Having calcined the mercury with that [substance], one should calcine again with the same. (RA 14.44a)

children.text:
koṭivedhī na saṃdeho vaktrasthaḥ khecaraṃ padam //
                    (RA_14.44.2)
children.translated_text: It becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter without doubt; kept in the mouth, [one attains] the station of <s>Khecara</s> (sky-rover). (RA 14.44b)
With that proportion, one should transmute both metal and the body. (RA 14.45a)
One should make a divine pill with diamond-accomplished [mercury] in gold. (RA 14.45b)
By this sequential method, one should kill [the mercury] as much as possible. (RA 14.46a)
That ash of mercury, O Goddess, destroys all diseases. (RA 14.46b)

children.text:
lohadehakrāmakaguṭikā hemnā ca sārayitvādau candrārkaṃ
                    lepayet tataḥ / (47.1)
children.translated_text: A pill that makes metals and the body traverse — having first extracted [it] with gold, one should then coat [it with] silver-and-gold [alloy]. (RA 14.47a)
At one-thirty-second proportion, half-gold, it becomes enhanced beyond the base measure. (RA 14.47b)
The wise one should make a pill the size of a <s>badara</s> (jujube) seed. (RA 14.48a)

children.text:
yathā lohe tathā dehe kramate nānyathā kvacit //
                    (RA_14.48.2)
children.translated_text: As [it traverses] metal, so [it traverses] the body — it works nowhere otherwise. (RA 14.48b)
Mercury-bound by diamond, paired with gold, combined with magnetite and copper — (RA 14.49a)
one should color [it] seven times; that ingot, finely powdered, (RA 14.49b)
treated with menstrual blood, combined with five <s>Guñjā</s> [measures], (RA 14.50a)
placed on a birch-bark leaf, and then bound in cloth as a packet, (RA 14.50b)
it should be sweated, O Goddess of Gods, until it becomes a globule. (RA 14.50c)
<s>Lāṅgalī</s> (glory lily), <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Mustā</s> (nut grass), and <s>Indravāruṇī</s> (colocynth) — (RA 14.51a)

children.text:
eteṣāṃ nikṣipet piṇḍe vajragolaṃ tu veṣṭayet //
                    (RA_14.51.2)
children.translated_text: the pellet should be placed among these and the diamond-globule should be wrapped. (RA 14.51b)
Having placed it in a crucible and sealed it carefully, (RA 14.52a)

children.text:
bhūmau mūṣāṃ vinikṣipya puṭaṃ mūrdhni pradāpayet //
                    (52.2)
children.translated_text: one should bury the crucible in the ground and give a firing on top. (RA 14.52b)
By this very process, the great mercury attains binding. (RA 14.53)

children.text:
golakaṃ dhārayed vaktre varṣamekaṃ yadi priye /
                    (RA_14.54.1)
children.translated_text: If one holds the globule in the mouth for one year, O beloved, (RA 14.54a)
one lives for thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages), like a great and powerful <s>Nāga</s> (serpent-deity). (RA 14.54b)

children.text:
varṣair dvādaśabhiḥ sākṣāt rudrarūpas tu jāyate /
                    (RA_14.55.1)
children.translated_text: In twelve years, one visibly becomes of <s>Rudra</s>'s form. (RA 14.55a)

children.text:
gātrasya tasya prasvedāt aṣṭau lohās tu kāñcanam //
                    (55.2)
children.translated_text: By the perspiration of his body, all eight metals become gold. (RA 14.55b)

children.text: Entfernen von grauen Haaren durch vajrabhasma
children.translated_text: [Removal of gray hair through diamond-ash:]
Diamond-ash and mercury, combined with gold — (RA 14.56a)

children.text:
vaktrasthaṃ kurute yas tu so 'bdāt palitavarjitaḥ //
                    (56.2)
children.translated_text: one who keeps [this] in the mouth, within a year, is freed from gray hair. (RA 14.56b)
[Ingot from mica etc. → longevity:]

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam / (57.1)
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, silver, copper, and gold, (RA 14.57a)
pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), magnetite (<s>kānta</s>), and iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — one should make these in equal portions. (RA 14.57b)
Placed in a sealed crucible and smelted, an ingot forms instantly. (RA 14.58a)

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam //
                    (RA_14.58.2)
children.translated_text: That ingot, finely powdered, [combined] with fluid mercury, [forms] a globule. (RA 14.58b)
One part of killed diamond and four parts of the globule — (RA 14.59a)
ground in a heated mortar, the mercury becomes ash (<s>bhasma</s>). (RA 14.59b)
One should kill [it] in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus through the sequence of seven chains (<s>saṃkalikā</s>). (RA 14.60a)

children.text:
guñjāmātraṃ tu tadbhasma madhvājyena tu lehayet //
                    (RA_14.60.2)
children.translated_text: One <s>guñjā</s>-measure of that ash should be licked with honey and ghee. (RA 14.60b)
Through application for one year, that person attains a lifespan of ten thousand [years]. (RA 14.61a)
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, of great strength and valor. (RA 14.61b)

children.text: tadbhasmapalam ekaṃ tu palaikaṃ gandhakasya ca / (62.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur, (RA 14.62a)
placed in a sealed crucible and smelted — an ingot forms instantly. (RA 14.62b)
One lives for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, like the mighty <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāmadeva). (RA 14.63a)
By his urine and excrement, the eight metals become gold. (RA 14.63b)
That ingot should then be colored with tin-mica-skull cup (<s>vaṅgābhrakakapālinā</s>). (RA 14.64a)
One should color it seven times — it becomes like saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) in hue. (RA 14.64b)
Having rolled it together with gold, processed by triple extraction (<s>sāraṇātraya</s>), (RA 14.65a)
with one-thousandth of that proportion, one should transmute all metals. (RA 14.65b)

children.text:
kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam /
                    (66.1)
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, silver, copper, and gold, (RA 14.66a)

children.text:
tīkṣṇaṃ ca baddhasūtaṃ ca mākṣikaṃ ca samanvitam //
                    (66.2)
children.translated_text: iron, bound mercury, and pyrite — combined together, (RA 14.66b)
placed in a sealed crucible and smelted — an ingot forms instantly. (RA 14.67a)
Having rolled it together with gold, processed by triple extraction, (RA 14.67b)
with one-hundredth proportion of that, one should effect the transmutation of copper. (RA 14.68a)
Divine gold is produced, fit for the ornaments of the gods. (RA 14.68b)
One part bound mercury, one part lead (<s>pannaga</s>), (RA 14.69a)
one part gold, and one part mica-and-magnetite — (RA 14.69b)

children.text:
ekīkṛtya tu taddhāmyaṃ rase jīrṇe tu jārayet /
                    (RA_14.70.1)
children.translated_text: having combined them all, [they] should be smelted; when [the mica] is digested in the mercury, one should calcine [it]. (RA 14.70a)
With one-hundredth proportion of that, one should effect the transmutation of copper. (RA 14.70b)
One part of bound mercury and one part of tin (<s>kuṭila</s>) — (RA 14.71a)
placed in a sealed crucible and smelted, an ingot forms instantly. (RA 14.71b)

children.text:
tasya khoṭasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgaikaṃ gandhakasya ca /
                    (72.1)
children.translated_text: One part of that ingot and one part of sulfur — (RA 14.72a)
placed in a sealed crucible and smelted until only tin remains. (RA 14.72b)
By this sequential method, having quenched the tin sextuple, (RA 14.73a)
by this sequential method, one should bear [i.e., apply] the lead sextuple. (RA 14.73b)
Then one should color that mercury with the skull-cup of iron and copper. (RA 14.74a)
One should color it carefully until it becomes saffron-like in hue. (RA 14.74b)
Having rolled it together with gold, processed by triple extraction, (RA 14.75a)

children.text:
śatāṃśe vedhayet śulvaṃ divyaṃ hema prajāyate //
                    (RA_14.75.2)
children.translated_text: at one-hundredth proportion, one should transmute copper — divine gold is produced. (RA 14.75b)
I shall now describe another [method] — the supreme fluid-preparation (<s>dravasaṃskāra</s>). (RA 14.76)
One should color purified gold with the skull-cup of iron and copper. (RA 14.77a)
One part of cooked seed and one part of fluid mercury — (RA 14.77b)
ground with a medium acid, a globule forms instantly. (RA 14.77c)
One part of killed diamond and four parts of the globule — (RA 14.78a)
ground in a heated mortar, the mercury becomes ash. (RA 14.78b)
Kill [the mercury] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> (mountain) apparatus by the sevenfold-chain procedure. (RA 14.79.1)

children.text:
tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt madhyamāmlena mardayet //
                    (79.2)
children.translated_text: That ash, again afterwards, should be ground with a medium sour [liquid]. (RA 14.79.2)
One should carefully apply three hundred and sixty firings (<s>puṭas</s>). (RA 14.80.1)
That ash becomes divine, resembling red lead (<s>sindūra</s>) in color. (RA 14.80.2)
With that, one should transmute silver — at a thousandth ratio, [it becomes] gold. (RA 14.81.1)
One part of killed diamond, sixteen parts of mercury. (RA 14.81.2)
Ground sequentially with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>; (RA 14.82.1)
kill [it] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus — it becomes ash instantly. (RA 14.82.2)
Even with a thousand blowings, when blown [in the furnace], it does not depart [i.e., remains stable]; (RA 14.83.1)

children.text:
īdṛśaṃ bhasmasūtaṃ ca dehe lohe ca yojayet //
                    (RA_14.83.2)
children.translated_text: such ash-mercury should be employed in the body and in metals. (RA 14.83.2)
[Editorial note: Use of this ash-mercury for copper transmutation.]

children.text: tadbhasmapalam ekaṃ tu palam ekaṃ tu gandhakam / (84.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulphur; (RA 14.84.1)
placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) and blown — an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) is produced instantly. (RA 14.84.2)
That ingot should then be colored by the <s>kāpāli</s>-sequence procedure; (RA 14.85.1)
by the triple extraction (<s>sāraṇātraya</s>) method, one should give transmutation of copper (<s>śulvavedha</s>). (RA 14.85.2)

children.text:
melana von bhasmasūta und nāga bhasmasūtapalaikaṃ ca palaikaṃ
                    pannagasya ca / (86.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Combination of ash-mercury and lead.] One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury and one <s>pala</s> of lead (<s>pannaga</s>); (RA 14.86.1)
by firing, an ash is produced, resembling red lead in color. (RA 14.86.2)

children.text:
tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścād gopittena tu mardayet /
                    (RA_14.87.1)
children.translated_text: That ash, again afterwards, should be ground with cow's bile (<s>gopitta</s>); (RA 14.87.1)
having placed it in a copper vessel, grind with an iron pestle. (RA 14.87.2)
Then cook on a gentle fire until there is union with lead. (RA 14.88)
[Editorial note: With this product, copper becomes gold.]
One part of that ash and one part of a gold ball; (RA 14.89.1)
having made them one and ground together, along with the penetrating agent (<s>krāmaṇa</s>); (RA 14.89.2)
with that, <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> [silver alloy] at a thousandth ratio [becomes] gold. (RA 14.90.1)
By this sequential procedure, tin-ash is produced. (RA 14.90.2)
With that, at a thousandth ratio, one should give transmutation of copper; (RA 14.91.1)
that copper becomes silver, resembling a conch, <s>kunda</s> flower, or the moon. (RA 14.91.2)

children.text:
śulbavedha mit mṛtapārada śvetābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca
                    kāntākāntaṃ tathāyasam / (92.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Copper transmutation with killed mercury.] The essence of white mica and <s>kāntākānta</s> (double-lodestone) and iron; (RA 14.92.1)

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ tathā śvetaṃ vaikrāntaṃ ca kadambakam //
                    (92.2)
children.translated_text: tin, silver, and white <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>kadamba</s> [alloy]; (RA 14.92.2)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an ingot like a conch or the moon [results]; (RA 14.93.1)

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam //
                    (RA_14.93.2)
children.translated_text: that ingot [ground to] fine powder, [combined] with melted mercury into a ball. (RA 14.93.2)
One part of killed diamond, four parts of the ball; (RA 14.94.1)
grind in a heated mortar — the mercury becomes ash. (RA 14.94.2)
Kill [it] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sevenfold-chain procedure; (RA 14.95.1)
then an ash is produced, resembling a conch, <s>kunda</s> flower, or the moon. (RA 14.95.2)

children.text:
tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palamekaṃ tu gandhakam /
                    (RA_14.96.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulphur; (RA 14.96.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an ingot is produced instantly. (RA 14.96.2)
Having revolved with silver, extracted by the triple extraction method; (RA 14.97.1)
with that, at a thousandth ratio, one should give transmutation of copper. (RA 14.97.2)
[Editorial note: Tin transmutation with mercury-ash (1).] Eight <s>palas</s> of iron-mercury, eight <s>palas</s> of melted mercury; (RA 14.98.1)
grind in a heated mortar with the juice of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>challī</s>. (RA 14.98.2)
Instantly a lump is produced — a ball [formed] with the iron; (RA 14.99.1)
grind in a heated mortar — it becomes ash instantly. (RA 14.99.2)
Kill [it] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sevenfold-chain procedure; (RA 14.100.1)
with that, at a sixteenth ratio, one should give transmutation of tin. (RA 14.100.2)
One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulphur; (RA 14.101.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an ingot is produced instantly. (RA 14.101.2)

children.text:
tasya khoṭasya bhāgaṃ ca tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ ca tatsamam /
                    (102.1)
children.translated_text: One part of that ingot and an equal [amount of] iron powder; (RA 14.102.1)

children.text:
dvau bhāgau drutasūtasya sarvam ekatra mardayet //
                    (102.2)
children.translated_text: two parts of melted mercury — grind everything together. (RA 14.102.2)

children.text:
taptakhalle tu saṃmardya golako bhavati kṣaṇāt /
                    (RA_14.103.1)
children.translated_text: Having ground in a heated mortar, a ball is produced instantly; (RA 14.103.1)
kill [it] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sevenfold-chain procedure. (RA 14.103.2)
All that becomes ash, resembling a conch, <s>kunda</s> flower, or the moon; (RA 14.104.1)

children.text:
tadbhasma kārayet khoṭaṃ tīkṣṇena dvaṃdvitaṃ saha //
                    (104.2)
children.translated_text: that ash should be made into an ingot, paired with iron. (RA 14.104.2)
By this sequential procedure, by the sevenfold-chain method; (RA 14.105.1)
that ash should then be calcined, extracted by the triple extraction method. (RA 14.105.2)
With that, at a <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred-thousand) ratio, one should give transmutation of tin; (RA 14.106.1)
one <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury should be coated on purified tin. (RA 14.106.2)

children.text:
mardayed āyase pātre vaṅgaṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt /
                    (RA_14.107.1)
children.translated_text: Grind in an iron vessel — the tin dies instantly; (RA 14.107.1)

children.text:
śulbavedha mit mṛtavaṅga dvipalaṃ mṛtavaṅgasya
                    tāracūrṇapaladvayam // (107.2)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Copper transmutation with killed tin.] Two <s>palas</s> of killed tin, two <s>palas</s> of silver powder; (RA 14.107.2)

children.text:
dvipalaṃ gandhakaṃ dadyāt palaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇasya ca /
                    (108.1)
children.translated_text: add two <s>palas</s> of sulphur and one <s>pala</s> of borax; (RA 14.108.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an ingot is produced instantly. (RA 14.108.2)
One <s>pala</s> of that ingot's powder and one <s>pala</s> of melted mercury; (RA 14.109.1)
grind with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice — a ball is produced instantly. (RA 14.109.2)
With that, at a sixteenth ratio, one should give transmutation of copper; (RA 14.110.1)
in place of tin, put lead; in place of silver, put gold. (RA 14.110.2)

children.text:
tārāriṣṭavedha pūrvavat kramayogeṇa rasaṃ khoṭaṃ tu kārayet
                    / (111.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Tārāriṣṭa</s> transmutation as before.] By the same sequential procedure, make the mercury into an ingot; (RA 14.111.1)

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam //
                    (111.2)
children.translated_text: that ingot [ground to] fine powder, [combined] with melted mercury into a ball. (RA 14.111.2)
With that, at a sixteenth ratio, one should transmute <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (silver alloy). (RA 14.112)
One <s>pala</s> of killed tin and one <s>pala</s> of mercury; (RA 14.113.1)
one <s>pala</s> of essence-powder — combine these three together. (RA 14.113.2)
Grind with citron juice — a ball is produced instantly. (RA 14.114)

children.text:
vaṅgastambhana mit mṛtavajra mṛtavajrasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgāś
                    catvāri golakam / (115.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Tin stabilization with killed diamond.] One part of killed diamond, four parts of the ball; (RA 14.115.1)
grind together in a mortar, combined with herbal juice. (RA 14.115.2)

children.text:
mārayed bhūdhare yantre puṭānāṃ saptakena tu /
                    (RA_14.116.1)
children.translated_text: Kill [it] in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with seven firings; (RA 14.116.1)

children.text:
tat sarvaṃ jāyate bhasma vajrasyaiva prabhāvataḥ //
                    (116.2)
children.translated_text: all that becomes ash, by the very power of the diamond. (RA 14.116.2)
Sea-salt and <s>triphalā</s>, O Goddess — add to the midst of the ash; (RA 14.117.1)
having made all into one and ground, [soak] in <s>vajrī</s> milk for three days. (RA 14.117.2)
Place in a <s>viśvāmitra</s>-skull [vessel] and fire in the <s>bhūdhara</s> [apparatus]; (RA 14.118.1)
all that becomes ash, resembling a conch, <s>kunda</s> flower, or the moon. (RA 14.118.2)
With that, merely a barley-grain's measure, tin is stabilized (<s>stambhita</s>) instantly; (RA 14.119.1)

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ tathā sattvaṃ samasūtena golakam // (119.2)
children.translated_text: tin, silver, and essence — [combine] with equal mercury into a ball. (RA 14.119.2)

children.text:
anena kramayogeṇa mārayec ca pṛthak pṛthak /
                    (RA_14.120.1)
children.translated_text: By this sequential procedure, one should kill [them] each separately; (RA 14.120.1)

children.text:
tat sarvaṃ jāyate bhasma vajrasyaiva prabhāvataḥ //
                    (120.2)
children.translated_text: all that becomes ash, by the very power of the diamond. (RA 14.120.2)
[Editorial note: Perfected mercury (?)] One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury and two <s>palas</s> of tin-ash; (RA 14.121.1)
two <s>palas</s> of killed silver and two <s>palas</s> of essence-ash; (RA 14.121.2)
five <s>palas</s> of conch-powder and eight <s>palas</s> of sea-salt; (RA 14.122.1)
eight <s>palas</s> of borax — grind everything together. (RA 14.122.2)
Having ground with <s>vajrī</s> milk, apply fourteen firings; (RA 14.123.1)
this is the perfected mercury (<s>siddharasa</s>) itself — rare even for the gods. (RA 14.123.2)

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ tu drāvayet paścāt bhāṇḍe caiva tu mṛnmaye /
                    (124.1)
children.translated_text: Then one should melt tin in an earthen vessel; (RA 14.124.1)
add the perfected ash and stir with a metal rod. (RA 14.124.2)

children.text:
vāpayec ca prayatnena yāvat kaṭhinatāṃ vrajet /
                    (RA_14.125.1)
children.translated_text: Sublimate carefully until it attains hardness; (RA 14.125.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — it becomes fine silver. (RA 14.125.2)

children.text: Herstellung von gutem Silber durch Beimischung von Zinn
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Production of good silver by addition of tin.]
Sometimes, when the silver is fired, one should add tin again; (RA 14.126.1)

children.text:
pattre dāhe kaṣe chede tattāraṃ śāśvataṃ bhavet //
                    (126.2)
children.translated_text: in the tests of foil, burning, touchstone, and cutting — that silver becomes permanent. (RA 14.126.2)

children.text: stambhitaṃ tat tu golaṃ ca ṣoḍaśāṃśasamanvitam / (127.1)
children.translated_text: That stabilized [tin], made into a ball, combined with a sixteenth part; (RA 14.127.1)
one part of killed diamond — grind together. (RA 14.127.2)
<s>Devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> — grind with their juice; (RA 14.128.1)

children.text:
mārayed bhūdhare yantre puṭānāṃ saptakena tu //
                    (RA_14.128.2)
children.translated_text: kill in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with seven firings. (RA 14.128.2)

children.text:
tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt dīpayantreṇa pācayet //
                    (RA_14.129)
children.translated_text: That ash, again afterwards, should be cooked in a lamp-apparatus (<s>dīpāyantra</s>). (RA 14.129)

children.text:
vaṅgastambhana mit bhasmasūta bhasmasūtapalaikaṃ ca
                    śvetābhrakapaladvayam / (130.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Tin stabilization with ash-mercury.] One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury and two <s>palas</s> of white mica; (RA 14.130.1)
one <s>pala</s> of conch-powder and one <s>pala</s> of borax; (RA 14.130.2)
having combined all that, grind with <s>vajrī</s> milk. (RA 14.130.3)
Then one should give fourteen firings (<s>puṭa</s>) with wild cow-dung cakes. (RA 14.131)
This mercury, in a grain-measure, stabilizes tin instantly. (RA 14.131)

children.text:
nāgavedha mit mṛtasūta kṛṣṇābhrakapalaikaṃ tu dve pale
                    mṛtasūtakam / (132.1)
children.translated_text: Lead transmutation: one <s>pala</s> of killed mica (<s>kṛṣṇābhraka</s>), two <s>palas</s> of killed mercury, (RA 14.132)
and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur — combining [these], one should then grind. (RA 14.132)
Diligently ground, it becomes a ball instantly. (RA 14.133)
One part of killed diamond (<s>mṛtavajra</s>) and four parts of the ball — (RA 14.134)
one should grind for one <s>prahara</s> [three hours] — the mercury becomes ash. (RA 14.134)
With wild cow-dung alone, one should give a firing on [level] ground. (RA 14.135)
By this graduated method, perform [this] seven cycles. (RA 14.135)
With that very [preparation], one should effect lead transmutation at one-hundredth ratio. (RA 14.136)
Then one should color that ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) with copper-mica powder (<s>śulvābhrakakapālin</s>). (RA 14.136)
Again, one should color it afterwards with iron-copper powder (<s>tīkṣṇaśulvakapālin</s>); (RA 14.137)
again, one should color it afterwards with lead-mica powder (<s>nāgābhrakakapālin</s>). (RA 14.137)
Revolving with gold, extracted through triple extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>), (RA 14.138)
with that very [preparation], one should effect copper transmutation at one-thousandth ratio. (RA 14.138)
Divine gold is produced — the supreme ornament of the gods. (RA 14.139)

children.text:
candrārkarañjana mit vajrabhasma vajrabhasma snuhīkṣīre
                    puṭitaṃ daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ / (140.1)
children.translated_text: Moon-and-sun coloring: diamond-ash, fired ten times in <s>snuhī</s> [euphorbia] milk — (RA 14.140)

children.text:
tattulyaṃ mardayet sūtaṃ devadālyā rasaiḥ puṭet //
                    (140.2)
children.translated_text: one should grind an equal amount of mercury, [then] fire with <s>devadālī</s> juice. (RA 14.140)

children.text:
tattulyaṃ ca puṭettīkṣṇaṃ triphalāyā rasena tu /
                    (RA_14.141.1)
children.translated_text: An equal amount of iron should be fired with <s>triphalā</s> juice; (RA 14.141)
an equal amount of lead should be fired with <s>mahimā</s>, <s>rāṭa</s>, and <s>rūṣaka</s> [herbs]. (RA 14.141)
That indeed bestows gold-color, combined at one-twentieth proportion; (RA 14.142)
at one-sixty-fourth proportion, this colors pure silver. (RA 14.142)
With that at one-eighth proportion, one should coat lead foils; (RA 14.143)
one should fire and kill the lead [until it becomes] resembling red <s>sindūra</s> [vermilion]. (RA 14.143)
An equal amount of gold should be killed, [then] fired in <s>kāñcanāra</s> juice; (RA 14.144)
an equal amount of copper should be killed with <s>gṛhakanyā</s> [aloe vera] juice. (RA 14.144)
Afterwards, one should fire with acid until it resembles vermilion; (RA 14.145)

children.text:
candrārkaṃ rañjayet tena śatāṃśena tu vedhayet //
                    (145.2)
children.translated_text: with that, one should color the moon-and-sun [silver and gold] — one should transmute at one-hundredth ratio. (RA 14.145)

children.text: sabījaṃ bījavarjaṃ vā vajreṇa saha sūtakam / (146.1)
children.translated_text: With or without seed, mercury together with diamond — (RA 14.146)
that ash one should then grind with gold-leaf juice. (RA 14.146)

children.text:
tenaiva vedhayecchulvaṃ śulvaṃ tāre tu yojayet //
                    (RA_14.147)
children.translated_text: With that one should transmute copper; [then] one should combine copper with silver. (RA 14.147)

children.text:
vajreṇa dvaṃdvayed dhema hemnā ca dvaṃdvayed rasam /
                    (148.1)
children.translated_text: One should pair diamond with gold; with gold one should pair mercury; (RA 14.148)

children.text:
rasena dvaṃdvayed dehaṃ sa deho hy ajarāmaraḥ //
                    (RA_14.148.2)
children.translated_text: with mercury one should pair the body — that body indeed becomes free from old age and death. (RA 14.148)
Unification of all pairs: plaintain stem (<s>kadalīkanda</s>), antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), saturated with nightshade (<s>kaṇṭakārī</s>) juice — (RA 14.149)
[this is] the penetrating agent (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) for all metals, [effecting] unification in all binary [combinations]. (RA 14.149)
Gold pairing: all five parts of <s>timira</s> [a plant], combined with <s>mārjārī</s>-seed — (RA 14.150)
combining and grinding together, one should transmute the diamond with that very [paste]. (RA 14.150)
Placed in a diamond-crucible and blown, one should effect the gold pairing. (RA 14.151)

children.text:
vajramelāpaka, tejaspuṅkha (?) kāntapāṣāṇacūrṇaṃ tu bhūlatā
                    rāmaṭhaṃ madhu / (152.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond unification, luster-feather (?): lodestone powder, <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>rāmaṭha</s> [asafoetida], and honey, (RA 14.152)
<s>guñjā</s>, borax, glass, crab bones, and <s>snuhī</s> [euphorbia] milk. (RA 14.152)

children.text:
etat sarvaṃ samaṃ yojyaṃ strīstanyena ca mardayet /
                    (153.1)
children.translated_text: All these should be combined in equal parts, ground with woman's breast-milk; (RA 14.153)
applied as crucible-coating, at the end, the diamond unification [is achieved] successfully. (RA 14.153)
In intense fire, in a diamond-crucible, hard diamonds unite; (RA 14.154)

children.text:
susūkṣmā rajakā bhūtvā hy ekībhāvaṃ vrajanti te //
                    (154.2)
children.translated_text: becoming very fine colorants, they merge into oneness. (RA 14.154)
By the combination of glass and borax, when blown, [the diamond] attains purity; (RA 14.155)
with many crucibles, a mass of luster (<s>tejaḥpuñja</s>) is produced. (RA 14.155)

children.text:
vajrahemamelana mṛtavajrasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa hāṭakam
                    / (156.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond-gold unification: one part of killed diamond, sixteen parts of gold, (RA 14.156)

children.text:
śvetakācasya cūrṇaṃ tu bhāgān ṣoḍaśa dāpayet //
                    (RA_14.156.2)
children.translated_text: and sixteen parts of white glass powder — one should add [these]. (RA 14.156)
Placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) and blown, one should effect diamond-binding; (RA 14.157)
by this graduated method, one should perform seven rounds. (RA 14.157)

children.text:
milate tatkṣaṇaṃ vajraṃ hemnā tu salilaṃ yathā //
                    (157.3)
children.translated_text: The diamond unites with gold instantly, like water. (RA 14.157)

children.text:
vajrahemamelana cūrṇe narakapālasya mṛtavajraṃ tu dāpayet /
                    (158.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond-gold unification: in the powder of a human skull, one should add killed diamond; (RA 14.158)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown, it unites with gold instantly. (RA 14.158)

children.text:
vajrahemamelana bhṛṅgapakṣaṃ nṛkeśaṃ ca mṛtakāntaṃ
                    saṭaṅkaṇam / (159.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond-gold unification: wasp-wing, human hair, killed lodestone with borax, (RA 14.159)
and dung of a young calf — one should grind with woman's breast-milk. (RA 14.159)

children.text:
mūṣālepaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vajre hema ca dāpayet /
                    (RA_14.160.1)
children.translated_text: Then making a crucible-coating, one should add diamond and gold; (RA 14.160)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — the diamond unites, not otherwise. (RA 14.160)

children.text:
vajrahemamelana kāntaṃ vajraṃ tathā guñjā gandhakaṃ ca
                    catuṣṭayam / (161.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond-gold unification: lodestone, diamond, <s>guñjā</s>, and sulfur — [these] four, (RA 14.161)

children.text:
stanakṣīreṇa piṣṭaṃ tu mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet //
                    (RA_14.161.2)
children.translated_text: ground with breast-milk — one should make a crucible-coating. (RA 14.161)
Placed in a sealed crucible and blown, the diamond unites instantly. (RA 14.162)
Liquid-binding: killed diamond should be steeped with milk of the northern <s>vāruṇī</s>; (RA 14.163)
in the midst of a gold-cake, one should place the diamond. (RA 14.163)
One should wrap with birch-bark (<s>bhūrjapatra</s>), and wrap externally with cloth; (RA 14.164)
it should be placed continuously in the midst of grain for one fortnight. (RA 14.164)

children.text:
uddhṛtaṃ tat prayatnena vajrabandhaṃ tu kārayet /
                    (165.1)
children.translated_text: Extracting that carefully, one should effect diamond-binding; (RA 14.165)

children.text:
drutā vajrās tu tenaiva melanīyās tu pārvati //
                    (RA_14.165.2)
children.translated_text: melted diamonds should then be united with that very [preparation], O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 14.165)
That should be known as liquid-binding (<s>drutabandha</s>) — [it] transmutes at a hundred-thousand[-fold] ratio. (RA 14.166)

children.text:
ratnānāṃ tu tathā sarvān vedhayitvā yathāvidhi /
                    (RA_14.167.1)
children.translated_text: Having similarly transmuted all gems according to proper method, (RA 14.167)
[this] hundred-thousand-fold transmuter bestows perfection of the body (<s>dehasiddhi</s>). (RA 14.167)
Gem-melting and mercury-unification: <s>musalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vandhyākarkoṭī</s>, <s>kandapadminī</s>, (RA 14.168)
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>nīlasindūrī</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>nāgabalā</s> likewise. (RA 14.168)
The juices of these, and the melted [essences] of the gems, [placed] in a bronze vessel, (RA 14.169)
holding [them] in sunlight, one should make fire below. (RA 14.169)

children.text:
oṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ kṛtvā svacchaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ /
                    (170.1)
children.translated_text: Having made the juice of the herbs, clarifying again and again, (RA 14.170)

children.text:
yāmamātraṃ ca gharme tu drutirmilati vai rasam //
                    (170.2)
children.translated_text: in three hours in the heat, the liquid [gem] indeed unites with mercury. (RA 14.170)

children.text:
na teṣāṃ krāmaṇaṃ śakyaṃ vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api //
                    (RA_14.171)
children.translated_text: The penetration of those [gems] cannot be described even in a hundred years. (RA 14.171)
Rock salt, neem (<s>nimba</s>) leaves, <s>vākucī</s>, wrapped in a reed — (RA 14.172)
unification with the melted mica-juice is considered supreme. (RA 14.172)
Diamond pairs [with everything], O Goddess; diamond kills mercury; (RA 14.173)
[this] is called killing with seed, and also ingot-binding. (RA 14.173)

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi kim anyac chrotum icchasi //
                    (RA_14.174)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 14.174)
Chapter 15
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said: (RA 15.1)
With the great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>), auxiliary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>), and metals, O Supreme Lord, (RA 15.1)
command the complete binding of the king of mercury. (RA 15.1)
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said: (RA 15.2)

children.text:
vedha mit vaikrānta vaikrāntasya tu bhāgaikaṃ cāṣṭabhāgaṃ tu
                    sūtakam / (2.2)
children.translated_text: Transmutation with <s>vaikrānta</s> [a type of tourmaline]: one part of <s>vaikrānta</s> and eight parts of mercury, (RA 15.2)
one-seventh of gold, <s>dvipadī</s> juice, and borax. (RA 15.2)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavet priye /
                    (3.1)
children.translated_text: Ground to a vanished paste and dried, blown, it becomes an ingot, O Beloved; (RA 15.3)

children.text:
sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet //
                    (RA_15.3.2)
children.translated_text: adding antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), borax, and glass, one should repeatedly purify. (RA 15.3)
Revolving with equal gold, [placing] the mercury in a crucible, then (RA 15.4)
one should make that [undergo] equal-measure consumption with pure mercury. (RA 15.4)
One should blow <s>vaikrānta</s> at one-sixteenth proportion by the previous method; (RA 15.5)
by the process of ten cycles (<s>saṃkalikā</s>), the transmutation [increases] tenfold. (RA 15.5)
By the process of seven cycles, the transmutation [increases] tenfold; (RA 15.6)

children.text:
vaikrānto vajravat jñeyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
                    (RA_15.6.2)
children.translated_text: <s>vaikrānta</s> should be known as [equivalent to] diamond — no deliberation is needed here. (RA 15.6)

children.text:
punar anyaṃ pravakṣyāmi prayogaṃ bhuvi durlabham //
                    (RA_15.6.3)
children.translated_text: I shall now describe another procedure, rare on earth. (RA 15.6)
<s>Vaikrānta</s> calcination (?): the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, O Queen of the Gods, combined with mercury, (RA 15.7)
calcined with equal gold — one should deposit in a stone vessel. (RA 15.7)
Having stayed one month buried in the ground, [then] carefully extracted, (RA 15.8)

children.text: eṣa devi raso divyo dehadravyakaro bhavet // (RA_15.8.2)
children.translated_text: this, O <s>Devī</s>, is the divine mercury — it effects the body-substance [transformation]. (RA 15.8)

children.text: vaikrāntakās tu ye kecit triphalāyā rasena ca / (9.1)
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>vaikrāntas</s> [there are], with <s>triphalā</s> juice, (RA 15.9)
with <s>bhūmyāmalaka</s> essence and <s>vasuhaṭṭa</s> juice, (RA 15.9)
each one, O <s>Devī</s>, steamed for seven days and ground likewise, (RA 15.10)
well-blown in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>) — the ingot becomes imperishable. (RA 15.10)

children.text:
kāntaṃ rūpyaṃ sakanakaṃ pāradaṃ caiva yojayet /
                    (RA_15.11.1)
children.translated_text: One should combine magnetite (<s>kanta</s>), silver (<s>rupya</s>), gold, and mercury; (RA 15.11.1)
copper in a third part, combined with channel-collyrium (<s>srotojnjana</s>); (RA 15.11.2)

children.text:
tat dhmātaṃ khoṭatāṃ yāti dehalohakaraṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_15.11.3)
children.translated_text: when blown, it reaches the state of an alloy (<s>khota</s>) and becomes a transformer of body and metal. (RA 15.11.3)

children.text: śvetavaikrānta -> agnisaharasa -> vedha, gegen jarā etc.
children.translated_text: [White <s>vaikranta</s> -> fire-resistant mercury -> transmutation, against aging etc.]
White <s>vaikranta</s> powder should be ground with horse urine; (15.12.1)

children.text:
ādau susvinnam ādāya pale palaśataṃ kṣipet //
                    (RA_15.12.2)
children.translated_text: having first well-steamed [it], one should add one hundred <s>palas</s> per <s>pala</s>. (RA 15.12.2)
A calx of silver is produced, with the appearance of pure crystal; (RA 15.13.1)
that calx, the discerning one should combine with mercury in equal proportion. (RA 15.13.2)
One should make silver move (digest) in mercury, ground with horse urine; (RA 15.14.1)
heated in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamusa</s>), gradually with gentle fire. (RA 15.14.2)
Combined with <s>kramana</s> (transmuting agent), the discerning one [places it] inside a crucible; (RA 15.15.1)
for one day and night, or three nights — the mercury becomes fire-resistant. (RA 15.15.2)
By [mere] touch, it will turn all metals into silver; (RA 15.16.1)
when consumed in the manner to be described, it destroys old age and poverty. (RA 15.16.2)
The procedure of the red [<s>vaikranta</s>] will be described — it destroys old age and poverty. (15.17.1)
Its powder should be treated seven times with the water of <s>vyaghri</s>-tuber. (15.17.2)

children.text:
palaṃ tasya palaṃ hemnaḥ palaṃ śuddharasasya ca /
                    (RA_15.18.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that, one <s>pala</s> of gold, and one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury — (RA 15.18.1)

children.text:
śuddhaṃ bhasma bhavet sarvaṃ punarhemaśataṃ kṣipet /
                    (18.2)
children.translated_text: all becomes purified calx; then one should add a hundred [parts] gold; (15.18.2)
that calx is produced quickly, with lustre equal to pure gold. (RA 15.18.3)

children.text:
tadbhasma rasarāje tu punarhemnā ca melayet /
                    (RA_15.19.1)
children.translated_text: That calx, in the king of mercury, should again be combined with gold; (RA 15.19.1)
it becomes fire-resistant, O Goddess — then the mercury becomes supreme. (RA 15.19.2)
The mercury becomes a touch-transmuter; the great mercury, a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 15.20)

children.text: raktavaikrāntasattvaṃ ca hemnā tu saha melayet / (21.1)
children.translated_text: The essence of red <s>vaikranta</s> should be combined with gold; (15.21.1)

children.text:
samaṃ taṃ jārayet sūtaṃ sārayitvā samena tu /
                    (RA_15.21.2)
children.translated_text: equally, one should calcine that mercury; having extracted [it] equally, (RA 15.21.2)
with a thousandth part, one should transmute metals — there is no doubt here. (RA 15.21.3)
[Black <s>vaikranta</s> -> alloy -> transmutation of all metals]
One part black <s>vaikranta</s> and a <s>pala</s>-part of purified mercury — (15.22.1)

children.text:
ekatra mardayet khalle cūrṇaṃ ca bhavati dvayam //
                    (RA_15.22.2)
children.translated_text: one should grind together in a mortar; the two become powder. (RA 15.22.2)
One part of this powder and a thousand parts of gold — (RA 15.23.1)

children.text:
ekatra mardayet tāvad yāvad bhasma tu jāyate //
                    (RA_15.23.2)
children.translated_text: one should grind together until calx is produced. (RA 15.23.2)
One should blow that in a sealed crucible until an alloy (<s>khota</s>) forms. (RA 15.24)
For consumption, one should add purified mercury in equal proportion to that; (RA 15.25.1)
it transmutes all metals by mere touch, O <s>Parvati</s>. (RA 15.25.2)
[Freshly prepared substance -> transmutation of all metals]

children.text: taccūrṇam abhrakaṃ caiva rasena saha mardayet / (26.1)
children.translated_text: That powder and mica should be ground together with mercury; (15.26.1)

children.text:
ekatra mardayet tāvad yāvad bhasma prajāyate //
                    (RA_15.26.2)
children.translated_text: one should grind together until calx is produced. (RA 15.26.2)

children.text:
dhamet tad andhamūṣāyāṃ yāvat khoṭo bhaviṣyati /
                    (RA_15.27.1)
children.translated_text: One should blow that in a sealed crucible until an alloy forms; (RA 15.27.1)

children.text:
samāṃśaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ tasya piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ //
                    (27.2)
children.translated_text: the wise one should make a pellet (<s>pistika</s>) for consumption, in equal proportion to that. (15.27.2)
It transmutes all metals into gold by mere touch. (RA 15.28.1)
[Freshly prepared substance -> transmutation of all metals]

children.text: taccūrṇam abhrakaṃ caiva rasena saha mardayet // (28.2)
children.translated_text: That powder and mica should be ground together with mercury. (15.28.2)
One should steam and calcine — then it becomes fire-resistant; (RA 15.29.1)

children.text:
sa rasaḥ sāritaś caiva sarvalohāni vidhyati //
                    (RA_15.29.2)
children.translated_text: that mercury, extracted, transmutes all metals. (RA 15.29.2)

children.text:
pīta = rakta, kṛṣṇa pītavarṇe'pi vaikrānte raktakṛṣṇavidhir
                    mataḥ // (30)
children.translated_text: [Yellow = red, black:] For yellow-colored <s>vaikranta</s> too, the procedure for red and black is prescribed. (15.30)
Yellow <s>vaikranta</s> powder, combined with gold powder, (RA 15.31.1)
with the powder of yellow mica, having combined — the great mercury, (RA 15.31.2)
steamed and ground, within a month becomes a fire-resistant mercury. (RA 15.31.3)

children.text:
śvetaṃ pītaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ raktavarṇaṃ tathaiva ca /
                    (32.1)
children.translated_text: White, yellow, black, and red-colored — (15.32.1)
thus <s>vaikranta</s> is of four varieties in color, O beautiful-complexioned one. (RA 15.32.2)

children.text:
vajrasthāne tu vaikrānto melanaṃ paramaṃ matam /
                    (RA_15.33.1)
children.translated_text: In place of diamond, <s>vaikranta</s> is considered the supreme combiner; (RA 15.33.1)

children.text: dehalohakaro yaś ca pārado lauhavat priye // (RA_15.33.2)
children.translated_text: the mercury that transforms both body and metal [becomes] like iron, O beloved. (RA 15.33.2)
Blue-colored <s>vaikranta</s>, combined with mercury, is killed. (RA 15.34)
That which is combined with honey and ghee — (15.35.1)
one should consume [it] for a <s>mandala</s> (cycle of days), O Goddess — one lives as long as the sun, moon, and stars. (RA 15.35.2)

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo yogaḥ tasya tasya prayogataḥ / (36.1)
children.translated_text: Whatever combination is prescribed for whatever [substance], by the application of that, (15.36.1)
having combined mercury in the measure of one <s>gunja</s>, with the three sweets (<s>trimadhura</s> = honey, ghee, sugar), (RA 15.36.2)
wholesome food of milk, ghee, and rice should be eaten; other food should be avoided. (RA 15.37)
In solitude, seated on a cot, a man free from attachments, (RA 15.38.1)
should always recite the <s>rasa-mrtyunjaya</s> (mercury-death-conquering) mantra in the heart-interior; (15.38.2)

children.text:
paśūnāṃ vimukhastatra strīṇāṃ caiva na darśanam /
                    (RA_15.38.3)
children.translated_text: turning away from animals there, and not looking at women; (RA 15.38.3)
with the entire body smeared with ash, devoted to mantra and meditation, (RA 15.38.4)
a mortal man continues for a year — his perfection is without doubt. (RA 15.38.5)
[Mercury-binding -> seeing holes in the earth]
Mercury combined with <s>vaikranta</s>-essence should be ground in lime-acid (<s>lungamla</s>); (15.38.6)
one should heat with lukewarm heating and fill with water. (RA 15.38.7)

children.text:
sattvaṃ sūtaṃ ca saṃmiśrya dhamet syād rasabandhanam /
                    (39.1)
children.translated_text: Having mixed the essence and mercury, one should blow — mercury-binding occurs. (15.39.1)

children.text:
baddhaṃ rasaṃ mukhe kṣiptvā bhūmichidrāṇi paśyati //
                    (39.2)
children.translated_text: Having placed the bound mercury in the mouth, one sees holes in the earth [i.e., hidden treasures]. (15.39.2)

children.text: niṣkam ekaṃ ca vaikrāntam aśvamūtreṇa mardayet / (40.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>niska</s> of <s>vaikranta</s> should be ground with horse urine (15.40.1)
for one day, O Goddess — having ground [it], it becomes killed. (RA 15.40.2)
Having done this for four days, one should add equal mercury; (RA 15.41.1)
grinding and steaming as before, with a pure mind. (RA 15.41.2)
Seven pairs, each one [weighing] seven or eight <s>palas</s> — (RA 15.42.1)
one should grind with citron juice and give sixty-four heating-cycles. (RA 15.42.2)
Resembling the rising dawn in color, it transmutes all metals. (RA 15.42.3)

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca rasaṃ hemasamaṃ bhavet / (43.1)
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica and mercury, becoming equal to gold, (15.43.1)
placed in a diamond-crucible (<s>vajramusa</s>) and blown — reaches the state of an alloy. (RA 15.43.2)

children.text:
baddhaṃ rasaṃ mukhe kṣiptvā hy ajarāmaratāṃ vrajet //
                    (RA_15.44)
children.translated_text: Having placed the bound mercury in the mouth, one attains agelessness and immortality. (RA 15.44)
Having mixed calx with that very [substance], it becomes equal to black mica; (RA 15.45.1)

children.text:
eben hergest. Produkt (?) -> bandhana, Verzehr ->
                        koṭivedhirasa
children.translated_text: [Freshly prepared product (?) -> binding, consumption -> ten-million-fold transmuting mercury]
with the water of <s>salya</s>-<s>visalya</s> root, one should grind for a day. (15.45.2)
Placed inside a <s>bhramara</s> (bee) apparatus, the heating-cycle lasts seven days. (15.46.1)

children.text:
tacchuddhaṃ bhasma sevyaṃ syāt guñjāmānaṃ tu maṇḍalam //
                    (46.2)
children.translated_text: That purified calx should be consumed — in the measure of one <s>gunja</s>, for a <s>mandala</s> [of days]. (15.46.2)
