Starting from one, the middle is five, then one again — this is recommended; (RA 15.47.1)
by binding as before, O Goddess, the great mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 15.47.2)
[Transmutation with magnetite:] Red-colored magnetite, with lustre like lac-juice, (15.48.1)
when split, resembling woman's blood — that powder, combined with mercury, (RA 15.48.2)
should be ground with goat's blood; blown, it becomes an alloy, O beloved. (RA 15.48.3)

children.text:
sa sūtaḥ śatavedhī tu sarvavyādhiharo bhavet /
                    (RA_15.49.1)
children.translated_text: That mercury becomes a hundred-fold transmuter and a destroyer of all diseases; (RA 15.49.1)
one should hold the pill in the mouth — one lives for a thousand years. (RA 15.49.2)
Yellow-colored magnetite, when split, with lustre equal to gold — (RA 15.50.1)
transmutes all metals into gold by mere touch, O beautiful one. (RA 15.50.2)

children.text: rasakhoṭa -> schrittweiser vedha bis hin zu Gold
children.translated_text: [Mercury-alloy -> stepwise transmutation up to gold]
<s>Langali</s>, oleander (<s>karavira</s>), leadwort (<s>citraka</s>), <s>girikarnnika</s>, (15.51.1)
woman's breast-milk, borax (<s>tanka</s>), and antimony (<s>sauvira</s>) — one should make a crucible-coating. (RA 15.51.2)
Bismuth (<s>capala</s>) in double [proportion to the coating], mercury double the bismuth, gold double the mercury — (RA 15.52.1)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu tat kuryāt andhamūṣāgataṃ dhamet //
                    (RA_15.52.2)
children.translated_text: one should make [it into] a vanished-pellet (<s>nastapista</s>) and blow in a sealed crucible. (RA 15.52.2)

children.text:
tatra sthito rasendro'yaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ /
                    (RA_15.53.1)
children.translated_text: The king of mercury stationed therein becomes a beautiful alloy; (RA 15.53.1)

children.text:
śatāṃśaṃ vedhayen nāgaṃ guñjāvarṇas tu jāyate //
                    (RA_15.53.2)
children.translated_text: at a hundredth part, one should transmute lead — it becomes <s>gunja</s>-colored. (RA 15.53.2)
With a hundredth part of that lead, copper becomes red-hued; (RA 15.54.1)
with a hundredth part of that copper, silver is transmuted into gold. (RA 15.54.2)

children.text: capalasya tu ṣaḍbhāgāḥ tārabhāgās tu sapta ca / (55.1)
children.translated_text: Six parts of bismuth (<s>capala</s>), seven parts of silver (<s>tara</s>), (15.55.1)

children.text:
aṣṭau kanakabhāgās tu nava bhāgā rasasya tu //
                    (RA_15.55.2)
children.translated_text: eight parts of gold, and nine parts of mercury — (RA 15.55.2)
thirty parts combined together, O one honored by the gods. (RA 15.56)

children.text:
citrakaṃ karavīraṃ ca lāṅgalī gṛdhraviṭ tathā /
                    (RA_15.57.1)
children.translated_text: Leadwort (<s>citraka</s>), oleander (<s>karavira</s>), <s>langali</s>, and vulture's excrement (<s>grddhravit</s>), (RA 15.57.1)
ground in citron juice — one should make a crucible-coating. (RA 15.57.2)
Having sealed and blown, O Goddess, a beautiful alloy forms; (RA 15.58.1)
with a hundredth part of that alloy, the transmuted lead becomes dawn-colored. (RA 15.58.2)

children.text:
tena nāgena viddhaṃ tu śulvaṃ guñjānibhaṃ bhavet /
                    (RA_15.59.1)
children.translated_text: With that lead, the transmuted copper becomes <s>gunja</s>-colored; (RA 15.59.1)

children.text:
tena śulvena tāraṃ tu viddhaṃ bhavati kāñcanam //
                    (RA_15.59.2)
children.translated_text: with that copper, the transmuted silver becomes gold. (RA 15.59.2)

children.text: hemābhaṃ capalaṃ devi pādārdhena tu saṃyutam / (60.1)
children.translated_text: Gold-colored bismuth (<s>capala</s>), O Goddess, combined with a half-quarter, (15.60.1)

children.text:
pādena kanakaṃ dattvā kunaṭyā mardayet kṣaṇam //
                    (RA_15.60.2)
children.translated_text: with a quarter of gold added, one should grind momentarily with <s>kunati</s>. (RA 15.60.2)
<s>Langali</s>, leadwort (<s>citraka</s>), woman's breast-milk, oleander (<s>karavira</s>), (RA 15.61.1)

children.text:
gṛdhraviṣṭhā tathā sarvaṃ mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet //
                    (RA_15.61.2)
children.translated_text: vulture's excrement — all [of these] should be made into a crucible-coating. (RA 15.61.2)

children.text:
tanmadhye tu sthitaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ /
                    (62.1)
children.translated_text: Placed within [the crucible] and smelted, a beautiful ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) forms. (RA 15.62a)

children.text:
pūrvoktaṃ vedhayed etaṃ nirbījaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_15.62.2)
children.translated_text: One should transmute it as previously described — seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) gold results. (RA 15.62b)

children.text:
rasabandha sutapte lohapātre ca kṣipec ca palapūrṇakam /
                    (63.1)
children.translated_text: For mercury-binding: in a well-heated iron vessel, one should place one <s>pala</s> [of mercury]. (RA 15.63a)

children.text: sabījaṃ pāradaṃ kṛtvā capalasya tu vāpayet / (RA_15.63.2)
children.translated_text: Having made the mercury seeded (<s>sabīja</s>), one should add <s>Capala</s> (bismuth). (RA 15.63b)
The mercury is bound, lac-colored, like a great elephant [captured] by an elephant. (RA 15.63c)
One <s>pala</s> of pure mercury and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur — (RA 15.63d)
having combined them, grinding with the juice of <s>Dhuttūra</s> (datura), (RA 15.63e)
one should treat by the wheel-method (<s>cakrayoga</s>) — the mercury becomes ash (<s>bhasma</s>). (RA 15.63f)
Placed in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) and smelted, a beautiful ingot forms. (RA 15.64a)

children.text:
sūtaṃ hema ca nāgaṃ ca candrārkau cāpi vedhayet //
                    (RA_15.64.2)
children.translated_text: Mercury, gold, and lead — and [the ingot] transmutes silver-and-gold alloy. (RA 15.64b)
One <s>pala</s> of pure mercury and one <s>karṣa</s> of sulfur — (RA 15.65a)
one should grind in a smooth mortar, flooded with <s>Devadālī</s> juice. (RA 15.65b)

children.text:
mardayet tu karāṅgulyā gandhapiṣṭis tu jāyate //
                    (RA_15.65.3)
children.translated_text: Grinding with the finger, a sulfur-cake (<s>gandhapiṣṭi</s>) is produced. (RA 15.65c)
With fresh lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) juice, one should grind for one day. (RA 15.66a)
Then with a decoction of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) root, one should grind for three days. (RA 15.66b)
One should make an auspicious tablet (<s>vaṭikā</s>) combined with the five fluxes (<s>pañcadrāvaka</s>). (RA 15.67a)
That tablet should be coated with <s>palāśa</s> root-paste. (RA 15.67b)
When smelted, a white ingot forms; with glass and borax, (RA 15.68a)
one should purify it carefully until it attains clarity. (RA 15.68b)

children.text:
tatkhoṭaṃ rañjayed devi triguṇaṃ pannagaṃ tataḥ /
                    (RA_15.69.1)
children.translated_text: That ingot should be colored, O Goddess; then with triple lead (<s>pannaga</s>), (RA 15.69a)
one should color it a hundred times with purified mica-skull cup. (RA 15.69b)

children.text:
śulve tāre ca khoṭo'yaṃ sahasrāṃśena vedhakaḥ /
                    (RA_15.70.1)
children.translated_text: This ingot transmutes copper and silver at one-thousandth proportion. (RA 15.70a)

children.text:
ghoṣavedha gandhakena hate sūte mṛtalohāni vāhayet //
                    (70.2)
children.translated_text: [For] sound-transmutation (<s>ghoṣavedha</s>): in mercury killed with sulfur, one should add killed metals. (RA 15.70b)
Rolling [it] with gold again, in equal proportion, make [it] consume [the gold]. (RA 15.71a)

children.text:
jārite śulvatāre ca ghoṣaṃ vidhyati sūtakaḥ //
                    (RA_15.71.2)
children.translated_text: When [the gold] is calcined, the mercury transmutes copper and silver with a sound. (RA 15.71b)
Having made the mercury equal to gold, with half the sulfur-cake amount of sulfur, (RA 15.72a)
combined with <s>Dvipadī</s> (bipedal plant) menstrual blood, one should grind with borax. (RA 15.72b)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca tat śulvaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavet tataḥ /
                    (73.1)
children.translated_text: That [forms a] vanished-cake (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>) with copper; smelted, an ingot results. (RA 15.73a)

children.text:
sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet //
                    (73.2)
children.translated_text: Adding <s>sauvīra</s> (antimony), borax, and glass, one should purify repeatedly. (RA 15.73b)

children.text: akṣīṇo milate hemni samāvartas tu jāyate / (RA_15.74.1)
children.translated_text: Undiminished, it merges with gold; a rolling (<s>samāvarta</s>) is produced. (RA 15.74a)
In equal proportion with gold, one should make [the mercury] consume with pure mercury. (RA 15.74b)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca tacchulvaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavet tataḥ /
                    (75.1)
children.translated_text: That copper [forms a] vanished-cake; smelted, an ingot results. (RA 15.75a)
Combined with <s>Dvipadī</s> menstrual blood, one should grind with borax. (RA 15.75b)
At one-sixteenth proportion of silver-and-gold, the transmuted [product] becomes gold. (RA 15.76a)

children.text:
hemārdhaṃ militaṃ tat tu mātṛkāsamatāṃ vrajet //
                    (RA_15.76.2)
children.translated_text: That, merged with half-gold, attains equality with the base measure. (RA 15.76b)
By the chain-method (<s>saṃkalikāyoga</s>), one should effect transmutation ten-fold greater. (RA 15.77a)
As with gold, so with silver — one should apply the seed-principles from the beginning. (RA 15.77b)
[For] the eight-metal gold-transmutation: bound by the third chain, one should transmute at one-six-hundredth proportion. (RA 15.78a)
With four times that, at one-thousandth proportion — [it becomes] gold. (RA 15.78b)
By this sequential method, if seven chains [are accomplished], (RA 15.79a)
it makes all eight metals into divine gold, O beautiful one. (RA 15.79b)
[Further processing of the product → longevity, divinity:]

children.text:
taṃ punaś cūrṇayitvā tu puṭedbhasma prajāyate /
                    (80.1)
children.translated_text: That, powdered again and fired, becomes ash. (RA 15.80a)
It destroys all diseases, O Goddess, when one <s>pala</s> of it is consumed. (RA 15.80b)
With two <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>; with three <s>palas</s>, the [lifespan] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (RA 15.81a)

children.text:
catuḥpale tu rudratvam īśaḥ pañcapale bhavet //
                    (RA_15.81.2)
children.translated_text: With four <s>palas</s>, the state of <s>Rudra</s>; with five <s>palas</s>, one becomes <s>Īśa</s>. (RA 15.81b)
When six <s>palas</s> are consumed, O Goddess, one attains the body of <s>Sadāśiva</s>. (RA 15.82)

children.text:
vaṅgastambhana sūtakaṃ gandhakaṃ tāraṃ meṣavallīrasena ca /
                    (83.1)
children.translated_text: [Tin-stabilization:] Mercury, sulfur, silver, and <s>Meṣavallī</s> (ram-creeper) juice — (RA 15.83a)
one should grind for three days with iron, then combine with one-quarter part of tin. (RA 15.83b)
Placed in a sealed crucible and smelted, it stabilizes tin instantly. (RA 15.83c)
Powdered sulfur, O Goddess, treated with <s>Markaṭī</s> (monkey-plant) juice — (RA 15.84a)

children.text:
bhāvayec chatavārāṃs tu jīvabhasma tu gacchati //
                    (RA_15.84.2)
children.translated_text: one should treat [it] a hundred times; it then attains the state of living ash (<s>jīvabhasma</s>). (RA 15.84b)

children.text: dīpayen mṛnmaye pātre rasena saha saṃyutam / (RA_15.85.1)
children.translated_text: One should heat in an earthen vessel, combined with mercury, (RA 15.85a)
heated by sun-heat, combined with <s>Markaṭī</s> juice. (RA 15.85b)

children.text:
gandhakaṃ grasate sūtaḥ piṣṭikā bhavati kṣaṇāt //
                    (RA_15.85.3)
children.translated_text: The mercury swallows the sulfur — a cake (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) forms instantly. (RA 15.85c)
[Sulfur-cake preparation:] With <s>Tilaparṇī</s> (sesame-leaf plant) juice alone, one should treat the sulfur, O beloved — (RA 15.86a)

children.text:
sapta vārāṃs tu deveśi chāyāśuṣkaṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
                    (RA_15.86.2)
children.translated_text: seven times, O Goddess, shade-dried each time. (RA 15.86b)
Purified and distilled mercury, measured at one <s>pala</s>, O beloved, (RA 15.87a)
placed in a crucible, combined with <s>Narendrarasa</s> (king's mercury/realgar), (RA 15.87b)
one should calcine in a sand-apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>); [add] the treated sulfur again. (RA 15.87c)

children.text:
truṭitruṭi pradātavyaṃ gandhakaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ /
                    (RA_15.88.1)
children.translated_text: Sulfur should be given bit by bit (<s>truṭi truṭi</s>), again and again. (RA 15.88a)
By this sequential method, a sulfur-cake (<s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s>) is produced. (RA 15.88b)

children.text:
gandhapiṣṭikā gandhapāṣāṇacūrṇaṃ tu kanakasya rasena tu /
                    (89.1)
children.translated_text: [Sulfur-cake application:] Sulfur-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>) powder with the juice of gold — (RA 15.89a)
having combined all, ground in a mortar according to procedure, (RA 15.89b)

children.text: ātape sthāpayed devi kanakasya rasena tat // (RA_15.89.3)
children.translated_text: one should place it in the sun, O Goddess, with the juice of gold. (RA 15.89c)

children.text:
bhāvayet saptavārāṃs tu strīpuṣpeṇa tu saptadhā /
                    (RA_15.90.1)
children.translated_text: One should treat it seven times, and with woman's menstrual blood (<s>strīpuṣpa</s>) seven times. (RA 15.90a)
One <s>pala</s> of pure mercury should then be given to calamine (<s>kharpara</s>). (RA 15.90b)
Treated sulfur should be given, combined with human bile. (RA 15.91a)
Swinging [it] by sun-heat, a cake forms instantly. (RA 15.91b)
Sulfur, finely powdered, with gram-acid (<s>caṇakāmla</s>), O <s>Bhairavī</s> — (RA 15.92a)

children.text:
bhāvayet saptavārāṃs tu strīpuṣpena ca saptadhā //
                    (RA_15.92.2)
children.translated_text: one should treat it seven times, and with woman's menstrual blood seven times. (RA 15.92b)
In the midst of fluid mercury, camphor (<s>karpūra</s>) and sulfur in equal [measure] — (RA 15.93a)
one should add and place in a cowshed; after seven days, a sulfur-cake [results]. (RA 15.93b)
The seed of <s>Kaṭukośātakī</s> (bitter sponge-gourd) and the tuber of <s>Caṇḍālī</s> (wild plant) — (RA 15.94a)
ground with breast milk, one should coat the cake with that [paste]. (RA 15.94b)

children.text:
puṭayed bhūdhare yantre stambhate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
                    (RA_15.95.1)
children.translated_text: Firing in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus, it becomes stabilized — of this there is no doubt. (RA 15.95a)
In a gold container, one should make a rolling (<s>samāvarta</s>). (RA 15.95b)
With one-eighth proportion of that, one should give transmutation of lead. (RA 15.96a)
That lead becomes divine, resembling vermilion in color. (RA 15.96b)
With that lead, at one-eighth proportion, one should give transmutation of copper. (RA 15.97a)
At one-sixteenth proportion of that, one should give transmutation of silver. (RA 15.97b)
That silver becomes gold — [this is] the view of the accomplished <s>Yogeśvarī</s>. (RA 15.98)

children.text:
nāgamāraṇa mit gandhapiṣṭi gandhapiṣṭipalaikaṃ tu
                    nāgapiṣṭipalāṣṭakam / (99.1)
children.translated_text: [Lead-killing with sulfur-cake:] One <s>pala</s> of sulfur-cake and eight <s>palas</s> of lead-cake — (RA 15.99a)
one should coat the lead-leaves [with the paste] and then dry in the shade. (RA 15.99b)
With a pellet of <s>Āṭarūṣaka</s> (Malabar nut), one should coat the lead-leaves. (RA 15.100a)
In wild cow-dung cakes, O Goddess, one should give three firings. (RA 15.100b)
That lead is killed divinely, resembling vermilion in color. (RA 15.101)
[Further processing of lead-ash → gold:]
One <s>pala</s> of that lead and eight <s>palas</s> of copper powder — (RA 15.102a)
one should grind with <s>Vāsaka</s> (Malabar nut) juice for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours). (RA 15.102b)
One should kill [them] in a distillation apparatus — the copper dies instantly. (RA 15.102c)
At one-sixteenth proportion of that, one should give transmutation of silver. (RA 15.103a)
Divine gold is produced, supreme [among] ornaments for the gods. (RA 15.103b)

children.text: yā kācid gandhapiṣṭī tu ādau nāgaṃ tu mārayet / (104.1)
children.translated_text: Whatever sulfur-cake [one has] — first one should kill lead; (RA 15.104a)

children.text:
nāgaṃ tu vedhayecchulvaṃ śulvaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet /
                    (104.2)
children.translated_text: the lead should transmute copper; the copper should transmute silver. (RA 15.104b)
Divine gold is produced — [this is] the declared accomplished method (<s>siddhayoga</s>). (RA 15.104c)
Sulfur combined with honey, ground with <s>Harabīja</s> (Śiva's seed) — (RA 15.105a)
buried in the ground for six months — silver becomes gold. (RA 15.105b)
Rubbing with that [substance] destroys skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). (RA 15.106a)
Combined with ghee, it destroys wound-diseases. (RA 15.106b)
Through application for one year, that person attains a lifespan of a thousand [years]. (RA 15.106c)

children.text:
kramavedha mit mṛtarasa śuddhasūtapalaikaṃ ca palaikaṃ
                    tālakasya ca / (107.1)
children.translated_text: [Sequential transmutation with killed mercury:] One <s>pala</s> of pure mercury and one <s>pala</s> of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>) — (RA 15.107a)
having combined them, grinding with the juice of <s>Unmattaka</s> (datura), (RA 15.107b)
one should kill [them] in a wheel-apparatus (<s>cakrayantra</s>) — the mercury becomes ash. (RA 15.107c)
Placed in a sealed crucible and smelted, a beautiful ingot forms. (RA 15.108a)

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ ca śulvaṃ ca kramaśo vedhayed rasaḥ //
                    (108.2)
children.translated_text: The mercury [so prepared] transmutes tin, silver, and copper sequentially. (RA 15.108b)
One <s>pala</s> of pure tin and one <s>pala</s> of mercury, (RA 15.109a)
two <s>palas</s> of orpiment, ground with datura juice — (RA 15.109b)
one should kill in a distillation apparatus; by smelting, it attains the state of an ingot. (RA 15.109c)

children.text: piṣṭī aus haritāla und gandha -> khoṭa
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Cake from orpiment and sulfur → alloy.]
One <s>pala</s> of orpiment cake (<s>tālapiṣṭī</s>) and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur; (RA 15.110.1)

children.text:
dve pale śuddhasūtasya dinamekaṃ tu tena vai //
                    (RA_15.110.2)
children.translated_text: two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury — [grind] for one day with that. (RA 15.110.2)
Having combined and ground [them] with the juice of <s>unmattaka</s> (thorn-apple), (RA 15.111.1)
one should kill [it] in the distillation apparatus; by blowing, one should bring it to alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) state. (RA 15.111.2)

children.text: piṣṭī aus nāga, sūta und manaḥśilā -> khoṭa
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Cake from lead, mercury, and realgar → alloy.]
One <s>pala</s> of purified lead and one <s>pala</s> of mercury; (RA 15.112.1)
two <s>palas</s> of realgar (<s>kunaṭī</s>) — one should grind all together. (RA 15.112.2)
One should kill [it] in the distillation apparatus; by blowing, one should bring it to alloy state. (RA 15.112.3)

children.text: piṣṭī aus heman und gandha -> khoṭa
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Cake from gold and sulfur → alloy.]
One <s>pala</s> of gold cake (<s>hemapiṣṭi</s>) and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur; (RA 15.113.1)
having combined and ground [them] with the juice of <s>dhuttūraka</s> (Datura), (RA 15.113.2)
one should kill [it] in the distillation apparatus; by blowing, one should bring it to alloy state. (RA 15.113.3)

children.text:
kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca hāṭakam /
                    (114.1)
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, lodestone, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), and gold, (RA 15.114.1)

children.text:
śuddhaśulvaṃ ca tāraṃ ca mākṣikaṃ samabhāgikam /
                    (RA_15.114.2)
children.translated_text: purified copper, silver, and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — in equal portions; (RA 15.114.2)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an alloy is produced instantly. (RA 15.114.3)
[Editorial note: Further processing of this alloy → alloy.]
One <s>pala</s> of that alloy and one <s>pala</s> of mercury; (RA 15.115.1)

children.text:
paladvayaṃ kunaṭyāś ca sarvam ekatra mardayet /
                    (RA_15.115.2)
children.translated_text: two <s>palas</s> of realgar (<s>kunaṭī</s>) — one should grind all together. (RA 15.115.2)
One should kill [it] in the distillation apparatus; by blowing, one should bring it to alloy state. (RA 15.115.3)
One <s>pala</s> of black mica and one <s>pala</s> of zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>); (RA 15.116.1)
one <s>pala</s> of mercury — all combined together, O Beloved. (RA 15.116.2)
One should grind with the juice of <s>unmattaka</s> (thorn-apple) for two <s>praharas</s> (six hours); (RA 15.117.1)
one should grind for one day, combined with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). (RA 15.117.2)

children.text:
guṭikāṃ kārayed devi chāyāśuṣkāṃ tu kārayet /
                    (RA_15.118.1)
children.translated_text: One should make a pill, O Goddess — one should dry it in shade; (RA 15.118.1)
placed in a great fire and blown — the mercury becomes an alloy. (RA 15.118.2)
[Editorial note: Further processing of this alloy → ten-million-fold transmuting mercury.]
One should purify that alloy by combining white glass and borax; (RA 15.119.1)
rolling together with gold, extracted by the triple extraction method. (RA 15.119.2)
With that, at a thousandth ratio, one should give transmutation of copper; (RA 15.120.1)
by this sequential procedure, the mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 15.120.2)
Two seeds of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) and one <s>pala</s> of mercury; (RA 15.121.1)
having ground with citron (<s>jambīra</s>) juice, one should dry [it] in shade. (RA 15.121.2)

children.text:
tumbī ca meghanādā ca kākajaṅghā ca cūlikā /
                    (RA_15.122.1)
children.translated_text: <s>Tumbī</s> (bottle gourd), <s>meghanāda</s> (thunder-plant), <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>cūlikā</s> — (RA 15.122.1)
in a crucible smeared with woman's breast-milk, one should deposit [it]. (RA 15.122.2)
One should blow with <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) charcoals — an imperishable alloy is produced. (RA 15.123)

children.text:
rasakhoṭa mit palāśa-ￖl palāśatailaṃ saṃmardya yāvat syād
                    rasapiṣṭikā / (124.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury-alloy with <s>palāśa</s> oil.] Having ground with <s>palāśa</s> oil until it becomes a mercury-cake, (RA 15.124.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an alloy is produced instantly. (RA 15.124.2)

children.text:
vedha nach piṣṭīstambhana pūrvaśuddhena sūtena saha hemnā ca
                    pārvati / (125.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Transmutation after cake-stabilization.] With previously purified mercury together with gold, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, (RA 15.125.1)

children.text:
golakaṃ kārayet tena mardayitvā drutaṃ kṛtam //
                    (RA_15.125.2)
children.translated_text: one should make a ball by grinding that which has been rendered fluid. (RA 15.125.2)
Seeds of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> (Butea), cotton seeds, <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia), (RA 15.126.1)

children.text:
yavaciñcā tu vandhyā ca rājikā ca samanvitam //
                    (RA_15.126.2)
children.translated_text: <s>yavaciñcā</s>, barren [variety], and <s>rājikā</s> (mustard) — combined [together]; (RA 15.126.2)

children.text:
sūkṣmapiṇḍīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tena liptvā tu golakam /
                    (RA_15.127.1)
children.translated_text: having made all into fine pellets, one should coat the ball with that; (RA 15.127.1)
with seven firings, O Goddess, cake-stabilization (<s>piṣṭikāstambhana</s>) is achieved. (RA 15.127.2)

children.text:
bṛhatpuṭaṃ tato dattvā mūṣāyāṃ tat tu bhāvayet /
                    (RA_15.128.1)
children.translated_text: Then, having given a large firing, one should heat that in a crucible; (RA 15.128.1)

children.text:
samāvartaṃ tu taṃ sūtaṃ samahemnā niyojitam /
                    (RA_15.128.2)
children.translated_text: that mercury, rolled together, combined with equal gold — (RA 15.128.2)
at a hundredth ratio, one should transmute silver and gold, O one honored by the gods. (RA 15.128.3)

children.text: punas tenaiva yogena piṣṭīstambhaṃ tu kārayet / (129.1)
children.translated_text: Again, by the same procedure, one should perform cake-stabilization; (RA 15.129.1)

children.text:
sārayitvā tato hemnā vedhayec ca sahasrakam //
                    (RA_15.129.2)
children.translated_text: having extracted with gold, one should transmute a thousand[-fold]. (RA 15.129.2)

children.text:
evaṃ lakṣāṇi koṭiṃ ca vedhayet kramayogataḥ /
                    (RA_15.130.1)
children.translated_text: Thus, one should transmute a hundred thousand and then ten million, by the sequential procedure; (RA 15.130.1)

children.text:
saptasaṃkalikād ūrdhvaṃ kṛtvā vaktre tu golakam /
                    (130.2)
children.translated_text: after the seventh chain [of operations], having placed the ball in the mouth, (RA 15.130.2)
within one year, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 15.130.3)
<s>Cāṇḍālī</s> and <s>Rākṣasī</s> [herbs], and mercury born from the <s>kuṇḍagola</s> [process], (RA 15.131.1)

children.text:
bījaṃ sūtaṃ ca vaikrāntaṃ mardayet praharatrayam //
                    (131.2)
children.translated_text: seeds, mercury, and <s>vaikrānta</s> — one should grind for three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours). (RA 15.131.2)
Having made a purified ball, placed in a sealed crucible, one should fire [it]; (RA 15.132.1)

children.text:
khoṭas tu jāyate devi sudhmātaḥ khadirāgninā //
                    (RA_15.132.2)
children.translated_text: an alloy is produced, O Goddess — well-blown with <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) fire. (RA 15.132.2)
[Editorial note: Alloy from various substances.]
With the flowers of <s>Cāṇḍālī</s> and <s>Rākṣasī</s>, mercury, honey, ghee, and borax, (RA 15.133.1)
one should combine mica together with one of the eight great minerals (<s>mahārasa</s>); (RA 15.133.2)

children.text:
nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ samaṃ sūtaṃ hema tāramathāpi vā /
                    (RA_15.134.1)
children.translated_text: lead, tin, equal mercury, gold or alternatively silver, (RA 15.134.1)
mica or melted essence — one should grind for two <s>praharas</s> (six hours). (RA 15.134.2)
The ball, dried in shade, placed in a sealed crucible, should be blown; (RA 15.135.1)

children.text:
dattvā laghupuṭaṃ devi khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ //
                    (RA_15.135.2)
children.translated_text: having given a light firing, O Goddess — a beautiful alloy is produced. (RA 15.135.2)
<s>Rambhā</s> (plantain), <s>vīrā</s>, the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia), <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>yavaciñcikā</s>, (RA 15.136.1)
<s>vārāhī</s>, <s>gorambhā</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s> — (RA 15.136.2)
mercury ground with these has no rebirth (i.e. is permanently killed); (RA 15.137.1)
by the previous sequential procedure, a beautiful alloy is produced. (RA 15.137.2)

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā ca cakrāṅkā balā ca tulasī tathā / (138.1)
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>cakrāṅkā</s>, <s>balā</s>, and <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil), (RA 15.138.1)
<s>mahāsomā</s>, <s>ahivallī</s>, and <s>sūryāvarta</s>, O Beautiful One — (RA 15.138.2)

children.text:
ebhis tu marditaḥ sūtaḥ pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ vrajet //
                    (138.3)
children.translated_text: mercury ground with these attains alloy-state as before. (RA 15.138.3)

children.text: mukhena grasate grāsaṃ jāraṇā tena sundari / (139.1)
children.translated_text: With its mouth, [the mercury] swallows the food (<s>grāsa</s>) — thereby [achieving] digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>), O Beautiful One; (RA 15.139.1)
ground with the roots of garlic, <s>narā</s>, and mustard (<s>rājikā</s>), O one of excellent complexion — (RA 15.139.2)
heated with a divine-herb firing — this is the characteristic of the mercury-alloy. (RA 15.139.3)
This secret has been told to you — to be understood by practitioners of mercury-science (<s>rasavādin</s>); (RA 15.140.1)
by my grace, O Goddess of the Gods, its accomplishment [is certain] — there is no doubt. (RA 15.140.2)
The milk of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) with <s>kāñjīka</s> (sour gruel), seeds of gold, (RA 15.141.1)
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>indravāruṇī</s>, and <s>viṣamuṣṭikā</s>; (RA 15.141.2)
with water from <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) root — one should grind the mercury with that. (RA 15.141.3)

children.text:
same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ /
                    (RA_15.142.1)
children.translated_text: Equal mercury with equal gold — the wise one should make a cake (<s>piṣṭikā</s>); (RA 15.142.1)
one should grind the great minerals for the cake-purpose with herbal juices. (RA 15.142.2)
Having ground for three <s>yāmas</s> (nine hours), the wise one should make a ball; (RA 15.143.1)
having bound the cake, one should cook [it] in sulfur-oil. (RA 15.143.2)
The ball, placed in a sealed crucible, should be dried in shade; (RA 15.144.1)

children.text:
tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā khadirāgnau tu dhāmayet /
                    (RA_15.144.2)
children.translated_text: then, having given a light firing, one should blow with <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) fire; (RA 15.144.2)

children.text:
khoṭas tu jāyate hemni saha hemnā tu sārayet /
                    (RA_15.144.3)
children.translated_text: an alloy is produced — one should extract it together with gold; (RA 15.144.3)

children.text:
akṣīṇo milate hemni samāvartaś ca jāyate //
                    (RA_15.144.4)
children.translated_text: it merges undiminished in gold — a rolled[-together] alloy is produced. (RA 15.144.4)
By merely consuming that mercury, a person attains a divine body; (RA 15.145.1)
the mercury, colored and stepped-up, transmutes all metals. (RA 15.145.2)
[Editorial note: Transmutation with equal-portion consumption.] One should grind mercury with herbal juices; (RA 15.146.1)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu taṃ kṛtvā pūrvayogena dhāmayet //
                    (RA_15.146.2)
children.translated_text: having made it into a destroyed cake (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>), one should blow by the previous procedure. (RA 15.146.2)

children.text:
khoṭas tu jāyate divyaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśena vedhayet /
                    (RA_15.147.1)
children.translated_text: A divine alloy is produced — one should transmute at a sixteenth ratio; (RA 15.147.1)
bound through the chain-procedure, it transmutes tenfold [more] progressively. (RA 15.147.2)

children.text:
rasapiṣṭikā mṛgadūrvā candravallī pakvā ciñcā tathaiva ca /
                    (148.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury cake.] <s>Mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>candravallī</s>, ripe <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind), and likewise (RA 15.148.1)

children.text:
kokilā karavīraṃ ca bījaṃ conmattakasya ca /
                    (RA_15.148.2)
children.translated_text: <s>kokilā</s>, <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), and the seed of <s>unmattaka</s> (thorn-apple); (RA 15.148.2)
combined with <s>kākāṇḍī</s> fruit — one should grind, O Beautiful Goddess. (RA 15.148.3)

children.text:
samahemni samaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ //
                    (RA_15.149)
children.translated_text: Equal mercury with equal gold — the wise one should make a cake. (RA 15.149)

children.text:
rasakhoṭa athavā sārayitvā tu samena saha sūtakam /
                    (150.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury-alloy.] Or, having extracted together with equal mercury, (RA 15.150.1)
one should grind the great mineral for the cake-purpose with herbal juices. (RA 15.150.2)
Having ground for three <s>yāmas</s> (nine hours), one should then make a ball; (RA 15.151.1)
the ball, placed in a sealed crucible, should be dried in shade. (RA 15.151.2)

children.text:
tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā dhmātaḥ khoṭo bhavet priye //
                    (RA_15.152)
children.translated_text: Then, having given a light firing, an alloy is produced when blown, O Beloved. (RA 15.152)
[Mercury]-treatment with the juices of <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>tamāsa</s>, and <s>soma</s>; (RA 15.153.1)
with the roots of the three [herbs], <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>rāmaṭha</s> (asafoetida) — [the mercury] is killed. (RA 15.153.2)

children.text:
samena hemnā saṃyuktāṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ /
                    (RA_15.154.1)
children.translated_text: The wise one should make a cake combined with equal gold; (RA 15.154.1)
and one should make a silver cake with equal mercury. (RA 15.154.2)
By the previous sequential procedure, a beautiful alloy is produced; (RA 15.155.1)
placed in a sealed crucible, [buried] in earth, one should steam with cow-dung fire. (RA 15.155.2)

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā cūrṇabandho bhavet tataḥ /
                    (156.1)
children.translated_text: For one day-and-night or three nights — then powder-binding (<s>cūrṇabandha</s>) is achieved; (RA 15.156.1)
that powder-binding produces transmutation tenfold [more] progressively. (RA 15.156.2)
[Editorial note: Mercury ingot.] <s>Śūlinī</s>-juice-mercury combined with <s>srotoñjana</s> (antimony); (RA 15.157.1)
by the pellet procedure as before, a fine ingot is produced. (RA 15.157.2)
<s>Srotoñjana</s> (antimony) [combined] with <s>satagara</s> [poison], mercury conjoined with the triple pellet; (RA 15.158.1)
blow [it] concentrated in fire — the mercury becomes the performer of all operations. (RA 15.158.2)
Gold-mica, silver-mica, copper-mica, mica-iron; (RA 15.159.1)
tin-mica and lead-mica — transmute with equal mercury. (RA 15.159.2)
Ground with whatever herbs are available, combined with the great mineral; (RA 15.160.1)
with gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead; (RA 15.160.2)

children.text:
ebhir vyastaiḥ samastair vā piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā same samām /
                    (161.1)
children.translated_text: with these, separately or all together, having made an equal pellet; (RA 15.161.1)
kill by the previously stated method in the womb-apparatus (<s>garbhayantra</s>) with husk-fire. (RA 15.161.2)

children.text:
samāṃśaṃ sūtakaṃ dattvā vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
                    (162.1)
children.translated_text: Adding equal mercury, again and again repeatedly; (RA 15.162.1)
various ingots are produced — the great mineral bound with lodestone. (RA 15.162.2)
By the chain procedure, transmutation increases tenfold. (RA 15.163)

children.text:
khoṭaḥ poṭastathā bhasma dhūliḥ kalkaś ca pañcamaḥ /
                    (164.1)
children.translated_text: Ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>), flake (<s>poṭa</s>), ash (<s>bhasma</s>), powder (<s>dhūli</s>), and paste (<s>kalka</s>) as the fifth — (RA 15.164.1)
these, through the chain-ball [procedures], yield the fruits of all bindings. (RA 15.164.2)
[Editorial note: <s>Nigala</s>-binding.] The alkali born from <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) and <s>sarja</s> (resin), <s>brahmabījas</s> (seeds of <s>Brahma</s>-plant), <s>guggulu</s>; (RA 15.165.1)
adding double [the amount of] rock salt, the skilled one should grind. (RA 15.165.2)
Having made a pellet-wrapping with this paste, O beautiful one; (RA 15.166.1)
making [the crucible] the size of a <s>bilva</s> fruit, [use] a very strong and auspicious crucible. (RA 15.166.2)

children.text:
ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā mūṣāmadhye rasaṃ kṣipet /
                    (167.1)
children.translated_text: Placing salt above and below, throw the mercury into the center of the crucible; (RA 15.167.1)
the crucible-coating to be applied should be of burnt conch powder and the like. (RA 15.167.2)

children.text:
mukhaṃ tasyā dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā loṇamṛttikayā punaḥ /
                    (168.1)
children.translated_text: Having firmly sealed the mouth with salt-clay; (RA 15.168.1)

children.text:
kārayec ca sudhālepaṃ chāyāśuṣkaṃ ca kārayet //
                    (RA_15.168.2)
children.translated_text: apply a lime-coating and let it dry in the shade. (RA 15.168.2)
This <s>nigala</s>-binding has been described — it should not be told even to one's son. (RA 15.169)
With husk-fire on the ground, one should perform gentle steaming; (RA 15.170.1)
applying a firing for the duration of a day and night, carefully. (RA 15.170.2)

children.text:
evaṃ mūṣā maheśāni rasasya khoṭatāṃ nayet /
                    (RA_15.171.1)
children.translated_text: Thus this crucible [procedure], O Great Goddess, brings the mercury to the ingot state; (RA 15.171.1)
well-blown with <s>khadira</s> (acacia) charcoal, the king of mercury attains the ingot state. (RA 15.171.2)

children.text:
sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā khoṭaṃ tu śodhayet /
                    (172.1)
children.translated_text: Adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass, one should purify the ingot; (RA 15.172.1)

children.text:
akṣīṇo milate hemni samāvartas tu jāyate //
                    (RA_15.172.2)
children.translated_text: undiminished, it unites with gold — an even revolving [mercury] is produced. (RA 15.172.2)
That [ingot should be made to] consume an equal amount of pure mercury; (RA 15.173.1)
blow by the former method — bring the king of mercury to the ingot state. (RA 15.173.2)
By the chain procedure, transmutation increases tenfold. (RA 15.174)
<s>Palāśa</s> seed-exudate, <s>kokilā</s> [plant], <s>unmatta</s> [datura], and <s>vāruṇī</s>; (RA 15.175.1)
combined with <s>śūlinī</s>-juice, grind with rock salt. (RA 15.175.2)
Having made a pellet-wrapping, bind with the <s>nigala</s> [procedure]. (RA 15.176)
The <s>nigala</s> in the crucible, O Goddess, is coated by <s>Śiva</s>'s command; (RA 15.177.1)
for the transformation of mercury, it should be placed in a great fire. (RA 15.177.2)
[Editorial note: <s>Nigala</s> of mica.] With a sheet of mica, <s>vajra</s> [euphorbia]-<s>arka</s> milk, <s>sindhu</s> [salt]; (RA 15.178.1)
with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), metal slag (<s>lohakiṭṭa</s>), and sand-clay. (RA 15.178.2)

children.text:
ebhis tu nigalair baddhaḥ pāradīyo mahārasaḥ /
                    (RA_15.179.1)
children.translated_text: With these <s>nigalas</s>, the mercurial great mineral, once bound, (RA 15.179.1)
does not transgress its boundary — like the ocean [does not transgress] the shore. (RA 15.179.2)
[Editorial note: Various types of <s>nigala</s>.]
Oil, <s>arka</s>-milk, <s>vārāhī</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> — [constitute] the best <s>nigala</s>; (RA 15.180.1)
crow's dung, <s>brahmabījas</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> — an excellent <s>nigala</s>. (RA 15.180.2)
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, crab bones (<s>karkaṭāsthi</s>), O beautiful one; (RA 15.181.1)
sea-salt and <s>sāmbara</s> salt — [constitute] the best <s>nigala</s>. (RA 15.181.2)
Milk of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, <s>kokilā</s> plant; (RA 15.182.1)
seeds of <s>karaka</s> [tree] — grind at one-eighth [the proportion] of metal. (RA 15.182.2)
Another <s>nigala</s>: <s>gojihvā</s> roots; another: a woman's menstrual blood; (RA 15.183.1)
<s>vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, <s>snuhī</s>-<s>arka</s> milk, and rock salt; (RA 15.183.2)
<s>jvālinī</s> and crow's excrement — this is a praised best <s>nigala</s>. (RA 15.183.3)
Salt, borax, alkali, realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), and sulphur; (RA 15.184.1)
and also sour date (<s>āmlavetasa</s>), <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), and cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), in equal parts; (RA 15.184.2)
grind [this] best <s>nigala</s> with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>. (RA 15.184.3)
One should wrap the pellet with one of these <s>nigalas</s>; (RA 15.185.1)

children.text:
lohamūṣāgataṃ prāgvat khoṭaṃ kṛtvā tu vedhayet //
                    (185.2)
children.translated_text: having made an ingot as before in a metal crucible, one should transmute. (RA 15.185.2)
I shall describe the second ball (<s>golaka</s>) — the excellent pellet-stabilization. (RA 15.186)
The urine of a two-legged [human] royal [person], rock salt, mica, and <s>guggulu</s>; (RA 15.187.1)

children.text:
piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena mṛdā tu punar aṣṭadhā //
                    (187.2)
children.translated_text: having wrapped the pellet with the paste, [and then] with clay eight times over. (RA 15.187.2)
With husk-fire on the ground, one should perform gentle steaming; (RA 15.188.1)

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet //
                    (188.2)
children.translated_text: for a day and night, or three nights — bring [it] to the ingot state as before. (RA 15.188.2)
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, mica (<s>gagana</s>), <s>vimala</s> (iron pyrites), gem; (RA 15.189.1)

children.text:
sauvarcalaṃ saindhavaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gugguluṃ tathā //
                    (189.2)
children.translated_text: <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, rock salt, borax, and <s>guggulu</s> likewise. (RA 15.189.2)

children.text:
dvipadīrajasā mūtraṃ suślakṣṇaṃ tac ca mardayet /
                    (190.1)
children.translated_text: [Mix with] human royal urine and grind very smooth; (RA 15.190.1)

children.text:
piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet //
                    (190.2)
children.translated_text: having wrapped the pellet with the paste, bring to the ingot state as before. (RA 15.190.2)
Poison-seeds, <s>brahmabījas</s>, seeds of gold [plant]; (RA 15.191.1)
roots of <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>. (RA 15.191.2)
<s>Kokilā</s>, <s>arka</s>-<s>snuhī</s> milk, rock salt, mica, and <s>guggulu</s>; (RA 15.192.1)

children.text:
piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet //
                    (192.2)
children.translated_text: having wrapped the pellet with the paste, bring to the ingot state as before. (RA 15.192.2)
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, crow's excrement, <s>guggulu</s>; (RA 15.193.1)
the roots of <s>śvetāśvamāra</s>, the root of <s>kanakavāruṇī</s>. (RA 15.193.2)
Oil combined with rock salt — the skilled one should grind; (RA 15.194.1)

children.text:
piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet //
                    (194.2)
children.translated_text: having wrapped the pellet with the paste, bring to the ingot state as before. (RA 15.194.2)
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabījas</s>, the two <s>jīrakas</s> (cumins), <s>guggulu</s>; (RA 15.195.1)
rock salt, mica, crab bones, borax, and <s>jvālinī</s> juice. (RA 15.195.2)

children.text:
piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena mṛdā tu punar aṣṭadhā /
                    (RA_15.196.1)
children.translated_text: Having wrapped the pellet with the paste, [and then] with clay eight times over; (RA 15.196.1)
with husk-fire on the ground, one should perform gentle steaming. (RA 15.196.2)

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendraṃ khoṭatāṃ nayet /
                    (197.1)
children.translated_text: For a day and night, or three nights — bring the king of mercury to the ingot state; (RA 15.197.1)
by the tenfold-chain procedure, the great mineral becomes a sound-transmuter (<s>śabdavedhin</s>). (RA 15.197.2)

children.text: śaṃkarasya dvibhāgaṃ tu pāradasya trayaṃ tathā / (198.1)
children.translated_text: Two parts of the <s>saṃkara</s> (alloy) and three parts of mercury; (RA 15.198.1)

children.text:
piṣṭikāṃ kārayet tena taptakhalle tu kāñjike //
                    (RA_15.198.2)
children.translated_text: one should make a pellet from that, in a heated mortar with sour gruel. (RA 15.198.2)
Having made an ingot with the <s>nigala</s> as before, one should transmute; (RA 15.199.1)
by the tenfold-chain procedure, the great mineral becomes a sound-transmuter. (RA 15.199.2)
[Editorial note: Preparation of a 'hungry mercury' (<s>bubhukṣitarasa</s>).]
With bound mercury, the king [of metals], realgar (<s>śilā</s>), sulphur, and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>); (RA 15.200.1)
with lodestone powder, combined with <s>bhūlatā</s> plants. (RA 15.200.2)
This mercury, placed in a crucible and blown, O one praised by the gods, (RA 15.201.1)
swallows the minerals, auxiliary minerals, metals, gems, and jewels, (RA 15.201.2)
in the womb of an open crucible — like the submarine fire (<s>vaḍavānala</s>). (RA 15.201.3)

children.text: mākṣikaṃ daradaṃ caiva gandhakaṃ ca manaḥśilā / (202.1)
children.translated_text: Pyrite, cinnabar, sulphur, and realgar; (RA 15.202.1)

children.text:
rājāvartaṃ pravālaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ tutthakaṃ tathā //
                    (202.2)
children.translated_text: lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>), coral (<s>pravāla</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and blue vitriol (<s>tutthaka</s>). (RA 15.202.2)
The yellow and red groups should be soaked, mixed with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil; (RA 15.203.1)

children.text:
khoṭaṃ haṇḍikayā pakvaṃ drutaṃ hi nalike kṣipet //
                    (203.2)
children.translated_text: the ingot, cooked in a pot, when melted, should be thrown into a tube. (RA 15.203.2)

children.text:
haṇḍyāṃ tu sikatāṃ dattvā trirātram api dhāmayet //
                    (RA_15.204)
children.translated_text: Having placed sand in the pot, one should blow for three nights. (RA 15.204)

children.text:
āranālena tat svinnaṃ dolāyāṃ dhṛtameva ca /
                    (RA_15.205.1)
children.translated_text: Steamed with sour gruel, and held in a swing[-apparatus]; (RA 15.205.1)
thus, the colored mercury becomes a creator of body and wealth. (RA 15.205.2)

children.text:
udghāṭa udghāṭaḥ paramaḥ proktaḥ sarvakarmahitaḥ paraḥ /
                    (206.1)
children.translated_text: The <s>udghāṭa</s> (opening) — the supreme [procedure] has been described, beneficial to all operations; (RA 15.206.1)

children.text:
chattrī pataṃgī durdrāvī durmelī naiva jāyate /
                    (RA_15.206.2)
children.translated_text: [a mercury that is] umbrella-forming, moth-like [in volatility], hard-to-melt, hard-to-combine — [these faults] do not arise; (RA 15.206.2)
and it produces a change of color; it splits [metals], O best-colored one. (RA 15.206.3)

children.text:
bandham evaṃ drutaṃ kṛtvā kurute vajrajāraṇam /
                    (RA_15.207.1)
children.translated_text: Having thus quickly made the binding, it performs diamond-calcination; (RA 15.207.1)

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi kimanyac chrotum icchasi //
                    (207.2)
children.translated_text: tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 15.207.2)
Chapter] 16.
The Glorious Goddess said: (RA 16.1.2)
How is the melting (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) of bound mercury-king [accomplished], O Lord? (RA 16.1.3)
And how [is] the calcination of diamond and the like — please instruct, O Master! (RA 16.1.4)
The Glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said: (RA 16.2.1)

children.text:
pāradadrāvaṇa taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu strīrajobhis tu
                    bhāvayet // (2.2)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Melting of mercury.] That ingot should be soaked as fine powder with a woman's menstrual blood. (RA 16.2.2)
<s>Punarnava</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, plantain (<s>rambhā</s>) tuber, a woman's menstrual blood; (RA 16.3.1)
<s>maṇimantha</s>, realgar mineral (<s>śilādhātu</s>) — grind everything together. (RA 16.3.2)
Covered with this paste, combined with sublimated mercury; (RA 16.4.1)

children.text:
taṃ rasaṃ bhūrjapattre tu baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tataḥ //
                    (RA_16.4.2)
children.translated_text: That mercury, tied in a birch-bark (<s>bhūrjapatra</s>) bundle, (RA 16.4)
should be steamed in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>), O Queen of the Gods, for three days. (RA 16.5)
By this graduated method, the killed mercury becomes liquid. (RA 16.5)

children.text:
rasadrāvaṇa und -jāraṇa ārdrakaṃ mūlakaṃ śuṇṭhī laśunaṃ hiṅgu
                    mākṣikam / (6.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury-liquefaction and calcination: fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), radish (<s>mūlaka</s>), dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), garlic (<s>laśuna</s>), asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), (RA 16.6)
the three alkalis (<s>trikṣāra</s>), five salts (<s>pañcalavaṇa</s>), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), and sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), (RA 16.6)
combined with the sour group (<s>amlavarga</s>), one should make a ball, O Beloved. (RA 16.6)

children.text: tasya madhyagatā piṣṭī dolāyāṃ svedanena tu / (RA_16.7.1)
children.translated_text: The cake [of mercury] placed in its midst, by steaming in the swing-apparatus, (RA 16.7)

children.text: dravate nātra saṃdeho drutaṃ jārayate rasam // (RA_16.7.2)
children.translated_text: it melts — there is no doubt — and the melted [mercury] calcines the [other] substances. (RA 16.7)
The bound great mineral (<s>mahārasa</s>), O <s>Devī</s>, one should liquefy by the foot-method (<s>pādayoga</s>); (RA 16.8)
to the liquid foot [one-quarter], one should add [more]; having liquefied, it melts again. (RA 16.8)
Thus, having made the bound [mercury] liquid in equal, double, and triple [proportions], (RA 16.9)

children.text:
tasmin drute jāraṇā ca kartavyā karmavedibhiḥ //
                    (RA_16.9.2)
children.translated_text: calcination should be performed on that liquid by those who know the operations. (RA 16.9)
Mercury calcination: <s>kukkuṭī</s>-bulb, <s>mārjārī</s>, <s>uccaṭā</s>, and <s>Īśvarī</s> [herbs], (RA 16.10)

children.text:
kṣīrakañcukayā yuktaṃ sveditaṃ ca drutaṃ rasam //
                    (RA_16.10.2)
children.translated_text: combined with <s>kṣīrakañcukā</s> — the steamed and liquefied mercury; (RA 16.10)
the liquid [mercury], processed in the swing-apparatus, [with] <s>kukkuṭī</s> etc. for three days; (RA 16.11)

children.text:
ārdrakādyair drutaṃ caiva tatsūtaṃ svedyatāṃ vrajet //
                    (11.2)
children.translated_text: and also liquefied with fresh ginger etc. — that mercury attains the state of [being ready for] steaming. (RA 16.11)
Just as diamond [is processed], one should calcine the liquid mercury, O One Worshipped by the Gods; (RA 16.12)
the lord of that [process] should be known as the God of Gods, the World-Teacher. (RA 16.12)

children.text: vidhāya khoṭaṃ yat kiṃcit mṛtakotthāpite rase / (13.1)
children.translated_text: Having prepared any kind of ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>), in mercury [that has been] killed and then revived, (RA 16.13)

children.text:
ṣaḍguṇaṃ hema jāryaṃ tu sārayet sāraṇātrayam //
                    (RA_16.13.2)
children.translated_text: sixfold gold should be calcined, [then] one should extract through triple extraction. (RA 16.13)
With that at one-crore ratio, one should effect copper transmutation; (RA 16.14)
divine gold is produced — the ornament adorning the gods. (RA 16.14)

children.text:
punas tat tu rasendrasya vajraratnāni jārayet /
                    (RA_16.15.1)
children.translated_text: Furthermore, one should calcine diamond-gems in that king of mercury; (RA 16.15)
in the womb of an open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>), in intense fire, it calcines instantly. (RA 16.15)
[Section: Melting of gems]
With <s>uccaṭā</s>, <s>mīnanayanā</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and red <s>citraka</s> [herbs] — (RA 16.16)
with these, gems melt quickly — sapphire (<s>nīla</s>), ruby (<s>māṇikya</s>), and pearl (<s>mauktika</s>). (RA 16.16)

children.text:
sūtajāraṇa viṣṇukrāntā ca cakrāṅkā kumārī yavaciñcikā /
                    (17.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury calcination: <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>cakrāṅkā</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and tamarind (<s>yavaciñcikā</s>); (RA 16.17)
diamonds, rubies (<s>padmarāga</s>), and <s>rājāvarta</s>-type <s>sasyaka</s> [minerals] — (RA 16.17)

children.text:
oṣadhīnāṃ dravaṃ dattvā tapte sūte vinikṣipet //
                    (RA_16.17.3)
children.translated_text: having added the liquid of the herbs, one should throw [them] into heated mercury. (RA 16.17)
Afterwards, gems should be added — they melt like water. (RA 16.18)
One should steam in the swing-apparatus, O <s>Devī</s>, and calcine with the alkali-method (<s>viḍayoga</s>); (RA 16.19)
in the womb of an open crucible, in intense fire, one should calcine instantly. (RA 16.19)
Ingot-calcination: with conch [shell] and <s>arka</s> [calotropis] milk, sealed-heated a hundred times — (RA 16.20)
that seed, combined with alkali, should be steeped with the sour group. (RA 16.20)
With alkali-salt (<s>viḍa</s>), cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), <s>rājāvarta</s>, and coral (<s>pravāla</s>), (RA 16.21)

children.text:
gandhakaḥ śilayā yuktaḥ khoṭānāṃ jāraṇe hitaḥ //
                    (RA_16.21.2)
children.translated_text: sulfur combined with realgar — [these are] beneficial for calcination of ingots. (RA 16.21)
Calcination of bound gold: by the combination of crucible-coating etc., the calcination of bound gold [is effected]; (RA 16.22)

children.text: tat kṣepāj jāyate devi viḍayogena jāraṇam // (RA_16.22.2)
children.translated_text: by adding that, O <s>Devī</s>, calcination occurs through the alkali-method. (RA 16.22)
Afterwards, gold should be added with liquid at one-thirty-sixth proportion. (RA 16.23)
Then indeed, a halo of rays is produced around the king of mercury, (RA 16.24)
pervaded transversely, upward, and downward, filled with a mass of luster. (RA 16.24)

children.text:
itthaṃ śuddho bhavet sūtaḥ cintāmaṇiriva svayam /
                    (RA_16.25.1)
children.translated_text: Thus purified, the mercury becomes like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) itself; (RA 16.25)

children.text:
sadevaiḥ pūjyate siddhaiḥ dvitīya iva śaṃkaraḥ //
                    (RA_16.25.2)
children.translated_text: it is worshipped by gods and <s>siddhas</s>, like a second <s>Śaṃkara</s>. (RA 16.25)
A benefactor of the worlds, a bestower of enjoyment and liberation; (RA 16.26)
one should calcine the great sapphire (<s>mahānīla</s>) by the method of the [twenty-five] <s>tattva</s>-number sequence. (RA 16.26)
When it revolves clockwise, then that mercury [becomes] sky-going (<s>khecara</s>); (RA 16.27)
it transmutes all metals in immeasurable quantities, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 16.27)

children.text:
kāpālirañjana evaṃ jīrṇasya sūtasya śṛṇu kāpālirañjanam //
                    (28)
children.translated_text: Skull-cup coloring (<s>kāpālirañjana</s>): now hear the skull-cup coloring of the digested mercury. (RA 16.28)
One <s>pala</s> of copper foil, half a <s>pala</s> of sulfur, (RA 16.29)
one <s>karṣa</s> of borax, one <s>karṣa</s> of mercury-soot (<s>rasakajjalī</s>), (RA 16.29)
one <s>karṣa</s> of pyrite — one should combine everything together; (RA 16.30)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown, it becomes an ingot instantly. (RA 16.30)
[Section: Further processing — transformation into gold (<s>kāpālikayoga</s>)]

children.text:
taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu caṇakāmlena mardayet /
                    (31.1)
children.translated_text: That ingot, [ground to] fine powder, one should grind with gram-acid (<s>caṇakāmla</s>); (RA 16.31)
with wild cow-dung alone, one should give fourteen firings. (RA 16.31)
It becomes resembling a firefly (<s>indragopaka</s>) — there is no doubt in this. (RA 16.32)

children.text:
taccūrṇaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ śuddhatāraṃ tu rañjayet /
                    (RA_16.33.1)
children.translated_text: That powder, combined with honey, should color pure silver; (RA 16.33)

children.text:
rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi śobhanaṃ hema jāyate //
                    (RA_16.33.2)
children.translated_text: one should color three times — beautiful gold is produced. (RA 16.33)
This is the skull-cup method (<s>kāpālika yoga</s>) — it colors all metals; (RA 16.34)

children.text:
rañjayed baddhasūtaṃ ca vajrabandhaṃ ca rañjayet //
                    (34.2)
children.translated_text: it colors bound mercury, and also colors diamond-bound [preparations]. (RA 16.34)
[Section: Coloring by various methods]
One <s>pala</s> of brass (<s>āra</s>) powder, or one <s>pala</s> of killed lead, (RA 16.35)
or one <s>pala</s> of tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhraka</s>), or one <s>pala</s> of iron powder — (RA 16.35)
triple copper with lead and tin, each combined with one part; (RA 16.36)
or triple copper with one [part] each of ochre, or iron and pyrite; (RA 16.36)

children.text:
athavā tīkṣṇabhāgau dvau trayo ghoṣā navoragāḥ /
                    (RA_16.37.1)
children.translated_text: or two parts iron, three parts <s>ghoṣa</s> [tin-ore], nine [parts] mercury; (RA 16.37)
nine parts of copper and four parts of brass. (RA 16.37)
Or, O Goddess of the God of Gods, two <s>palas</s> of pyrite, (RA 16.38)
one [<s>pala</s>] of peacock-neck vitriol (<s>mayūragrīvatuttha</s>), and one <s>pala</s> of killed lead. (RA 16.38)
Or, one part each of tin and lead, O One Worshipped by the Gods, (RA 16.39)
two [parts] iron, three [parts] copper, and four [parts] gold-pyrite (<s>hematāpya</s>). (RA 16.39)
Or, <s>vimala</s> [iron pyrites], <s>vaikrānta</s>, tin, lead, and brass (<s>rītikā</s>); (RA 16.40)
or with copper, or gold, <s>vimala</s>, and mercury. (RA 16.40)
Any one of these, O <s>Devī</s>, combined with the previously described procedure, (RA 16.41)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — it becomes an ingot instantly. (RA 16.41)
One should fire by the previous method, [and] color by the previous method. (RA 16.42)
Lead, copper, and iron — [this is] the supreme skull-cup method; (RA 16.43)

children.text:
tenaiva rañjayet tāraṃ saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
                    (RA_16.43.2)
children.translated_text: with that one should color silver seven times, again and again. (RA 16.43)

children.text:
tenaiva rañjayed dhema saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
                    (RA_16.44.1)
children.translated_text: With that one should color gold seven times, again and again; (RA 16.44)
this is the best matured seed (<s>pakvabīja</s>) — one should employ [it] in all operations. (RA 16.44)

children.text:
tārarañjana vaṅgatīkṣṇaṃ kapālī ca śulvaṃ tāraṃ tu rañjayet /
                    (45.1)
children.translated_text: Silver-coloring: tin-iron skull-cup, and copper — one should color silver; (RA 16.45)
it colors all metals until [they become] resembling saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>). (RA 16.45)
<s>Vaikrānta</s>-lead skull-cup should color pure silver; (RA 16.46)

children.text:
rañjayet saha hemnā tu bhavet kuṅkumasannibham //
                    (RA_16.46.2)
children.translated_text: one should color together with gold — it becomes resembling saffron. (RA 16.46)
Gold-coloring: quenched in red oil — it destroys metal-migration (<s>saṃkrānti</s>); (RA 16.47)
brass skull-cup powder should color pure silver. (RA 16.47)
With <s>vimala</s> [iron pyrites] and lead, the skull-cup [method], O Supreme Goddess, (RA 16.48)
colors all metals — silver and gold especially. (RA 16.48)

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi jāyate hema śobhanam / (RA_16.49.1)
children.translated_text: Coloring three times, beautiful gold is produced; (RA 16.49)

children.text:
tenaiva rañjayed dhema saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
                    (RA_16.49.2)
children.translated_text: with that one should color gold seven times, again and again. (RA 16.49)
Gold-coloring: quenched in salt-water — it destroys metal-migration; (RA 16.50)

children.text:
vaṅganāgaṃ tathā kāntaṃ śulvaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca mākṣikam //
                    (50.2)
children.translated_text: tin, lead, lodestone, copper, iron, and pyrite. (RA 16.50)
<s>Ravi</s> [copper]-lead skull-cup should color pure silver; (RA 16.51)

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi tārāriṣṭaṃ tu jāyate / (RA_16.51.2)
children.translated_text: coloring three times, <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> [silver-destroyer] is produced; (RA 16.51)
with that one should color gold seven times, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 16.51)
Quenched in the red group [of substances] — it destroys metal-migration; (RA 16.52)
tin, lead, and copper skull-cup, O One Worshipped by the Gods. (RA 16.52)
With jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), blue glass (<s>nīlakāca</s>), vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), sour-salt (<s>amlalavaṇa</s>), (RA 16.53)
and a paste of poison-bile-acid — one should destroy the migration-blackness (<s>saṃkrāntikālikā</s>). (RA 16.53)
Ochre (<s>gairika</s>), sulfur, and mercury — one should grind with sesame oil; (RA 16.54)
one should coat silver foils, adding a copper skull-cup. (RA 16.54)

children.text:
ūrdhvādhas tv andhamūṣāyāṃ śubhraṃ hemadalaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_16.55)
children.translated_text: Above and below in a sealed crucible — bright gold-leaf is produced. (RA 16.55)
One part of orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), one part of ochre (<s>gairika</s>), (RA 16.56)
one part of pyrite paste (<s>mākṣikakalka</s>), and four [parts] of the ball; (RA 16.56)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — it colors gold instantly. (RA 16.56)
By this graduated method, one should color four times; (RA 16.57)
this is the best matured seed, having luster like the young sun. (RA 16.57)
With that, an enhancement of two color-grades is produced at one-sixteenth proportion. (RA 16.58)
Quenched in red oil — it destroys metal-migration; (RA 16.59)

children.text: rasakasya tu kāpālī candrārkaṃ tu śatāṃśataḥ / (59.2)
children.translated_text: zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) skull-cup [colors] silver and gold at one-hundredth ratio; (RA 16.59)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — beautiful gold is produced. (RA 16.59)
[Section: Preparation of an ingot, coloring]
One <s>pala</s> of pure lead and one <s>karṣa</s> of liquid mercury — (RA 16.60)
one should extract in an extraction-apparatus (<s>sāraṇāyantra</s>) — the mercury becomes an ingot. (RA 16.60)

children.text:
khoṭasya palamekaṃ tu mākṣikasya palaṃ tathā /
                    (RA_16.61.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of alloy (<s>khota</s>) and one <s>pala</s> of pyrite (<s>maksika</s>) — (RA 16.61.1)
having combined and ground together with the juice of gold (<s>kanaka</s>-rasa), (RA 16.61.2)
one should cook in an earthen vessel — it becomes saffron (<s>kunkuma</s>)-colored. (RA 16.61.3)
Combined with the previous paste, one should make an alloy as before; (RA 16.62.1)
this powder, [produced] by the <s>kapalika</s>-method, one should grind with acid. (RA 16.62.2)
One should heat in cycles by the previous method; one should color by the previous method. (RA 16.63)
Having bound mercury by whatever [means], with gold, sulfur (<s>gandha</s>), realgar (<s>sila</s>), and orpiment (<s>uraga</s>), (16.64.1)
sequentially wrapped and blown — it transmutes a hundredfold. (RA 16.64.2)

children.text:
ādau tu baddhasūtaṃ ca vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ manaḥśilā /
                    (RA_16.65.1)
children.translated_text: First the bound mercury, then tin (<s>vanga</s>), silver (<s>tara</s>), and realgar (<s>manahsila</s>) — (RA 16.65.1)

children.text:
krameṇa veṣṭayet dhmātaṃ śatavedhī na saṃśayaḥ //
                    (RA_16.65.2)
children.translated_text: sequentially wrapped and blown — it is a hundred-fold transmuter, without doubt. (RA 16.65.2)

children.text: anena kurute tāraṃ kanakena tu kāñcanam // (RA_16.66)
children.translated_text: With this, one makes silver; with gold, [one makes] gold. (RA 16.66)

children.text:
sūto mṛto hanti samena vaṅgaṃ tenaiva hanyād dviguṇaṃ ca
                    tāram / (67.1)
children.translated_text: Killed mercury transmutes tin in equal proportion; with that, one should transmute double the silver; (16.67.1)

children.text:
tāraṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiraviṃ karoti hemāpi tadvat phaṇihemayogāt //
                    (67.2)
children.translated_text: silver, sixty-four times [treated], becomes gold — likewise gold [improves] by the lead-gold combination. (16.67.2)
[Preparation of ten-million-fold transmuting mercury (?)]

children.text:
mṛtarasapalamekaṃ pañcanāgaṃ ca dadyāt kanakapalavimiśraṃ
                    dhmātasūtāvaśeṣam / (68.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of killed mercury and five [<s>palas</s>] of lead should be given, mixed with one <s>pala</s> of gold, blown until only mercury remains; (16.68.1)

children.text:
punar api śatavārānevameva krameṇa bhavati ca rasarājaḥ
                    koṭivedhī krameṇa // (68.2)
children.translated_text: again, a hundred times in this very sequence — the king of mercury becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter progressively. (16.68.2)

children.text: mṛtasūtapalaikaṃ tu dve pale daradasya ca / (69.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of killed mercury and two <s>palas</s> of cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), (16.69.1)
four <s>palas</s> of sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) and three <s>palas</s> of <s>kankustha</s>, (RA 16.69.2)

children.text:
śilāyāḥ pañcakaṃ caiva gopittena tu mardayet //
                    (RA_16.69.3)
children.translated_text: and five [<s>palas</s>] of realgar (<s>sila</s>) — one should grind with cow's bile (<s>gopitta</s>). (RA 16.69.3)
One <s>pala</s> of lead sheets should be coated with that paste; (RA 16.70.1)
one should kill by the heating-cycle method — this lead is killed instantly. (RA 16.70.2)

children.text:
vaṭikāṃ kārayetpaścāt ṣaṣṭiṃ trīṇi śatāni ca /
                    (RA_16.71.1)
children.translated_text: One should make pills afterward — three hundred and sixty [pills]; (RA 16.71.1)
each pill afterward should be ground with cow's bile. (RA 16.71.2)

children.text: anena kramayogeṇa śataṃ dadyāt puṭāni ca / (RA_16.72.1)
children.translated_text: By this sequential method, one should give a hundred heating-cycles. (RA 16.72.1)
This lead becomes, O Goddess, vermilion-dawn colored. (RA 16.72.2)

children.text:
śatāṃśena ca tenaiva tāre vedhaṃ pradāpayet /
                    (RA_16.73.1)
children.translated_text: With a hundredth part of that, one should effect transmutation of silver; (RA 16.73.1)
that silver becomes, O Goddess, a supreme ornament for the gods. (RA 16.73.2)
One <s>pala</s> of killed lead and gold leaf equal to that — (RA 16.74.1)
one should kill by the heating-cycle method — the gold is killed instantly. (RA 16.74.2)
That calx, combined with one [part] lead, and gold leaf equal to that — (RA 16.75.1)
one should kill by the heating-cycle method — the gold is killed instantly. (RA 16.75.2)
By this sequential method, one should perform three times. (RA 16.76.1)
With a thousandth part of that, one should effect transmutation of silver. (RA 16.76.2)
By this easily accomplished procedure, that silver becomes gold. (RA 16.77.1)
[Paste-transmutation:] Now I shall describe paste-transmutation (<s>kalkavedha</s>), easily accomplished, O Queen of the Gods. (16.77.2)
<s>Palasa</s> (Butea), neem (<s>nimba</s>), bael (<s>bilva</s>), <s>aksa</s> (Terminalia), cotton (<s>karpasa</s>), sharp gourd (<s>katutumbini</s>), (RA 16.78.1)
<s>kanguni</s> and sharp oils — each one [individually] kills mercury. (RA 16.78.2)

children.text:
same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ tāraṃ tāmramathāpi vā /
                    (RA_16.79.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury equal to gold, and silver or copper [also], (RA 16.79.1)
among the eight great minerals and likewise the four sub-minerals — (RA 16.79.2)
with fruit-acid and sour gruel (<s>kanjika</s>), one should grind in a mortar on charcoal-free [ground]; (RA 16.80.1)
or on heated iron, with an iron fist, over gentle fire. (RA 16.80.2)
In the previously described sand-apparatus, having added oil, the discerning one (RA 16.81.1)
should grind for a fortnight, day and night, without laziness. (RA 16.81.2)
That paste is produced — the best, granting <s>dharma</s>, <s>kama</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>moksa</s>; (RA 16.82.1)
it transmutes the eight metals — [a feat] difficult to achieve even for the gods. (RA 16.82.2)

children.text:
nāśayet sakalān rogān palaikena na saṃśayaḥ /
                    (RA_16.83.1)
children.translated_text: It destroys all diseases with [just] one <s>pala</s>, without doubt. (RA 16.83.1)
Combined with the three pungents (<s>trikatu</s>) and three fruits (<s>triphala</s>), one should consume with honey and ghee. (RA 16.83.2)

children.text:
hemnā tu baddhaṃ guñjaikaṃ tāreṇa dve sureśvari /
                    (RA_16.84.1)
children.translated_text: One <s>gunja</s> bound with gold, two with silver, O Queen of the Gods, (RA 16.84.1)
three <s>gunjas</s> with copper — within a year, one becomes ageless and immortal. (RA 16.84.2)
Moon-faced women, adorned with all ornaments, serve [him]; (RA 16.85.1)
having made a nasal application (<s>nasya</s>) of <s>triphala</s>-seed, honey, and ghee at night, (16.85.2)

children.text:
rasaṃ tu bhakṣayet prātarajīrṇaṃ naiva jāyate /
                    (RA_16.86.1)
children.translated_text: one should consume mercury in the morning — indigestion never occurs. (RA 16.86.1)
The wise one should consume sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) as drink, ointment, and <s>kankustha</s>. (16.86.2)
One should consume mercury by the <s>pala</s>, bowed to by gods and demons; (16.87.1)
one becomes like heated gold in appearance, with lustre like the young sun. (RA 16.87.2)

children.text:
vedhayet sarvalohāni chede dāhe na saṃśayaḥ /
                    (RA_16.88.1)
children.translated_text: One transmutes all metals — in cutting and burning, without doubt. (RA 16.88.1)

children.text:
baddhā tu saṃkalābandhair vaṭikā khecarī bhavet //
                    (RA_16.88.2)
children.translated_text: Bound with successive bindings (<s>samkala</s>), the pill becomes a sky-rover (<s>khecari</s>). (RA 16.88.2)
The great creepers (<s>mahalata</s>): <s>Kakajangha</s>, <s>Brhati</s>, <s>Sarapunkha</s>, <s>Ajasrngika</s>, (16.89.1)

children.text:
śivā śakralatā kanyā saptaitās tu mahālatāḥ //
                    (RA_16.89.2)
children.translated_text: <s>Siva</s>, <s>Sakralata</s>, and <s>Kanya</s> — these seven are the great creepers. (RA 16.89.2)
The most secret of secrets has been declared, combined with the oil of <s>vatari</s> (castor); (16.90.1)

children.text:
same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ tāre tāmre 'thavā priye //
                    (RA_16.90.2)
children.translated_text: mercury equal to gold, in silver or copper, O beloved — (RA 16.90.2)
one should add one among the eight great minerals, and likewise the sub-minerals; (RA 16.91.1)
one should grind on a mortar-stone until it becomes unconscious (completely ground). (RA 16.91.2)
One should steam with sour rice-water (<s>aranala</s>) and grind like the previous paste; (RA 16.92.1)

children.text:
tac ca lohasya dehasya tattatkarmasu yojayet //
                    (RA_16.92.2)
children.translated_text: that [preparation] should be employed for the respective operations on metal and body. (RA 16.92.2)
One [part] each of gold and mica, and two [parts] of mercury, (16.93.1)
or one [part] each of silver and mica, and two [parts] of mercury — (RA 16.93.2)

children.text:
piṣṭikāṃ kārayet tena nigalena ca bandhayet /
                    (RA_16.94.1)
children.translated_text: one should make a pellet (<s>pistika</s>) with that and bind with a <s>nigala</s> (clamp/chain); (RA 16.94.1)
in heating-cycles, pellet-binding [is done] with a ball (<s>gola</s>) and clamp (<s>nigala</s>). (RA 16.94.2)
I shall now describe another [method] — powder-binding (<s>curna-bandha</s>), O Queen of the Gods. (16.95)
Having added borax (<s>tankana</s>) to the pellet, ground with woman's fluid (<s>dvipadi-rasa</s>), (RA 16.96.1)

children.text:
naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ tat dhāmayitvā puṭe pacet //
                    (RA_16.96.2)
children.translated_text: the vanished-pellet, when dry, should be blown and then heated in a cycle. (RA 16.96.2)
One should wrap, O Queen of the Gods, with a ball and clamp; (RA 16.97.1)
with husk-fire on the ground, one should perform gentle steaming. (RA 16.97.2)

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā cūrṇaṃ bhavati śobhanam /
                    (RA_16.98.1)
children.translated_text: For one day and night, or three nights — a beautiful powder is produced. (RA 16.98.1)
Due to the absence of bound successive-bindings, the transmuter becomes twofold. (RA 16.98.2)
I shall now describe another [method] — the extremely rare cloth-binding (<s>patta-bandha</s>). (16.99)
Green vitriol (<s>kasisa</s>), borax (<s>tankana</s>), alkali (<s>ksara</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), sulfur (<s>gandha</s>), mica (<s>abhraka</s>), (16.100.1)
mercury — ground with citron (<s>matulunga</s>) juice for one <s>yama</s> (three hours). (RA 16.100.2)
A ball made of tin (<s>vanga</s>), silver (<s>tara</s>), mica (<s>abhra</s>), mercury, and <s>snuhi</s>-milk — (RA 16.101.1)
one should wrap with birch-bark (<s>bhurja-pattra</s>) and bind with cloth-thread. (16.101.2)

children.text:
ūrdhvādho gomayaṃ dattvā bhūmadhye svedayet tataḥ /
                    (102.1)
children.translated_text: Having placed cow-dung above and below, one should then steam [it] buried in the earth. (16.102.1)
One should perform grinding and steaming three times in this very manner. (RA 16.102.2)
One should coat according to regional custom and grind with jaggery (<s>guda</s>) and sour gruel (<s>kanjika</s>); (RA 16.103.1)
in a crucible coated with datura (<s>dhattura</s>) juice, one should place [it]. (RA 16.103.2)

children.text:
baddhvā mūṣāmukhaṃ devi saṃdhilepaṃ tu kārayet /
                    (RA_16.104.1)
children.translated_text: Having sealed the crucible's mouth, O Goddess, one should make a joint-coating; (RA 16.104.1)
one should place the crucible inside salt, and a larger crucible outside. (RA 16.104.2)

children.text:
mukhaṃ tasyāś ca mūṣāyā baddhvā loṇamṛdā tataḥ /
                    (RA_16.105.1)
children.translated_text: The mouth of that outer crucible, having sealed with salt-clay, (RA 16.105.1)
with husk-fire on the ground, one should perform gentle steaming. (RA 16.105.2)

children.text:
ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā citradharmā bhavanti te /
                    (RA_16.106.1)
children.translated_text: For one day and night, or three nights — they acquire variegated properties. (RA 16.106.1)
By this very method, one should perform seven times. (RA 16.106.2)

children.text:
antarbahiś ca baddhāste dharmaśuddhā bhavanti te //
                    (RA_16.107)
children.translated_text: Bound internally and externally, they become purified in [their] properties. (RA 16.107)
Mercury killed by sulfur, <s>kanksi</s>, green vitriol (<s>kasisa</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), (16.108.1)
<s>snuhi</s>-milkweed, borax (<s>tankana</s>), and <s>gunja</s> (abrus) — ground with sun-plant (<s>ravi</s>) milk — (RA 16.108.2)
they become aged (<s>puranaka</s>) quickly, granting <s>dharma</s>, <s>kama</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>moksa</s>. (RA 16.108.3)

children.text:
pañcabhāgaṃ tu śulvasya dvibhāgaṃ kuñjarasya ca /
                    (109.1)
children.translated_text: Five parts of copper and two parts of tin (<s>kunjara</s>), (16.109.1)
one should make leaf-forms (<s>daladharma</s>) and coat by the previous method. (RA 16.109.2)

children.text:
rasendro rañjati hy evaṃ kartavyaṃ sāraṇādikam /
                    (RA_16.110.1)
children.translated_text: The king of mercury is indeed colored thus — one should perform extraction (<s>sarana</s>) and the like. (RA 16.110.1)

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi kim anyac chrotum icchasi //
                    (110.2)
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Queen of the Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (16.110.2)
The glorious <s>Devi</s> said: (17.1.1)

children.text:
drāvaṇaṃ rañjanaṃ caiva pāradasya śrutaṃ mayā /
                    (RA_17.1.2)
children.translated_text: Liquefaction (<s>dravana</s>) and coloring (<s>ranjana</s>) of mercury have been heard by me; (RA 17.1.2)
please describe extraction (<s>sarana</s>) and transmuting application (<s>kramana</s>) in order. (RA 17.1.3)
The glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said: (17.2.1)

children.text: Herstellung eines vedhakas mit versch. sāraṇa-Prozeduren
children.translated_text: [Preparation of a transmuter with various extraction procedures]
Having made a cow-udder-shaped crucible (<s>gostani musa</s>), in the form of a datura flower, (17.2.2)

children.text:
tadardhaṃ pūrayet tailaṃ rañjitaṃ ca rasaṃ kṣipet //
                    (RA_17.2.3)
children.translated_text: one should fill half with oil and add the colored mercury. (RA 17.2.3)
With husk-fire on the outside of the crucible, one should apply [heat]; (RA 17.3.1)
the alloy (<s>khotaka</s>) combined with a twentieth part of lead, forming a circular mass (<s>samavarta</s>), (RA 17.3.2)
one should drop in with long tongs — [the mercury] becomes extracted (<s>sarita</s>). (RA 17.3.3)
With double gold thereafter, counter-extraction (<s>pratisarita</s>) is produced; (RA 17.4.1)
then with triple gold, secondary extraction (<s>anusarita</s>) is produced. (RA 17.4.2)
One should calcine by the alkaline-compound (<s>vida</s>) method as before, again and again; (RA 17.5.1)

children.text: anena vidhinā devi bhaveddvedhā tu vedhakaḥ // (RA_17.5.2)
children.translated_text: by this procedure, O Goddess, the transmuter becomes twofold. (RA 17.5.2)
[Editorial note: Mercury stepping-up.] <s>Bhūlatā</s>, red realgar (<s>śoṇitaśilā</s>), poison, borax, and mercury, (RA 17.6.1)
with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), ground with woman's breast-milk — [this is] a stepping-up [formula] for projection and coating. (RA 17.6.2)

children.text:
krāmaṇa indragopo viṣaṃ kāntaṃ daradaṃ rudhiraṃ tathā /
                    (7.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Stepping-up.] <s>Indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), poison, lodestone, cinnabar, and blood; (RA 17.7.1)
zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) and sesame oil — [this is] a stepping-up [formula] for projection and coating. (RA 17.7.2)

children.text:
krāmaṇa bhūlatā mākṣikaśilā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ rudhiraṃ viṣam /
                    (8.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Stepping-up.] <s>Bhūlatā</s>, pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), borax, blood, and poison; (RA 17.8.1)
crow's excrement, breast-milk, and the ear-wax of a she-buffalo; (RA 17.8.2)
<s>rāmaṭha</s> (asafoetida) too, O Great Goddess — [this is] a stepping-up [formula] for projection and coating. (RA 17.8.3)

children.text:
krāmaṇa bhūlatā lāṅgalī śṛṅgī kākaviṣṭhā ca śailajam /
                    (9.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Stepping-up.] <s>Bhūlatā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, crow's excrement, and <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch); (RA 17.9.1)
<s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, beeswax (<s>madhūcchiṣṭa</s>), blood, and the dust of the biped [woman]; (RA 17.9.2)

children.text:
surasā brahmasomā ca gṛdhrakarṇī ca lakṣaṇā /
                    (RA_17.10.1)
children.translated_text: <s>surasā</s> (holy basil), <s>brahmasomā</s>, <s>gṛdhrakarṇī</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>; (RA 17.10.1)
and the ear-wax of a buffalo — [this is] a stepping-up [formula] for projection and coating. (RA 17.10.2)
[Editorial note: Mercury stepping-up.] The eye-dirt of a <s>gaṇḍola</s> (iguana), a poisonous frog, and a buffalo — (RA 17.11.1)
combined with blood — [this is] the supreme stepping-up of mercury. (RA 17.11.2)

children.text:
rasakrāmaṇa viṣaṃ surendragopaś ca rocanā guggulustathā /
                    (12.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury stepping-up.] Poison, <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal), <s>rocanā</s> (ox gallstone), and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium); (RA 17.12.1)

children.text:
strīstanyaṃ caiva tair yukto lohe tu kramate rasaḥ //
                    (12.2)
children.translated_text: with woman's breast-milk — combined with these, the mercury steps up into metal. (RA 17.12.2)
[Editorial note: Mercury stepping-up.] With <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (sandalwood), <s>nimba</s> (neem) exudate, woman's breast-milk, poison, and borax, (RA 17.13.1)

children.text: goghṛtena samāyukto lohe tu kramate rasaḥ // (RA_17.13.2)
children.translated_text: combined with cow's ghee — the mercury steps up into metal. (RA 17.13.2)

children.text:
rasakrāmaṇa arivargahatau vaṅganāgau dvau krāmaṇaṃ param //
                    (14)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury stepping-up.] Tin and lead, killed by the enemy-group — [these form] the supreme stepping-up. (RA 17.14)
<s>Mātṛvāha</s> (a plant), crab, and the inner dirt of a conch; (RA 17.15.1)
and the exudate of <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) — [this is] the supreme stepping-up of mercury. (RA 17.15.2)
One should apply the stepping-up of the king of mercury at the time of transmutation; (RA 17.16.1)

children.text:
krāmaṇaṃ yo na jānāti śramastasya nirarthakaḥ //
                    (RA_17.16.2)
children.translated_text: one who does not know the stepping-up — his labor is fruitless. (RA 17.16.2)
Hereafter I shall declare the gold and silver leaf [procedures]. (RA 17.17)
Lead and mercury, ground equally, combined with the twelve aromatics; (RA 17.18.1)
ground in <s>dhattūraka</s> (Datura) juice — a pill in the shape of a chickpea. (RA 17.18.2)
