Four parts of silver and three parts of copper — (RA 17.19.1)

children.text:
samyag āvartya deveśi guṭikaikāṃ tu nikṣipet //
                    (RA_17.19.2)
children.translated_text: having properly rolled [them] together, O Goddess of the Gods, one should deposit one pill therein. (RA 17.19.2)

children.text: anena kramayogeṇa tāre tāmraṃ tu vāhayet / (RA_17.20.1)
children.translated_text: By this sequential procedure, one should carry copper into silver; (RA 17.20.1)

children.text:
yāvat tu jāyate raktaṃ tāraṃ caiva na saṃśayaḥ //
                    (RA_17.20.2)
children.translated_text: until red gold-silver is produced — there is no doubt. (RA 17.20.2)
Two parts of this should be taken, and five parts of silver; (RA 17.21.1)
combined with one part of gold, when melted, it becomes eightfold gold. (RA 17.21.2)
Copper killed with sulfur, combined with cinnabar; (RA 17.22.1)

children.text:
ārdrakaṃ mūlakaṃ śuṇṭhī laśunaṃ hiṅgu mākṣikam //
                    (RA_17.22.2)
children.translated_text: fresh ginger, radish, dry ginger, garlic, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) — (RA 17.22.2)
one should grind with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) and coat lead plates; (RA 17.23.1)
by firing, the lead dies — [becoming] vermilion-red in appearance. (RA 17.23.2)

children.text:
tat tāre triguṇe vyūḍhaṃ nirbījaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_17.24)
children.translated_text: That, carried into silver in triple proportion, becomes seedless (pure) gold. (RA 17.24)
[Editorial note: Silver coloring — black.]
With sulfur, orpiment (<s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s>), cinnabar, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), zinc (<s>kharpara</s>), and mercury; (RA 17.25.1)
in increasing proportions, with honey and ghee — one should coat with a fifth portion. (RA 17.25.2)
By firing and dry-firing, the silver becomes black in two ways. (RA 17.26)
Yellow sulfur, coated with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) exudate; (RA 17.27.1)
by giving three firings, the silver becomes gold. (RA 17.27.2)
[Editorial note: Silver coloring — removing whiteness.]
The yellow, black, and red groups, finely powdered as available; (RA 17.28.1)
soaked in cow's ghee, applied to silver by pouring — [this] destroys whiteness. (RA 17.28.2)
The red, yellow, and black groups, abundantly [soaked] with goat's milk; (RA 17.29.1)
one should keep [them] on silver for seven days — by pouring, redness increases. (RA 17.29.2)
When, by pouring and sprinkling, [the silver attains] the luster of a cat's eye — (RA 17.30.1)
that silver is called a leaf (<s>dala</s>) — the supreme blending (<s>melana</s>) is considered [complete]. (RA 17.30.2)

children.text: śulvasya kāṃsyakṛṣṇaṃ tu rasakena tu rañjayet / (31.1)
children.translated_text: The copper-black of bell-metal — one should color with zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>); (RA 17.31.1)

children.text:
dvau bhāgau tasya śulvasya tārasyaikaṃ ca melayet //
                    (31.2)
children.translated_text: two parts of that copper and one of silver should be blended. (RA 17.31.2)

children.text:
tadā tasya rasendrasya melanaṃ paramaṃ matam /
                    (RA_17.32.1)
children.translated_text: Then, of that mercury-king, the supreme blending is considered [complete]; (RA 17.32.1)
one should transmute with purified mercury at a hundredth ratio, O Queen of the Gods. (RA 17.32.2)
Gold, pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), and salt — one should grind with honey and ghee; (RA 17.33.1)
until it becomes saffron-colored (<s>kuṅkumābha</s>), with that one should cook in a lead vessel. (RA 17.33.2)

children.text:
samaṃ śulvaṃ tato deyaṃ tacchulvaṃ tārapattrake /
                    (RA_17.34.1)
children.translated_text: Equal copper should then be added — that copper [placed] on a silver plate; (RA 17.34.1)

children.text:
trivāraṃ śodhayed dattvā śuddhaṃ hemadalaṃ bhavet //
                    (34.2)
children.translated_text: purified three times by application — it becomes a pure gold leaf. (RA 17.34.2)

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ śulvaṃ tāraṃ ca pañcakam /
                    (35.1)
children.translated_text: Tin, lead, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), copper, and silver — these five; (RA 17.35.1)

children.text:
trivāraṃ śodhayed dattvā śuddhaṃ hemadalaṃ bhavet //
                    (35.2)
children.translated_text: purified three times by application — it becomes a pure gold leaf. (RA 17.35.2)
Orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), sulfur-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), zinc (<s>kharpara</s>), and poison; (RA 17.36.1)
combined with citron, coating tin metal — one should cook by firing. (RA 17.36.2)
Cinnabar, sulfur-stone, pyrite, rock salt, and poison; (RA 17.37.1)
combined with citron, coating iron metal — one should cook by firing. (RA 17.37.2)
Realgar (<s>kunaṭī</s>), sulfur-stone, pyrite, rock salt, and poison; (RA 17.38.1)
combined with citron, coating lead metal — one should cook by firing. (RA 17.38.2)

children.text: sarvaṃ hemadale vāhyaṃ hema baddhena vedhayet // (39)
children.translated_text: All should be carried into gold leaf — one should transmute with bound [mercury]. (RA 17.39)

children.text: tulyāṃśau hemakariṇau tīkṣṇaṃ dviguṇam eva ca / (40.1)
children.translated_text: Equal portions of gold and lodestone, and iron in double [proportion]; (RA 17.40.1)

children.text:
vyūḍhaṃ raktagaṇaiḥ siktaṃ tattāraṃ kanakaṃ bhavet //
                    (40.2)
children.translated_text: carried [together] and sprinkled with the red group — that silver becomes gold. (RA 17.40.2)

children.text: śulvaṃ tāpyahataṃ kṛtvā varanāgaṃ tu rañjayet / (41.1)
children.translated_text: Having made copper killed with pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), one should color excellent lead; (RA 17.41.1)

children.text:
taṃ nāgaṃ vāhayet tāre yāvad dhemadalaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_17.41.2)
children.translated_text: that lead should be carried into silver until it becomes gold leaf. (RA 17.41.2)
Poison equal to mercury, sulfur, combined with triple antimony (<s>añjana</s>); (RA 17.42.1)

children.text:
amlena tridinaṃ piṣṭvā tārārkau melayet samau //
                    (RA_17.42.2)
children.translated_text: having ground with acid for three days, one should blend silver and gold equally. (RA 17.42.2)
Cooked with the five earths, one should fire — with silver remaining; (RA 17.43.1)
thus, by three repetitions, one should color the silver to the finest [quality]. (RA 17.43.2)
Four parts each of tin-alloy and copper separately; (RA 17.44.1)
twelve [parts] of oil separately, and two each of brass (<s>rītikā</s>) and silver; (RA 17.44.2)
one part of gold — with silver remaining; (RA 17.45.1)
having the luster of a cat's eye, O Goddess — it becomes an excellent gold leaf. (RA 17.45.2)
Eight parts of silver, four parts of copper, two of lead, one of gold — (RA 17.46.1)

children.text:
sarvaṃ tato raktagaṇena siktaṃ tārāvaśeṣaṃ kanakaṃ karoti //
                    (46.2)
children.translated_text: all then sprinkled with the red group, with silver remaining — it makes gold. (RA 17.46.2)

children.text: rājāvartaṃ caturthaṃ ca daradaṃ ca pravālakam / (47.1)
children.translated_text: One quarter <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), cinnabar, and coral; (RA 17.47.1)
combined with gold and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>) — one should make [them] in equal portions. (RA 17.47.2)
Three parts of zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) — one should grind with ewe's milk; (RA 17.48.1)

children.text:
vaṭikāṃ kārayet paścāt chāyāyāṃ śoṣayet tataḥ //
                    (RA_17.48.2)
children.translated_text: one should make a pill, and then dry [it] in shade. (RA 17.48.2)
Combined with the five solvents (<s>pañcadrāvaka</s>), one should grind on a stone slab; (RA 17.49.1)
with this perfected paste, one should apply to <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (silver alloy). (RA 17.49.2)
The first [time] with equal paste, the second with half of that; (RA 17.50.1)
the third with a quarter portion — <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> is produced. (RA 17.50.2)

children.text:
pattre dāhe kaṣe chede hema taccākṣayaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_17.51)
children.translated_text: In the tests of foil, burning, touchstone, and cutting — that gold becomes imperishable. (RA 17.51)

children.text: gold:: rañjana:: black; extraction from silver
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold coloring — black; extraction from silver.]

children.text: sūtakaṃ daradaṃ tāpyaṃ gandhakaṃ kunaṭī tathā / (52.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury, cinnabar, pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), sulfur, and realgar (<s>kunaṭī</s>); (RA 17.52.1)
taken in progressively increasing [proportions], one should coat copper plates. (RA 17.52.2)
Having ground in the juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s> (wood-sorrel), one should give five firings; (RA 17.53.1)
that powder should be carried into silver — this becomes gold-extraction. (RA 17.53.2)

children.text: kanake yojayed devi kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ bhavet tataḥ // (RA_17.54)
children.translated_text: When applied to gold, O Goddess, it becomes black-colored thereby. (RA 17.54)
Having ground turmeric (<s>niśā</s>) with cow's urine, one should coat and pour on copper; (RA 17.55.1)
by hundred-fold purification, it becomes golden silver. (RA 17.55.2)
Now, copper extracted from bell-metal, or solidified [copper], O Beloved — (RA 17.56.1)

children.text:
ṣaḍguṇena tu nāgena śodhayitvā tato budhaḥ //
                    (RA_17.56.2)
children.translated_text: having purified with sixfold lead, the wise one — (RA 17.56.2)
should pour fifty [parts] of <s>sindhuvāra</s> (Vitex) into the mercury medium; (RA 17.57.1)

children.text:
kuṣmāṇḍasya rase paścāt saptavāraṃ tu dāpayet //
                    (RA_17.57.2)
children.translated_text: afterwards, one should immerse in the juice of <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd) seven times. (RA 17.57.2)

children.text:
tathā takre niśāyukte taptataptaṃ ca dāpayet /
                    (RA_17.58.1)
children.translated_text: Then in buttermilk combined with turmeric, one should immerse [it] heated-and-heated; (RA 17.58.1)
parrot-beak-and-<s>kiṃśuka</s>-colored, red when cut, and soft. (RA 17.58.2)

children.text:
tāpyena vāpyaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tat śulvaṃ kālikayā gatam //
                    (RA_17.59)
children.translated_text: That entire copper, applied with pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), acquires dark coating. (RA 17.59)
Cinnabar, <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame tree) juice, red <s>citraka</s> (leadwort); (RA 17.60.1)
the two turmerics, O Beautiful-hipped One — one should grind with goat's urine. (RA 17.60.2)
One should give [it as] pouring-application on copper seven times — without doubt; (RA 17.61.1)

children.text:
śulvaṃ sindūravarṇaṃ ca varaṃ hemadalaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_17.61.2)
children.translated_text: the copper [becomes] vermilion-colored — it becomes an excellent gold leaf. (RA 17.61.2)
Double [portions of] iron and tin-alloy — one should carry dark <s>ghoṣa</s> (bell-metal); (RA 17.62.1)
or, from a metalworker, in sequential one-two-three <s>pala</s> amounts. (RA 17.62.2)

children.text:
tripañcakaṃ ca nāgasya śulvasya ca palaṃ tathā /
                    (RA_17.63.1)
children.translated_text: Fifteen [parts] of lead and one <s>pala</s> of copper likewise; (RA 17.63.1)
when blown, what remains becomes like refined gold in appearance. (RA 17.63.2)
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), <s>śigru</s> (moringa), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), <s>karavīra</s> (oleander); (RA 17.64.1)
with <s>snuhī</s>-<s>arka</s> milk, tamarind acid, [and] <s>vajrakanda</s> (a tuber); (RA 17.64.2)
combined with buffalo milk — one should prepare a liquor (<s>surā</s>), O Goddess. (RA 17.64.3)
With <s>snuhī</s>-<s>arka</s> milk and salts, one should coat copper plates; (RA 17.65.1)
in the liquor mentioned first, one should cook for one day. (RA 17.65.2)
Coat as before [to produce] fire-colored [sheets] and sprinkle repeatedly with liquor; (RA 17.66.1)
revolve many times, making with <s>kuṇḍa</s>-cowrie shells. (RA 17.66.2)
Sublimate with <s>sarjikā</s> and <s>sindhudatta</s> salts and employ in operations. (RA 17.67)
One <s>pala</s> of <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) combined with gold and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>); (RA 17.68.1)
half a <s>pala</s> of rock salt, combined with citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice. (RA 17.68.2)
Then cook — when smelled, [it is] like saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>); (RA 17.69.1)
a paste like a firefly (<s>indragopa</s>) — calcine by the firing method. (RA 17.69.2)
That paste combined with honey, along with sugar and borax; (RA 17.70.1)
having made all into one and ground, cook with cow's milk. (RA 17.70.2)

children.text:
prāg eva śodhitaṃ śulvaṃ rasakalkena rañjayet /
                    (RA_17.71.1)
children.translated_text: Copper, previously purified, should be colored with the <s>rasaka</s> paste; (RA 17.71.1)

children.text:
rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi jāyate hema śobhanam //
                    (RA_17.71.2)
children.translated_text: color three times — fine gold is produced. (RA 17.71.2)
Soak <s>muni</s> (agastya) flowers, oleander (<s>karavīra</s>), and realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); (RA 17.72.1)

children.text:
tatpūrvaṃ rañjitaṃ śulvaṃ śilayā ca tathā yutam /
                    (RA_17.72.2)
children.translated_text: that previously colored copper, combined with realgar likewise; (RA 17.72.2)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — fine gold is produced. (RA 17.72.3)
With that same <s>rasaka</s> paste, make a silver pellet; (RA 17.73.1)
sprinkle <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil — that becomes divine gold. (RA 17.73.2)
<s>Arjunī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>padmacāriṇī</s>, <s>śakravāruṇī</s>; (RA 17.74.1)

children.text:
suvarṇā cauṣadhībhiś ca gairikeṇa tu pārvati /
                    (RA_17.74.2)
children.translated_text: <s>suvarṇā</s> (gold-plant) and other herbs, and ochre (<s>gairika</s>), O <s>Pārvatī</s>; (RA 17.74.2)

children.text:
viliptaṃ śulvapattraṃ tu niṣiktaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet //
                    (74.3)
children.translated_text: a copper sheet coated [with these] and sprinkled — becomes gold. (RA 17.74.3)
Peacock-throat vitriol (<s>mayūragrīvatuttha</s>), saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine); (RA 17.75.1)
the dung of a young calf, and <s>hālāhala</s> poison; (RA 17.75.2)
and red <s>citraka</s> powder — make all in equal parts. (RA 17.75.3)
Grind with medium sour [liquid] and dry in the shade; (RA 17.76.1)
combining with honey, coat lead (<s>nāga</s>) sheets. (RA 17.76.2)
Placed in a sealed mute crucible and blown — it colors the lead instantly. (RA 17.77)
With the juice of <s>śāka</s> leaves alone, sprinkle seven times; (RA 17.78.1)
or twenty-eight times, in the oil born of <s>bhūnāga</s>; (RA 17.78.2)
that lead becomes divine — [fit for] ornaments of the gods. (RA 17.78.3)
Alternatively, <s>bhūlatā</s> powder and lead powder in equal parts; (RA 17.79.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — when heated, sprinkle with oil. (RA 17.79.2)
When done thus seven times, it becomes sixteen-<s>varṇa</s> [colored gold]. (RA 17.80)
Dung of a young calf, lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), and sandalwood; (RA 17.81.1)
<s>haṃsapāda</s>-cinnabar, <s>bilva</s> pulp, and jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>). (RA 17.81.2)
Lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>) and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, with <s>śāka</s> leaf-water; (RA 17.82.1)
lead (<s>bhujaṅga</s>) would become gold by sprinkling a hundred times. (RA 17.82.2)
Madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), the two turmerics (<s>rajanīdvandva</s>), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, gold-pyrite; (RA 17.83.1)
safflower (<s>kausumbha</s>), product of poison-<s>sindhu</s>, cinnabar, and red sandalwood. (RA 17.83.2)
Combined with <s>śāka</s> leaves and <s>palāśa</s> flowers; (RA 17.84.1)
by sprinkling a hundred times, it colors the lead, O beloved. (RA 17.84.2)
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, arsenic-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>), and the two turmerics; (RA 17.85.1)
soak seven times with the juice of <s>cāmīkara</s> [gold-plant]. (RA 17.85.2)
Quenched in <s>śiṃśapā</s> [rosewood] oil, sublimated seven times; (RA 17.86.1)

children.text:
nāgaṃ rañjati ca kṣipraṃ rañjitaṃ cākṣayaṃ bhavet //
                    (86.2)
children.translated_text: the lead is colored quickly — and once colored, it becomes imperishable. (RA 17.86.2)
Coral (<s>vidruma</s>), cinnabar, and iron — sublimated with this; (RA 17.87.1)
sprinkle with the juice of madder and <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame tree) and <s>śāka</s>. (RA 17.87.2)
By sublimation and sprinkling, colored in sequence thus; (RA 17.88.1)

children.text: bhujago hematāṃ yāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // (RA_17.88.2)
children.translated_text: the lead (<s>bhujaga</s>) attains gold-hood — no deliberation is needed here. (RA 17.88.2)

children.text:
tāradala uktaṃ hemadalaṃ devi varaṃ tāradalaṃ śṛṇu //
                    (RA_17.89)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Silver-leaf.] Having described gold-leaf, O Goddess, now hear the excellent silver-leaf. (RA 17.89)

children.text:
śvetābhraṃ kāñjike svinnaṃ trivāraṃ puṭitaṃ tataḥ /
                    (90.1)
children.translated_text: White mica, steamed in sour gruel, then fired three times; (RA 17.90.1)
tin with a little borax should be sublimated in purified copper. (RA 17.90.2)

children.text:
pañcamāṃśena miśraṃ tat tāraṃ tālaṃ ca vedhayet /
                    (RA_17.91.1)
children.translated_text: Mixed at one-fifth, that should transmute silver and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>); (RA 17.91.1)

children.text:
tattālaṃ melayet tāre drutaṃ siktena vedhayet //
                    (RA_17.91.2)
children.translated_text: unite that orpiment with silver — transmute with the melted quenched [preparation]. (RA 17.91.2)
Mercury and rock salt, one [part] each; sesame and <s>sarjī</s> (alkali), two [parts] each; (RA 17.92.1)
one <s>ṭaṅka</s> [of borax] — grind with gold-juice (<s>kanakarasa</s>) for three days. (RA 17.92.2)
Coat copper sheets with that, and blow when revolved; (RA 17.93.1)
grind <s>iṅgudī</s> together with <s>tāla</s>-root with sour curds (<s>dadhy-amla</s>). (RA 17.93.2)
Pour molten copper into the midst of that — seven times yields the leaf; (RA 17.94.1)
combine with one-third of the seed, O Supreme Goddess. (RA 17.94.2)
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>hayaghnī</s>, <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>; (RA 17.95.1)
<s>godhāvatī</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, white <s>arka</s>, <s>śakravāruṇī</s>. (RA 17.95.2)
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), and <s>pañcāṅgulī</s>; (RA 17.96.1)
<s>punarnava</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, and <s>cakramardaka</s>. (RA 17.96.2)
<s>Guḍūcī</s> and <s>hiṃsrā</s> — one, two, three, and four [parts]; (RA 17.97.1)
after fermentation (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) with buffalo's milk for seven days, O beloved; (RA 17.97.2)
when sprinkling is performed, purification of copper is produced. (RA 17.97.3)
Coat copper sheets with orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) at one-sixteenth; (RA 17.98.1)
having placed in a sealed crucible, revolve three times. (RA 17.98.2)
The white group: threefold alkali — conch, rock salt, and <s>sarjikā</s>; (RA 17.99.1)

children.text:
dantāḥ kapardāḥ kambuś ca śuktayaḥ śulvavāpanāḥ //
                    (RA_17.99.2)
children.translated_text: teeth, cowrie shells, conch, and oyster shells — [these are] copper-sublimates. (RA 17.99.2)
At one-quarter [proportion], by sprinkling with liquor, it becomes nail-white [pale]. (RA 17.100)
Three parts of lodestone, and two [parts] of <s>āra</s> (brass) and silver; (RA 17.101.1)
ten parts of tin — transmute by the silver-transmutation [method]. (RA 17.101.2)

children.text: ārasya dviguṇaṃ tāraṃ tārāt kāntaṃ caturguṇam / (102.1)
children.translated_text: Double the <s>āra</s> in silver; fourfold the lodestone over silver; (RA 17.102.1)
eightfold tin over lodestone — transmute by the silver-transmutation [method]. (RA 17.102.2)

children.text: tālaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā vajrīkṣīreṇa marditam / (103.1)
children.translated_text: Having made orpiment and mercury equal, ground with <s>vajrī</s> milk; (RA 17.103.1)

children.text:
puṭaṃ dattvā tu yantreṇa sattvaṃ patati śobhanam //
                    (103.2)
children.translated_text: having applied firing with the apparatus — a fine essence falls down. (RA 17.103.2)
Having revolved tin, O Queen of the Gods, grind with <s>vajrī</s> milk; (RA 17.104.1)
twenty-one times — the best purification of tin. (RA 17.104.2)

children.text: tadvaṅgaṃ jārayet sūtaṃ samaṃ vā dviguṇādikam // (105)
children.translated_text: That tin should calcine mercury — in equal or double-and-more [proportion]. (RA 17.105)
With <s>bhallāta</s> (marking nut), <s>rājikā</s> (mustard) oil, conch powder, and flux (<s>viḍa</s>); (RA 17.106.1)

children.text:
nāgavaṅgau bhavet tena samaṃ vaṅgena sāraṇāt //
                    (RA_17.106.2)
children.translated_text: lead and tin [are produced] thereby — by extracting with equal tin. (RA 17.106.2)
And by sprinkling with alkali-water — similarly the seed in many ways; (RA 17.107.1)
I shall describe the method by which softening is produced. (RA 17.107.2)

children.text:
mṛdūkaraṇa (gen.) ghṛtaṃ dadhi payaḥ kṣaudraṃ
                    bilvajambīrakadravaiḥ / (108.1)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Softening (of metals).] Ghee, curds, milk, honey, [combined] with <s>bilva</s> and citron (<s>jambīra</s>) juices; (RA 17.108.1)
combined with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>) and sesame — [this is] a softening agent by sprinkling. (RA 17.108.2)
Elephant tusk, horse hoof, ram's horn, and steel (<s>sairibha</s>); (RA 17.109.1)
combined with conch exudate — sprinkle seven times. (RA 17.109.2)
Split a thousandfold, the leaf attains softness. (RA 17.110)
In the oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> [<s>Celastrus</s>] and safflower, or in <s>kārañja</s> [<s>Pongamia</s>] oil; (RA 17.111.1)
quenching is greatly recommended by the experts for gold. (RA 17.111.2)

children.text: āvartyamānaṃ tāre ca yadi tannaiva nirmalam / (112.1)
children.translated_text: If when being revolved in silver it does not become pure; (RA 17.112.1)
by sublimation with glass and borax, it quickly attains purity. (RA 17.112.2)
[Editorial note: <s>Candrārka</s> (moon-sun alloy): softening.]
With honey, <s>madhu</s> [Madhuca], ram's ghee, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> [earth], jaggery, and rock salt; (RA 17.113.1)
sublimation with oyster shell, conch, and liquor — <s>candrārka</s> becomes soft. (RA 17.113.2)
With honey, oil, and ghee, and by quenching in calf's urine; (RA 17.114.1)
softness is produced even in the leaves of hard essences. (RA 17.114.2)
With tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) juice, sea salts, milk, and <s>arka</s> fire; (RA 17.115.1)
purified silver is produced, resembling a conch, <s>kunda</s> flower, or the moon. (RA 17.115.2)

children.text:
yadi tannirmalaṃ naiva tadā tadvat punaḥ pacet /
                    (RA_17.116.1)
children.translated_text: If it does not become pure, then cook it again as before; (RA 17.116.1)
this procedure is declared and honored for silver operations. (RA 17.116.2)
[Editorial note: Gold: coloring: red.]
<s>Kaṅguṇī</s> oil, madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), the two turmerics, and saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>); (RA 17.117.1)
by quenching, [the preparation] makes gold [with] luster like the young sun. (RA 17.117.2)
Adding half copper [and] sulphur, and half that of killed mercury; (RA 17.118.1)
grind with the juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s> (wood-sorrel) for three days. (RA 17.118.2)
Drenched with <s>citraka</s> juice, coat the pale gold; (RA 17.119.1)
having cooked with the five clays, O Goddess — this is the best gold-enhancement. (RA 17.119.2)

children.text: gold:: vedha:: pāṇḍura => divya (improvement of colour)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold: transmutation: pale → divine (improvement of color).]

children.text: hema śulvaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ samabhāgāni kārayet / (120.1)
children.translated_text: Gold, copper, and iron in equal parts; (RA 17.120.1)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an ingot is produced instantly. (RA 17.120.2)
One part of the ingot, combined with mercury and gold; (RA 17.121.1)
cook with sour <s>anuja</s> [liquid] until it becomes like saffron. (RA 17.121.2)

children.text:
śatāṃśena tu tenaiva vedhayed dhema pāṇḍuram /
                    (RA_17.122.1)
children.translated_text: With that, at a hundredth ratio, transmute pale gold; (RA 17.122.1)
divine gold is produced — a two-<s>varṇa</s> enhancement results. (RA 17.122.2)
Until it becomes pure, fire with salt-ash; (RA 17.123.1)
quench in red oil — fine gold is produced. (RA 17.123.2)
Gold-ochre (<s>svarṇagairika</s>) and sulphur, ground with pungent oil; (RA 17.124.1)
Or, in citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) acid, <s>Rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>). (RA 17.124b)
Or, pigeon-dung (<s>viṭkapota</s>) [ash], <s>Rājāvarta</s>, and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) — (RA 17.125a)
by firing, they make white gold into saffron-hued (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) [gold]. (RA 17.125b)
The powder of <s>Rājāvarta</s>, with <s>Śirīṣa</s> (albizzia) flower-juice, (RA 17.126a)
treated many times — added at one-eightieth proportion, it bestows color. (RA 17.126b)

children.text: śataśaḥ kaṅguṇītaile tāmraṃ hemnā samaṃ drutam / (127.1)
children.translated_text: Copper melted a hundred times in <s>Kaṅguṇī</s> (celastrus) oil, equal to gold, (RA 17.127a)
with pyrite added as quenching — at one-hundredth proportion, it produces color. (RA 17.127b)
With cotton seeds, cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), rock salt, and ochre (<s>gairika</s>), (RA 17.128a)
with <s>pattrālaktaka</s> (leaf-lac), <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder), red sandalwood, and coral (<s>vidruma</s>), (RA 17.128b)
combined with jaggery, marking nut (<s>bhallātaka</s>), fat, calf dung, and brick — (RA 17.129a)
by quenching, white gold becomes sun-colored. (RA 17.129b)

children.text:
varṇapuṭa (?) raktāṣṭakaṃ trayo bhāgāḥ trayo bhāgāḥ
                    samudrajam / (130.1)
children.translated_text: [Color-firing:] Three parts of the red-group-of-eight, three parts of sea-salt — (RA 17.130a)
with the water of white <s>arka</s> (calotropis) leaf, the firing bestows color. (RA 17.130b)

children.text:
raktapītau samau kṛtvā tābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca mākṣikam /
                    (131.1)
children.translated_text: Having made the red and yellow [colorants] equal, with pyrite equal to those — (RA 17.131a)
stirring with <s>karañja</s> (pongamia) oil, one should smelt in a sealed crucible. (RA 17.131b)
Once [the gold is treated], at one-tenth of the yellow [colorant]; ten [times], at one-hundredth of the yellow; (RA 17.132a)
a hundred [times], at one-thousandth of the yellow; with half [that amount], it transmutes a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million). (RA 17.132b)
Salt treated a hundred times in <s>kiṃśuka</s> (butea) juice — (RA 17.133a)
with borax by a firing, it bestows color-enhancement. (RA 17.133b)

children.text: lohacūrṇaṃ trayo bhāgā gairikaṃ dviguṇaṃ tathā / (134.1)
children.translated_text: Three parts of iron powder and double that of ochre — (RA 17.134a)
one should moisten with honey, white lotus (<s>kumuda</s>) water, and [cow's] urine. (RA 17.134b)
One should grind with <s>kodrava</s> (millet) and place in a cowshed. (RA 17.135a)

children.text:
aśītyaṃśena tad idaṃ vāpād varṇapradaṃ bhavet //
                    (RA_17.135.2)
children.translated_text: That, at one-eightieth proportion, by quenching, bestows color. (RA 17.135b)
Gold with excess copper — one should fire in a sealed crucible. (RA 17.136a)
Then quenching with mineral-water is recommended. (RA 17.136b)
Coated with sea-salt and ochre, melted — it attains softness. (RA 17.137a)
Coated with cow-dung ash in equal proportion, one should apply. (RA 17.137b)
Gold with excess copper, by firing, attains purity. (RA 17.138)
Having coated the crucible with a paste of <s>nāgāsthi</s> (lead-bone, litharge) ash, the discerning one (RA 17.139a)
should place [the gold] in a sealed crucible — it becomes permanent gold-foil. (RA 17.139b)

children.text:
tatas tan mṛdubhir ghoṭaiḥ samprasārya vicakṣaṇaḥ /
                    (140.1)
children.translated_text: Then, the discerning one, having spread it out with gentle hammering, (RA 17.140a)

children.text:
taptataptaṃ niṣektavyaṃ yāvat tan mṛdutāṃ vrajet //
                    (140.2)
children.translated_text: should quench it while heated again and again, until it attains softness. (RA 17.140b)
Having coated it with a paste of sea-salt mineral, the discerning one (RA 17.141a)
should place it on a <s>palāśa</s> (butea) leaf and burn it with mild fire. (RA 17.141b)

children.text:
tāvat pacet paced dhīmān yāvannirmalatāṃ vrajet /
                    (142.1)
children.translated_text: The wise one should cook and re-cook until it attains purity. (RA 17.142a)

children.text:
tatas tacchītale kṛtvā toye nirvāpayet tataḥ //
                    (RA_17.142.2)
children.translated_text: Then, having cooled it, one should quench it in water. (RA 17.142b)

children.text:
tāvad eva vidhiḥ kāryo yāvad varṇaḥ samāgataḥ //
                    (RA_17.143)
children.translated_text: This procedure should be performed until the [proper] color is obtained. (RA 17.143)
Then one should heat it again, combined with cow-dung powder. (RA 17.144a)
Heated from the [sun's] heat, the wise one should throw it into salt. (RA 17.144b)
The well-drawn gold should then be cooked with salt and ochre. (RA 17.145a)

children.text:
karṣakeṇa tu saṃśodhya bhūyo bhūyo vicakṣaṇaḥ //
                    (RA_17.145.2)
children.translated_text: The discerning one should purify with a scraper, again and again. (RA 17.145b)
One should coat and fire for the purpose of generating color. (RA 17.146a)
<s>Tārāriṣṭa</s> (silver alloy), O Goddess, should be cooked with red oil. (RA 17.146b)

children.text: niṣecayec ca śataśo dalaṃ rajyati rakṣitam // (RA_17.147)
children.translated_text: Quenching a hundred times — the foil, when preserved, takes on color. (RA 17.147)
One should carry the mercury and subsidiary mineral group into lead and tin. (RA 17.148a)

children.text:
nāgavaṅgau punaḥ śulve śulvaṃ tāre tu nirvahet //
                    (148.2)
children.translated_text: Lead and tin in turn into copper; copper into silver. (RA 17.148b)

children.text:
tāraṃ niṣiktaṃ deveśi raktataile punaḥ punaḥ /
                    (RA_17.149.1)
children.translated_text: Silver, O Goddess, quenched in red oil again and again — (RA 17.149a)
auspicious gold is produced, free from all defects. (RA 17.149b)
Combined with half-gold, the residue of mercury (<s>rasocchiṣṭa</s>) is commended. (RA 17.150a)
Divine gold is produced, supreme, equal to the base-measure. (RA 17.150b)

children.text:
vaṅgābhraṃ sitatāpyaṃ vā śailaṃ vā vāpayet site /
                    (151.1)
children.translated_text: Tin-mica, or white pyrite, or bitumen (<s>śaila</s>) — one should quench in silver. (RA 17.151a)
That, at one-tenth proportion in silver, bestows color-enhancement. (RA 17.151b)
[Hundredth-proportion method:] Ninety-eight parts of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. (RA 17.152)
Each one-part of mercury-gold [added] is known as a hundred-fold transmutation. (RA 17.153a)
By this sequential method, [it becomes] a thousandth-proportion transmuter. (RA 17.153b)

children.text:
mūṣāṃ tu gostanīṃ kṛtvā dalapūrṇāṃ tathā dṛḍhām /
                    (154.1)
children.translated_text: Having made a cow-udder-shaped crucible, filled with foils, sturdy — (RA 17.154a)
one should smelt the foil; when that becomes pure and lustrous — (RA 17.154b)

children.text:
krāmaṇena samāyuktaṃ rasaṃ dattvā tu vedhayet /
                    (RA_17.155.1)
children.translated_text: having added mercury endowed with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (traversing power), one should transmute. (RA 17.155a)
The foil-leaf, coated with mercury, placed inside a copper vessel, (RA 17.155b)
coated on top with clay, applying mild fire — (RA 17.156a)
the intelligent one should always roll [it] with seed [metal] and store [it]. (RA 17.156b)

children.text:
ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tilacūrṇaṃ ca śītale tu nivāpayet /
                    (RA_17.157.1)
children.translated_text: Borax and sesame powder — one should quench in the cooled [product]. (RA 17.157a)

children.text:
rasasiddhaṃ tu kanakaṃ pakṣaikaṃ sthāpayed bhuvi /
                    (157.2)
children.translated_text: The mercury-perfected gold should be stored in the ground for one fortnight. (RA 17.157b)
Having extracted and then opened it, it may be sold, O Goddess. (RA 17.157c)

children.text:
punar anyaṃ pravakṣyāmi rasavedho yathā bhavet //
                    (RA_17.158)
children.translated_text: I shall now describe another [method] — how mercury-transmutation operates. (RA 17.158)
[Lead → gold, transmutation with mercury:]
Two <s>palas</s> of sesame-and-mustard powder should be given, (RA 17.159a)

children.text:
dve pale ca haridrāyā ekatraiva tu mardayet //
                    (RA_17.159.2)
children.translated_text: two <s>palas</s> of turmeric — one should grind everything together. (RA 17.159b)
One should grind in an earthen vessel, five <s>palas</s> of lead; (RA 17.160a)
one should add perfected mercury and stir with a rod. (RA 17.160b)

children.text:
punaś ca vāpayet tāvat yāvat kaṭhinatāṃ vrajet /
                    (RA_17.161.1)
children.translated_text: One should add again and again until it attains hardness. (RA 17.161a)
That lead becomes divine, with luster resembling <s>Jāmbūnada</s> (river-gold). (RA 17.161b)
I shall describe the unsealing (<s>udghāṭa</s>) of mercury-transmuted lead. (RA 17.162)

children.text: ghoṣākṛṣṭaṃ tu yat śulvaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśena yojayet / (163.1)
children.translated_text: Copper drawn by sound (<s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s>) — one should combine at one-sixteenth proportion. (RA 17.163a)
Having combined all and rolled [them], one should quench in goat's urine. (RA 17.163b)
Freed from all defects, beautiful gold is produced. (RA 17.163c)
This is renowned as 'metal-transmutation' (<s>lohavedha</s>), O Goddess, in its extended form. (RA 17.164)

children.text:
yathā lohe tathā dehe kartavyaḥ sūtakaḥ sadā /
                    (RA_17.165.1)
children.translated_text: As [it works] in metal, so in the body — mercury should always be employed. (RA 17.165a)
It produces equality, O Goddess, entering both body and metal. (RA 17.165b)

children.text:
pūrvaṃ lohe parīkṣeta tato dehe prayojayet /
                    (RA_17.166.1)
children.translated_text: First one should test on metal; then apply to the body. (RA 17.166a)

children.text:
tan mam ācakṣva deveśi kim anyac chrotum icchasi //
                    (RA_17.166.2)
children.translated_text: Tell me about that, O Goddess of Gods — what else do you wish to hear? (RA 17.166b)
Chapter] 18
The blessed Goddess spoke: (RA 18.1a)

children.text: lohavedhās tvayā deva yad artham upavarṇitāḥ / (RA_18.1.2)
children.translated_text: O God, the metal-transmutations you have described in detail — (RA 18.1b)

children.text:
taṃ dehavedham ācakṣva yena syāt khecarī gatiḥ //
                    (RA_18.1.3)
children.translated_text: describe the body-transmutation (<s>dehavedhā</s>) by which the state of sky-roving (<s>khecarīgati</s>) is attained. (RA 18.1c)
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> spoke: (RA 18.2a)

children.text:
prathamaṃ śodhayed dehaṃ paścāt kalkaṃ samācaret /
                    (RA_18.2.2)
children.translated_text: First one should purify the body; then one should perform the paste-treatment (<s>kalka</s>). (RA 18.2b)

children.text:
anyathā na bhavet siddhiḥ rase caiva rasāyane //
                    (RA_18.2.3)
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there will be no <s>siddhi</s> in mercury or in rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 18.2c)

children.text: prātaḥ prātaḥ pibed ādau tridinaṃ ghṛtasaindhavam / (3.1)
children.translated_text: Every morning, first one should drink ghee with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) for three days. (RA 18.3a)

children.text:
ketakyāḥ stanajaṃ kvāthaṃ tadanu tridinaṃ pibet //
                    (RA_18.3.2)
children.translated_text: Then one should drink a decoction of <s>Ketakī</s> (screwpine) breast-milk for three days. (RA 18.3b)
Having performed sweating (<s>svedana</s>) by the proper method, with barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>) and sugar, (RA 18.4a)
one should drink a decoction of <s>Varā</s> (triphala) for three days, O one worshipped by gods and demons. (RA 18.4b)
A decoction of <s>Kaṭukarohiṇī</s> (hellebore) — when purgation is properly achieved, (RA 18.5a)
for three days, one should eat barley-food (<s>yāvakānna</s>) combined with ghee. (RA 18.5b)
By consuming pills of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) seed and anthelmintics — (RA 18.6a)
one should cause the expulsion of worms; then with <s>Kākeṣṭa</s> (crow's favorite) water — (RA 18.6b)
from <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), pepper (<s>marica</s>), rock salt, turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>), black pepper (<s>kaṇa</s>), and dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), (RA 18.7a)
with <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalakī), jaggery, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> (embelia) — [one should take] the powder for three days. (RA 18.7b)
Having thus purified [the body], [one should eat] rice food with milk, green gram (<s>mudga</s>) broth, and barley-gruel. (RA 18.8a)
Then, having become strong, one should follow the rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) procedure. (RA 18.8b)
With <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) juice, ghee, honey, and milks from the <s>surataru</s> (wish-fulfilling trees), (RA 18.9a)
one should churn out oil, O Goddess, in two, four, or six <s>pala</s> measures. (RA 18.9b)
In small, medium, or large measures, one should drink daily for three months. (RA 18.10a)

children.text:
āroṭaṃ bhakṣayet paścāt jīrṇaṃ ca tadanantaram //
                    (RA_18.10.2)
children.translated_text: Afterwards, one should consume <s>āroṭa</s> (mercury-sublimate), and then [wait for] its digestion. (RA 18.10b)

children.text:
kṣetrīkṛtya tato dehaṃ tato bhakṣyaṃ tu vardhayet //
                    (RA_18.11)
children.translated_text: Having made the body into a field (<s>kṣetrīkṛtya</s>) [i.e., prepared], one should then increase the dosage. (RA 18.11)
Purified with mica and pyrite, then distilled, (RA 18.12a)
the mercury — ground with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (amaranth) and <s>bhṛṅga</s> (eclipta) — [and then] deposited, (RA 18.12b)
should be consumed as <s>āroṭa</s> — first, for body-accomplishment (<s>dehasiddhi</s>). (RA 18.12c)

children.text:
rasāyana (cont.) athavā bhasmatāṃ prāptaṃ ṣaḍvāraṃ
                    kalkayogataḥ / (13.1)
children.translated_text: [Rejuvenation continued:] Or, the mercury having reached the state of ash, through six rounds of paste-treatment — (RA 18.13a)
for a full year, one should consume the <s>āroṭaka</s> (mercury-sublimate). (RA 18.13b)
With shilajit, honey, <s>viḍaṅga</s> (embelia), ghee, iron, <s>abhayā</s> (terminalia), mercury, and pyrite consumed — (RA 18.14a)
the weak bodily constituents (<s>dhātu</s>) are replenished in fifteen days, as the moon [waxes]. (RA 18.14b)
With <s>Bakakanyā</s> (crane-maiden plant) juice, honey, two kinds of turmeric (<s>dvi-niśā</s>), <s>triphala</s>, and jaggery — (RA 18.15a)
the mercury, made into a paste, combined with mica, magnetite, honey, and ghee — (RA 18.15b)
having eaten [it], one attains immortality — [this is] the supreme body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). (RA 18.15)
The powder of mica-essence (<s>abhrakasattva</s>), or of lodestone (<s>kāntaloha</s>), (RA 18.16)
or of iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), O Great Goddess, steeped in <s>triphalā</s> decoction, (RA 18.16)
until it resembles collyrium (<s>añjana</s>), purified through cloth-straining, (RA 18.17)
with <s>bhṛṅgāmalaka</s> essence and with turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>) juice, (RA 18.17)
sealed-heated, combined with mercury, accompanied by ghee and honey, (RA 18.18)
placed inside an iron case, established in grain for one month; (RA 18.18)
one should lick [it] with ghee and honey — [this is] the supreme body-preparation. (RA 18.19)
By using thus for one year, a man attains a thousand-year lifespan. (RA 18.19)

children.text:
rasasiddheḥ purā hema guñjāmātraṃ dine dine /
                    (RA_18.20.1)
children.translated_text: Before mercury-perfection (<s>rasasiddhi</s>), one should eat gold, a <s>guñjā</s>-measure daily, (RA 18.20)
for the purpose of body-perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>) — [then] mercury-perfection is achieved. (RA 18.20)
Lodestone-mica-essence (<s>kāntābhrasattva</s>) with mercury, slightly calcined with gold, (RA 18.21)
one should lick first, with equal [portions of] honey and ghee — [this is] the supreme body-preparation. (RA 18.21)

children.text:
varṣaṃ varṣārdham athavā pūrvamevaṃ tu bhakṣayet //
                    (RA_18.22)
children.translated_text: For one year, or half a year — one should eat as previously [described]. (RA 18.22)
Mercury digested with diamond, O <s>Devī</s>, is proclaimed the best; (RA 18.23)
digested with gold is middling; digested with silver is the lowest, O Beloved. (RA 18.23)
When gold-digested ash-mercury is consumed, one attains the state of <s>Rudra</s>; (RA 18.24)

children.text:
viṣṇutvaṃ tārajīrṇe tu brahmatvaṃ bhāskareṇa tu //
                    (RA_18.24.2)
children.translated_text: the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with silver-digested; the state of <s>Brahmā</s> with sun[-metal, i.e. gold]; (RA 18.24)
with iron-digested, [one becomes] Lord of Wealth [<s>Kubera</s>]; with mercury [digested in] quicksilver, the state of the Sun; (RA 18.25)

children.text: vājare tu śaśāṅkatvam analatvaṃ tu rohaṇe / (RA_18.25.2)
children.translated_text: with tin, the state of the Moon; with copper, the state of Fire. (RA 18.25)
In general, with iron, a man attains the state of <s>Indra</s>. (RA 18.25)

children.text:
evaṃ yo lohajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayed bhasmasūtakam /
                    (RA_18.26.1)
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever eats metal-digested ash-mercury — (RA 18.26)

children.text:
jalena jalarūpaḥ syāt sthalena sthalatāṃ vrajet //
                    (RA_18.26.2)
children.translated_text: with water he becomes water-formed; with land he attains the state of land. (RA 18.26)
In [the element of] fire, [he becomes] fiery; stronger than even wind; (RA 18.27)
a destroyer, creator, self-manifested, a bestower of curses and boons. (RA 18.27)

children.text:
yatra mūtrapurīṣaṃ tu sādhakas tu parityajet /
                    (RA_18.28.1)
children.translated_text: Wherever the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) discharges urine and feces, (RA 18.28)

children.text:
pāṣāṇo mṛnmayaṃ tatra spaṣṭaṃ bhavati kāñcanam //
                    (RA_18.28.2)
children.translated_text: stone and clay there manifestly become gold. (RA 18.28)
The sweat of his limbs transmutes the eight metals; (RA 18.29)

children.text:
tat sarvaṃ kanakaṃ nityaṃ bhakṣite dvādaśe pale /
                    (RA_18.29.2)
children.translated_text: all that [becomes] gold perpetually — when twelve <s>palas</s> have been consumed, (RA 18.29)
[one becomes] equal to <s>Rudra</s>, O Great Goddess, a causer of freedom from old age and death. (RA 18.29)

children.text:
bhasmasūtaṃ tathā tāraṃ bhakṣayet ṣoḍaśaṃ palam /
                    (RA_18.30.1)
children.translated_text: Ash-mercury with silver — one should consume sixteen <s>palas</s>; (RA 18.30)
or one should eat silver-digested ash-mercury; (RA 18.30)

children.text:
śulvaṃ ca vaṅgaghoṣaṃ ca tatsvedāt tāratāṃ vrajet //
                    (30.3)
children.translated_text: copper, tin, and tin-ore — by his sweat, [these] attain the state of silver. (RA 18.30)
Or one should eat iron-digested ash-mercury; (RA 18.31)

children.text:
mūtreṇa tasya spṛṣṭaṃ tu vaṅgaṃ vrajati tāratām //
                    (RA_18.31.2)
children.translated_text: touched by his urine, tin attains the state of silver. (RA 18.31)
By a single quenching, stabilization of lead and tin [is achieved]. (RA 18.32)

children.text:
guñjāmātraṃ rasaṃ devi hemajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet /
                    (RA_18.33.1)
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s>-measure of mercury, O <s>Devī</s>, gold-digested — one should eat; (RA 18.33)
two <s>guñjās</s> of silver-digested; three of copper-digested. (RA 18.33)
For iron-, mica-, and lodestone[-digested mercury], one <s>māṣa</s> [is the dose]; one <s>guñjā</s> produces liquefaction; (RA 18.34)
diamond- and <s>vaikrānta</s>-digested [mercury] should be consumed accompanied by ghee. (RA 18.34)
Lead, tin, mercury, ash, combined with poison and subsidiary poison — (RA 18.35)

children.text:
mātrāyuktaṃ tataś caiva bhakṣayec ca rasāyane //
                    (RA_18.35.2)
children.translated_text: properly dosed, one should then consume for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). (RA 18.35)

children.text:
hema tāraṃ tathā kāntaṃ jāyate'gnisahaṃ kramāt /
                    (RA_18.36.1)
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and lodestone become fire-resistant gradually; (RA 18.36)
this bound king of mercury bestows perfection of the body. (RA 18.36)
With diamond, lodestone, pyrite (<s>mākṣīka</s>), <s>vaikrānta</s>, mica, and gold — (RA 18.37)

children.text:
etair jīrṇair yathālābhaṃ rasaḥ śasto rasāyane //
                    (RA_18.37.2)
children.translated_text: digested with these as available, mercury is recommended for rejuvenation. (RA 18.37)
The six auxiliary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>) too should be conveyed for the purpose of consumption; (RA 18.38)
one should consume one <s>pala</s> of iron-digested [mercury]. (RA 18.38)
For ten thousand years, with diamond-body, he lives. (RA 18.39)

children.text:
evaṃ ca dvādaśapalaṃ tīkṣṇajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet /
                    (RA_18.40.1)
children.translated_text: Thus, one should consume twelve <s>palas</s> of iron-digested [mercury]; (RA 18.40)
thus one lives a great <s>kalpa</s>; at the end of dissolution, one goes to <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 18.40)
With one <s>pala</s> of copper-digested ash-[mercury], one attains a hundred-thousand-year lifespan; (RA 18.41)
with two <s>palas</s>, a crore-year lifespan; with three <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>. (RA 18.41)
With four <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; with five <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>; (RA 18.42)

children.text:
ṣaṣṭhe pale ca samprāpte mahākalpaṃ sa jīvati //
                    (RA_18.42.2)
children.translated_text: when the sixth <s>pala</s> is reached, he lives a great <s>kalpa</s>. (RA 18.42)
With one <s>pala</s> of gold-digested ash-[mercury], the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>; (RA 18.43)
with two <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; with three <s>palas</s>, the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>; (RA 18.43)
with four <s>palas</s>, O Queen of the Gods, a man attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 18.43)
When three <s>palas</s> of gold-digested ash-mercury are consumed in sequence, (RA 18.44)
eighty-eight thousand <s>yoginīs</s>, proud in their power, (RA 18.44)
stand as his servants; the man becomes capable of assuming any form at will. (RA 18.44)
Whatever form he contemplates, he becomes the bearer of that very form; (RA 18.45)
one should consume [up to] eleven <s>palas</s> of gold-ash in measured [doses]. (RA 18.45)
One <s>guñjā</s>-measure, O Queen of the Gods, knowing one's own digestive fire-strength, (RA 18.46)
concealing [the dose] with ghee, honey, and betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>) — one should enjoy women. (RA 18.46)

children.text:
eko hi doṣaḥ sūkṣmo'yaṃ bhakṣite bhasmasūtake /
                    (RA_18.47.1)
children.translated_text: There is one subtle defect in consuming ash-mercury — (RA 18.47)
for twenty-one days, O Fair-Hipped One, a man becomes blinded by lust. (RA 18.47)
A thousand women he could arouse within a day; (RA 18.48)
through sexual contact, O Fair-Hipped One, the mercury penetrates the body. (RA 18.48)
Through sexual contact, O Fair-Hipped One, indigestion [of mercury] occurs for him. (RA 18.49)
When the semen is agitated by intercourse, gradually over twenty-one days, (RA 18.50)
danger to life arises — therefore one should abandon intercourse. (RA 18.50)
Conversation with a young woman should be done; massage of limbs by a young woman — (RA 18.51)
by whose mere touch, the mercury penetrates the body. (RA 18.51)
Just as desire arises from gazing upon a beautiful woman's form, (RA 18.52)

children.text:
tathā krāmyati deveśi sūtako'sau tataḥ kramāt //
                    (RA_18.52.2)
children.translated_text: so too, O Queen of the Gods, that mercury penetrates gradually. (RA 18.52)
She whose vulva resembles a <s>pīpal</s>-leaf, even and auspicious — (RA 18.53)

children.text:
tādṛśyāḥ surataṃ devi bhājanaṃ tu rasāyane //
                    (RA_18.53.2)
children.translated_text: intercourse with such a woman, O <s>Devī</s>, is the vessel for rejuvenation. (RA 18.53)

children.text:
nirmāṃsaś caiva dīrghaś ca bhagaḥ śuṣkaśirāstathā /
                    (54.1)
children.translated_text: A vulva that is fleshless, elongated, with dry veins — (RA 18.54)
always a cause of poverty — one should avoid that in rejuvenation. (RA 18.54)
One should perpetually satisfy with <s>arghya</s> [offerings], offer fish and meat, (RA 18.55)
worship the lords of <s>yogīs</s> and <s>yoginīs</s> with mantras, and seek forgiveness. (RA 18.55)
One should avoid the eight-<s>ka</s>-group [prohibited foods], and pungent, sour, and salty [substances]. (RA 18.55)
With one <s>pala</s> of mica-digested [mercury], one is not overcome by diseases; (RA 18.56)

children.text:
dvitīye śukravṛddhiḥ syāt tṛtīye balavān bhavet //
                    (RA_18.56.2)
children.translated_text: with the second [<s>pala</s>], increase of semen; with the third, one becomes strong. (RA 18.56)

children.text:
caturthe palitaṃ hanti valīṃ jayati pañcame /
                    (RA_18.57.1)
children.translated_text: With the fourth, gray hair is destroyed; with the fifth, wrinkles are conquered; (RA 18.57)
with the sixth, [one becomes] a retainer of scriptures and eloquent; with the seventh, a conqueror of eye-diseases. (RA 18.57)
With the eighth, one attains eagle-vision (<s>tārkṣyadṛṣṭi</s>), the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the power of <s>Brahmā</s>; (RA 18.58)
by using nine <s>palas</s>, one attains communion with the gods. (RA 18.58)
By using ten <s>palas</s>, one becomes a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>. (RA 18.59)
For the protection of the mercury's potency, one should give offerings daily; (RA 18.60)
one should recite the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> mantra — [then] mercury-perfection arises. (RA 18.60)

children.text:
same tu vimale jīrṇe yo rasaṃ bhakṣayen naraḥ /
                    (RA_18.61.1)
children.translated_text: When equal <s>vimala</s>-digested, whoever eats that mercury, (RA 18.61)
ten thousand years he lives, O Supreme Goddess. (RA 18.61)

children.text: dviguṇe vimale jīrṇe daśalakṣaṃ sa jīvati / (RA_18.62.1)
children.translated_text: When digested with double <s>vimala</s>, one lives a hundred thousand [years]; (RA 18.62)

children.text: triguṇe vimale jīrṇe daśakoṭiṃ ca jīvati // (RA_18.62.2)
children.translated_text: when digested with triple <s>vimala</s>, one lives a hundred million [years]. (RA 18.62)

children.text:
jīrṇe caturguṇe devi rasaḥ khecaratāṃ nayet /
                    (RA_18.63.1)
children.translated_text: When digested with quadruple, O <s>Devī</s>, the mercury leads to sky-going (<s>khecara</s>) state; (RA 18.63)
then, when digested with quintuple, the great mercury [becomes] a touch-transmuter. (RA 18.63)
As with <s>vimala</s>-digested, so with gold-pyrite (<s>hemamākṣika</s>)-digested — (RA 18.64)

children.text:
tat phalaṃ labhate devi tasya vīrye sa jīvati //
                    (RA_18.64.2)
children.translated_text: one obtains that same fruit, O <s>Devī</s>; by its potency he lives. (RA 18.64)
Now I shall describe another [preparation] — diamond-ash rejuvenation (<s>vajrabhasmarasāyana</s>). (RA 18.65)
First, one should calcine sulfur in mercury, O One Worshipped by the Gods; (RA 18.66)

children.text:
dāpayet triguṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ samaṃ hema ca sūtake //
                    (RA_18.66.2)
children.translated_text: one should add triple iron and equal gold to the mercury. (RA 18.66)
With that very gold-digested [mercury], one should coat the diamond-gem; (RA 18.67)
with young calf dung, one should then wrap that diamond. (RA 18.67)

children.text:
baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tena puṭapākaṃ tu dāpayet /
                    (RA_18.68.1)
children.translated_text: Having tied it in a bundle, one should give sealed-heating; (RA 18.68)
Instantly, a calx is produced, resembling conch, jasmine, and moon [in whiteness]. (RA 18.68.2)
That diamond-calx (<s>vajrabhasma</s>), O beautiful one, should be made equal to [the weight of] the pellet; (RA 18.69.1)
that mercury-ball-powder, one should grind until the body [of mercury] disappears. (RA 18.69.2)
Again, that ball-powder, with calf-dung; (RA 18.70.1)

children.text:
mūṣālepaṃ tu tenaiva ardhārdhena tu kārayet //
                    (RA_18.70.2)
children.translated_text: one should make a crucible-coating with that itself, in half-and-half proportion. (RA 18.70.2)
One should blow that in a sealed crucible — swooned and diamond-calcined; (RA 18.71.1)
by a thousand blowings, calx is produced in an instant. (RA 18.71.2)
Half-and-half [proportion of] calx is obtained, resembling cow's milk, O beloved. (RA 18.72)

children.text:
snehe dhṛtaṃ ca yat kalkaṃ kaṅguṇītailasaṃyutam /
                    (RA_18.73.1)
children.translated_text: The paste held in oil (<s>sneha</s>), combined with <s>kanguni</s> oil — (RA 18.73.1)
after thrice seven days (twenty-one days), O beautiful-hipped one, purification of the body occurs. (RA 18.73.2)
Sesame-seed amount of diamond-calx and gold-calx equal to that — (RA 18.74.1)
blown with datura (<s>dhattura</s>) coating — it destroys wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 18.74.2)
Eight <s>palas</s> of pure gold, combined with killed mercury — (RA 18.75.1)
one should grind with medium acid — a globule forms instantly. (RA 18.75.2)

children.text:
ardhaṃ ca prāpyate bhasma gokṣīrasadṛśaṃ priye //
                    (RA_18.76)
children.translated_text: Half [the amount of] calx is obtained, resembling cow's milk, O beloved. (RA 18.76)
One part of killed diamond and four parts of the globule — (RA 18.77.1)
one should grind in a heated mortar (<s>taptakhalla</s>) — the mercury becomes ash. (RA 18.77.2)
One should kill [it] in the <s>Bhudhara</s> apparatus by the method of seven successive bindings; (RA 18.78.1)

children.text:
tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt madhyamāmlena mardayet //
                    (78.2)
children.translated_text: that calx, then afterward, one should grind with medium acid. (18.78.2)
One should carefully give three hundred and sixty heating-cycles; (RA 18.79.1)
that calx is produced, O Goddess, resembling vermilion-dawn [in color]. (RA 18.79.2)
That calx, in the amount of one <s>pala</s>, one should lick combined with honey and ghee; (RA 18.80.1)
one should lick thus seven times, on a milk diet, with senses controlled. (RA 18.80.2)

children.text:
dvitīye saptame caiva bhakṣayec ca paladvayam /
                    (RA_18.81.1)
children.translated_text: In the second [set of] seven, one should consume two <s>palas</s>; (RA 18.81.1)
by this progressive increase, one should consume seven sets of seven. (RA 18.81.2)
By that increase, one becomes a <s>siddha</s>, a man of divine brilliance; (RA 18.82.1)

children.text:
rudrāyuṣaṃ bhavet tasya khecaratvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
                    (RA_18.82.2)
children.translated_text: he attains the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s> and sky-roving power (<s>khecaratva</s>), without doubt. (RA 18.82.2)
By his urine and excrement, the eight metals [become] gold. (RA 18.83)
One <s>pala</s> of that calx, combined with <s>kramana</s> (transmuting agent) — (RA 18.84.1)
from that substance, twelve thousand <s>palas</s> of lead (<s>bhujangama</s>) (RA 18.84.2)
become divine gold, ornaments fit for the gods. (RA 18.84.3)
Eight <s>palas</s> of magnetite (<s>kanta</s>) powder and eight <s>palas</s> of mercury — (RA 18.85.1)
having combined and ground together, ground with <s>bijapura</s> (citron) acid, (RA 18.85.2)
one should grind in a heated mortar — a globule forms instantly. (RA 18.85.3)
One part of killed diamond and four parts of the globule — (RA 18.86.1)
having combined and ground together — the mercury becomes ash. (RA 18.86.2)
One should kill [it] in the <s>Bhudhara</s> apparatus by the method of seven successive bindings; (RA 18.87.1)

children.text:
tadbhasmabhāgam ekaṃ tu bhāgaikaṃ gandhakasya ca /
                    (RA_18.87.2)
children.translated_text: one part of that calx and one part of sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) — (RA 18.87.2)
placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an alloy (<s>khota</s>) forms instantly. (RA 18.87.3)
Thirty-two [parts] of killed alloy and twenty [parts] of pure gold, (RA 18.88.1)
silver, copper, mica-essence, and magnetite-essence as the fourth — (18.88.2)
twelve parts each — one should combine all together. (RA 18.88.3)
Placed in a sealed crucible and blown — an alloy forms instantly; (RA 18.89.1)
from thirty-two combined alloys, one should make fine powder. (18.89.2)
That fine alloy-powder, combined with <s>arota</s> mercury, (RA 18.90.1)
one should grind with medium acid — a globule forms instantly. (RA 18.90.2)

children.text:
golakasya pale dve ca mṛtakāntasya tatsamam /
                    (RA_18.91.1)
children.translated_text: Two <s>palas</s> of the globule and killed magnetite equal to that — (RA 18.91.1)
having combined and ground together with the juice of <s>Meghanada</s> (cloud-roarer plant), (RA 18.91.2)
and with the juice of <s>Munipuspa</s> (sage-flower) — one should grind for one day. (RA 18.91.3)
One should make pills, O Goddess — three hundred and sixty. (RA 18.92)
Of those, one pill, combined with ghee, <s>triphala</s>, and honey, (RA 18.93.1)
one should consume for one year — the man attains the lifespan of <s>Brahma</s>. (RA 18.93.2)

children.text:
sarvāstā bhakṣayet paścāt rudrāyuḥ sa bhavennaraḥ //
                    (RA_18.94)
children.translated_text: Having consumed all of them afterward, that man attains the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>. (RA 18.94)
Now, one [pill] held in the mouth, O beautiful immortal one — (RA 18.95.1)
it forcefully destroys all diseases and gray hair. (RA 18.95.2)
I shall describe the regimen for the diamond-essence elixir (<s>vajrasattva-rasayana</s>). (RA 18.96)

children.text:
vajrabaddhas tu yo devi raso'yaṃ vajratāṃ nayet /
                    (RA_18.97.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury that is diamond-bound, O Goddess — this mercury attains the nature of diamond; (RA 18.97.1)

children.text:
tena baddhās tu ye dehāste dehā vajrarūpiṇaḥ //
                    (RA_18.97.2)
children.translated_text: those bodies that are bound by it — those bodies become diamond-formed. (RA 18.97.2)

children.text:
tilamātraṃ rasaṃ devi brahmāyur daśa jīvati /
                    (RA_18.98.1)
children.translated_text: A sesame-seed amount of mercury, O Goddess — one lives for ten lifespans of <s>Brahma</s>; (RA 18.98.1)

children.text:
yavamātraṃ rasaṃ devi viṣṇukoṭiṃ sa jīvati //
                    (RA_18.98.2)
children.translated_text: a barley-grain amount of mercury, O Goddess — one lives for ten million [lifespans of] <s>Visnu</s>. (RA 18.98.2)
A <s>gunja</s>-amount, O Queen of the Gods — one attains the lifespan of a <s>Mahakalpa</s>; (RA 18.99.1)
a <s>masa</s>-amount, O beautiful-hipped one — one becomes equal to Me in qualities. (RA 18.99.2)

children.text:
mantrahīnena subhage na sa gamyo bhaviṣyati /
                    (RA_18.100.1)
children.translated_text: Without <s>mantra</s>, O beautiful one, he shall not attain it; (RA 18.100.1)
there is no accomplishment of <s>sadhana</s> (practice) for him, even in hundreds of tens of millions of births. (RA 18.100.2)
This deluded one wanders about, bereft of the teaching of the clan (<s>kulasasana</s>). (RA 18.101)
Gods and demons create thousands of obstacles for him; (RA 18.102.1)
the <s>Devis</s> — those who move through the sky and those who roam the earth, O Queen of the Gods — (RA 18.102.2)

children.text:
svapne taṃ bhajayitvā tu retorakte haranti tāḥ /
                    (RA_18.103.1)
children.translated_text: having enjoyed him in dreams, they steal his semen and blood; (RA 18.103.1)
through that very semen-channel, they steal the consumed mercury. (RA 18.103.2)
The planets beginning with the Sun (<s>Bhaskara</s>), O Goddess, roar in their own forms; (RA 18.104.1)

children.text:
kṣatriyasya tu rūpeṇa devā vai garjayanti ca //
                    (RA_18.104.2)
children.translated_text: in the form of a <s>ksatriya</s> (warrior), the gods indeed cause roaring. (RA 18.104.2)
<s>Pisacas</s> (flesh-eating spirits) in the form of <s>vaisyas</s> (merchants), <s>raksasas</s> (demons) in the form of <s>sudras</s> (laborers); (RA 18.105.1)
others in human form — they visit [him] in the interval of sleep. (RA 18.105.2)
They devour bones and flesh in dreams, O divine beauty; (RA 18.106.1)

children.text:
svapnānte prāpyate bhrāntiḥ prāyaḥ paśyati mānavaḥ /
                    (106.2)
children.translated_text: at the end of the dream, confusion arises — man mostly [only] sees [this]. (18.106.2)

children.text:
vajrabhasma haranty eva svapnānte kṣobhayanti ca //
                    (106.3)
children.translated_text: They steal the diamond-calx and cause disturbance at the end of dreams. (18.106.3)
When the pure golden [mercury] is consumed, they flee in the ten directions — (RA 18.107.1)
<s>bhutas</s> (ghosts), <s>pretas</s> (hungry spirits), <s>pisacas</s>, <s>sakinis</s> (witches), <s>guhyakas</s> (hidden beings), and others. (RA 18.107.2)

children.text:
vajrāṇāṃ māraṇe ye tu lohānāṃ vā rasasya tu /
                    (RA_18.108.1)
children.translated_text: In the killing of diamonds, or of metals, or of mercury — (RA 18.108.1)

children.text:
varjanīyāḥ prayatnena prayuktāṃs tān śṛṇu priye //
                    (108.2)
children.translated_text: what must be avoided with effort — hear about those employed [obstacles], O beloved. (18.108.2)
Their methods of application, employed by those who bestow methods — (RA 18.109.1)

children.text:
evaṃ vadanti bhūtādyā bhīṣayanti sma taṃ naram //
                    (109.2)
children.translated_text: thus do the <s>bhutas</s> and others speak, frightening that man. (18.109.2)

children.text:
rañjako rāgakārī syāt krāmaṇaḥ krāmaṇe hitaḥ /
                    (RA_18.110.1)
children.translated_text: The coloring-agent (<s>ranjaka</s>) effects coloring; the transmuting agent (<s>kramana</s>) is beneficial in transmutation; (RA 18.110.1)

children.text:
bandhakā dṛḍhakārāś ca tathā puṣṭikarāḥ smṛtāḥ //
                    (110.2)
children.translated_text: the binding agents (<s>bandhaka</s>) make [things] firm, and the nourishing agents (<s>pustikara</s>) are also recognized. (18.110.2)
One should consume [mercury] variously with semen, blood, excrement, and urine; (RA 18.111.1)
but that which is tainted by lead (<s>naga</s>) and tin (<s>vanga</s>) causes skin diseases (<s>kustha</s>). (RA 18.111.2)
<s>Triphala</s>, nutmeg (<s>jati</s>), cubeb (<s>kankola</s>), mixed with camphor (<s>karpura</s>) juice, (RA 18.112.1)
and catechu (<s>khadira</s>), ground with equal water — one should consume the mercury. (RA 18.112.2)

children.text:
payasā kaṭukaṃ ghṛṣṭvā pathyaṃ krāmaṇam uttamam /
                    (113.1)
children.translated_text: Bitter [substance] (<s>katuka</s>) rubbed with milk — this is a wholesome and excellent <s>kramana</s> (transmuting agent); (18.113.1)
but ground with breast-milk and gold, this should not be eaten, O Queen of the Gods. (RA 18.113.2)
By consuming <s>Alambusa</s>, magnetite (<s>ayaskanta</s>), and orpiment (<s>talaka</s>), (RA 18.114.1)

children.text:
dehe krāmati sūtendro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
                    (RA_18.114.2)
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury courses through the body — no deliberation is needed here. (RA 18.114.2)

children.text:
avaśyaṃ kramate sūtaḥ strīyoge krāmaṇaṃ param /
                    (RA_18.115.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury necessarily courses [through the body]; sexual union (<s>striyoga</s>) is the supreme <s>kramana</s>; (RA 18.115.1)

children.text:
brahmacaryeṇa vā yogī sadā seveta sūtakam //
                    (RA_18.115.2)
children.translated_text: or by <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), the <s>yogin</s> should always serve (consume) mercury. (RA 18.115.2)

children.text:
samādhiḥ kāraṇaṃ tac ca krāmaṇaṃ paramaṃ matam //
                    (RA_18.116)
children.translated_text: <s>Samadhi</s> (deep meditation) is the [ultimate] cause — that is considered the supreme <s>kramana</s>. (RA 18.116)
One should consume mercury in the morning; wholesome [food] after two <s>yamas</s> (six hours); (18.117.1)

children.text:
no laṅghayet triyāmaṃ tu madhyāhne na tu bhojayet //
                    (117.2)
children.translated_text: one should not fast for three <s>yamas</s> (nine hours); one should not eat at midday. (18.117.2)
Excessive drinking, excessive eating, excessive sleep, excessive wakefulness, (RA 18.118.1)
excessive association with women, and excessive walking — these should be avoided. (18.118.2)
Excessive anger, excessive joy, excessive greed, excessive desire, (RA 18.119.1)
dry argumentation, water-sports, and excessive worry — these should be avoided. (RA 18.119.2)

children.text:
kakārāṣṭaka kūṣmāṇḍaṃ karkaṭīṃ caiva kāliṅgaṃ kāravellakam /
                    (120.1)
children.translated_text: [The eight 'ka'-items:] Pumpkin (<s>kusmanda</s>), cucumber (<s>karkati</s>), watermelon (<s>kalinga</s>), bitter gourd (<s>karavellaka</s>), (18.120.1)
safflower (<s>kusumbhaka</s>), spine gourd (<s>karkota</s>), banana (<s>kadali</s>), and black nightshade (<s>kakamacika</s>) — (RA 18.120.2)
these eight 'ka'-items should be avoided by one who consumes mercury. (RA 18.120.3)

children.text:
pātakaṃ ca na kartavyaṃ paśusaṅgaṃ vivarjayet /
                    (RA_18.121.1)
children.translated_text: Sinful acts should not be performed; contact with animals should be avoided; (RA 18.121.1)

children.text:
liṅgacchāyāṃ na laṅgheta nārīchāyāṃ tathaiva ca //
                    (121.2)
children.translated_text: one should not step over the shadow of a <s>linga</s> (Siva emblem), nor likewise the shadow of a woman. (18.121.2)

children.text:
catuḥpathe na gantavyaṃ viṇmūtraṃ na ca laṅghayet /
                    (122.1)
children.translated_text: One should not go to a crossroads; one should not step over excrement or urine. (18.122.1)

children.text:
surāṇāṃ nindanaṃ devi strīṇāṃ nindāṃ ca varjayet //
                    (122.2)
children.translated_text: Disparagement of the gods, O Goddess, and disparagement of women should be avoided. (18.122.2)

children.text:
satyaṃ ca vacanaṃ brūyādapriyaṃ na vadedvacaḥ //
                    (RA_18.123)
children.translated_text: One should speak truthful words and should not utter unpleasant speech. (RA 18.123)
Horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>), linseed oil (<s>atasītaila</s>), sesame, black gram (<s>māṣa</s>), lentils (<s>masūraka</s>), (RA 18.124.1)
pigeon-meat, sour-gruel food, and buttermilk-rice — one should avoid. (RA 18.124.2)
That which is pungent, sour, sharp, salty, slimy, and bile-producing; (RA 18.125.1)
sesame oil, yogurt, milk, grapes, <s>kola</s> (jujube), and <s>parūṣaka</s> (Grewia); (RA 18.125.2)
jujube (<s>badara</s>), <s>cirabilva</s>, mango (<s>sahakāra</s>), <s>suvarcala</s> (a salt), (RA 18.126.1)

children.text:
nāraṅgaṃ kāñcanāraṃ ca śobhāñjanam api tyajet //
                    (RA_18.126.2)
children.translated_text: orange (<s>nāraṅga</s>), <s>kāñcanāra</s> (Bauhinia), and <s>śobhāñjana</s> (moringa) — one should also abandon. (RA 18.126.2)

children.text:
kṣudhārto naiva tiṣṭheta ajīrṇaṃ naiva kārayet /
                    (RA_18.127.1)
children.translated_text: One should not remain afflicted by hunger; one should not cause indigestion; (RA 18.127.1)

children.text:
na vādajalpanaṃ kuryāt divāsvāpaṃ na kārayet //
                    (RA_18.127.2)
children.translated_text: one should not engage in disputatious talk; one should not sleep during the day. (RA 18.127.2)

children.text:
naivedyaṃ naiva bhuñjīta karpūraṃ varjayet sadā /
                    (128.1)
children.translated_text: One should not eat temple-offerings (<s>naivedya</s>); one should always avoid camphor; (RA 18.128.1)
saffron-paste application should be avoided; one should avoid dancing on the ground. (RA 18.128.2)

children.text:
nāgniṃ spṛśet tu pādena na gā vā brāhmaṇānna ca /
                    (129.1)
children.translated_text: One should not touch fire with the foot, nor cows, nor <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; (RA 18.129.1)

children.text:
na hanyāt kumārīṃ ca vātulānapi varjayet //
                    (RA_18.129.2)
children.translated_text: one should not harm a young girl; and one should avoid the insane. (RA 18.129.2)

children.text:
divārātraṃ japenmantraṃ snātavyaṃ ca dine dine //
                    (RA_18.130)
children.translated_text: Day and night one should recite mantras; one should bathe every day. (RA 18.130)

children.text:
hitaṃ ca mudgā dugdhānnaṃ śālyannaṃ ca samāhitam /
                    (131.1)
children.translated_text: Beneficial [foods are]: green gram (<s>mudga</s>), milk-rice, and <s>śāli</s> (fine rice) food, properly [prepared]; (RA 18.131.1)

children.text:
śākaṃ paunarnavaṃ devi meghanādaṃ ca vāstukam /
                    (RA_18.131.2)
children.translated_text: the vegetable of <s>punarnava</s> (Boerhavia), O Goddess, <s>meghanāda</s> (a plant), and <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium); (RA 18.131.2)
rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), <s>mustā</s> (nut-grass), and lotus roots — one should eat. (RA 18.131.3)
One whose breasts are newly sprouted, who is dark-complexioned, beautiful, fortunate, and auspicious, (RA 18.132.1)
endowed with divine radiance, with increased power of desire, (RA 18.132.2)

children.text:
saṃnidhāne ca kartavyā vṛddhaiś ca parirakṣitā //
                    (132.3)
children.translated_text: should be kept in proximity and protected by elders. (RA 18.132.3)
One who is dark, fair-skinned, with excessively large limbs, or of bad character — one should never resort to [such a woman]. (RA 18.133)

children.text:
tilakaṃ kuṅkumaṃ gandhaṃ kastūryā ca manoharam /
                    (RA_18.134.1)
children.translated_text: Tilaka mark, saffron, fragrance, and the enchanting [scent of] musk; (RA 18.134.1)
fragrant flowers, a comfortable bed, and desired food — (RA 18.134.2)
comfortable dwelling itself is declared the stepping-up (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) of mercury; (RA 18.135.1)
discourse on self-knowledge, worship, and especially of <s>Śiva</s>. (RA 18.135.2)

children.text:
etāṃs tu samayān bhadre na laṅghedrasabhakṣaṇe /
                    (RA_18.136.1)
children.translated_text: These observances, O Auspicious One, one should not transgress while consuming mercury; (RA 18.136.1)
from transgression, various symptoms — the signs thereof are now described. (RA 18.136.2)

children.text:
rasarāje tvajīrṇe tu pratyayo'yaṃ bhavet priye /
                    (RA_18.137.1)
children.translated_text: When the king of mercury is [in a state of] indigestion, these indications appear, O Beloved: (RA 18.137.1)

children.text:
mūrcchā śoko bhramaḥ kampaḥ chardirmoho jvarastathā //
                    (137.2)
children.translated_text: fainting, grief, dizziness, trembling, vomiting, delusion, and fever; (RA 18.137.2)
hiccups, shivering, colic pains, drowsiness, lethargy, and loss of appetite; (RA 18.138.1)
penile rigidity, excessive diarrhea, cough, dyspnea, and yawning; (RA 18.138.2)
in the ears, mouth, eyes, abdomen, testicles, belly, head, (RA 18.139.1)
and penis — burning sensation and digestive weakness, and doubt [of life] in the entire body. (RA 18.139.2)

children.text:
anyāṃś caiva mahāvyādhīn rasājīrṇe tu lakṣayet //
                    (RA_18.140)
children.translated_text: And other great diseases should be observed in mercury-indigestion. (RA 18.140)
Sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), <s>sarjikā</s> alkali, steeped in bitter gourd (<s>kāravallī</s>) juice, (RA 18.141.1)
combined with cow's urine and rock salt — one should drink that as the stepping-up [remedy]. (RA 18.141.2)
The juice of <s>mokṣaka</s> (a plant), O Goddess, the juice of <s>rājakoṣātakī</s> (a gourd), (RA 18.142.1)
<s>sindhuka</s>, black cow's urine, steeped in bitter gourd juice, (RA 18.142.2)
combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) — in mercury-indigestion, a person should drink [this]. (RA 18.142.3)

children.text:
rasājīrṇe na jīvet tu mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
                    (RA_18.143.1)
children.translated_text: In mercury-indigestion, one does not survive — one dies, there is no doubt in this; (RA 18.143.1)

children.text:
rasāyane sujīrṇe tu tena sarvaṃ vidhīyate //
                    (RA_18.143.2)
children.translated_text: when the mercury-elixir is well-digested, thereby everything is accomplished. (RA 18.143.2)

children.text:
yadā suptastadaṅgaṃ ca strī stanenaiva gharṣayet /
                    (144.1)
children.translated_text: When [the practitioner] is asleep, a woman should rub his body with her breast; (RA 18.144.1)

children.text:
vāmena mardayed evaṃ sūtaḥ krāmati nirvyathaḥ //
                    (RA_18.144.2)
children.translated_text: one should massage with the left [hand] thus — the mercury steps up without pain. (RA 18.144.2)
In a windless, solitary place, an underground chamber, free from disturbance, (RA 18.145.1)
protected from cold and heat, eating wholesome food, eating lightly, (RA 18.145.2)
within the prescribed days, one attains accomplishment — there is no doubt in this. (RA 18.145.3)
With all [types of] food, accomplishment is attained in double the days; (RA 18.146.1)
from exposure to cold and wind, in triple the days progressively; (RA 18.146.2)

children.text:
atimārgasya dharmaiś ca divasais tu caturguṇaiḥ //
                    (146.3)
children.translated_text: and by the practices of the excessive path, in quadruple the days. (RA 18.146.3)
Now I shall declare the transmutation [of the body], preceded by the accomplishment of the body (<s>dehasiddhi</s>); (RA 18.147.1)
out of affection for you, O Goddess of the Gods, this elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>) has been declared. (RA 18.147.2)
The first is skin-transmutation (<s>tvagvedha</s>), O Goddess; the second is flesh-transmutation (<s>māṃsavedha</s>); (RA 18.148.1)
the third is blood-transmutation (<s>raktavedha</s>); and the fourth is bone-transmutation (<s>asthivedha</s>). (RA 18.148.2)

children.text:
pañcamo majjavedhaḥ syāt nāḍīvedhas tu ṣaṣṭhakaḥ /
                    (149.1)
children.translated_text: The fifth is marrow-transmutation (<s>majjavedha</s>); the sixth is channel-transmutation (<s>nāḍīvedha</s>); (RA 18.149.1)

children.text:
saptamo dhātuvedhaś ca aṣṭamaḥ kavacasya tu //
                    (RA_18.149.2)
children.translated_text: the seventh is essence-transmutation (<s>dhātuvedha</s>); and the eighth is armor[-transmutation] (<s>kavacavedha</s>). (RA 18.149.2)

children.text:
tvacā vedhena deveśi pannagaḥ kuṭilo bhavet /
                    (RA_18.150.1)
children.translated_text: By skin-transmutation, O Goddess of the Gods, tin (<s>pannaga</s>) becomes crooked [gold]; (RA 18.150.1)
by flesh-transmutation, O Beautiful One, the crooked [gold] becomes true gold. (RA 18.150.2)
By bone-transmutation, O Goddess of the Gods, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) attains gold-nature; (RA 18.151.1)
by marrow-transmutation, O Beautiful-hipped One, all eight metals are transmuted. (RA 18.151.2)

children.text:
kavacasya tu vedhena mṛnmaye kāñcanaṃ bhavet /
                    (RA_18.152.1)
children.translated_text: By armor-transmutation, even clay becomes gold; (RA 18.152.1)

children.text:
vedhe tu hemavimale majjño hema prajāyate //
                    (RA_18.152.2)
children.translated_text: in transmutation with pure gold, marrow-[level mercury] produces gold. (RA 18.152.2)

children.text:
tāre māṃsaṃ sureśāni jīrṇasūtaś ca vedhayet /
                    (RA_18.153.1)
children.translated_text: Flesh[-level mercury] transmutes silver, O Queen of the Gods, and well-digested mercury transmutes; (RA 18.153.1)

children.text:
alake vimale tāpye tīkṣṇe tāre ca bhāskare //
                    (RA_18.153.2)
children.translated_text: in <s>alaka</s>, in <s>vimala</s>, in pyrite, in iron, in silver, and in gold. (RA 18.153.2)

children.text:
krāmaṇe tu bhavet takraṃ śarkarā mākṣikaṃ tathā /
                    (154.1)
children.translated_text: For the stepping-up [process], buttermilk, sugar, and <s>mākṣika</s> (honey) [are used]; (RA 18.154.1)
the buttermilk of tawny and black cows — that, O Goddess, [is used] in the elixir practice. (RA 18.154.2)
<s>Sāttvika</s> (pure) is cow's buttermilk; <s>rājasa</s> (passionate) is that produced from a buffalo cow; (RA 18.155.1)

children.text:
tāmasaṃ māhiṣaṃ takraṃ deyaṃ naiva rasāyane //
                    (RA_18.155.2)
children.translated_text: <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) is buffalo buttermilk — it should never be given in elixir practice. (RA 18.155.2)

children.text:
ārdrakasya raso devi tathā pūgaphalāni ca /
                    (RA_18.156.1)
children.translated_text: The juice of fresh ginger, O Goddess, and betel-nut (<s>pūga</s>) fruits; (RA 18.156.1)
rubbing with fresh butter — [this is] the supreme stepping-up of mercury. (RA 18.156.2)
Inferior is [that derived] from vegetable roots; middling is that born from fruit-roots; (RA 18.157.1)
the best, O Goddess of the Gods, is zinc ore (<s>rasaka</s>) in the elixir [practice]. (RA 18.157.2)
By iron-transmutation, [the body becomes] blue-colored; by copper, ruddy in luster; (RA 18.158.1)
by silver, moon-like; by gold, golden in appearance. (RA 18.158.2)
One who sees smoke[-visions], with [the mercury] placed in the mouth — within a month, attains the state of sky-wanderer (<s>khecara</s>); (RA 18.159.1)
a touch-transmuter, with [the mercury] placed in the mouth — within two months, grants accomplishment. (RA 18.159.2)
In three months, a hundred-ten-million[-fold transmuter]; in four, a ten-ten-million; (RA 18.160.1)

children.text:
pañcabhiḥ pañcakoṭiś ca ṣaḍbhiḥ syāt koṭivedhakaḥ //
                    (160.2)
children.translated_text: in five, five-ten-million; in six, a ten-million-fold transmuter. (RA 18.160.2)
Thus, progressively, [the mercury] makes the body free from old age and death; (RA 18.161.1)
the sovereignty of <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and other [supernatural] powers — command-accomplishment is born. (RA 18.161.2)
In seven [months], a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter; in eight, ten-thousand again; (RA 18.162.1)

children.text:
sahasraṃ navabhir māsair daśamāsaiḥ śataṃ punaḥ //
                    (162.2)
children.translated_text: a thousand in nine months; in ten months, a hundred again. (RA 18.162.2)
From his urine, feces, phlegm, and bodily excretions — (RA 18.163.1)
by mere application, stones and other [substances] on earth attain gold-nature. (RA 18.163.2)
Transmutation at a sixty-fourth ratio — from one month, a tenfold transmuter; (RA 18.164.1)
a thirty-second-ratio transmuter — from one year, transmutes the body. (RA 18.164.2)

children.text:
kuñcitāgrās tu yatkeśā yā śyāmā padmalocanā /
                    (RA_18.165.1)
children.translated_text: She whose hair has curling tips, who is dark-complexioned and lotus-eyed, (RA 18.165.1)

children.text:
vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyāḥ saṃkīrṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet //
                    (165.2)
children.translated_text: whose hips are broad and whose heart is narrow — (RA 18.165.2)
she in whom menstruation appears during the dark fortnight (<s>kṛṣṇapakṣa</s>), (RA 18.166.1)

children.text: kāminī sā samākhyātā uttamā ca rasāyane // (RA_18.166.2)
children.translated_text: that young woman is declared the beloved — the best in elixir practice. (RA 18.166.2)
Through embracing, touching, sexual union, and conversation — (RA 18.167.1)
[one becomes] freed from all diseases, free from wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 18.167.2)

children.text:
nāsau chidyeta śastraiś ca pāvakena na dahyate /
                    (RA_18.168.1)
children.translated_text: He cannot be cut by weapons, nor burned by fire; (RA 18.168.1)
with the speed of wind, of great brilliance — like another <s>Kāmadeva</s> (god of love). (RA 18.168.2)

children.text:
icchayā jāyate dṛśyo hyadṛśyaś caiva jāyate /
                    (RA_18.169.1)
children.translated_text: By his will, he becomes visible; and indeed he becomes invisible; (RA 18.169.1)
