by his mere touch, all metals [become] gold. (RA 18.169.2)
In that terrible single ocean, when all moving and unmoving [beings] are destroyed, (RA 18.170.1)
where even the gods dissolve — the <s>Siddha</s> dissolves there [alone]. (RA 18.170.2)

children.text:
idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ mayā proktaṃ sureśvari //
                    (RA_18.171)
children.translated_text: This supreme secret has been declared by me, O Queen of the Gods. (RA 18.171)
Those who are good people, knowers of essence, devoted to mercury-digestion practices — (RA 18.172.1)
they are called mercury-practitioners (<s>rasavādin</s>); the others are mere quarrelsome speakers. (RA 18.172.2)
Again, I shall declare another pill, extremely rare in mercury [science]. (RA 18.173)
Tin, lead, copper, mica, gold, and silver — combined; (RA 18.174.1)
with diamond, iron, and the rest — the mercury is prepared by practitioners. (RA 18.174.2)
Having combined all those together, placed within a crucible, one should blow — (RA 18.175.1)
A divine pill is produced, named <s>Vajrāṅgasundarī</s> (Diamond-Body Beauty). (RA 18.175b)
Kept in the mouth, it is declared to bestow <s>siddhi</s> and to destroy old age and death. (RA 18.176)
Victorious in battle, a hero of diamond-body (<s>vajradeha</s>), of great strength, (RA 18.177a)
always dear to all the worlds, and a favorite of women. (RA 18.177b)

children.text:
vajravyomajasattvakaṃ sakanakaṃ candraṃ raviṃ kāntakaṃ nāgaṃ
                    vaṅgam athāyasaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ sūtaṃ kṛtaṃ tatsamam / (178.1)
children.translated_text: Diamond, mica-essence, together with gold, [the essences of] moon (silver), sun (gold), magnetite, lead, tin, iron — strongly [combined], mercury made equal to all these — (RA 18.178a)

children.text:
vaktrasthaṃ rasagolakaṃ ratikaraṃ sarvārthadaṃ tāpahaṃ
                    varṣaikena nihanti doṣanicayaṃ kalpāyuṣo jāyate // (178.2)
children.translated_text: the mercury-globule kept in the mouth bestows pleasure, grants all purposes, removes suffering; within a year it destroys the host of defects — one attains a lifespan of a <s>kalpa</s>. (RA 18.178b)
In the previously accomplished mercury, O Goddess, one should add gold in one-quarter proportion. (RA 18.179a)
With one <s>pala</s>-proportion of killed diamond, one should add mica-essence. (RA 18.179b)
With <s>Kṣīrakañcukī</s> (milk-covering plant) water and <s>Suradālī</s> (divine creeper) juice, (RA 18.180a)

children.text:
vidhinā mardayitvā tu naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu kārayet //
                    (RA_18.180.2)
children.translated_text: having ground according to the proper method, one should make it into a vanished-cake (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>). (RA 18.180b)
Having added a pinch of magnetite (<s>kānta</s>) powder, one should smelt [it] in a sealed crucible. (RA 18.181a)
A divine pill is produced — kept in the mouth, it bestows all <s>siddhis</s>. (RA 18.181b)
<s>Subhaga</s> (good-fortune mineral), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), diamond, and mica, (RA 18.182a)

children.text:
hema śulvaṃ tathā tāraṃ samabhāgāni kārayet /
                    (RA_18.182.2)
children.translated_text: gold, copper, and silver — one should make [these] in equal portions. (RA 18.182b)
A diamond-bound pill, kept in the mouth, bestows all <s>siddhis</s>. (RA 18.182c)
<s>Bhrāmaka</s> (wandering [mineral]) and pyrite, along with the three metals, (RA 18.183a)
combined with <s>Śaktibīja</s> (the seed-syllable of power), along with the three seeds — (RA 18.183b)
mercury ground with the <s>Tridaṇḍī</s> [apparatus], made into a single globule, (RA 18.184a)
placed in a sealed crucible and smelted — one should make a rolling (<s>samāvarta</s>). (RA 18.184b)

children.text:
pūjāṃ kṛtvā kṣipedvaktre ṣaṇmāsāt sa bhavet priye /
                    (185.1)
children.translated_text: Having performed worship, one should place it in the mouth — within six months, O beloved, (RA 18.185a)
one becomes fearless to all enemies, diamond-bodied, of great strength. (RA 18.185b)
<s>Nandikeśa</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and others who steal [the mercury] being consumed — (RA 18.186a)

children.text:
naṣṭachāyā na dṛśyante haste dadati bhasma ca //
                    (RA_18.186.2)
children.translated_text: they become invisible, their shadows lost, and they place ash in [one's] hand. (RA 18.186b)

children.text:
hriyamāṇaṃ rasaṃ tais tu mūḍhabuddhirna paśyati /
                    (187.1)
children.translated_text: The deluded-minded one does not perceive the mercury being stolen by them. (RA 18.187a)
He tells all beings: 'There is no <s>siddhi</s> for me in rejuvenation.' (RA 18.187b)

children.text:
manasā rasasiddhis tu tathā kleśo mayā kṛtaḥ /
                    (RA_18.188.1)
children.translated_text: 'The mercury-<s>siddhi</s> [I sought] mentally — such was the effort I made. (RA 18.188a)
The loss of substances was caused by me, the dim-witted, the deluded one.' (RA 18.188b)

children.text:
īdṛśaṃ naiva jānāti vidhihīnaṃ mayā kṛtam /
                    (RA_18.189.1)
children.translated_text: He does not even know that it was done by him without proper procedure. (RA 18.189a)
The sinful one maligns the science — he does not recognize his own faulty actions. (RA 18.189b)

children.text:
vidhihīno raso devi naiva sidhyet kadācana /
                    (RA_18.190.1)
children.translated_text: Mercury [used] without proper procedure, O Goddess, never succeeds. (RA 18.190a)
For one who lacks [knowledge of] the science, O Goddess, there is never <s>siddhi</s>, O fair-faced one. (RA 18.190b)

children.text:
aśubhaiḥ karmabhiḥ sarvaiḥ sampradāyo na sidhyati /
                    (191.1)
children.translated_text: Through all inauspicious actions, the tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>) does not succeed. (RA 18.191a)

children.text:
na sidhyedrasaśāstre tu na sidhyet tādṛśo guruḥ //
                    (191.2)
children.translated_text: Nor does one succeed in the science of mercury; nor does such a teacher succeed. (RA 18.191b)

children.text:
na prāpet tādṛśīmājñāṃ naiva jñānaṃ ca tādṛśam /
                    (RA_18.192.1)
children.translated_text: Nor does one obtain such a command [from the deity]; nor such knowledge. (RA 18.192a)

children.text:
na prāpet tādṛśīṃ nārīm ekacittāṃ varānane //
                    (RA_18.192.2)
children.translated_text: Nor does one obtain such a woman — single-minded, O fair-faced one. (RA 18.192b)

children.text:
na prāped rasavantaṃ ca tāṃ ca devīṃ rasāṅkuśīm /
                    (193.1)
children.translated_text: Nor does one obtain the one who possesses mercury, nor that Goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>. (RA 18.193a)

children.text:
yasya tuṣṭaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāt tasya siddhī rasāyane //
                    (193.2)
children.translated_text: One with whom <s>Śiva</s> himself is pleased — for him alone [there is] <s>siddhi</s> in rejuvenation. (RA 18.193b)
I shall now describe another [procedure] — the supreme globule-binding (<s>golabandha</s>), (RA 18.194a)
by merely consuming which, one becomes free from old age and immortal. (RA 18.194b)
Sulfur, mica, and magnetite together, sun-[copper], calamine (<s>kharpara</s>), and gold, (RA 18.195a)

children.text:
samaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ rasendrasya baddhaṃ kṛtvā tu golakam //
                    (195.2)
children.translated_text: with equal iron — having bound the mercury-lord into a globule — (RA 18.195b)
five <s>palas</s> of mercury-lord should be combined in equal proportion. (RA 18.196a)
One should grind with the water of seven lemons, along with the globule. (RA 18.196b)

children.text:
chāyāviśuṣkaṃ golaṃ tu śaśibhāvaṃ karoti tat /
                    (RA_18.197.1)
children.translated_text: The globule, dried in the shade, attains a moon-like quality (<s>śaśibhāva</s>). (RA 18.197a)

children.text:
etat sarvaṃ vimardyaṃ tu sūtakaṃ golakasya ca //
                    (RA_18.197.2)
children.translated_text: All this should be ground — the mercury along with the globule. (RA 18.197b)

children.text:
tat karīṣāgninā bhūmau mṛdusvedaṃ tu kārayet /
                    (RA_18.198.1)
children.translated_text: That should be gently sweated on the ground with a cow-dung fire. (RA 18.198a)
This globule, kept in the mouth, bestows <s>cāmaratā</s> (lordship with the fly-whisk). (RA 18.198b)
The fruit born of the mercury-globule cannot be expressed in words. (RA 18.199a)
In rejuvenation, it produces color [in the body]; it bestows mercury-<s>siddhi</s>. (RA 18.199b)
Fragrant unguents, betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>), musk (<s>kastūrī</s>), saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), aloe-wood (<s>aguru</s>), (RA 18.200a)
sandalwood, deer-navel [musk], <s>kaṅkola</s> (cubeb), and nutmeg (<s>jātikāphala</s>), (RA 18.200b)

children.text:
anyāni ca sugandhīni snāne pāne pradāpayet //
                    (RA_18.200.3)
children.translated_text: and other fragrant substances — one should provide [these] in bathing and drinking. (RA 18.200c)

children.text:
kuñcitāgrās tu yat keśā yā śyāmā padmalocanā /
                    (RA_18.201.1)
children.translated_text: She whose hair has curled tips, who is dark-complexioned, lotus-eyed, (RA 18.201a)

children.text:
vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyāḥ saṃkīrṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet //
                    (201.2)
children.translated_text: whose hips are broad and whose heart is contracted — (RA 18.201b)
she whose menstrual flow appears in the dark fortnight — (RA 18.202a)

children.text: kāminī sā samākhyātā uttamā ca rasāyane // (RA_18.202.2)
children.translated_text: that young woman is declared to be the <s>kāminī</s> (passionate one), the best for rejuvenation. (RA 18.202b)
Through embracing, touching, intercourse, and conversation, (RA 18.203a)
one becomes freed from all diseases, free from wrinkles and gray hair. (RA 18.203b)
A hundred diseases are destroyed when [pills] the size of barley grains (RA 18.204a)
are held in the mouth — one lives for three hundred years. (RA 18.204b)
Now, sixteen [pills], O Goddess, for sixteen years — (RA 18.205a)

children.text:
dhṛtāni mukhamadhye tu teṣu vakṣyāmi ye guṇāḥ //
                    (RA_18.205.2)
children.translated_text: held in the mouth — I shall describe the qualities [that arise] from these. (RA 18.205b)

children.text:
nāsau chidyeta śastraiś ca pāvakena na dahyate /
                    (RA_18.206.1)
children.translated_text: He cannot be cut by weapons, nor burnt by fire. (RA 18.206a)
Swift as the wind, of great splendor, like another <s>Kāmadeva</s> (god of love). (RA 18.206b)

children.text:
icchayā jāyate dṛśyo hyadṛśyaś caiva jāyate /
                    (RA_18.207.1)
children.translated_text: By will he becomes visible; by will he becomes invisible. (RA 18.207a)
By his mere touch, all metals become gold. (RA 18.207b)
I shall now describe another diamond-binding (<s>vajrabandha</s>), O one worshipped by the gods. (RA 18.208)
One whose limbs are deficient or excessive, afflicted with disease, hunchbacked, bent, (RA 18.209a)
with crooked feet, hands devoid of offspring, with senses debilitated by old age — (RA 18.209b)
even one who is dull, stammering, mute, or immobile — (RA 18.210a)
freed from the shell-like skin [of old age], he stands alive [renewed]. (RA 18.210b)
By the power of this bound [mercury], when a rolling (<s>samāvarta</s>) is made, (RA 18.211a)
one should take mercury of ten-million-fold transmutation power, combined with six pellets. (RA 18.211b)

children.text:
ekaikasya tu madhyasthāṃ guṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ //
                    (RA_18.212)
children.translated_text: In the center of each one, the wise one should make a pill. (RA 18.212)

children.text:
guṭikāḥ pañcasaṃkhyātāḥ ṣaṣṭhī caiva tu pañcamī /
                    (213.1)
children.translated_text: The pills are five in number, and the sixth is the fifth [i.e., the central one]. (RA 18.213a)
The sixfold pellet [requires] a beautiful copper vessel. (RA 18.213b)

children.text:
ūrdhvaṃ puruṣamātraṃ tu puruṣārdhaṃ ca maṇḍalam /
                    (213.3)
children.translated_text: The height [of the vessel should be] one person's height; the circumference, half a person. (RA 18.213c)
Four-mouthed [i.e., having four openings], made of wood — one should offer [fuel] upon it. (RA 18.213d)
One should coat [the interior] with ghee and great oil (<s>mahātaila</s>) in equal proportion. (RA 18.214a)

children.text:
pūjayitvā kaṭāhaṃ tu dikpālāṃś caiva pūjayet //
                    (RA_18.214.2)
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the cauldron, one should also worship the guardians of the directions (<s>dikpāla</s>). (RA 18.214b)

children.text:
kumārīṃ pūjayet paścād dadyāddikṣu baliṃ tathā /
                    (RA_18.215.1)
children.translated_text: One should worship a maiden (<s>kumārī</s>), then give offerings in the [four] directions. (RA 18.215a)

children.text:
dhamanaṃ tatra kurvīta caturdikṣu śanaiḥ śanaiḥ //
                    (215.2)
children.translated_text: One should perform bellowing there, in the four directions, gradually. (RA 18.215b)

children.text:
sutaptaṃ ca vidhātavyaṃ nirdhūmaṃ ca yadā bhavet /
                    (216.1)
children.translated_text: When it is well-heated and when it becomes smokeless, (RA 18.216a)
then, having bowed to the teacher, the deity, the moon, sun, and other planets, (RA 18.216b)

children.text:
nakṣatrāṇi ca sampūjya ātmānaṃ tatra nikṣipet //
                    (RA_18.216.3)
children.translated_text: and having worshipped the constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>), one should cast oneself into it. (RA 18.216c)
Earth, water, fire, air, and space — (RA 18.217a)
one should recognize [these stages as] exceedingly rare and apply the form of <s>siddhi</s>. (RA 18.217b)

children.text:
kalalaṃ ca bhavet sarvaṃ puraś cāpo vinikṣipet /
                    (RA_18.218.1)
children.translated_text: All becomes a liquid mass (<s>kalala</s>); then, at the beginning, one should pour water. (RA 18.218a)
One should recognize the red color [stage]; one should unite fire with fire. (RA 18.218b)

children.text:
māṃsapiṇḍaṃ bhavet tatra vāyuṃ tatraiva nikṣipet /
                    (219.1)
children.translated_text: A lump of flesh forms there; one should then cast in the wind [element]. (RA 18.219a)

children.text:
kāntavarṇaṃ tadā kāryaṃ nikṣipet khaṃ kapālake //
                    (219.2)
children.translated_text: Then the beautiful color should be produced; one should cast space [element] into the skull-cup. (RA 18.219b)

children.text:
dhamantaṃ hemasaṃkāśaṃ kṣāratvaṃ taṃ tu pādayet //
                    (RA_18.220)
children.translated_text: While being bellowed [i.e., heated], when gold-like in appearance, one should make it alkaline. (RA 18.220)
Making a great roar there — the sacred <s>hum</s>-sound worshipped by the gods — (RA 18.221a)

children.text:
uttiṣṭhati na sandehaḥ puṣṭāṅgo bhāskaro yathā /
                    (RA_18.221.2)
children.translated_text: he rises up, without doubt, with nourished limbs, like the sun. (RA 18.221b)
Of divine splendor, of great body, of divine sight, of great strength. (RA 18.221c)
A [chariot] resounding with bell-sound extending a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, well-worshipped, (RA 18.222a)
blazing, golden, divine, adorned with gems and rubies, (RA 18.222b)
rich with garlands of flowers and banners, decorated with nets of tiny bells, (RA 18.223)
mounted on the supreme aerial chariot (<s>vimāna</s>), with the sounds of conches and trumpets, (RA 18.223b)
with songs and music of <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), with captivating dances, (RA 18.224a)
adorned with all divine ornaments, embellished with celestial garlands, (RA 18.224b)
endowed with sidelong glances and passion, beautiful in form, intoxicated with joy — (RA 18.225a)
without doubt, a divine maiden comes toward [him]. (RA 18.225b)

children.text:
gṛhītvā sādhakendraṃ ca siddhaloke vaset tataḥ //
                    (RA_18.226)
children.translated_text: Taking the supreme practitioner (<s>sādhakendra</s>), he then dwells in the world of the <s>Siddhas</s>. (RA 18.226)
Divine baths and drinks, divine ornaments — he (RA 18.227)
enjoys a hundred thousand <s>siddha</s>-maidens afflicted by desire. (RA 18.227)
In that terrible single ocean [of dissolution], when the moving and stationary [beings] are destroyed, (RA 18.228)
where even the gods dissolve — the <s>siddha</s> dissolves there too. (RA 18.228)
This fierce [dissolution] called <s>Bhūtakālāntaka</s> [Destroyer of the Time of Beings] has been described. (RA 18.229)

children.text:
tattvato'yaṃ mahādevi yadā kartuṃ na śakyate /
                    (RA_18.230.1)
children.translated_text: When this, O Great Goddess, cannot in truth be accomplished, (RA 18.230)
then perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) shall come in this very body. (RA 18.230)
